## Overview

    

When you develop OpenBMC services, you need a fast feedback loop: change code, build it, push it to a running system, and verify the result. A full `bitbake obmc-phosphor-image` rebuild takes 30 minutes or more, which makes iterative development painfully slow.

This guide teaches you the **devtool modify-build-deploy** cycle that reduces your iteration time to under 5 minutes. You will learn how to extract a recipe’s source code, make changes, build only the modified recipe, deploy the updated binary to a running QEMU instance, and debug it with gdbserver – all without rebuilding the entire image.

By the end of this guide, you will have hands-on experience modifying `phosphor-state-manager`, deploying your changes to QEMU, and verifying them with D-Bus commands.

**Key concepts covered:**

* Extracting recipe source with `devtool modify`
* Incremental builds with `devtool build`
* Deploying binaries via SCP and `devtool deploy-target`
* Remote debugging with gdbserver and GDB
* Complete worked example with phosphor-state-manager

---

## Prerequisites

    

Before starting this guide, make sure you have:

* A working OpenBMC build environment ([Environment Setup](/openbmc-guide-tutorial/docs/01-getting-started/02-environment-setup.html))
* A completed first build of `obmc-phosphor-image` ([First Build](/openbmc-guide-tutorial/docs/01-getting-started/03-first-build.html))
* QEMU running with the ast2600-evb image ([Building QEMU](/openbmc-guide-tutorial/docs/01-getting-started/05-qemu-build.html))
* Familiarity with devtool basics ([Development Workflow](/openbmc-guide-tutorial/docs/01-getting-started/04-development-workflow.html))

This guide assumes you can SSH into your QEMU instance at `localhost:2222` with credentials `root` / `0penBmc`. Start QEMU before proceeding.

---

## Step 1: Extract Source with devtool modify

    

The `devtool modify` command extracts a recipe’s source code into a local workspace directory where you can edit it freely. The build system automatically redirects future builds of that recipe to use your local copy instead of fetching from upstream.

### Initialize Your Build Environment

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="nb">cd </span>openbmc
<span class="nb">.</span> setup ast2600-evb
```

</div></div>

### Extract the Recipe Source

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Extract phosphor-state-manager source to your workspace</span>
devtool modify phosphor-state-manager
```

</div></div>

This command performs three actions:

1. Clones the recipe’s source repository into `workspace/sources/phosphor-state-manager/`
2. Creates a bbappend file at `workspace/appends/phosphor-state-manager.bbappend`
3. Configures the build system to use your local source for all future builds

### Verify the Extraction

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check that the recipe is now in your workspace</span>
devtool status

<span class="c"># Expected output:</span>
<span class="c"># phosphor-state-manager  /path/to/openbmc/build/ast2600-evb/workspace/sources/phosphor-state-manager</span>

<span class="c"># Browse the source tree</span>
<span class="nb">ls </span>workspace/sources/phosphor-state-manager/
```

</div></div>

You see the full source tree including `meson.build`, source files under `host_state_manager.cpp`, `chassis_state_manager.cpp`, and other service implementations.

### Understand the Workspace Layout

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
workspace/
├── sources/
│   └── phosphor-state-manager/    # Your editable source code (git repo)
│       ├── meson.build
│       ├── host_state_manager.cpp
│       ├── chassis_state_manager.cpp
│       ├── bmc_state_manager.cpp
│       └── ...
└── appends/
    └── phosphor-state-manager.bbappend  # Auto-generated build redirect
```

</div></div>

The workspace source directory is a full git repository. You can use `git diff`, `git stash`, and `git commit` to manage your changes just like any other git project.

---

## Step 2: Build Incrementally with devtool build

    

After modifying source code, you use `devtool build` to compile only the changed recipe. This skips fetching, patching, and building all other recipes, reducing build time from 30+ minutes to 1-3 minutes.

### Make a Code Change

    

Open a source file and add a visible marker so you can verify your change on the target:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="nb">cd </span>workspace/sources/phosphor-state-manager
```

</div></div>

Edit `bmc_state_manager.cpp` and add a log message near the top of the constructor or an initialization function:

<div class="language-cpp highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c1">// Add this line after the existing includes</span>
<span class="cp">#include</span> <span class="cpf">
// Inside the BMCStateManager constructor or relevant init path, add:
lg2::info("DEVTOOL-TEST: phosphor-state-manager modified successfully");
```

The exact location depends on the current upstream code. Look for the `BMCStateManager` constructor in `bmc_state_manager.cpp` and add the log line at the beginning of the function body.

### Build the Modified Recipe

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Return to the build directory</span>
<span class="nb">cd</span> /path/to/openbmc/build/ast2600-evb

<span class="c"># Build only phosphor-state-manager</span>
devtool build phosphor-state-manager
```

</div></div>

The build takes 1-3 minutes. Watch for any compilation errors in the output. If you see errors, fix them in the source file and run `devtool build` again.

### Locate the Build Output

    

After a successful build, find the compiled binaries:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Find the built binary</span>
find tmp/work/<span class="k">*</span>/phosphor-state-manager/<span class="k">*</span>/image <span class="nt">-name</span> <span class="s2">"phosphor-bmc-state-manager"</span> <span class="nt">-type</span> f

<span class="c"># Typical location:</span>
<span class="c"># tmp/work/armv7ahf-vfpv4d16-openbmc-linux-gnueabi/phosphor-state-manager/1.0+git*/image/usr/bin/phosphor-bmc-state-manager</span>
```

</div></div>

You can also find all installed files from the recipe by listing the `image/` directory. This shows you exactly what the recipe installs on the target system.

### Rebuild After Additional Changes

    

The devtool build cycle is fully incremental. Each time you edit source files and run `devtool build`, only the changed files are recompiled:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Edit source...</span>
vi workspace/sources/phosphor-state-manager/bmc_state_manager.cpp

<span class="c"># Rebuild (only recompiles changed files)</span>
devtool build phosphor-state-manager
```

</div></div>
---

## Step 3: Deploy to Target

    

You have two options for getting your modified binary onto the running QEMU instance: manual SCP or `devtool deploy-target`. Each has advantages depending on your workflow.

### Option A: Deploy via SCP (Manual)

    

SCP gives you precise control over which files you copy and where they go. This is useful when you want to replace a single binary without touching anything else.

**Find the binary on the target:**

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># SSH into QEMU to find where the binary lives</span>
ssh <span class="nt">-p</span> 2222 root@localhost <span class="s2">"which phosphor-bmc-state-manager"</span>
<span class="c"># Output: /usr/bin/phosphor-bmc-state-manager</span>
```

</div></div>

**Copy the built binary to the target:**

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># From your build host, SCP the new binary</span>
scp <span class="nt">-P</span> 2222 <span class="se">\</span>
    tmp/work/armv7ahf-vfpv4d16-openbmc-linux-gnueabi/phosphor-state-manager/1.0+git<span class="k">*</span>/image/usr/bin/phosphor-bmc-state-manager <span class="se">\</span>
    root@localhost:/usr/bin/phosphor-bmc-state-manager
```

</div></div>

The OpenBMC root filesystem is a read-only overlay by default on some configurations. If SCP fails with a “read-only file system” error, remount the filesystem read-write first: `ssh -p 2222 root@localhost "mount -o remount,rw /"`.

**Restart the service to load the new binary:**

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
ssh <span class="nt">-p</span> 2222 root@localhost <span class="s2">"systemctl restart xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC"</span>
```

</div></div>

**Verify the service is running with your changes:**

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
ssh <span class="nt">-p</span> 2222 root@localhost <span class="s2">"systemctl status xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC"</span>
ssh <span class="nt">-p</span> 2222 root@localhost <span class="s2">"journalctl -u xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC --no-pager -n 20"</span>
```

</div></div>

Look for your `DEVTOOL-TEST` log message in the journal output.

### Option B: Deploy via devtool deploy-target (Automated)

    

`devtool deploy-target` automates the file copy process. It deploys all files that the recipe installs (binaries, configuration files, libraries) to the correct locations on the target.

**Set up SSH key access (one-time setup):**

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Generate an SSH key if you do not have one</span>
ssh-keygen <span class="nt">-t</span> ed25519 <span class="nt">-f</span> ~/.ssh/id_openbmc <span class="nt">-N</span> <span class="s2">""</span>

<span class="c"># Copy the key to the QEMU target</span>
ssh-copy-id <span class="nt">-p</span> 2222 <span class="nt">-i</span> ~/.ssh/id_openbmc root@localhost
```

</div></div>

**Deploy all recipe files to the target:**

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
devtool deploy-target phosphor-state-manager root@localhost:2222
```

</div></div>

This command:

1. Identifies all files the recipe installs (binaries, configs, systemd units)
2. Copies them to the correct paths on the target via SSH
3. Preserves file permissions and ownership

`devtool deploy-target` uses SSH internally, so you need password-less SSH access (key-based) or you will be prompted for the password multiple times.

**Restart the service after deployment:**

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
ssh <span class="nt">-p</span> 2222 root@localhost <span class="s2">"systemctl restart xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC"</span>
```

</div></div>

**Verify the deployment:**

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
ssh <span class="nt">-p</span> 2222 root@localhost <span class="s2">"journalctl -u xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC --no-pager -n 20"</span>
```

</div></div>

### Undeploy from Target

    

If you need to revert the target to its original state, use `devtool undeploy-target`:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
devtool undeploy-target phosphor-state-manager root@localhost:2222
```

</div></div>

This removes all files that `deploy-target` installed and restores the originals.

### When to Use SCP vs deploy-target

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Situation | Recommended Method |
| --- | --- |
| Replace a single binary quickly | SCP |
| Deploy recipe with many files (bins + configs + units) | `devtool deploy-target` |
| Target has no SSH key set up | SCP with password |
| Need to revert changes easily | `devtool deploy-target` (supports undeploy) |
| Deploying to real hardware over network | `devtool deploy-target` |

</div>
---

## Step 4: Iterative Debug with gdbserver

    

When log messages are not enough to diagnose a problem, you can attach a debugger to a running service on the target. This section shows you how to use gdbserver on the QEMU target and connect to it with GDB on your build host.

### Install gdbserver on the Target

    

The default OpenBMC image may not include gdbserver. You have two ways to add it.

**Option A: Add gdbserver to the image (recommended for repeated use):**

Add the following to your `conf/local.conf` before building:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># In conf/local.conf</span>
IMAGE_INSTALL:append <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s2">" gdbserver"</span>
```

</div></div>

Then rebuild the image:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
bitbake obmc-phosphor-image
```

</div></div>

**Option B: Build and deploy gdbserver separately:**

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Build gdbserver as a standalone package</span>
devtool modify gdb
devtool build gdb

<span class="c"># Deploy just gdbserver to target</span>
scp <span class="nt">-P</span> 2222 <span class="se">\</span>
    tmp/work/armv7ahf-vfpv4d16-openbmc-linux-gnueabi/gdb/<span class="k">*</span>/image/usr/bin/gdbserver <span class="se">\</span>
    root@localhost:/usr/bin/gdbserver
```

</div></div>

### Attach gdbserver to a Running Service

    

On the QEMU target, find the process ID of the service you want to debug and attach gdbserver:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># SSH into the target</span>
ssh <span class="nt">-p</span> 2222 root@localhost

<span class="c"># Find the PID of the service</span>
pidof phosphor-bmc-state-manager
<span class="c"># Example output: 1234</span>

<span class="c"># Attach gdbserver to the running process on port 3333</span>
gdbserver <span class="nt">--attach</span> :3333 1234
```

</div></div>

gdbserver pauses the process and waits for a GDB client to connect.

Attaching gdbserver pauses the target process. Other OpenBMC services that depend on the paused service may time out or report errors. This is expected during debugging.

### Start gdbserver with a New Process

    

If you prefer to start the service under gdbserver from the beginning (to catch initialization issues):

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># On the target, stop the service first</span>
ssh <span class="nt">-p</span> 2222 root@localhost

systemctl stop xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC

<span class="c"># Start under gdbserver</span>
gdbserver :3333 /usr/bin/phosphor-bmc-state-manager
```

</div></div>

### Connect from the Host with GDB

    

On your build host, you need an ARM-compatible GDB. The OpenBMC SDK provides one, or you can use the one built by bitbake:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Find the cross GDB in your build environment</span>
find tmp/work/x86_64-linux <span class="nt">-name</span> <span class="s2">"arm-openbmc-linux-gnueabi-gdb"</span> <span class="nt">-type</span> f 2>/dev/null

<span class="c"># Or use the SDK's GDB if you have the SDK installed</span>
<span class="c"># Typically at: /opt/openbmc-sdk/sysroots/x86_64-pokysdk-linux/usr/bin/arm-openbmc-linux-gnueabi/arm-openbmc-linux-gnueabi-gdb</span>
```

</div></div>

Connect to the remote gdbserver:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Start GDB with the unstripped binary (contains debug symbols)</span>
arm-openbmc-linux-gnueabi-gdb <span class="se">\</span>
    tmp/work/armv7ahf-vfpv4d16-openbmc-linux-gnueabi/phosphor-state-manager/1.0+git<span class="k">*</span>/image/usr/bin/phosphor-bmc-state-manager
```

</div></div>

Inside the GDB session:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
(gdb) target remote localhost:3333
Remote debugging using localhost:3333
...

(gdb) break bmc_state_manager.cpp:42
Breakpoint 1 at 0x...: file bmc_state_manager.cpp, line 42.

(gdb) continue
Continuing.
```

</div></div>

QEMU forwards port 3333 from the target if you add `-net user,hostfwd=tcp::3333-:3333` to your QEMU command line. Alternatively, since you already have SSH access, you can use an SSH tunnel: `ssh -p 2222 -L 3333:localhost:3333 root@localhost`.

### Common GDB Commands for OpenBMC Debugging

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `bt` | Print backtrace of the current thread |
| `info threads` | List all threads in the process |
| `thread 2` | Switch to thread 2 |
| `p variable_name` | Print the value of a variable |
| `watch variable_name` | Break when a variable changes |
| `info breakpoints` | List all breakpoints |
| `continue` | Resume execution |
| `next` | Step over (execute next line) |
| `step` | Step into (enter function calls) |
| `finish` | Run until current function returns |

</div>

### Build with Debug Symbols

    

For the most useful debugging experience, ensure your recipe builds with debug symbols. Add this to `conf/local.conf`:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Enable debug symbols for all recipes</span>
DEBUG_BUILD <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s2">"1"</span>

<span class="c"># Or enable debug symbols for a specific recipe only</span>
DEBUG_FLAGS:pn-phosphor-state-manager <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s2">"-g -Og"</span>
```

</div></div>

Debug builds produce larger binaries and run slightly slower. Use this only during active debugging and remove it when you are done.

---

## Complete Worked Example: Modify phosphor-state-manager

    

This section walks through the entire modify-build-deploy-verify cycle from start to finish. Follow each step exactly to build confidence with the workflow.

### Background

    

`phosphor-state-manager` manages BMC, chassis, and host power states in OpenBMC. It exposes D-Bus interfaces that other services use to query and control system power. You will add a custom property to the BMC state manager and verify it appears on D-Bus.

### Step 1: Start QEMU

    

If QEMU is not already running, start it in a separate terminal:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="nb">cd </span>openbmc/build/ast2600-evb

qemu-system-arm <span class="nt">-m</span> 1G <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-M</span> ast2600-evb <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-nographic</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-drive</span> <span class="nv">file</span><span class="o">=</span>tmp/deploy/images/ast2600-evb/obmc-phosphor-image-ast2600-evb.static.mtd,format<span class="o">=</span>raw,if<span class="o">=</span>mtd <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-net</span> nic <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-net</span> user,hostfwd<span class="o">=</span>tcp::2222-:22,hostfwd<span class="o">=</span>tcp::2443-:443,hostfwd<span class="o">=</span>udp::2623-:623
```

</div></div>

Wait for the login prompt (takes 2-3 minutes). Verify SSH access:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
ssh <span class="nt">-p</span> 2222 root@localhost <span class="s2">"obmcutil state"</span>
```

</div></div>

### Step 2: Extract the Source

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="nb">cd </span>openbmc
<span class="nb">.</span> setup ast2600-evb

<span class="c"># Extract phosphor-state-manager</span>
devtool modify phosphor-state-manager

<span class="c"># Verify</span>
devtool status
```

</div></div>

### Step 3: Examine the Current State on the Target

    

Before making changes, observe the current D-Bus state so you can compare later:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Query the BMC state object</span>
ssh <span class="nt">-p</span> 2222 root@localhost <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC </span><span class="se">\</span><span class="s2">
     /xyz/openbmc_project/state/bmc0"</span>
```

</div></div>

You see properties like `CurrentBMCState`, `RequestedBMCTransition`, and others. Note the current values.

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check the service journal</span>
ssh <span class="nt">-p</span> 2222 root@localhost <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"journalctl -u xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC --no-pager -n 10"</span>
```

</div></div>

### Step 4: Make the Code Change

    

Navigate to the workspace source and add a log message:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="nb">cd </span>workspace/sources/phosphor-state-manager
```

</div></div>

Edit `bmc_state_manager.cpp`. Find the `BMC::BMC` constructor (or the `discoverInitialState` method) and add a log line:

<div class="language-cpp highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c1">// Add near the top of the constructor or discoverInitialState():</span>
<span class="n">lg2</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">info</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"DEVTOOL-GUIDE: BMC State Manager started with devtool modifications"</span><span class="p">);</span>
```

</div></div>

Save the file.

### Step 5: Build

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Return to build directory</span>
<span class="nb">cd</span> /path/to/openbmc/build/ast2600-evb

<span class="c"># Build only the modified recipe</span>
devtool build phosphor-state-manager
```

</div></div>

Watch the output for `NOTE: Tasks Summary: ...` at the end. A successful build shows zero failed tasks.

If the build fails with a meson error, check that your code change has correct C++ syntax. Common mistakes include missing semicolons and unmatched braces. Run `devtool build phosphor-state-manager` again after fixing.

### Step 6: Deploy to QEMU

    

Use SCP to deploy the modified binary:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Find the built binary path</span>
<span class="nv">BINARY</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="si">$(</span>find tmp/work/armv7ahf-vfpv4d16-openbmc-linux-gnueabi/phosphor-state-manager/ <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-path</span> <span class="s2">"*/image/usr/bin/phosphor-bmc-state-manager"</span> <span class="nt">-type</span> f | <span class="nb">head</span> <span class="nt">-1</span><span class="si">)</span>

<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"Deploying: </span><span class="nv">$BINARY</span><span class="s2">"</span>

<span class="c"># Copy to target</span>
scp <span class="nt">-P</span> 2222 <span class="s2">"</span><span class="nv">$BINARY</span><span class="s2">"</span> root@localhost:/usr/bin/phosphor-bmc-state-manager
```

</div></div>

### Step 7: Restart and Verify

    

Restart the service on the target and check for your log message:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Restart the BMC state manager service</span>
ssh <span class="nt">-p</span> 2222 root@localhost <span class="s2">"systemctl restart xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC"</span>

<span class="c"># Wait a moment for the service to start</span>
<span class="nb">sleep </span>2

<span class="c"># Check service status</span>
ssh <span class="nt">-p</span> 2222 root@localhost <span class="s2">"systemctl status xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC"</span>
```

</div></div>

Verify your log message appears in the journal:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
ssh <span class="nt">-p</span> 2222 root@localhost <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"journalctl -u xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC --no-pager -n 30 | grep DEVTOOL-GUIDE"</span>
```

</div></div>

You should see output similar to:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<timestamp> ast2600-evb phosphor-bmc-state-manager[1234]: DEVTOOL-GUIDE: BMC State Manager started with devtool modifications
```

</div></div>

Verify the D-Bus interface is still functioning correctly:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Query BMC state - should return valid state</span>
ssh <span class="nt">-p</span> 2222 root@localhost <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC </span><span class="se">\</span><span class="s2">
     /xyz/openbmc_project/state/bmc0 </span><span class="se">\</span><span class="s2">
     xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC CurrentBMCState"</span>

<span class="c"># Expected: s "xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC.BMCState.Ready"</span>
```

</div></div>

### Step 8: Iterate

    

Now that you have a working deploy cycle, you can iterate quickly:

1. Edit source in `workspace/sources/phosphor-state-manager/`
2. Run `devtool build phosphor-state-manager`
3. SCP the binary to the target
4. Restart the service
5. Check the logs

Each iteration takes 2-3 minutes instead of 30+.

### Step 9: Clean Up

    

When you are done experimenting, reset your workspace:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Remove the recipe from your workspace</span>
devtool reset phosphor-state-manager

<span class="c"># Verify it is removed</span>
devtool status
```

</div></div>

`devtool reset` deletes your workspace source directory. If you want to keep your changes, commit them with `git commit` inside the workspace source directory first. You can also use `devtool finish phosphor-state-manager meta-your-layer` to save changes as a bbappend with patches.

    <tr>
      <th>Command</th>

## Troubleshooting

    

### Issue: devtool build fails with “Nothing PROVIDES”

    

**Symptom**: Build error mentioning missing dependencies.

**Cause**: The recipe depends on other recipes that have not been built yet.

**Solution**:

1. Build the full image first to populate the sstate cache:
    
```
bitbake obmc-phosphor-image
```
2. Then use `devtool build`:
    
```
devtool build phosphor-state-manager
```

### Issue: SCP fails with “Permission denied”

    

**Symptom**: `scp: /usr/bin/phosphor-bmc-state-manager: Permission denied`

**Cause**: The target filesystem is mounted read-only or the file is in use.

**Solution**:

1. Remount the filesystem read-write:
    
```
ssh -p 2222 root@localhost "mount -o remount,rw /"
```
2. Stop the service before copying:
    
```
ssh -p 2222 root@localhost "systemctl stop xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC"
scp -P 2222 "$BINARY" root@localhost:/usr/bin/phosphor-bmc-state-manager
ssh -p 2222 root@localhost "systemctl start xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC"
```

### Issue: Service fails to start after deploying new binary

    

**Symptom**: `systemctl status` shows the service in “failed” state.

**Cause**: The new binary may have a runtime error, missing library, or ABI mismatch.

**Solution**:

1. Check the journal for error details:
    
```
ssh -p 2222 root@localhost \
    "journalctl -u xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC --no-pager -n 50"
```
2. Verify the binary is the correct architecture:
    
```
ssh -p 2222 root@localhost "file /usr/bin/phosphor-bmc-state-manager"
# Expected: ELF 32-bit LSB executable, ARM, ...
```
3. Check for missing shared libraries:
    
```
ssh -p 2222 root@localhost "ldd /usr/bin/phosphor-bmc-state-manager"
```

### Issue: gdbserver connection refused

    

**Symptom**: GDB reports “Connection refused” when connecting to the remote target.

**Cause**: Port forwarding is not configured or gdbserver is not running.

**Solution**:

1. Verify gdbserver is running on the target:
    
```
ssh -p 2222 root@localhost "ps aux | grep gdbserver"
```
2. Use an SSH tunnel instead of direct port forwarding:
    
```
# Set up tunnel in a separate terminal
ssh -p 2222 -L 3333:localhost:3333 root@localhost -N

# Then connect GDB to localhost:3333
(gdb) target remote localhost:3333
```

### Issue: GDB cannot find source files

    

**Symptom**: GDB shows `No source file named...` when setting breakpoints by file name.

**Cause**: The debug symbol paths in the binary do not match your host filesystem.

**Solution**: Set the source search path in GDB:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
(gdb) set substitute-path /usr/src/debug workspace/sources/phosphor-state-manager
(gdb) directory workspace/sources/phosphor-state-manager
```

</div></div>

### Debug Commands Cheat Sheet

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check service status on target</span>
ssh <span class="nt">-p</span> 2222 root@localhost <span class="s2">"systemctl status xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC"</span>

<span class="c"># View live logs</span>
ssh <span class="nt">-p</span> 2222 root@localhost <span class="s2">"journalctl -u xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC -f"</span>

<span class="c"># List D-Bus objects owned by state manager</span>
ssh <span class="nt">-p</span> 2222 root@localhost <span class="s2">"busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC"</span>

<span class="c"># Introspect a specific D-Bus object</span>
ssh <span class="nt">-p</span> 2222 root@localhost <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC </span><span class="se">\</span><span class="s2">
     /xyz/openbmc_project/state/bmc0"</span>

<span class="c"># Check what files a recipe installs</span>
devtool build phosphor-state-manager
find tmp/work/<span class="k">*</span>/phosphor-state-manager/<span class="k">*</span>/image <span class="nt">-type</span> f

<span class="c"># Check workspace status</span>
devtool status
```

</div></div>
---

# Gerrit Contribution Guide

    

Submit your first patch to the OpenBMC project using Gerrit code review.

</li>

2. [Verify the Hook](#verify-the-hook)

  </li>

1. [Rebase on Latest Master](#rebase-on-latest-master)

  </li>

1. [Why Upstream-First Matters](#why-upstream-first-matters)
2. [What Requires Upstream Submission](#what-requires-upstream-submission)
3. [Referencing Upstream Commits](#referencing-upstream-commits)

  </li>
  <li><a href="#quick-reference" id="markdown-toc-quick-reference">Quick Reference</a></li>
  <li><a href="#troubleshooting" id="markdown-toc-troubleshooting">Troubleshooting</a>    
1. [Issue: Push rejected with “missing Change-Id”](#issue-push-rejected-with-missing-change-id)
2. [Issue: Push rejected with “committer email does not match”](#issue-push-rejected-with-committer-email-does-not-match)
3. [Issue: Push rejected with “not permitted”](#issue-push-rejected-with-not-permitted)
4. [Issue: SSH connection times out](#issue-ssh-connection-times-out)

---

## Overview

    

OpenBMC uses [Gerrit](https://gerrit.openbmc.org/) for code review, not GitHub pull requests. Every change to the OpenBMC codebase goes through Gerrit review before it merges into the upstream repository.

This guide walks you through the entire contribution workflow: account creation, SSH setup, commit conventions, patch submission, reviewer feedback, CI validation, and the upstream-first kernel policy.

**Key concepts covered:**

* Creating a Gerrit account and configuring SSH access
* Installing the commit-msg hook for Change-Id generation
* Submitting patches with `git push origin HEAD:refs/for/master`
* Updating patches with `git commit --amend`
* Understanding Jenkins CI results and common failures
* OpenBMC’s upstream-first kernel policy

---

## Prerequisites

    

Before starting this guide, make sure you have:

* A working OpenBMC build environment ([Environment Setup](/openbmc-guide-tutorial/docs/01-getting-started/02-environment-setup.html))
* A completed first build of `obmc-phosphor-image` ([First Build](/openbmc-guide-tutorial/docs/01-getting-started/03-first-build.html))
* A GitHub account (used for Gerrit authentication)
* Git installed and configured with your name and email

OpenBMC Gerrit uses your GitHub account for authentication. You do not need to create a separate Gerrit account.

---

## Step 1: Create Your Gerrit Account

    

### Sign In and Configure

    

1. Open [https://gerrit.openbmc.org/](https://gerrit.openbmc.org/) and click **Sign In**.
2. Select **GitHub** as the authentication provider and authorize the application.
3. In Gerrit **Settings**, verify your display name and email under **Profile** and **Email Addresses**.

Verify your local git configuration matches your Gerrit email:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
git config <span class="nt">--global</span> user.name <span class="s2">"Your Full Name"</span>
git config <span class="nt">--global</span> user.email <span class="s2">"your-email@example.com"</span>
```

</div></div>

Your git `user.email` must match the email registered in Gerrit. Mismatched emails cause a “committer email does not match” rejection on push.

### Sign the Contributor License Agreement (CLA)

    

OpenBMC requires a signed CLA before you can submit patches:

1. In Gerrit Settings, go to **Agreements**.
2. Click **New Contributor Agreement**, select individual or corporate, and sign it.

If you contribute on behalf of your employer, check whether your company has already signed a corporate CLA. Contact the [OpenBMC mailing list](https://lists.ozlabs.org/listinfo/openbmc) if you are unsure.

---

## Step 2: Configure SSH Access

    

Gerrit uses SSH for git push and pull operations. Generate an SSH key pair and register the public key with Gerrit.

### Generate and Register Your Key

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Generate an SSH key (skip if you already have one)</span>
ssh-keygen <span class="nt">-t</span> ed25519 <span class="nt">-C</span> <span class="s2">"your-email@example.com"</span> <span class="nt">-f</span> ~/.ssh/id_openbmc
```

</div></div>

Copy the public key and add it in Gerrit under **Settings** > **SSH Keys**:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="nb">cat</span> ~/.ssh/id_openbmc.pub
```

</div></div>

### Configure SSH for Gerrit

    

Add a host entry to `~/.ssh/config` (create the file if it does not exist):

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
Host gerrit.openbmc.org
    User your-gerrit-username
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_openbmc
    Port 29418
```

</div></div>

Replace `your-gerrit-username` with your Gerrit username from Settings > Profile.

### Verify Connectivity

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
ssh <span class="nt">-p</span> 29418 gerrit.openbmc.org
```

</div></div>

A successful connection displays a “Welcome to Gerrit Code Review” banner.

If you see “Permission denied (publickey)”, verify that your SSH config points to the correct key file and that the public key is registered in Gerrit.

---

## Step 3: Install the commit-msg Hook

    

Gerrit tracks patches using a unique `Change-Id` in each commit message. The `commit-msg` hook generates this identifier automatically on every `git commit`.

### Clone and Install the Hook

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Clone the repository (example: phosphor-logging)</span>
git clone ssh://gerrit.openbmc.org:29418/openbmc/phosphor-logging
<span class="nb">cd </span>phosphor-logging

<span class="c"># Install the commit-msg hook</span>
scp <span class="nt">-p</span> <span class="nt">-P</span> 29418 gerrit.openbmc.org:hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/
<span class="nb">chmod</span> +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
```

</div></div>

### Verify the Hook

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">""</span> <span class="o">>></span> README.md
git add README.md
git commit <span class="nt">-m</span> <span class="s2">"Test commit-msg hook"</span>
git log <span class="nt">-1</span>
```

</div></div>

You should see a `Change-Id:` line appended to the commit message. After verifying, reset the test:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
git reset HEAD~1
git checkout <span class="nt">--</span> README.md
```

</div></div>

If the `Change-Id` line is missing, the hook is not installed correctly. Repeat the `scp` command above. Without a Change-Id, Gerrit rejects your push.

### Add the Hook to an Existing Clone

    

If you already cloned from GitHub, add the Gerrit remote and hook:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
git remote add gerrit ssh://gerrit.openbmc.org:29418/openbmc/<repo-name>
scp <span class="nt">-p</span> <span class="nt">-P</span> 29418 gerrit.openbmc.org:hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/
<span class="nb">chmod</span> +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
```

</div></div>
---

## Step 4: Submit a Patch

    

### Create a Topic Branch

    

Always work on a topic branch, never directly on `master`:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
git checkout master
git pull origin master
git checkout <span class="nt">-b</span> fix-typo-in-readme
```

</div></div>

### Commit with Sign-off

    

OpenBMC requires a `Signed-off-by` line in every commit (Developer Certificate of Origin). Use the `-s` flag:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
git add README.md
git commit <span class="nt">-s</span>
```

</div></div>

Write your commit message following this format:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
component: Short summary (50 chars or less)

Longer description explaining what you changed and why. Wrap at
72 characters. Focus on motivation, not mechanics.

Signed-off-by: Your Name <your-email@example.com>
Change-Id: Iabc123... (auto-generated by the hook)
```

</div></div>

The `-s` flag adds the `Signed-off-by` line automatically from your git config. You do not need to type it manually.

### Commit Message Guidelines

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Rule | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Start with component name and colon | `phosphor-logging: Fix memory leak` |
| Subject line under 50 characters | Short and descriptive |
| Imperative mood in subject | “Fix bug” not “Fixed bug” |
| Blank line after subject | Separates subject from body |
| Body wrapped at 72 characters | Readable in terminal and Gerrit |
| Explain *why*, not just *what* | The diff shows what changed |
| Include `Signed-off-by` (use `-s`) | Required for all patches |
| Keep the `Change-Id` line | Required for Gerrit tracking |

</div>

### Push to Gerrit

    

Push your commit using the special `refs/for/master` reference:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
git push origin HEAD:refs/for/master
```

</div></div>

Do **not** push to `refs/heads/master`. That attempts a direct push to master and is rejected. Always use `refs/for/master` to create a review.

A successful push shows a URL to your new review:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
remote:   https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-logging/+/12345 component: Short summary [NEW]
```

</div></div>

You can group related patches with a topic:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
git push origin HEAD:refs/for/master%topic<span class="o">=</span>fix-memory-leak
```

</div></div>
---

## Step 5: Update a Patch After Review

    

Reviewers may request changes. To update your patch, amend the existing commit and push again – do not create a new commit.

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Make the requested changes</span>
vi README.md
git add README.md

<span class="c"># Amend the existing commit (keeps the same Change-Id)</span>
git commit <span class="nt">--amend</span>

<span class="c"># Push the updated patch</span>
git push origin HEAD:refs/for/master
```

</div></div>

Gerrit detects the same `Change-Id` and creates a new **patch set** on the existing review.

Do not create a new commit for review updates. A new commit generates a new Change-Id and creates a separate review instead of updating the existing one.

### Rebase on Latest Master

    

If your patch falls behind master, rebase before pushing:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
git fetch origin
git rebase origin/master
<span class="c"># Resolve any conflicts, then:</span>
git rebase <span class="nt">--continue</span>
git push origin HEAD:refs/for/master
```

</div></div>

Rebasing preserves the `Change-Id`. Gerrit correctly associates the rebased commit with the original review.

---

## Step 6: Understand CI Integration

    

Every patch pushed to Gerrit triggers a Jenkins CI build. Jenkins compiles the code, runs tests, and reports results on the review.

### Jenkins Results

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Label | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Verified +1** | Build and tests passed |
| **Verified -1** | Build or tests failed |

</div>

Jenkins must report `Verified +1` before your patch can merge. A human reviewer must also approve with `Code-Review +2`. Click the build URL in the Jenkins comment to see full console output.

### Common CI Failure Reasons

    

**Compilation error**: Fix errors locally with `devtool build `, amend, and push again.

**Unit test failure**: Reproduce locally by building and checking test output. Fix the failing test before pushing.

**Formatting failure**: OpenBMC enforces `clang-format` for C/C++. Format your code before committing:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
clang-format <span class="nt">-i</span> path/to/your/file.cpp
```

</div></div>

**Merge conflict**: Rebase on latest master, resolve conflicts, and push.

Always build and test locally before pushing to Gerrit. This saves CI resources and reduces turnaround time.

---

## Step 7: Understand the Upstream-First Kernel Policy

    

OpenBMC follows a strict **upstream-first** policy for Linux kernel changes. Any kernel modification must first be submitted to the upstream Linux kernel (kernel.org) before it can be accepted into OpenBMC.

### Why Upstream-First Matters

    

* **Long-term maintenance**: Upstream patches are maintained by the Linux kernel community.
* **Quality assurance**: The upstream review process catches bugs early.
* **Broad compatibility**: Upstream drivers work across all platforms.
* **License compliance**: Keeps the OpenBMC kernel tree clean.

### What Requires Upstream Submission

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Change Type | Upstream Required? | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New device driver | Yes | ASPEED ADC driver |
| Device tree binding | Yes | New sensor node |
| Bug fix in existing driver | Yes | I2C timeout fix |
| Board device tree (.dts) | Yes (new SoC/board) | aspeed-bmc-vendor-board.dts |
| Kernel config change | No | Enable/disable CONFIG option |
| Backport of accepted patch | No | Cherry-pick from mainline |

</div>

### Referencing Upstream Commits

    

When backporting an upstream kernel patch, reference the commit in your message:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
ARM: dts: aspeed: Add sensor nodes for new platform

Backport upstream commit abc123def456 from Linux 6.x to the
OpenBMC kernel tree.

Upstream: https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/commit/?id=abc123def456
Signed-off-by: Your Name <your-email@example.com>
Change-Id: I...
```

</div></div>

If your change does not touch upstream kernel code (for example, a Yocto recipe change), the upstream-first policy does not apply.

---

## Quick Reference

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Clone from Gerrit | `git clone ssh://gerrit.openbmc.org:29418/openbmc/` |
| Install commit-msg hook | `scp -p -P 29418 gerrit.openbmc.org:hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/` |
| Submit new patch | `git push origin HEAD:refs/for/master` |
| Submit with topic | `git push origin HEAD:refs/for/master%topic=my-topic` |
| Update existing patch | `git commit --amend && git push origin HEAD:refs/for/master` |
| Check SSH access | `ssh -p 29418 gerrit.openbmc.org` |
| Query your open patches | `ssh -p 29418 gerrit.openbmc.org gerrit query owner:self status:open` |
| Download a patch locally | `git fetch origin refs/changes/45/12345/1 && git checkout FETCH_HEAD` |

</div>
---

## Troubleshooting

    

### Issue: Push rejected with “missing Change-Id”

    

**Symptom**: `git push` fails with “missing Change-Id in message footer”.

**Cause**: The `commit-msg` hook is not installed.

**Solution**: Install the hook, then amend the commit to trigger it:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
scp <span class="nt">-p</span> <span class="nt">-P</span> 29418 gerrit.openbmc.org:hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/
<span class="nb">chmod</span> +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
git commit <span class="nt">--amend</span> <span class="nt">--no-edit</span>
git push origin HEAD:refs/for/master
```

</div></div>

### Issue: Push rejected with “committer email does not match”

    

**Cause**: Your git `user.email` differs from Gerrit.

**Solution**: Update your email and amend:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
git config <span class="nt">--global</span> user.email <span class="s2">"your-gerrit-email@example.com"</span>
git commit <span class="nt">--amend</span> <span class="nt">--reset-author</span> <span class="nt">--no-edit</span>
git push origin HEAD:refs/for/master
```

</div></div>

### Issue: Push rejected with “not permitted”

    

**Cause**: Pushing to `refs/heads/master` instead of `refs/for/master`, or CLA not signed.

**Solution**: Use the correct reference and sign the CLA in Gerrit Settings > Agreements:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
git push origin HEAD:refs/for/master
```

</div></div>

### Issue: SSH connection times out

    

**Cause**: Firewall blocking port 29418.

**Solution**: Test with `nc -zv gerrit.openbmc.org 29418`. If blocked, ask your network administrator to allow outbound TCP on port 29418.

### Issue: Gerrit shows “Cannot merge”

    

**Cause**: A conflicting patch was merged while your review was pending.

**Solution**: Rebase and push:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
git fetch origin <span class="o">&&</span> git rebase origin/master
<span class="c"># Resolve conflicts, then:</span>
git rebase <span class="nt">--continue</span>
git push origin HEAD:refs/for/master
```

</div></div>
---

**Tested on**: Ubuntu 22.04, OpenBMC master branch (Kirkstone/Scarthgap), Gerrit 3.x

## Architecture Overview

    

OpenBMC follows a modular, service-oriented architecture built on Linux.

### High-Level Architecture

    

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph external["External Interfaces"]
        direction TB
        IPMI["IPMI  
(netipmid)"]
        Redfish["Redfish  
(bmcweb)"]
        WebUI["WebUI  
(webui-vue)"]
        SSH["SSH  
(dropbear)"]
        KVM["KVM  
(obmc-ikvm)"]
    end

    dbus["D-Bus (System Bus - Inter-process Communication)"]

    subgraph services["Phosphor Services"]

        subgraph row1[" "]
            State["State Manager"]
            Sensors["Sensors"]
            Logging["Logging"]
            Inventory["Inventory"]
        end
        subgraph row2[" "]
            Fan["Fan Control"]
            Power["Power Control"]
```

### Key Architectural Principles

    

1. **D-Bus as Central Nervous System**
    
* All services communicate via D-Bus
* Enables loose coupling and dynamic discovery
* Provides introspection and debugging capabilities
2. **Modular Services**
    
* Each function is a separate daemon
* Services can be replaced or customized independently
* Failures are isolated
3. **Configuration-Driven**
    
* Hardware configuration via JSON (Entity Manager)
* Service behavior via configuration files
* Build-time options via Yocto/meson
4. **Standard Interfaces**
    
* Redfish for modern management
* IPMI for legacy compatibility
* Standard Linux interfaces (hwmon, GPIO)

## Project Organization

    

### Repository Structure

    

The OpenBMC project spans multiple repositories:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
github.com/openbmc/
├── openbmc/                  # Main integration repository
├── phosphor-*/               # Core services
│   ├── phosphor-state-manager/
│   ├── phosphor-logging/
│   ├── phosphor-dbus-interfaces/
│   └── ...
├── bmcweb/                   # HTTP/Redfish server
├── dbus-sensors/             # Sensor daemons
├── entity-manager/           # Hardware discovery
├── meta-phosphor/            # Yocto layer
├── docs/                     # Documentation
└── ...
```

</div></div>

### Key Repositories

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Repository | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `openbmc/openbmc` | Main build integration, machine configs |
| `phosphor-dbus-interfaces` | D-Bus interface definitions (YAML) |
| `phosphor-state-manager` | BMC/Chassis/Host state control |
| `phosphor-logging` | Event logging |
| `dbus-sensors` | Sensor monitoring daemons |
| `bmcweb` | HTTP server, Redfish, WebUI backend |
| `entity-manager` | Hardware discovery and configuration |
| `phosphor-pid-control` | Thermal/fan control |

</div>

### Meta-Layer Structure

    

OpenBMC uses Yocto layers:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
openbmc/
├── meta-phosphor/           # Core OpenBMC layer
│   ├── recipes-phosphor/    # Phosphor service recipes
│   └── classes/             # BitBake classes
├── meta-openpower/          # OpenPOWER-specific
├── meta-ibm/                # IBM machines
├── meta-google/             # Google machines
├── meta-facebook/           # Facebook/Meta machines
├── meta-aspeed/             # ASPEED SoC support
└── meta-<vendor>/           # Your machine layer
```

</div></div>

## Build System

    

OpenBMC uses [Yocto Project](https://www.yoctoproject.org/) for building.

### Yocto Concepts

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Concept | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Recipe (.bb)** | Build instructions for a package |
| **Layer** | Collection of related recipes |
| **Machine** | Target hardware configuration |
| **Image** | Complete firmware image recipe |
| **BitBake** | Build tool that processes recipes |

</div>

```mermaid
    machine --> parse
    parse --> packages
    packages --> image
```

### Common D-Bus Tools

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># List all services</span>

<span class="c"># Inspect an object</span>
busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0

<span class="c"># Get a property</span>

<span class="c"># Call a method</span>
busctl call xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0 <span class="se">\</span>

    MethodName <signature> <arguments>
```

## Service Management

    

OpenBMC uses systemd for service management.

### Key systemd Commands

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># List OpenBMC services</span>
systemctl list-units <span class="s1">'xyz.openbmc_project.*'</span>

<span class="c"># Check service status</span>
systemctl status xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host.service

<span class="c"># View service logs</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host.service <span class="nt">-f</span>

<span class="c"># Restart a service</span>
systemctl restart xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host.service

<span class="c"># Check boot time</span>
systemd-analyze
systemd-analyze blame
```

</div></div>

### Service Dependencies

    

Services declare dependencies via systemd units:

<div class="language-ini highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Example: /lib/systemd/system/xyz.openbmc_project.Example.service
</span><span class="nn">[Unit]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Description</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">Example Service</span>
<span class="py">After</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">xyz.openbmc_project.ObjectMapper.service</span>
<span class="py">Requires</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">xyz.openbmc_project.ObjectMapper.service</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="nn">[Service]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">ExecStart</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">/usr/bin/example-daemon</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="nn">[Install]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">WantedBy</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">multi-user.target</span>
```

OpenBMC uses **Gerrit** for code review:

1. Clone with commit-msg hook:
    
```
git clone ssh://openbmc.gerrit/openbmc/phosphor-logging
scp -p openbmc.gerrit:hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/
```
2. Create feature branch
3. Make changes, commit with Change-Id
4. Push for review:
    
```
git push origin HEAD:refs/for/master
```
5. Address review feedback
6. Merge when approved

### Coding Standards

    

* C++: Follow [OpenBMC C++ style guide](https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/cpp-style-and-conventions.md)
* Python: PEP 8
* Commit messages: Conventional format with Change-Id

## Overview

    

D-Bus is the central communication system in OpenBMC. All services expose their functionality through D-Bus, enabling:

* **Loose coupling**: Services don’t need to know about each other’s implementation
* **Discovery**: Services can be found dynamically at runtime
* **Introspection**: Interfaces can be explored without documentation
* **Language agnostic**: Any language with D-Bus bindings can participate

---

## D-Bus Concepts

    

### Core Components

    

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    daemon["D-Bus Daemon  
(Message Router)"]

    subgraph services["Connected Services"]
        direction LR
        A["Service A  
xyz.openbmc_project.ServiceA"]
        B["Service B  
xyz.openbmc_project.ServiceB"]
        C["Service C  
xyz.openbmc_project.ServiceC"]
    end

    daemon <--> A
    daemon <--> B
    daemon <--> C
```

> **ASCII-art version (for comparison)**

  <div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                         D-Bus Daemon                            │
│                    (Message Router)                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
         │                    │                    │
         ▼                    ▼                    ▼
┌─────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────┐
│    Service A    │  │    Service B    │  │    Service C    │
│                 │  │                 │  │                 │
│ Well-known name │  │ Well-known name │  │ Well-known name │
│ xyz.openbmc_    │  │ xyz.openbmc_    │  │ xyz.openbmc_    │
│ project.ServiceA│  │ project.ServiceB│  │ project.ServiceC│
└─────────────────┘  └─────────────────┘  └─────────────────┘
```

</div>  </div>

### Terminology

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Term | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Bus** | Communication channel | System bus (shared by all) |
| **Service** | Application connected to bus | `xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host` |
| **Object** | Resource exposed by service | `/xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0` |
| **Interface** | Contract defining methods/properties | `xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host` |
| **Property** | Data exposed by object | `CurrentHostState` |
| **Method** | Action that can be invoked | `Reboot()` |
| **Signal** | Broadcast notification | `PropertiesChanged` |

</div>

### Naming Conventions

    

OpenBMC uses consistent naming:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
Service:   xyz.openbmc_project.<Category>.<Name>
Object:    /xyz/openbmc_project/<category>/<name>
Interface: xyz.openbmc_project.<Category>.<Name>
```

</div></div>

Examples:

* `xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host` - Host state service
* `/xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0` - Host 0 state object
* `xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value` - Sensor value interface

## Using busctl

    

`busctl` is the primary tool for D-Bus interaction.

### List Services

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># List all services</span>
busctl list

<span class="c"># Filter OpenBMC services</span>
busctl list | <span class="nb">grep </span>xyz.openbmc_project
```

</div></div>

### Explore Objects

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Show object tree for a service</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host

<span class="c"># Example output:</span>
<span class="c"># └─/xyz</span>
<span class="c">#   └─/xyz/openbmc_project</span>
<span class="c">#     └─/xyz/openbmc_project/state</span>
<span class="c">#       └─/xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0</span>
```

</div></div>

### Introspect Objects

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Show interfaces, methods, properties, signals</span>
busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0

<span class="c"># Example output:</span>
<span class="c"># NAME                                TYPE      SIGNATURE RESULT/VALUE</span>
<span class="c"># xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host      interface -         -</span>
<span class="c"># .CurrentHostState                   property  s         "xyz.openbmc_project..."</span>
<span class="c"># .RequestedHostTransition            property  s         "xyz.openbmc_project..."</span>
```

</div></div>

### Read Properties

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get a single property</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host <span class="se">\</span>
    CurrentHostState

<span class="c"># Output: s "xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host.HostState.Off"</span>
```

</div></div>

### Set Properties

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Set a property (request host power on)</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host <span class="se">\</span>
    RequestedHostTransition s <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host.Transition.On"</span>
```

</div></div>

### Call Methods

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Call a method</span>
busctl call xyz.openbmc_project.ObjectMapper <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/object_mapper <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.ObjectMapper <span class="se">\</span>
    GetSubTree sias <span class="s2">"/"</span> 0 1 <span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value"</span>
```

</div></div>

### Monitor Signals

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Watch for property changes</span>
busctl monitor xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host

<span class="c"># Watch all D-Bus traffic (verbose)</span>
dbus-monitor <span class="nt">--system</span>
```

</div></div>
---

## phosphor-dbus-interfaces

    

Interface definitions live in the `phosphor-dbus-interfaces` repository.

### YAML Format

    

Interfaces are defined in YAML:

<div class="language-yaml highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c1"># xyz/openbmc_project/Example/MyInterface.interface.yaml</span>
<span class="na">description</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="pi">></span>
    <span class="s">Example interface demonstrating YAML format.</span>

<span class="na">properties</span><span class="pi">:</span>
    <span class="pi">-</span> <span class="na">name</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">MyProperty</span>
      <span class="na">type</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">string</span>
      <span class="na">description</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">An example string property.</span>

    <span class="pi">-</span> <span class="na">name</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">MyValue</span>
      <span class="na">type</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">int32</span>
      <span class="na">description</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">An example integer property.</span>

<span class="na">methods</span><span class="pi">:</span>
    <span class="pi">-</span> <span class="na">name</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">DoSomething</span>
      <span class="na">description</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">Performs an action.</span>
      <span class="na">parameters</span><span class="pi">:</span>
          <span class="pi">-</span> <span class="na">name</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">Input</span>
            <span class="na">type</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">string</span>
            <span class="na">description</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">Input parameter.</span>
      <span class="na">returns</span><span class="pi">:</span>
          <span class="pi">-</span> <span class="na">name</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">Result</span>
            <span class="na">type</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">boolean</span>
            <span class="na">description</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">Success or failure.</span>

<span class="na">signals</span><span class="pi">:</span>
    <span class="pi">-</span> <span class="na">name</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">SomethingHappened</span>
      <span class="na">description</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">Emitted when something happens.</span>
      <span class="na">properties</span><span class="pi">:</span>
          <span class="pi">-</span> <span class="na">name</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">What</span>
            <span class="na">type</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">string</span>
```

</div></div>

### Type Signatures

    

D-Bus uses type signatures:

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Signature | Type | C++ Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `s` | String | `std::string` |
| `b` | Boolean | `bool` |
| `i` | Int32 | `int32_t` |
| `u` | Uint32 | `uint32_t` |
| `x` | Int64 | `int64_t` |
| `t` | Uint64 | `uint64_t` |
| `d` | Double | `double` |
| `o` | Object path | `sdbusplus::message::object_path` |
| `a` | Array | `std::vector` |
| `(...)` | Struct | `std::tuple` |
| `a{sv}` | Dict | `std::map>` |

</div>

## sdbusplus Library

    

`sdbusplus` is the C++ library for D-Bus in OpenBMC.

> **Source Reference**: sdbusplus
>   
>     Bus API: include/sdbusplus/bus.hpp
>     Examples: example/

### Creating a D-Bus Client

    

<div class="language-cpp highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="cp">#include</span> <span class="cpf"><sdbusplus/bus.hpp></span><span class="cp">
#include</span> <span class="cpf"><iostream></span><span class="cp">
</span>
<span class="kt">int</span> <span class="nf">main</span><span class="p">()</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="c1">// Connect to system bus</span>
    <span class="k">auto</span> <span class="n">bus</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">sdbusplus</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">bus</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">new_default</span><span class="p">();</span>

    <span class="c1">// Create method call</span>
    <span class="k">auto</span> <span class="n">method</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">bus</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">new_method_call</span><span class="p">(</span>
        <span class="s">"xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host"</span><span class="p">,</span>           <span class="c1">// Service</span>
        <span class="s">"/xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0"</span><span class="p">,</span>         <span class="c1">// Object</span>
        <span class="s">"org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties"</span><span class="p">,</span>          <span class="c1">// Interface</span>
        <span class="s">"Get"</span>                                        <span class="c1">// Method</span>
    <span class="p">);</span>

    <span class="c1">// Add arguments</span>
    <span class="n">method</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">append</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="c1">// Interface</span>
                  <span class="s">"CurrentHostState"</span><span class="p">);</span>               <span class="c1">// Property</span>

    <span class="c1">// Call and get reply</span>
    <span class="k">auto</span> <span class="n">reply</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">bus</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">call</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">method</span><span class="p">);</span>

    <span class="c1">// Extract result</span>
    <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">variant</span><span class="o"><</span><span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">string</span><span class="o">></span> <span class="n">value</span><span class="p">;</span>
    <span class="n">reply</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">read</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">value</span><span class="p">);</span>

    <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">cout</span> <span class="o"><<</span> <span class="s">"Host state: "</span> <span class="o"><<</span> <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">get</span><span class="o"><</span><span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">string</span><span class="o">></span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">value</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o"><<</span> <span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="p">;</span>

    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
```

</div></div>

### Creating a D-Bus Server

    

<div class="language-cpp highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="cp">#include</span> <span class="cpf"><sdbusplus/bus.hpp></span><span class="cp">
#include</span> <span class="cpf"><sdbusplus/server.hpp></span><span class="cp">
#include</span> <span class="cpf"><xyz/openbmc_project/Example/MyInterface/server.hpp></span><span class="cp">
</span>
<span class="c1">// Generated server binding</span>
<span class="k">using</span> <span class="n">MyInterfaceInherit</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">sdbusplus</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">server</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">object_t</span><span class="o"><</span>
    <span class="n">sdbusplus</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">xyz</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">openbmc_project</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">Example</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">server</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">MyInterface</span><span class="o">></span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">MyService</span> <span class="o">:</span> <span class="k">public</span> <span class="n">MyInterfaceInherit</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
  <span class="nl">public:</span>
    <span class="n">MyService</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">sdbusplus</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">bus_t</span><span class="o">&</span> <span class="n">bus</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">const</span> <span class="kt">char</span><span class="o">*</span> <span class="n">path</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">:</span>
        <span class="n">MyInterfaceInherit</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">bus</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">path</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="p">{</span>
        <span class="c1">// Initialize properties</span>
        <span class="n">myProperty</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"initial value"</span><span class="p">);</span>
    <span class="p">}</span>

    <span class="c1">// Property getter/setter are auto-generated</span>

    <span class="c1">// Implement methods</span>
    <span class="kt">bool</span> <span class="n">doSomething</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">string</span> <span class="n">input</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">override</span>
    <span class="p">{</span>
        <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">cout</span> <span class="o"><<</span> <span class="s">"doSomething called with: "</span> <span class="o"><<</span> <span class="n">input</span> <span class="o"><<</span> <span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="p">;</span>
        <span class="k">return</span> <span class="nb">true</span><span class="p">;</span>
    <span class="p">}</span>
<span class="p">};</span>

<span class="kt">int</span> <span class="nf">main</span><span class="p">()</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="k">auto</span> <span class="n">bus</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">sdbusplus</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">bus</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">new_default</span><span class="p">();</span>

    <span class="c1">// Request well-known name</span>
    <span class="n">bus</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">request_name</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"xyz.openbmc_project.Example"</span><span class="p">);</span>

    <span class="c1">// Create server object</span>
    <span class="n">MyService</span> <span class="n">myService</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">bus</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="s">"/xyz/openbmc_project/example"</span><span class="p">);</span>

    <span class="c1">// Process D-Bus events</span>
    <span class="k">while</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="nb">true</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="p">{</span>
        <span class="n">bus</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">process_discard</span><span class="p">();</span>
        <span class="n">bus</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">wait</span><span class="p">();</span>
    <span class="p">}</span>

    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
```

</div></div>

### Async with sdbusplus and Boost.Asio

    

<div class="language-cpp highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="cp">#include</span> <span class="cpf"><sdbusplus/asio/connection.hpp></span><span class="cp">
#include</span> <span class="cpf"><sdbusplus/asio/object_server.hpp></span><span class="cp">
#include</span> <span class="cpf"><boost/asio.hpp></span><span class="cp">
</span>
<span class="kt">int</span> <span class="nf">main</span><span class="p">()</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="n">boost</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">asio</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">io_context</span> <span class="n">io</span><span class="p">;</span>
    <span class="k">auto</span> <span class="n">conn</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">make_shared</span><span class="o"><</span><span class="n">sdbusplus</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">asio</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">connection</span><span class="o">></span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">io</span><span class="p">);</span>

    <span class="n">conn</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">request_name</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"xyz.openbmc_project.Example"</span><span class="p">);</span>

    <span class="n">sdbusplus</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">asio</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">object_server</span> <span class="n">server</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">conn</span><span class="p">);</span>

    <span class="k">auto</span> <span class="n">iface</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">server</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">add_interface</span><span class="p">(</span>
        <span class="s">"/xyz/openbmc_project/example"</span><span class="p">,</span>
        <span class="s">"xyz.openbmc_project.Example.MyInterface"</span>
    <span class="p">);</span>

    <span class="c1">// Add property</span>
    <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">string</span> <span class="n">myValue</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">"hello"</span><span class="p">;</span>
    <span class="n">iface</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">register_property</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"MyProperty"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">myValue</span><span class="p">,</span>
        <span class="c1">// Setter</span>
        <span class="p">[](</span><span class="k">const</span> <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">string</span><span class="o">&</span> <span class="n">newValue</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">string</span><span class="o">&</span> <span class="n">value</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">{</span>
            <span class="n">value</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">newValue</span><span class="p">;</span>
            <span class="k">return</span> <span class="nb">true</span><span class="p">;</span>
        <span class="p">}</span>
    <span class="p">);</span>

    <span class="n">iface</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">initialize</span><span class="p">();</span>

    <span class="n">io</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">run</span><span class="p">();</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
```

</div></div>
