## phosphor-objmgr (Object Mapper)

    

The Object Mapper tracks all D-Bus objects and their interfaces.

### Query Objects by Interface

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Find all objects implementing Sensor.Value</span>
busctl call xyz.openbmc_project.ObjectMapper <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/object_mapper <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.ObjectMapper <span class="se">\</span>
    GetSubTree sias <span class="s2">"/"</span> 0 1 <span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value"</span>
```

</div></div>

> The mapper exposes several other query methods on `xyz.openbmc_project.ObjectMapper` beyond `GetSubTree` and `GetObject`:
>   
>     **`GetAncestors`** – returns the objects that are ancestors of a given path (filtered to the requested interfaces). Useful for walking *up* the tree, e.g. from a sensor to its owning chassis.
>     **`GetAssociatedSubTree`** / **`GetAssociatedSubTreePaths`** – like `GetSubTree`, but restricted to paths that are an association endpoint of a supplied `associatedPath`.
>     **`GetAssociatedSubTreeById`** – resolves a subtree from an inventory `id` plus an `association` name, so you don’t need the full object path up front.

### Get Service for Object

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Find which service owns an object</span>
busctl call xyz.openbmc_project.ObjectMapper <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/object_mapper <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.ObjectMapper <span class="se">\</span>
    GetObject sas <span class="s2">"/xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0"</span> 0
```

</div></div>

### Using mapper CLI

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># List objects with interface</span>
mapper get-subtree / xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value

<span class="c"># Get service for object</span>
mapper get-service /xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0
```

</div></div>

### mapper Client Library (libmapper)

    

For C services that need to talk to the mapper without hand-rolling `busctl`-style calls, phosphor-objmgr ships a small C client library, **libmapper** (`libmapper/mapper.h`). It wraps the common lookups and, importantly, provides an **async “wait for object” primitive** used during boot ordering:

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Function | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `mapper_wait_async(bus, event, objs[], cb, userdata, &wait)` | Fire `cb` once every object path in `objs[]` has appeared on the bus |
| `mapper_subtree_async(bus, event, namespace, interface, cb, userdata, &subtree, op)` | Async subtree query (backed by `GetSubTreePaths`) |
| `mapper_get_object(bus, obj, &reply)` | Synchronous `GetObject` – returns the services + interfaces on a path |
| `mapper_get_service(bus, obj, &service)` | Convenience wrapper returning just the owning service name |

</div>

The async wait powers the templated **`mapper-wait@.service`** unit: a service can declare `After=` on `mapper-wait@-xyz-openbmc_project-...service` and systemd will block it until the required D-Bus object exists, rather than racing the object’s provider at startup.

<div class="language-ini highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Block a unit until a D-Bus object is present (path is systemd-escaped)
</span><span class="nn">[Unit]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">After</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">mapper-wait@-xyz-openbmc_project-state-host0.service</span>
<span class="py">Requires</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">mapper-wait@-xyz-openbmc_project-state-host0.service</span>
```

</div></div>
---

## Unit Failure Monitor

    

phosphor-objmgr also builds a small standalone tool, **phosphor-unit-failure-monitor** (from `fail-monitor/`), that watches a systemd unit and reacts when it fails. It reads the **`ActiveState`** property of a *source* unit and, if that state is `failed`, either starts or stops a *target* unit.

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-s`, `--source` | The unit to monitor (required) |
| `-t`, `--target` | The unit to start or stop when the source fails (required) |
| `-a`, `--action` | `start` or `stop` – what to do to the target (required) |

</div>

A typical use is a hardware watchdog takeover: if a fan-control service dies, hand control to a safe fallback target.

<div class="language-ini highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># fan-watchdog-monitor@.service (from meta-ibm)
</span><span class="nn">[Service]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">ExecStart</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">/usr/bin/phosphor-unit-failure-monitor </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">--source %i </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">--target obmc-fan-watchdog-takeover.target </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">--action start</span>
```

</div></div>

Internally the monitor calls `StartUnit`/`StopUnit` on `org.freedesktop.systemd1.Manager` after reading `ActiveState` from the source unit.

---

## D-Bus Associations

    

Associations link related objects together.

### Association Structure

    

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    sensor["/sensors/temp0  
  
associations:  
[inventory,sensors,  
/inventory/cpu0]"]
    inventory["/inventory/cpu0"]

    sensor -->|"sensors"| inventory
    inventory -->|"inventory"| sensor
```

> **ASCII-art version (click to expand)**

  <div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────┐           ┌─────────────────────┐
│  /sensors/temp0     │──────────▶│  /inventory/cpu0    │
│                     │  sensors  │                     │
│  associations:      │◀──────────│                     │
│  [inventory,sensors,│  inventory│                     │
│   /inventory/cpu0]  │           │                     │
└─────────────────────┘           └─────────────────────┘
```

</div>  </div>

### Query Associations

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get associations for an object</span>
busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.ObjectMapper <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/temperature/cpu0

<span class="c"># Look for 'associations' property and endpoints</span>
```

</div></div>
---

## Legacy D-Bus REST API

    

Before Redfish became the primary north-bound API, bmcweb exposed a **generic REST interface that maps directly onto D-Bus** (`features/openbmc_rest/openbmc_dbus_rest.hpp`). It is still present and handy for debugging, but is **largely superseded by Redfish** for production clients.

Treat this as a debugging/legacy interface. New integrations should use Redfish; the generic D-Bus REST API bypasses Redfish’s schema and access model.

The routes mirror the D-Bus object tree under `/xyz/...` and `/org/...`, plus a few helpers:

<div class="table-wrapper"><table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Route</th>
      <th>Method</th>
      <th>Action</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>`/xyz/
`, `/org/`
      `GET`
      Read an object’s interfaces and properties as JSON
    
    
      `/xyz//enumerate`
      `GET`
      Walk the whole subtree and dump every object/interface/property
    
    
      `/xyz/`
      `PUT` / `POST`
      Write a property or invoke a D-Bus method
    
    
      `/xyz/`
      `DELETE`
      Delete the object (if the owning service supports it)
    
    
      `/bus/system/`, `/list/`
      `GET`
      Enumerate bus names / all object paths
    
  

JSON is translated to and from native D-Bus types on the fly, using the object’s introspection data to pick signatures (`convertJsonToDbus` / `convertDBusToJSON`).

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Enumerate every sensor object and its properties in one call</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/enumerate

<span class="c"># Read a single property set</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0

<span class="c"># Write a property (PUT the D-Bus value as JSON)</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PUT <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{"data": "xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host.Transition.On"}'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0/attr/RequestedHostTransition
```

</div></div>

> **D-Bus monitoring over WebSockets.** bmcweb also exposes a `/subscribe/` WebSocket (`features/openbmc_rest/dbus_monitor.hpp`, `DbusWebsocketSession` / `SessionMap`) that streams D-Bus **`PropertiesChanged`** and **`InterfacesAdded`** signals to the browser as JSON – this is what drives live value updates in the web UI. The client opens the socket and sends a filter such as `{"paths": ["/xyz/openbmc_project/sensors"], "interfaces": ["xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value"]}`; matching signals then arrive as JSON messages. The bmcweb repo ships a runnable example, `scripts/websocket_test.py`, that streams sensor readings from a live BMC.

## Troubleshooting

    

### Common Issues

    

**Service not found:**

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check if service is running</span>
systemctl status xyz.openbmc_project.ServiceName

<span class="c"># Check service logs</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> xyz.openbmc_project.ServiceName
```

</div></div>

**Permission denied:**

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check D-Bus policy</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /usr/share/dbus-1/system.d/xyz.openbmc_project.<span class="k">*</span>.conf
```

</div></div>

**Property type mismatch:**

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Verify property type with introspect</span>
busctl introspect <service> <object> | <span class="nb">grep</span> 
```

### Debug Commands

    

```
# Verbose D-Bus monitoring
dbus-monitor --system "interface='xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host'"

# Check Object Mapper health
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.ObjectMapper

# List all interfaces on an object
busctl introspect   | grep interface
```

## Deep Dive

    

This section provides detailed technical information for developers who want to understand D-Bus internals in OpenBMC.

### D-Bus Message Flow Architecture

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        D-Bus Message Flow in OpenBMC                        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│  Client Application (e.g., bmcweb)                                          │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│  │  sdbusplus::bus::new_default()                                     │     │
│  │         │                                                          │     │
│  │         v                                                          │     │
│  │  bus.new_method_call(service, object, interface, method)           │     │
│  │         │                                                          │     │
│  │         v                                                          │     │
│  │  method.append(arg1, arg2, ...)  // Serialize arguments            │     │
│  │         │                                                          │     │
│  │         v                                                          │     │
│  │  bus.call(method)  ─────────────────────────────────────────┐      │     │
│  │         │                                     Wait for reply │      │     │
│  └─────────│─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│            │                                                   │            │
│            v                                                   │            │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │                     dbus-daemon (dbus-broker)                       │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │  1. Receive message from client socket                              │   │
│  │  2. Validate message format and permissions (policy)                │   │
│  │  3. Match destination service name to unique name (:1.XX)           │   │
│  │  4. Route message to destination socket                             │   │
│  │  5. Wait for reply from service                                     │   │
│  │  6. Route reply back to client                                      │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │  Name Registry:                                                     │   │
│  │  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │   │
│  │  │  :1.15 = xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host                       │  │   │
│  │  │  :1.23 = xyz.openbmc_project.ObjectMapper                     │  │   │
│  │  │  :1.42 = xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Manager                   │  │   │
│  │  │  :1.58 = xyz.openbmc_project.Logging                          │  │   │
│  │  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │   │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│            │                                                   ^            │
│            v                                                   │            │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │                   Service (e.g., phosphor-state-manager)            │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │  Event Loop (sd-event / boost::asio)                                │   │
│  │         │                                                           │   │
│  │         v                                                           │   │
│  │  Message Dispatch: match destination object path                    │   │
│  │         │                                                           │   │
│  │         v                                                           │   │
│  │  Interface Lookup: find registered interface handler                │   │
│  │         │                                                           │   │
│  │         v                                                           │   │
│  │  Method/Property Handler: execute callback                          │   │
│  │         │                                                           │   │
│  │         v                                                           │   │
│  │  Serialize reply and send ───────────────────────────────────┘      │   │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### Object Mapper Internals

    

The Object Mapper maintains a real-time view of all D-Bus objects:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      Object Mapper Data Structures                          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│  Interface-to-Objects Map:                                                  │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value:                                     │ │
│  │    - /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/temperature/ambient                  │ │
│  │    - /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/temperature/cpu0                     │ │
│  │    - /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/fan_tach/fan0                        │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  │  xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host:                                       │ │
│  │    - /xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0                                  │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  │  xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item:                                   │ │
│  │    - /xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/chassis/motherboard         │ │
│  │    - /xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/chassis/motherboard/cpu0    │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
│  Object-to-Services Map:                                                    │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/temperature/cpu0:                        │ │
│  │    - xyz.openbmc_project.HwmonTempSensor                               │ │
│  │        Interfaces: [xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value,                  │ │
│  │                     xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Threshold.Warning,      │ │
│  │                     xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Threshold.Critical,     │ │
│  │                     xyz.openbmc_project.Association.Definitions]       │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
│  Association Endpoints:                                                     │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/temperature/cpu0:                        │ │
│  │    inventory (forward) -> /xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/.../cpu0      │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  │  /xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/.../cpu0:                              │ │
│  │    sensors (reverse) -> /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/temperature/cpu0  │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
│  Update Mechanism:                                                          │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  1. Subscribe to org.freedesktop.DBus.ObjectManager signals            │ │
│  │  2. Subscribe to NameOwnerChanged for service tracking                 │ │
│  │  3. On InterfacesAdded: update maps, create association endpoints      │ │
│  │  4. On InterfacesRemoved: clean up maps, remove endpoints              │ │
│  │  5. On NameOwnerChanged: handle service start/stop                     │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### D-Bus Policy Configuration

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      D-Bus Security Policy                                  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│  Policy File Location: /usr/share/dbus-1/system.d/                          │
│                                                                             │
│  Policy Evaluation Order:                                                   │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  1. Check <deny> rules (most specific first)                           │ │
│  │  2. Check <allow> rules (most specific first)                          │ │
│  │  3. Default action (usually deny)                                      │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  │  Specificity: user > group > context > default                         │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
│  Example Policy: xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host.conf                        │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  <busconfig>                                                           │ │
│  │    <!-- Allow root to own the service name -->                         │ │
│  │    
│ │
│  │                           │ │
│  │                                                               │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  │               │ │
│  │                                              │ │
│  │              │ │
│  │                │ │
│  │                                                               │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  │                     │ │
│  │                                                  │ │
│  │                                              │ │
│  │                                                               │ │
│  │                                                            │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
│  Common Policy Patterns:                                                    │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  Pattern              │ Use Case                                       │ │
│  │  ─────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────── │ │
│  │  own="service.name"   │ Allow process to claim well-known name         │ │
│  │  send_destination     │ Allow sending messages to service              │ │
│  │  send_interface       │ Restrict to specific D-Bus interface           │ │
│  │  send_member          │ Restrict to specific method/property           │ │
│  │  receive_sender       │ Allow receiving signals from service           │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### D-Bus Type System Internals

    

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      D-Bus Type Serialization                               │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│  Wire Format Example: Sensor Reading Message                                │
│                                                                             │
│  Method Call: Get("xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value", "Value")              │
│                                                                             │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  Message Header (fixed format):                                        │ │
│  │  ┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────────────────┐  │ │
│  │  │ Endian   │ Type     │ Flags    │ Version  │ Body Length          │  │ │
│  │  │ 'l'      │ 0x01     │ 0x00     │ 0x01     │ 52                   │  │ │
│  │  │ (little) │ (method) │          │          │                      │  │ │
│  │  └──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────────────────────┘  │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  │  Header Fields (variable):                                             │ │
│  │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │ │
│  │  │  PATH:        /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/temperature/cpu0     │  │ │
│  │  │  INTERFACE:   org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties                   │  │ │
│  │  │  MEMBER:      Get                                               │  │ │
│  │  │  DESTINATION: xyz.openbmc_project.HwmonTempSensor               │  │ │
│  │  │  SIGNATURE:   ss                                                │  │ │
│  │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  │  Body (marshalled arguments):                                          │ │
│  │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │ │
│  │  │  String: "xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value" (32 bytes + NUL)    │  │ │
│  │  │  String: "Value" (5 bytes + NUL)                                │  │ │
│  │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
│  Reply Message: Variant containing double                                   │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  SIGNATURE: v (variant)                                                │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  │  Body:                                                                 │ │
│  │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │ │
│  │  │  Variant signature: "d" (1 byte + NUL)                          │  │ │
│  │  │  Padding: 5 bytes (align double to 8)                           │  │ │
│  │  │  Double value: 45.5 (8 bytes, IEEE 754)                         │  │ │
│  │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
│  Alignment Rules:                                                           │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  Type      │ Alignment │ Size                                          │ │
│  │  ──────────┼───────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────── │ │
│  │  BYTE      │ 1         │ 1                                             │ │
│  │  INT16     │ 2         │ 2                                             │ │
│  │  INT32     │ 4         │ 4                                             │ │
│  │  INT64     │ 8         │ 8                                             │ │
│  │  DOUBLE    │ 8         │ 8                                             │ │
│  │  STRING    │ 4         │ 4 (length) + data + NUL                       │ │
│  │  ARRAY     │ 4         │ 4 (length) + elements (aligned)               │ │
│  │  STRUCT    │ 8         │ sum of members (each aligned)                 │ │
│  │  VARIANT   │ 1         │ signature + value                             │ │
│  │  DICT      │ 8         │ array of struct{key, value}                   │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### PropertiesChanged Signal Mechanism

    

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   PropertiesChanged Signal Flow                             │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│  Sensor Service                        Subscriber (bmcweb, ipmid)           │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────┐     ┌──────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │                              │     │                                  │  │
│  │  // Update property value    │     │  // Subscribe to changes         │  │
│  │  sensorValue(newReading);    │     │  bus.add_match(                  │  │
│  │         │                    │     │    "type='signal',"              │  │
│  │         v                    │     │    "interface='org.freedesktop." │  │
│  │  // sdbusplus auto-emits:    │     │      "DBus.Properties',"         │  │
│  │  PropertiesChanged(          │     │    "member='PropertiesChanged'," │  │
│  │    "xyz.openbmc_project."    │     │    "arg0='xyz.openbmc_project."  │  │
│  │      "Sensor.Value",         │     │      "Sensor.Value'"             │  │
│  │    {"Value": variant(45.5)}, │     │  );                              │  │
│  │    []                        │     │         │                        │  │
│  │  );                          │     │         v                        │  │
│  │         │                    │     │  // Callback invoked             │  │
│  └─────────│────────────────────┘     │  handlePropertyChange(msg) {     │  │
│            │                          │    auto [iface, changed, inv] =  │  │
│            │                          │      msg.unpack();          │  │
│            │                          │    double val =                  │  │
│            │                          │      std::get(           │  │
│            │                          │        changed.at("Value"));     │  │
│            │                          │    // Update cache, emit SSE     │  │
│            v                          │  }                               │  │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────┐     │                                  │  │
│  │       dbus-daemon            │     └──────────────────────────────────┘  │
│  │                              │                    ^                      │
│  │  Match rules table:          │                    │                      │
│  │  ┌────────────────────────┐  │                    │                      │
│  │  │ :1.23 matches:         │  │                    │                      │
│  │  │   PropertiesChanged    │──│────────────────────┘                      │
│  │  │   on Sensor.Value      │  │                                           │
│  │  └────────────────────────┘  │                                           │
│  │                              │                                           │
│  └──────────────────────────────┘                                           │
│                                                                             │
│  Signal Contents:                                                           │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  Arg 0 (s):  Interface name that changed                               │ │
│  │  Arg 1 (a{sv}): Dictionary of changed properties and new values        │ │
│  │  Arg 2 (as): Array of invalidated property names (cache hints)         │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Overview

    

The **phosphor-state-manager** controls the power state of the BMC, chassis, and host. It’s the core component for:

* Powering on/off the server
* Rebooting the system
* Tracking system state
* Implementing power restore policies

```mermaid
---
title: State Manager Architecture
---
flowchart TB
    subgraph managers["State Managers"]
        direction LR
        bmc["BMC State Manager  
States: NotReady, Ready,  
Quiesced, UpdateInProg"]
        chassis["Chassis State Manager  
States: Off, On"]
        host["Host State Manager   
States: Off, Running,  
Quiesced, DiagMode"]
    end

    managers <--> dbus["D-Bus"]
    dbus <--> obmcutil["obmcutil  
(CLI interface)"]
```

## Setup & Configuration

    

### Build-Time Configuration (Yocto)

    

Include state manager in your image:

```bitbake
# In your machine .conf or image recipe
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " phosphor-state-manager"

# Include specific components
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " \
    phosphor-state-manager-bmc \
    phosphor-state-manager-chassis \
    phosphor-state-manager-host \
    phosphor-state-manager-discover-system-state \
"
```

### Meson Build Options

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
meson setup build <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-Dhost-gpios</span><span class="o">=</span>enabled <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-Dchassis-system-reset</span><span class="o">=</span>enabled <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-Dhost-state-options</span><span class="o">=</span>enabled <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-Dwarm-reboot</span><span class="o">=</span>enabled
```

</div></div>

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `host-gpios` | enabled | GPIO-based host state detection |
| `chassis-system-reset` | disabled | System reset support |
| `warm-reboot` | disabled | Warm reboot capability |
| `boot-count-max-allowed` | 3 | Max boot retry attempts |

</div>

### Runtime Enable/Disable

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check state manager services</span>
systemctl status xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC
systemctl status xyz.openbmc_project.State.Chassis
systemctl status xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host

<span class="c"># Restart state manager services</span>
systemctl restart xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC
systemctl restart xyz.openbmc_project.State.Chassis
systemctl restart xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host

<span class="c"># View logs</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host <span class="nt">-f</span>
```

</div></div>

### Power Restore Policy

    

Configure what happens after AC power loss:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get current policy</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.Settings <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/power_restore_policy <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Power.RestorePolicy PowerRestorePolicy

<span class="c"># Set policy options:</span>
<span class="c"># AlwaysOn  - Always power on after AC restore</span>
<span class="c"># AlwaysOff - Stay off after AC restore</span>
<span class="c"># Restore   - Return to previous state</span>

busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Settings <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/power_restore_policy <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Power.RestorePolicy PowerRestorePolicy s <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Power.RestorePolicy.Policy.Restore"</span>
```

</div></div>

### Boot Options Configuration

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get boot source override</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.Settings <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/boot <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Boot.Source BootSource

<span class="c"># Set boot source (Network, Disk, ExternalMedia, Default)</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Settings <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/boot <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Boot.Source BootSource s <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Boot.Source.Sources.Network"</span>

<span class="c"># Set boot mode (Regular, Safe, Setup)</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Settings <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/boot <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Boot.Mode BootMode s <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Boot.Mode.Modes.Setup"</span>

<span class="c"># Enable/disable boot override</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Settings <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/boot/one_time <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Object.Enable Enabled b <span class="nb">true</span>
```

</div></div>

### Auto-Reboot Configuration

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get auto-reboot setting</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.Settings <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/auto_reboot <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Boot.RebootPolicy AutoReboot

<span class="c"># Enable/disable auto-reboot</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Settings <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/auto_reboot <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Boot.RebootPolicy AutoReboot b <span class="nb">true</span>

<span class="c"># Set reboot attempts limit</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Settings <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/auto_reboot <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Boot.RebootAttempts AttemptsLeft u 3
```

</div></div>

### Watchdog Configuration

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get watchdog status</span>
busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.Watchdog <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/watchdog/host0

<span class="c"># Enable watchdog</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Watchdog <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/watchdog/host0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.State.Watchdog Enabled b <span class="nb">true</span>

<span class="c"># Set watchdog timeout (milliseconds)</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Watchdog <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/watchdog/host0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.State.Watchdog Interval t 300000

<span class="c"># Set watchdog action (None, HardReset, PowerOff, PowerCycle)</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Watchdog <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/watchdog/host0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.State.Watchdog ExpireAction s <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.State.Watchdog.Action.PowerCycle"</span>
```

</div></div>

### Via Redfish API

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get system state</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system | jq <span class="s1">'.PowerState, .BootProgress'</span>

<span class="c"># Set boot override</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>

    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{
        "Boot": {
            "BootSourceOverrideTarget": "Pxe",
            "BootSourceOverrideEnabled": "Once"
        }
    }'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system

<span class="c"># Set power restore policy</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{"PowerRestorePolicy": "AlwaysOn"}'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system
```

## State Managers

    

### BMC State Manager

    

Controls the BMC firmware state.

**D-Bus Interface:** `xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC`
**Object Path:** `/xyz/openbmc_project/state/bmc0`

<div class="table-wrapper">
| State | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `NotReady` | BMC is booting, services not ready |
| `Ready` | BMC fully operational |
| `Quiesced` | BMC in error state, limited operation |
| `UpdateInProgress` | Firmware update in progress |

</div>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check BMC state</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/state/bmc0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC CurrentBMCState
```

</div></div>

### Chassis State Manager

    

Controls chassis power (main power rails).

**D-Bus Interface:** `xyz.openbmc_project.State.Chassis`
**Object Path:** `/xyz/openbmc_project/state/chassis0`

<div class="table-wrapper">
| State | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Off` | Chassis power off (standby only) |
| `On` | Chassis power on |

</div>

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Transition | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Off` | Power off chassis |
| `On` | Power on chassis |

</div>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check chassis state</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.State.Chassis <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/state/chassis0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.State.Chassis CurrentPowerState

<span class="c"># Power on chassis</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.State.Chassis <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/state/chassis0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.State.Chassis RequestedPowerTransition s <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.State.Chassis.Transition.On"</span>
```

</div></div>

**Power status and Power-On Hours.** Beyond `On`/`Off`, the chassis manager
publishes `CurrentPowerStatus` on `xyz.openbmc_project.State.Chassis`, one of
`Good`, `BrownOut`, or `UninterruptiblePowerSupply` (`Undefined` before it is
known). The `chassis-check-power-status` helper blocks a power-on request when
the status is not `Good`. The manager also implements
`xyz.openbmc_project.State.PowerOnHours` — a `POHCounter` property that increments
while the chassis is on and is persisted across reboots (restored on start).

### Host State Manager

    

Controls the host CPU/OS state.

**D-Bus Interface:** `xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host`
**Object Path:** `/xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0`

<div class="table-wrapper">
| State | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Off` | Host not running |
| `Running` | Host running (booted or booting) |
| `Quiesced` | Host in error state |
| `DiagnosticMode` | Host in diagnostic mode |

</div>

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Transition | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Off` | Graceful shutdown |
| `On` | Power on and boot |
| `Reboot` | Graceful reboot |
| `GracefulWarmReboot` | Warm reboot (no power cycle) |
| `ForceWarmReboot` | Forced warm reboot |

</div>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check host state</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host CurrentHostState

<span class="c"># Power on host</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host RequestedHostTransition s <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host.Transition.On"</span>

<span class="c"># Graceful shutdown</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host RequestedHostTransition s <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host.Transition.Off"</span>
```

</div></div>

### Hypervisor State Manager

    

This manager is **IBM / PowerVM-specific** (`hypervisor_state_manager.cpp`) and
is built only for IBM Power systems. On other platforms it is absent.

Tracks the state of the PowerVM hypervisor as a second host instance.

**D-Bus Service:** `xyz.openbmc_project.State.Hypervisor`
**Object Path:** `/xyz/openbmc_project/state/hypervisor0`
**Interface:** `xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host` (it reuses the Host interface)

Unlike `host0`, this instance is intentionally limited:

* `RequestedHostTransition` **only accepts `On`** — any other value is rejected
(the service reports `BMCNotReady`).
* `CurrentHostState` is not driven by a power sequence; it is **derived from the
host’s `BootProgress`**:

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Host `BootProgress` | Hypervisor `CurrentHostState` |
| --- | --- |
| `Unspecified` | `Off` |
| `SystemInitComplete` | `Standby` |
| `OSRunning` | `Running` |

</div>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Read the hypervisor's derived state</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.State.Hypervisor <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/state/hypervisor0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host CurrentHostState
```

</div></div>

### Host Firmware Condition

    

An optional helper, **host-condition-gpio** (service
`phosphor-host-condition-gpio@.service`, source `host_condition_gpio/`), reports
whether host firmware is alive by reading a GPIO rather than by tracking a
transition. It looks for a GPIO line named `-ready` (active high) or
`-ready-n` (active low) and publishes the result on
`xyz.openbmc_project.Condition.HostFirmware`:

<div class="table-wrapper">
| `FirmwareCondition` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Running` | Ready GPIO asserted (host firmware is up) |
| `Off` | Ready GPIO deasserted |
| `Unknown` | No matching GPIO line, or a read error |

</div>

This lets other services ask “is the host actually running?” independently of
the state machine — for example to gate a power-on decision.

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Read the reported host firmware condition (path/service are platform-provided)</span>
busctl get-property <service> 
\
    xyz.openbmc_project.Condition.HostFirmware CurrentFirmwareCondition
```

## obmcutil Command

    

`obmcutil` is the CLI for state management.

### Basic Commands

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Show all system states</span>
obmcutil state

<span class="c"># Example output:</span>
<span class="c"># CurrentBMCState     : xyz.openbmc_project.State.BMC.BMCState.Ready</span>
<span class="c"># CurrentPowerState   : xyz.openbmc_project.State.Chassis.PowerState.Off</span>
<span class="c"># CurrentHostState    : xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host.HostState.Off</span>

<span class="c"># Power on</span>
obmcutil poweron

<span class="c"># Power off (graceful)</span>
obmcutil poweroff

<span class="c"># Chassis power on (without host boot)</span>
obmcutil chassison

<span class="c"># Chassis power off</span>
obmcutil chassisoff

<span class="c"># Reboot host</span>
obmcutil reboot

<span class="c"># BMC reboot</span>
obmcutil bmcreboot
```

</div></div>

### Status Commands

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Show boot progress</span>
obmcutil bootprogress

<span class="c"># Show operating system status</span>
obmcutil osstate

<span class="c"># Check if host is running</span>
obmcutil hoststate
```

</div></div>

### Recovery Commands

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Recover from quiesced state</span>
obmcutil recover

<span class="c"># Force immediate host off (emergency)</span>
obmcutil chassiskill
```

</div></div>

### Power On Sequence

    

```mermaid
---
title: Power On Sequence
---
flowchart LR
    bmc["BMC Ready"] -->|"obmcutil poweron"| chassis["Chassis On"]
    chassis -->|"Power rails enabled"| host["Host Running"]
    host -->|"CPU boot sequence"| os["OS Running"]
```

> **ASCII-art version (for comparison)**

  <div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────┐     ┌─────────┐     ┌─────────┐     ┌─────────┐
│  BMC    │     │ Chassis │     │  Host   │     │   OS    │
│  Ready  │────▶│   On    │────▶│ Running │────▶│ Running │
└─────────┘     └─────────┘     └─────────┘     └─────────┘
     │               │               │               │
     │  obmcutil     │  Power rails  │   CPU boot    │  OS boot
     │  poweron      │   enabled     │   sequence    │  complete
     ▼               ▼               ▼               ▼
```

## Scheduled Host Transitions

    

The optional **scheduled-host-transition** service (source
`scheduled_host_transition.cpp`, unit
`xyz.openbmc_project.State.ScheduledHostTransition@.service`) lets you queue a
power transition to run at a future wall-clock time.

**D-Bus Interface:** `xyz.openbmc_project.State.ScheduledHostTransition`
**Object Path:** `/xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0`

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ScheduledTime` | `uint64` | Epoch seconds at which to run the transition. `0` **cancels** any pending schedule. |
| `ScheduledTransition` | enum | Which `Host.Transition` to apply (e.g. `On`, `Off`) |

</div>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Choose the transition, then arm it for a specific epoch time</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.State.ScheduledHostTransition <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.State.ScheduledHostTransition ScheduledTransition s <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host.Transition.On"</span>

busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.State.ScheduledHostTransition <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.State.ScheduledHostTransition ScheduledTime t 1893456000

<span class="c"># Cancel a pending schedule</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.State.ScheduledHostTransition <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.State.ScheduledHostTransition ScheduledTime t 0
```

</div></div>

The schedule is persisted to a JSON file, so it survives a BMC reboot. The timer
arms against `CLOCK_REALTIME` (with `TFD_TIMER_ABSTIME | TFD_TIMER_CANCEL_ON_SET`),
so if the BMC’s clock is stepped — for example by NTP — the pending transition is
re-evaluated against the new time.

## Power Restore Policy

    

Configure what happens after AC power loss.

**D-Bus Interface:** `xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Power.RestorePolicy`
**Object Path:** `/xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/power_restore_policy`

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Policy | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `AlwaysOn` | Always power on after AC restore |
| `AlwaysOff` | Stay off after AC restore |
| `Restore` | Return to previous state |

</div>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get current policy</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.Settings <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/power_restore_policy <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Power.RestorePolicy PowerRestorePolicy

<span class="c"># Set policy to always on</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Settings <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/power_restore_policy <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Power.RestorePolicy PowerRestorePolicy s <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Power.RestorePolicy.Policy.AlwaysOn"</span>
```

</div></div>

## Security Checks

    

At BMC startup the **secure_boot_check** program (`secure_boot_check.cpp`)
validates the platform’s security posture and raises event logs when something is
wrong. It does **not** itself power down or quiesce the system — it records
findings for the rest of the stack to act on.

What it inspects:

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Check | Source |
| --- | --- |
| Secure boot enabled | `bmc-secure-boot` GPIO and a secure-boot sysfs attribute |
| ABR / golden-image active | an alternate-boot-region sysfs attribute |
| TPM measurement present | if a TPM device exists, its measurement sysfs value must be non-zero |
| Manufacturing mode | the `quiesce_on_hw_error` setting (LoggingSettings) gates whether violations are logged |

</div>

Event logs it can create:

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Error | Raised when |
| --- | --- |
| `xyz.openbmc_project.State.Error.TpmMeasurementFail` | TPM measurement is missing, empty, or zero |
| `xyz.openbmc_project.State.Error.SecurityCheckFail` | secure boot is disabled, or the ABR / golden image is active |

</div>

Because these are ordinary phosphor-logging events, wire your platform’s policy
(alerting, quiesce, or ignore in the lab) to the error identifiers above rather
than expecting `secure_boot_check` to enforce anything on its own.

## Troubleshooting

    

### Host won’t power on

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check chassis state first</span>
obmcutil state

<span class="c"># Check for errors in state manager</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host <span class="nt">-f</span>

<span class="c"># Verify power good signal</span>
gpioget gpiochip0 
```

### Stuck in Quiesced state

    

```
# Check what caused quiesce
journalctl -u xyz.openbmc_project.State.Host | grep -i error

# Recover
obmcutil recover
```

### Power restore not working

    

```
# Verify policy is set
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.Settings \
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/power_restore_policy \
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Power.RestorePolicy PowerRestorePolicy

# Check restore service
systemctl status phosphor-reset-host-recovery@0.service
```

## Deep Dive

    

Advanced implementation details for state manager developers.

### State Machine Internals

    

The state managers implement finite state machines with well-defined transitions:

```mermaid
---
title: Host State Machine
---
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Off
    Off --> Running : Transition.On
    Running --> Off : Transition.Off
    Off --> Quiesced : error
    Running --> Quiesced : error
    Quiesced --> Off : recover

    state "Transition States" as trans {
        TransitioningToOff
        TransitioningToRunning
        TransitioningToQuiesced
    }
```

**Internal Transition States:**

* `TransitioningToOff` - shutdown in progress
* `TransitioningToRunning` - boot in progress
* `TransitioningToQuiesced` - error handling

> **ASCII-art version (click to expand)**

  <div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Host State Machine                                   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│                            ┌───────────────┐                            │
│              ┌────────────▶│   Quiesced    │◀────────────┐              │
│              │             │  (error state)│             │              │
│              │             └───────────────┘             │              │
│              │                     │                     │              │
│              │ error               │ recover             │ error        │
│              │                     ▼                     │              │
│       ┌──────┴──────┐       ┌───────────────┐     ┌──────┴──────┐       │
│       │             │       │               │     │             │       │
│       │     Off     │◀──────│   Transition  │────▶│   Running   │       │
│       │             │       │    States     │     │             │       │
│       └──────┬──────┘       └───────────────┘     └──────┬──────┘       │
│              │                                           │              │
│              │              Transition.On                │              │
│              └───────────────────────────────────────────┘              │
│                             Transition.Off                              │
│                                                                         │
│   Internal Transition States:                                           │
│   ├── TransitioningToOff  (shutdown in progress)                        │
│   ├── TransitioningToRunning (boot in progress)                         │
│   └── TransitioningToQuiesced (error handling)                          │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div>  </div>

**State transition triggers:**

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Event | Source | Transition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D-Bus RequestedHostTransition | User/Redfish | Off→Running, Running→Off |
| Power Good GPIO change | Hardware | Off→Running (assert), Running→Off (deassert) |
| Watchdog timeout | Watchdog service | Running→Quiesced |
| Boot failure (max retries) | Boot counter | Running→Quiesced |

</div>

**Source reference**: [host_state_manager.cpp](https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-state-manager/blob/master/host_state_manager.cpp)

### GPIO Power Control Sequence

    

Power on/off involves precise GPIO sequencing:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Power On GPIO Sequence                               │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   Time ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────▶  │
│                                                                         │
│   POWER_BTN    ───┐     ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────  │
│   (active low)    └─────┘ (100-500ms pulse)                             │
│                                                                         │
│   ATX_PS_ON    ─────────────────┐                                       │
│                                 └─────────────────────────────────────  │
│                                                                         │
│   POWER_GOOD   ─────────────────────────┐                               │
│                                         └─────────────────────────────  │
│                     │           │       │                               │
│                     │           │       └─ State → Running              │
│                     │           └─ Wait for power good (timeout: 10s)   │
│                     └─ Power button pulse sent                          │
│                                                                         │
│   Implementation (power-control):                                       │
│   1. Assert POWER_BTN GPIO low                                          │
│   2. Wait powerPulseTimeMs (default: 200ms)                             │
│   3. Deassert POWER_BTN GPIO high                                       │
│   4. Wait for POWER_GOOD assert (timeout: powerOkWatchdogTimeMs)        │
│   5. If timeout → retry or fail                                         │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

**Power off sequence (graceful):**

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Graceful Power Off Sequence                          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   1. Send power button pulse (short press - ACPI S5 request)            │
│   2. Wait for OS to initiate shutdown (gracefulPowerOffWaitTime)        │
│   3. Wait for POWER_GOOD deassert                                       │
│   4. If timeout → force power off (long press)                          │
│                                                                         │
│   Force Power Off (chassiskill):                                        │
│   1. Assert POWER_BTN low for forcePowerOffTimeMs (4-10 seconds)        │
│   2. This bypasses ACPI, directly cuts power                            │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

**Source reference**: [power-control](https://github.com/openbmc/x86-power-control) or platform-specific GPIO control

### systemd Target Integration

    

State transitions trigger systemd targets for service orchestration:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    systemd Target Hierarchy                             │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   Power On Flow:                                                        │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ RequestedHostTransition = On                                    │   │
│   └────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                │                                        │
│                                ▼                                        │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ obmc-chassis-poweron@0.target                                   │   │
│   │ ├── phosphor-psu-monitor.service                                │   │
│   │ ├── phosphor-fan-monitor.service                                │   │
│   │ └── (platform power sequencing services)                        │   │
│   └────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                │ After=                                 │
│                                ▼                                        │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ obmc-host-startmin@0.target                                     │   │
│   │ ├── phosphor-host-state-manager.service                         │   │
│   │ └── (minimal host services)                                     │   │
│   └────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                │ After=                                 │
│                                ▼                                        │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ obmc-host-start@0.target                                        │   │
│   │ ├── phosphor-watchdog.service                                   │   │
│   │ ├── phosphor-ipmi-host.service                                  │   │
│   │ └── (full host services)                                        │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
│   Power Off Flow:                                                       │
│   obmc-host-stop@0.target → obmc-chassis-poweroff@0.target              │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

**Adding platform-specific services:**

<div class="language-ini highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># /lib/systemd/system/platform-power-on.service
</span><span class="nn">[Unit]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Description</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">Platform-specific power on sequence</span>
<span class="py">After</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">obmc-chassis-poweron@0.target</span>
<span class="py">Before</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">obmc-host-startmin@0.target</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="nn">[Service]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Type</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">oneshot</span>
<span class="py">ExecStart</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">/usr/bin/platform-power-sequence --on</span>
<span class="py">RemainAfterExit</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">yes</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="nn">[Install]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">WantedBy</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">obmc-host-start@0.target</span>
```

</div></div>

### Boot Count and Auto-Recovery

    

The boot counter tracks failed boot attempts and triggers recovery:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Boot Counter Implementation                          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   Boot Attempt Tracking:                                                │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ D-Bus: xyz.openbmc_project.State.Boot.Raw                       │   │
│   │ Path:  /xyz/openbmc_project/state/host0                         │   │
│   │ Properties:                                                     │   │
│   │   ├── BootRaw - Current boot count (persistent)                 │   │
│   │   └── AttemptsLeft - Remaining retries before quiesce           │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
│   Boot Flow:                                                            │
│   ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐          │
│   │ Power On │───▶│ Boot     │───▶│ Boot     │───▶│ Success  │          │
│   │          │    │ Count++  │    │ Watchdog │    │ Count=0  │          │
│   └──────────┘    └──────────┘    └────┬─────┘    └──────────┘          │
│                                        │                                │
│                                        │ Timeout                        │
│                                        ▼                                │
│                                   ┌──────────┐                          │
│                                   │ Check    │                          │
│                                   │ Attempts │                          │
│                                   └────┬─────┘                          │
│                                        │                                │
│                        ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐                │
│                        │                               │                │
│                        ▼                               ▼                │
│                   Attempts > 0                    Attempts = 0          │
│                   ┌──────────┐                    ┌──────────┐          │
│                   │ Reboot   │                    │ Quiesce  │          │
│                   │ (retry)  │                    │ (stop)   │          │
│                   └──────────┘                    └──────────┘          │
│                                                                         │
│   Configuration:                                                        │
│   └── BOOT_COUNT_MAX_ALLOWED (default: 3)                               │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

**Boot count reset conditions:**

* OS signals successful boot via IPMI
* Host reaches `OSRunning` boot progress
* Manual reset via `obmcutil recover`

### Power Restore Policy Implementation

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Power Restore Policy Flow                            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   AC Power Restored:                                                    │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ BMC boots → discover-system-state.service runs                  │   │
│   └────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                │                                        │
│                                ▼                                        │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ Read PowerRestorePolicy from D-Bus Settings                     │   │
│   └────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                │                                        │
│            ┌───────────────────┼───────────────────┐                    │
│            │                   │                   │                    │
│            ▼                   ▼                   ▼                    │
│       ┌─────────┐        ┌──────────┐        ┌─────────┐                │
│       │AlwaysOn │        │ Restore  │        │AlwaysOff│                │
│       └────┬────┘        └────┬─────┘        └────┬────┘                │
│            │                  │                   │                     │
│            ▼                  ▼                   ▼                     │
│       Power On          Read last state      Stay Off                   │
│                         from persistent                                 │
│                         storage                                         │
│                              │                                          │
│                    ┌─────────┴─────────┐                                │
│                    │                   │                                │
│                    ▼                   ▼                                │
│               Was Running         Was Off                               │
│               ┌─────────┐        ┌─────────┐                            │
│               │Power On │        │Stay Off │                            │
│               └─────────┘        └─────────┘                            │
│                                                                         │
│   Persistent State Storage:                                             │
│   └── /var/lib/phosphor-state-manager/chassisStateX/POH (Power-On-Hours)│
│   └── /var/lib/phosphor-state-manager/hostStateX/state                  │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

**Source reference**: [discover_system_state.cpp](https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-state-manager/blob/master/discover_system_state.cpp)

### Watchdog Integration

    

The host watchdog monitors for hangs during boot and runtime:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Watchdog Interaction                                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   Host Boot:                                                            │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ 1. State Manager sets RequestedHostTransition = On              │   │
│   │ 2. Watchdog service starts with boot timeout (default: 5 min)   │   │
│   │ 3. Host BIOS/OS pokes watchdog via IPMI periodically            │   │
│   │ 4. On successful boot, OS disables watchdog or sets new timeout │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
│   Watchdog Expiry Actions:                                              │
│   ┌──────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│   │ Action       │ Behavior                                        │    │
│   ├──────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤    │
│   │ None         │ Log event only                                  │    │
│   │ HardReset    │ Reset host (reboot)                             │    │
│   │ PowerOff     │ Power off host                                  │    │
│   │ PowerCycle   │ Power off, wait, power on                       │    │
│   └──────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                         │
│   D-Bus Watchdog Interface:                                             │
│   xyz.openbmc_project.State.Watchdog at /xyz/openbmc_project/watchdog/  │
│   ├── Enabled (bool)      - Watchdog active                             │
│   ├── Interval (uint64)   - Timeout in milliseconds                     │
│   ├── TimeRemaining       - Time until expiry                           │
│   └── ExpireAction        - Action on timeout                           │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### Source Code Reference

    

Key implementation files in [phosphor-state-manager](https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-state-manager):

<div class="table-wrapper">
| File | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `bmc_state_manager.cpp` | BMC state tracking |
| `chassis_state_manager.cpp` | Chassis power control |
| `host_state_manager.cpp` | Host state machine |
| `discover_system_state.cpp` | Power restore policy |
| `settings.cpp` | Persistent settings storage |
| `scheduled_host_transition.cpp` | Scheduled power on/off |

</div>
