## Overview

    

OpenBMC relies on systemd as its init system and service manager. Every daemon, one-shot script, and power-state transition is controlled through systemd units. Understanding how these units relate to each other is essential for developing or debugging OpenBMC services.

This guide covers the target hierarchy that drives the BMC boot sequence, the dependency directives that control service ordering, tools for diagnosing boot timing and failures, and the template unit mechanism that enables multi-host support. All commands run directly on the BMC and are fully testable in a QEMU ast2600-evb environment.

**Key concepts covered:**

* OpenBMC systemd target hierarchy (boot and power-on chains)
* Wants vs Requires and After vs Before semantics
* Boot time profiling with `systemd-analyze`
* Service failure debugging with `journalctl` and `systemctl`
* Multi-host template units (`@.service`, `%i` specifier)
* The `RemainAfterExit=yes` pattern for oneshot services

---

## OpenBMC Target Hierarchy

    

systemd uses **targets** as synchronization points. A target groups related services together and establishes ordering between boot phases. OpenBMC defines a custom set of targets on top of the standard systemd targets.

### BMC Boot Sequence

    

When the BMC powers on, systemd walks the following target chain to bring the system to a ready state:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    BMC Boot Target Chain                                │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   sysinit.target                                                        │
│        │                                                                │
│        ▼                                                                │
│   basic.target                                                          │
│        │                                                                │
│        ▼                                                                │
│   multi-user.target                                                     │
│        │  (standard Linux boot complete)                                │
│        ▼                                                                │
│   obmc-standby.target                                                   │
│        │  (BMC-specific services ready: D-Bus, mapper, REST/Redfish)    │
│        │                                                                │
│        │  BMC is now Ready.                                             │
│        │  Host power-on targets activate on user request.               │
│        │                                                                │
│        ▼                                                                │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │  Power-on chain (triggered by obmcutil poweron):                │   │
│   │                                                                 │   │
│   │  obmc-chassis-poweron@0.target                                  │   │
│   │       │  (PSU monitoring, fan control, power sequencing)        │   │
│   │       ▼                                                         │   │
│   │  obmc-host-startmin@0.target                                    │   │
│   │       │  (minimal host services: state manager, host check)     │   │
│   │       ▼                                                         │   │
│   │  obmc-host-start@0.target                                       │   │
│   │       │  (full host services: IPMI host, watchdog, SOL)         │   │
│   │       ▼                                                         │   │
│   │  Host is Running.                                               │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
│   Power-off chain (reverse order):                                      │
│   obmc-host-stop@0.target → obmc-chassis-poweroff@0.target              │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### What Each Target Provides

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Target | Services Pulled In |
| --- | --- |
| `multi-user.target` | systemd core, networking, sshd |
| `obmc-standby.target` | D-Bus broker, phosphor-mapper, bmcweb, state-manager |
| `obmc-chassis-poweron@.target` | PSU monitor, fan monitor, power sequencing |
| `obmc-host-startmin@.target` | Host state manager, host check services |
| `obmc-host-start@.target` | IPMI host, watchdog, SOL console, sensor polling |
| `obmc-host-stop@.target` | IPMI stop, graceful shutdown coordination |
| `obmc-chassis-poweroff@.target` | Power rail disable, fan ramp-down |

</div>

The `obmc-standby.target` is the dividing line between “BMC boot” and “host management.” The BMC state manager transitions to `Ready` when this target completes. Everything below it activates only when a host power-on is requested.

### Viewing the Target Hierarchy

    

Use `systemctl list-dependencies` to explore the live target tree on a running BMC:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Show what obmc-standby.target pulls in</span>
systemctl list-dependencies obmc-standby.target

<span class="c"># Show the full host power-on chain</span>
systemctl list-dependencies obmc-host-start@0.target

<span class="c"># Show reverse dependencies (what depends on a target)</span>
systemctl list-dependencies <span class="nt">--reverse</span> obmc-chassis-poweron@0.target

<span class="c"># Show all targets and their current state</span>
systemctl list-units <span class="nt">--type</span><span class="o">=</span>target
```

</div></div>

Add `--all` to `list-dependencies` to include inactive units. This helps you see services that are installed but not currently running.

---

## Wants, Requires, After, and Before

    

systemd separates two concepts that developers often confuse: **dependency** (whether to start a unit) and **ordering** (when to start it). OpenBMC services use both, and getting them wrong causes subtle boot failures.

### Dependency Directives: Wants vs Requires

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Directive | Effect | If dependency fails |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Wants=B.service` | Start B when A starts | A keeps running |
| `Requires=B.service` | Start B when A starts | A is stopped |
| `BindsTo=B.service` | Start B when A starts | A is stopped immediately |

</div>

**Wants** is the most common directive in OpenBMC. It creates a soft dependency: the system tries to start the wanted unit, but the wanting unit survives if the dependency fails.

**Requires** creates a hard dependency: if the required unit fails to start or is stopped, the requiring unit is also stopped. Use this sparingly – it creates brittle dependency chains.

<div class="language-ini highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Typical OpenBMC pattern: soft dependency with Wants
</span><span class="nn">[Unit]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Description</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">Phosphor Fan Monitor</span>
<span class="py">Wants</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">phosphor-fan-presence-tach.service</span>
<span class="py">After</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">phosphor-fan-presence-tach.service</span>
```

</div></div>

Never use `Requires=` when `Wants=` is sufficient. If a `Requires=` target fails transiently (for example, a sensor driver takes an extra second to load), the entire dependent chain collapses. OpenBMC targets use `Wants=` for this reason.

### Ordering Directives: After vs Before

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Directive | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `After=B.service` | Start A only after B finishes starting |
| `Before=B.service` | Start A before B begins starting |

</div>

`Wants=` and `After=` are independent. `Wants=B` without `After=B` starts both A and B simultaneously. `After=B` without `Wants=B` means A waits for B only if something else starts B. You almost always need both together.

### Common OpenBMC Ordering Patterns

    

#### Pattern 1: Start After D-Bus Is Available

    

Most OpenBMC services need the D-Bus broker running before they can register their interfaces:

<div class="language-ini highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="nn">[Unit]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Description</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">My OpenBMC Service</span>
<span class="py">After</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">dbus.service</span>
<span class="py">Wants</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">dbus.service</span>
```

</div></div>

#### Pattern 2: Start After Phosphor-Mapper

    

Services that need to look up other services through the object mapper must wait for it:

<div class="language-ini highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="nn">[Unit]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Description</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">My Mapper-Dependent Service</span>
<span class="py">After</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">mapper-wait@-xyz-openbmc_project-sensors.service</span>
<span class="py">Wants</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">mapper-wait@-xyz-openbmc_project-sensors.service</span>
```

</div></div>

The `mapper-wait@.service` template is a special helper that blocks until a specific D-Bus object path is available. The path `/xyz/openbmc_project/sensors` is encoded with dashes as `-xyz-openbmc_project-sensors` in the unit name.

#### Pattern 3: Start After Sensors Are Available

    

A service that processes sensor data should not start until the sensor daemons have registered their D-Bus objects:

<div class="language-ini highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="nn">[Unit]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Description</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">Thermal Policy Engine</span>
<span class="py">After</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">phosphor-hwmon-readall.service</span>
<span class="py">After</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">xyz.openbmc_project.EntityManager.service</span>
<span class="py">Wants</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">phosphor-hwmon-readall.service</span>
```

</div></div>

#### Pattern 4: Hook Into a Power-On Target

    

To run a custom script when the host powers on, use `WantedBy=` in the `[Install]` section:

<div class="language-ini highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="nn">[Unit]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Description</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">Platform-specific power on hook</span>
<span class="py">After</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">obmc-chassis-poweron@0.target</span>
<span class="py">Before</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">obmc-host-startmin@0.target</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="nn">[Service]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Type</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">oneshot</span>
<span class="py">ExecStart</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">/usr/bin/my-platform-power-on.sh</span>
<span class="py">RemainAfterExit</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">yes</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="nn">[Install]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">WantedBy</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">obmc-host-start@0.target</span>
```

</div></div>

#### Pattern 5: Service That Must Finish Before Another Starts

    

When a configuration service must complete before the main daemon starts:

<div class="language-ini highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># config-loader.service
</span><span class="nn">[Unit]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Description</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">Load sensor configuration</span>
<span class="py">Before</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">phosphor-pid-control.service</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="nn">[Service]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Type</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">oneshot</span>
<span class="py">ExecStart</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">/usr/bin/load-sensor-config.sh</span>
<span class="py">RemainAfterExit</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">yes</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="nn">[Install]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">WantedBy</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">multi-user.target</span>
```

</div></div>

### Dependency vs Ordering Summary

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Combination | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Wants=B` + `After=B` | Start B, then start A (most common) |
| `Requires=B` + `After=B` | Start B, then start A (hard dependency) |
| `After=B` (alone) | Wait for B if B is active (passive wait) |
| `Wants=B` (alone) | Start B in parallel (rarely correct) |
| `WantedBy=T.target` | T.target pulls this service in via Wants= |

</div>
---

## Boot Time Debugging

    

When the BMC boots slowly or a service fails to start, systemd provides powerful diagnostic tools. All of these commands work on the BMC over SSH (or via QEMU serial console).

### Profiling Boot Time with systemd-analyze

    

#### Overall Boot Time

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Show total boot time breakdown</span>
systemd-analyze

<span class="c"># Example output:</span>
<span class="c"># Startup finished in 1.234s (kernel) + 12.345s (userspace) = 13.579s</span>
<span class="c"># graphical.target reached after 12.000s in userspace</span>
```

</div></div>

#### Blame: Which Services Are Slowest

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># List services sorted by startup time (slowest first)</span>
systemd-analyze blame

<span class="c"># Example output:</span>
<span class="c"># 5.123s phosphor-image-signing.service</span>
<span class="c"># 3.456s obmc-flash-bmc-init.service</span>
<span class="c"># 2.789s phosphor-mapper.service</span>
<span class="c"># 1.234s phosphor-hwmon@org-openbmc-sensors.service</span>
<span class="c"># 0.987s bmcweb.service</span>
<span class="c"># 0.654s phosphor-certificate-manager@authority.service</span>
<span class="c"># ...</span>
```

</div></div>

On a typical QEMU environment, boot takes 15-30 seconds. On real hardware with flash storage, expect 30-90 seconds. Anything significantly above that indicates a problem worth investigating.

#### Critical Chain: The Longest Dependency Path

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Show the critical path to default.target</span>
systemd-analyze critical-chain

<span class="c"># Show the critical path to a specific target</span>
systemd-analyze critical-chain obmc-standby.target

<span class="c"># Example output:</span>
<span class="c"># obmc-standby.target @12.345s</span>
<span class="c"># └─bmcweb.service @8.123s +2.456s</span>
<span class="c">#   └─phosphor-certificate-manager@authority.service @6.789s +1.234s</span>
<span class="c">#     └─phosphor-mapper.service @3.456s +3.333s</span>
<span class="c">#       └─dbus.service @1.234s +0.567s</span>
<span class="c">#         └─basic.target @1.200s</span>
<span class="c">#           └─sockets.target @1.199s</span>
<span class="c">#             └─dbus.socket @0.987s</span>
```

</div></div>

The `@` values show when each unit started, and the `+` values show how long each unit took. The critical chain reveals which service is the actual bottleneck, not just which service is slow.

`systemd-analyze blame` shows raw duration. `systemd-analyze critical-chain` shows the actual bottleneck path. A service that takes 5 seconds is not a problem if it starts in parallel with a 10-second service on the critical path. Focus on the critical chain.

### Debugging Service Failures with journalctl

    

#### View Logs for a Specific Service

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Follow live logs for a service</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> phosphor-state-manager.service <span class="nt">-f</span>

<span class="c"># View recent logs (last 50 lines)</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> phosphor-state-manager.service <span class="nt">-n</span> 50

<span class="c"># View logs from this boot only</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> phosphor-state-manager.service <span class="nt">-b</span>

<span class="c"># View logs with full output (no truncation)</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> phosphor-state-manager.service <span class="nt">-b</span> <span class="nt">--no-pager</span>
```

</div></div>

You can also filter by priority (`-p err` for errors only) or view all boot errors across services with `journalctl -b -p err`.

### Tracing Dependency Chains with systemctl

    

When a service fails because of a dependency problem, trace the chain:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check service status and recent log output</span>
systemctl status phosphor-pid-control.service

<span class="c"># List what a unit depends on</span>
systemctl list-dependencies phosphor-pid-control.service

<span class="c"># List what depends on a unit (reverse)</span>
systemctl list-dependencies <span class="nt">--reverse</span> dbus.service

<span class="c"># Show the full unit file with all overrides applied</span>
systemctl <span class="nb">cat </span>phosphor-pid-control.service
```

</div></div>
---

## Multi-Host Template Units

    

OpenBMC supports platforms with multiple host CPUs. Each host is managed independently through systemd **template units**, which use the `@` syntax to create parameterized service instances.

### Template Unit Basics

    

A template unit has `@` in its filename before the suffix:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
obmc-host-start@.target      ← template (no instance)
obmc-host-start@0.target     ← instance 0 (first host)
obmc-host-start@1.target     ← instance 1 (second host)
```

</div></div>

The portion after `@` and before the suffix is the **instance identifier**. In OpenBMC, the instance identifier is typically the host number (0, 1, 2, …).

### The %i Specifier

    

Inside a template unit file, `%i` expands to the instance identifier at runtime:

<div class="language-ini highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># /lib/systemd/system/phosphor-host-state-manager@.service
</span><span class="nn">[Unit]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Description</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">Phosphor Host State Manager for host %i</span>
<span class="py">After</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">obmc-host-startmin@%i.target</span>
<span class="py">BindsTo</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">obmc-host-startmin@%i.target</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="nn">[Service]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">ExecStart</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">/usr/bin/phosphor-host-state-manager --host %i</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="nn">[Install]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">WantedBy</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">obmc-host-startmin@%i.target</span>
```

</div></div>

When systemd starts `phosphor-host-state-manager@0.service`, every `%i` becomes `0`. When it starts `phosphor-host-state-manager@1.service`, every `%i` becomes `1`.

### Common systemd Specifiers in OpenBMC

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Specifier | Expands To | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `%i` | Instance identifier | `0`, `1`, `2` |
| `%n` | Full unit name | `my-service@0.service` |
| `%p` | Unit prefix (before @) | `my-service` |

</div>

### OpenBMC Multi-Host Target Instances

    

Every power-management target in OpenBMC is a template. On a single-host platform, only `@0` instances exist. On a multi-host platform (for example, a 4-socket server), instances `@0` through `@3` activate independently:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Multi-Host Target Instances                          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   Single-Host Platform:                                                 │
│                                                                         │
│   obmc-chassis-poweron@0.target                                         │
│        └── obmc-host-startmin@0.target                                  │
│              └── obmc-host-start@0.target                               │
│                                                                         │
│   Multi-Host Platform (2 hosts):                                        │
│                                                                         │
│   obmc-chassis-poweron@0.target    obmc-chassis-poweron@1.target        │
│        │                                │                               │
│        ▼                                ▼                               │
│   obmc-host-startmin@0.target     obmc-host-startmin@1.target           │
│        │                                │                               │
│        ▼                                ▼                               │
│   obmc-host-start@0.target        obmc-host-start@1.target              │
│                                                                         │
│   Each host chain operates independently.                               │
│   Host 0 can be powered on while host 1 remains off.                    │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### Creating a Multi-Host Aware Service

    

When you write a service that must run per-host, create a template unit:

<div class="language-ini highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># /lib/systemd/system/my-host-monitor@.service
</span><span class="nn">[Unit]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Description</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">My Host Monitor for host %i</span>
<span class="py">After</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">obmc-host-startmin@%i.target</span>
<span class="py">BindsTo</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">obmc-host-startmin@%i.target</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="nn">[Service]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Type</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">simple</span>
<span class="py">ExecStart</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">/usr/bin/my-host-monitor --host %i</span>
<span class="py">Restart</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">on-failure</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="nn">[Install]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">WantedBy</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">obmc-host-start@%i.target</span>
```

</div></div>

Enable it for specific host instances:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Enable for host 0</span>
systemctl <span class="nb">enable </span>my-host-monitor@0.service

<span class="c"># Enable for host 1 (multi-host platform)</span>
systemctl <span class="nb">enable </span>my-host-monitor@1.service

<span class="c"># Start manually for testing</span>
systemctl start my-host-monitor@0.service

<span class="c"># Check status of a specific instance</span>
systemctl status my-host-monitor@0.service
```

</div></div>

### The RemainAfterExit Pattern

    

Many OpenBMC power-sequencing services are `Type=oneshot` scripts that run once and must be considered “active” after they exit. Without `RemainAfterExit=yes`, systemd marks a oneshot service as `inactive (dead)` after the script finishes, which breaks dependency chains that use `BindsTo=` or `After=`.

<div class="language-ini highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># /lib/systemd/system/chassis-power-on@.service
</span><span class="nn">[Unit]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Description</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">Chassis Power On Sequence for host %i</span>
<span class="py">After</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">obmc-chassis-poweron@%i.target</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="nn">[Service]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Type</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">oneshot</span>
<span class="py">ExecStart</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">/usr/bin/power-on-sequence.sh %i</span>
<span class="py">RemainAfterExit</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">yes</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="nn">[Install]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">WantedBy</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">obmc-host-startmin@%i.target</span>
```

</div></div>

`RemainAfterExit=yes` tells systemd to treat the service as `active (exited)` after the ExecStart command completes successfully. This is critical for oneshot services that other units depend on. Without it, `After=chassis-power-on@0.service` would see the service as “dead” and behave unpredictably.

### Inspecting Template Instances

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># List all instantiated units from a template</span>
systemctl list-units <span class="s1">'phosphor-host-state-manager@*'</span>

<span class="c"># Show the template unit file</span>
systemctl <span class="nb">cat </span>phosphor-host-state-manager@.service

<span class="c"># Show a specific instance's resolved configuration</span>
systemctl show phosphor-host-state-manager@0.service

<span class="c"># Check which instance specifier values are active</span>
systemctl list-units <span class="nt">--type</span><span class="o">=</span>target <span class="s1">'obmc-host-start@*'</span>
```

</div></div>
---

## Troubleshooting

    

### Issue: Service Starts Before Its Dependency Is Ready

    

**Symptom**: A service fails with “Connection refused” or “D-Bus name not found” errors during boot, but works when restarted manually.

**Cause**: The service has `Wants=` on its dependency but is missing `After=`. Both units start simultaneously, and the dependency loses the race.

**Solution**:

1. Add `After=` for the dependency:
    
```
[Unit]
Wants=phosphor-mapper.service
After=phosphor-mapper.service
```
2. Reload and restart:
    
```
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl restart my-service.service
```

### Issue: Service Is Not Started During Host Power-On

    

**Symptom**: Your service never starts when you run `obmcutil poweron`, even though it is enabled.

**Cause**: The `WantedBy=` in the `[Install]` section does not reference a power-on target, or the service was not properly enabled.

**Solution**:

1. Verify `[Install]` has `WantedBy=obmc-host-start@0.target`
2. Re-enable: `systemctl disable my-service && systemctl enable my-service`
3. Verify the symlink: `ls -la /etc/systemd/system/obmc-host-start@0.target.wants/`

### Issue: Oneshot Service Shows “inactive (dead)”

    

**Symptom**: A oneshot service runs successfully but shows `inactive (dead)`. Dependent services behave inconsistently.

**Cause**: Missing `RemainAfterExit=yes` in the unit file.

**Solution**: Add `RemainAfterExit=yes` to the `[Service]` section. The service then shows `active (exited)` instead of `inactive (dead)`.

### Issue: Boot Hangs at a Specific Target

    

**Symptom**: The BMC boot stalls and never reaches `obmc-standby.target`.

**Cause**: A service in the dependency chain has hung or timed out.

**Solution**:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Identify the stuck service</span>
systemctl list-jobs
systemctl list-units <span class="nt">--state</span><span class="o">=</span>activating

<span class="c"># Examine logs for the stuck service</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> stuck-service.service <span class="nt">-b</span> <span class="nt">--no-pager</span>

<span class="c"># Temporarily skip the stuck service</span>
systemctl mask stuck-service.service
<span class="c"># After debugging, unmask: systemctl unmask stuck-service.service</span>
```

</div></div>

Circular dependencies cause unpredictable boot order. If you see `Found ordering cycle` in the journal, review your `After=`/`Before=` directives and remove one direction of the cycle.

## Overview

    

**dbus-sensors** is a collection of sensor daemons that expose hardware sensor data via D-Bus. Each daemon handles a specific sensor type and integrates with Entity Manager for configuration.

```mermaid
---
title: dbus-sensors Architecture
---
flowchart TB
    subgraph sensors["Sensor Daemons"]
        direction LR
        adc["ADCSensor  
(ADC inputs)"]
        hwmon["HwmonTempSensor  
(I2C temps)"]
        psu["PSUSensor  
(PMBus PSU)"]
    end

    sensors --> dbus["D-Bus  
xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value"]
    dbus <--> em["Entity Manager  
(JSON Configuration)"]
    em --> kernel["Linux Kernel  
/sys/class/hwmon, /sys/bus/iio"]
```

> **ASCII-art version (for comparison)**

  <div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      dbus-sensors Architecture                 │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                │
│  ┌────────────────┐  ┌────────────────┐  ┌────────────────┐    │
│  │  ADCSensor     │  │ HwmonTempSensor│  │  PSUSensor     │    │
│  │  (ADC inputs)  │  │  (I2C temps)   │  │  (PMBus PSU)   │    │
│  └───────┬────────┘  └───────┬────────┘  └───────┬────────┘    │
│          │                   │                   │             │
│  ┌───────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────┐     │
│  │                     D-Bus                             │     │
│  │          xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value             │     │
│  └───────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┘     │
│                              │                                 │
│  ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐     │
│  │                   Entity Manager                      │     │
│  │              (JSON Configuration)                     │     │
│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                              │                                 │
│  ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐     │
│  │                   Linux Kernel                        │     │
│  │          /sys/class/hwmon, /sys/bus/iio               │     │
│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div>  </div>

---

## Sensor Daemons

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Daemon | Sensor Types | Data Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `adcsensor` | ADC voltage inputs | IIO subsystem |
| `hwmontempsensor` | I2C temperature sensors | hwmon sysfs |
| `psusensor` | PSU voltage, current, power | PMBus hwmon |
| `fansensor` | Fan tachometers, PWM | hwmon sysfs |
| `intrusionsensor` | Chassis intrusion | GPIO |
| `ipmbsensor` | IPMB sensors | IPMB interface |
| `mcutempsensor` | MCU temperature | I2C |
| `nvmesensor` | NVMe temperature | NVMe-MI |
| `externalsensor` | Virtual sensors | D-Bus input |

</div>
---

## Configuration & Setup

    

### Build-Time Configuration (Yocto)

    

Enable or disable specific sensor daemons in your machine configuration:

```bitbake
# In your machine .conf or image recipe

# Include all sensor daemons (default)
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " dbus-sensors"

# Or include specific sensor daemons only
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " \
    adcsensor \
    hwmontempsensor \
    fansensor \
    psusensor \
"

# Exclude specific daemons
RDEPENDS:${PN}:remove:pn-dbus-sensors = "intrusionsensor ipmbsensor"
```

### Meson Build Options

    

When building dbus-sensors from source:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># View all options</span>
meson configure build

<span class="c"># Common options</span>
meson setup build <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-Dadc</span><span class="o">=</span>enabled <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-Dhwmon-temp</span><span class="o">=</span>enabled <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-Dfan</span><span class="o">=</span>enabled <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-Dpsu</span><span class="o">=</span>enabled <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-Dintrusion</span><span class="o">=</span>disabled <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-Dipmb</span><span class="o">=</span>disabled <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-Dnvme</span><span class="o">=</span>enabled <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-Dexternal</span><span class="o">=</span>enabled
```

</div></div>

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `adc` | enabled | ADC voltage sensors |
| `hwmon-temp` | enabled | I2C temperature sensors |
| `fan` | enabled | Fan tachometer sensors |
| `psu` | enabled | PMBus PSU sensors |
| `intrusion` | enabled | Chassis intrusion sensor |
| `ipmb` | enabled | IPMB sensors |
| `nvme` | enabled | NVMe temperature sensors |
| `external` | enabled | External/virtual sensors |
| `mcu-temp` | enabled | MCU temperature sensor |

</div>

### Runtime Enable/Disable

    

Control sensor daemons at runtime via systemd:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Disable a sensor daemon</span>
systemctl disable xyz.openbmc_project.adcsensor
systemctl stop xyz.openbmc_project.adcsensor

<span class="c"># Enable a sensor daemon</span>
systemctl <span class="nb">enable </span>xyz.openbmc_project.hwmontempsensor
systemctl start xyz.openbmc_project.hwmontempsensor

<span class="c"># Check status</span>
systemctl status xyz.openbmc_project.fansensor

<span class="c"># List all sensor services</span>
systemctl list-units | <span class="nb">grep </span>sensor
```

</div></div>

### Sensor Custom Properties

    

Sensors support additional configuration properties in Entity Manager:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Exposes"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"CPU Temp"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"TMP75"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Bus"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Address"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"0x48"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">

            </span><span class="nl">"PowerState"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"On"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"ReadState"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"On"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"PollRate"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">1.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Offset"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"ScaleFactor"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">1.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Label"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"CPU Core Temperature"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"MaxValue"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">125</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"MinValue"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">-40</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">

            </span><span class="nl">"Thresholds"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="err">...</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PowerState` | string | When to poll: `On`, `BiosPost`, `Always` |
| `ReadState` | string | Alternate power state control |
| `PollRate` | float | Polling interval in seconds (default: 1.0) |
| `Offset` | float | Value offset adjustment |
| `ScaleFactor` | float | Multiplier for raw value |
| `Label` | string | Human-readable label |
| `MaxValue` | float | Maximum expected value |
| `MinValue` | float | Minimum expected value |

</div>

### Hysteresis Configuration

    

Configure threshold hysteresis to prevent alarm flapping:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Thresholds"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Direction"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"greater than"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"upper critical"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Severity"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Value"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">95</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Hysteresis"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">2.0</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

The alarm clears when value drops below `Value - Hysteresis` (93°C in this example).

---

## D-Bus Sensor Interface

    

All sensors implement `xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value`:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Introspect a sensor</span>
busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.ADCSensor <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/voltage/P12V

<span class="c"># Properties:</span>
<span class="c">#   Value          - Current sensor reading (double)</span>
<span class="c">#   MaxValue       - Maximum possible value</span>
<span class="c">#   MinValue       - Minimum possible value</span>
<span class="c">#   Unit           - Measurement unit</span>
```

</div></div>

### Threshold Interfaces

    

Sensors can have warning and critical thresholds:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Threshold.Warning
  - WarningHigh
  - WarningLow
  - WarningAlarmHigh
  - WarningAlarmLow

xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Threshold.Critical
  - CriticalHigh
  - CriticalLow
  - CriticalAlarmHigh
  - CriticalAlarmLow
```

</div></div>
---

## ADC Sensors

    

ADC sensors read analog voltage inputs via the Linux IIO subsystem.

### Device Tree Configuration

    

```dts
// In your device tree
&adc {
    status = "okay";
    pinctrl-names = "default";
    pinctrl-0 = <&pinctrl_adc0_default
                 &pinctrl_adc1_default>;
};
```

### Entity Manager Configuration

    

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Exposes"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Index"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"P12V"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"ScaleFactor"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">4.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"ADC"</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Index"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"P3V3"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"ScaleFactor"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">1.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"ADC"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Thresholds"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
                </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="nl">"Direction"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"greater than"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"upper critical"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="nl">"Severity"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="nl">"Value"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">3.6</span><span class="w">
                </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
                </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="nl">"Direction"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"less than"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"lower critical"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="nl">"Severity"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="nl">"Value"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">3.0</span><span class="w">
                </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"MyBoard"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Board"</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

### Key Properties

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Index` | ADC channel number (matches hwmon inX_input) |
| `Name` | Sensor name on D-Bus |
| `ScaleFactor` | Voltage divider ratio |
| `PowerState` | When to read (On, BiosPost, Always) |
| `Thresholds` | Warning/critical levels |

</div>

## Hwmon Temperature Sensors

    

For I2C temperature sensors (TMP75, LM75, etc.).

### Entity Manager Configuration

    

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Exposes"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Address"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"0x48"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Bus"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"CPU Temp"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"TMP75"</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Address"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"0x49"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Bus"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">

            </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"TMP75"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Thresholds"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
                </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="nl">"Direction"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"greater than"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"upper critical"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="nl">"Severity"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="nl">"Value"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">45</span><span class="w">
                </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"TempSensors"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Probe"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"TRUE"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Board"</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

### Supported Sensor Types

| Type | Chip | Common Uses |

| `TMP75` | TI TMP75 | Ambient temperature |
| `TMP421` | TI TMP421 | Remote diode sensing |
| `TMP112` | TI TMP112 | Low power temp |
| `LM75A` | NXP LM75A | General purpose |
| `EMC1413` | Microchip | Multi-channel |

</div>

<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">

        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">

## Virtual/External Sensors

    

For calculated values or sensors from external sources.

### Entity Manager Configuration

    

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Exposes"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Total Power"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"ExternalSensor"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Units"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Watts"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"MinValue"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"MaxValue"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2000</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"VirtualSensors"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Board"</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

### Setting Values via D-Bus

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># External sensors can be written to</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.ExternalSensor <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/power/Total_Power <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value Value d 450.5
```

</div></div>

The `externalsensor` daemon can enforce **staleness** on a writable sensor. Add a
`Timeout` (in seconds) to the Entity Manager entry: if no new value is written within
that window, the daemon’s reaper (`updateReaper`) invalidates the sensor and publishes
`NaN` on `Value`, so a stalled producer surfaces as “unavailable” instead of a stuck
last-known reading. A `Timeout` of `0` (or an omitted key) makes the sensor
non-perishable — it keeps its last written value indefinitely.

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Total Power"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"ExternalSensor"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Units"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Watts"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Timeout"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"MinValue"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"MaxValue"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2000</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>
---

## SMBPBI Sensors

    

The `smbpbi` daemon (service `xyz.openbmc_project.SMBPBI`) reads telemetry from a
management controller — typically an NVIDIA HMC/GPU — that exposes an **SMBus Post-Box
Interface (SMBPBI)** “virtual EEPROM” over I2C. Each Entity Manager entry of type
`SmbpbiVirtualEeprom` maps a byte offset in that virtual EEPROM to one D-Bus sensor.

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Exposes"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"GPU0 Temp"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"SmbpbiVirtualEeprom"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Bus"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Address"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"0x4f"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"ReadOffset"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Units"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"DegreesC"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"ValueType"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"UINT64"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"PollRate"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">1.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"MinValue"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"MaxValue"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">128</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"GPU Board"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Board"</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

The daemon issues a raw `I2C_RDWR` transfer to read the block at `ReadOffset`, then
decodes it according to `Units`: `convert2Temp` for `DegreesC`, `convert2Power` for
`Watts`, plus direct handling for `Joules` (energy) and `Volts` (voltage). The `Units`
value picks both the decode routine and the D-Bus object path
(`/xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/{temperature,power,energy,voltage}/…`).

When the management controller has not yet published a value, the SMBPBI block reads
back as all `0xFF`. The daemon treats that as “no data” and publishes `NaN` rather than
a bogus reading, so a consumer can tell a genuine zero from an absent one.

---

## Cable Monitoring

    

The `cable-monitor` daemon (service `xyz.openbmc_project.cablemonitor`) tracks whether
the cables a platform expects are actually present and raises Redfish events when one is
plugged or unplugged. Unlike the register-reading sensor daemons, it does not touch
hardware — it watches the **inventory** on D-Bus and compares it against a configured
expected list.

The expected cables come from a JSON file at
`/var/lib/cablemonitor/cable-config.json` with a `ConnectedCables` array of cable names:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"ConnectedCables"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="s2">"PCIe_Cable_0"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="s2">"PCIe_Cable_1"</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

At runtime the daemon subscribes to inventory objects that implement
`xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item.Cable` (published by Entity Manager) and reacts to
their `InterfacesAdded` / `InterfacesRemoved` signals; it also watches the config file
with inotify so an updated list is picked up without a restart. When an expected cable’s
inventory object appears it logs a `CableConnected` event, and when one disappears it
logs `CableDisconnected` (both in the `xyz.openbmc_project.State.Cable` namespace, routed
through phosphor-logging to the Redfish event log).

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Watch cable connect/disconnect events</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> xyz.openbmc_project.cablemonitor <span class="nt">-f</span>
```

</div></div>
---

## IPMB Sensors

    

The `ipmbsensor` daemon (service `xyz.openbmc_project.IpmbSensor`) reads sensors that
live behind an **IPMB** (Intelligent Platform Management Bus) satellite controller — a
BMC, ME (management engine), or voltage-regulator bridge — instead of on a local I2C
bus. It does not talk to the bus directly; it sends IPMI requests through the
`org.openbmc.Ipmb` D-Bus service (`/xyz/openbmc_project/Ipmi/Channel/Ipmb`,
`sendRequest` method), which an IPMB transport daemon relays onto the wire.

Each Entity Manager entry of type `IpmbSensor` names a bridge `Class` and a
`SensorType`:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Exposes"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"MB Temp"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"IpmbSensor"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Class"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"METemp"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"SensorType"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"temperature"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Address"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"0x2e"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Bus"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"HostSMbusIndex"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"PollRate"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">1.0</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"IPMB Board"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Board"</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `Class` | Bridge/reading protocol: `METemp`/`MESensor`, `PxeBridgeTemp`, `IRBridgeTemp`, `HSCBridge`, `MpsBridgeTemp`, `SMPro` |
| `SensorType` | Reading subtype: `temperature` (default), `voltage`, `power`, `current`, `utilization` |
| `Address` | IPMB device (satellite) address |
| `HostSMbusIndex` | SMBus index passed in bridged VR commands |

</div>

### SDR Auto-Discovery (IpmbSDRDevice)

    

Beyond the statically declared sensors above, the daemon can enumerate a satellite’s
sensors automatically by reading its **SDR (Sensor Data Record) repository**. The
`IpmbSDRDevice` class walks the repository — Get SDR Repository Info, Reserve SDR
Repository, then repeated Get SDR — and for every **Type-01 (Full Sensor Record)** entry
it parses the sensor name, unit, conversion factors, and thresholds, then creates a
matching D-Bus sensor. This lets a platform pick up all of a satellite BMC’s sensors
without listing each one in Entity Manager.

---

## MCU Temperature and NVMe Sensors

    

### MCU Temperature (mcutempsensor)

    

The `mcutempsensor` daemon (service `xyz.openbmc_project.MCUTempSensor`) reads a
temperature value from a microcontroller register over I2C. The Entity Manager entry
(type `MCUTempSensor`) gives the `Bus`, `Address`, and the register offset in `Reg`; the
daemon opens `/dev/i2c-` and issues an SMBus read-word at that register.

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Exposes"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"MCU Temp"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"MCUTempSensor"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Class"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"MCUTempSensor"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Bus"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Address"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"0x50"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Reg"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">4</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"MCU Board"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Board"</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

### NVMe (nvmesensor)

    

The `nvmesensor` daemon (service `xyz.openbmc_project.NVMeSensor`, config type
`NVME1000`) reads drive temperature over **NVMe-MI** using the Basic Management Command
on the drive’s SMBus/I2C interface. Drives usually sit behind an I2C mux, so the daemon
derives the **root bus** from the mux device’s `/mux_device` symlink and shares one
context per root bus. Each basic-management query runs on a dedicated worker thread so a
slow or unresponsive drive cannot stall the daemon’s main event loop.

---

## Threshold Configuration

    

### Threshold Levels

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Severity | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Warning |
| 1 | Critical |

</div>

### Direction

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Direction | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `greater than` | Alarm when value > threshold |
| `less than` | Alarm when value < threshold |

</div>

### Example with All Thresholds

    

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Thresholds"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Direction"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"greater than"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"upper critical"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Severity"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Value"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">90</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Direction"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"greater than"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"upper warning"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Severity"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Value"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">80</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Direction"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"less than"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"lower warning"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Severity"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Value"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Direction"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"less than"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"lower critical"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Severity"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Value"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

<span class="c"># List all sensors</span>

<span class="c"># Read sensor value</span>

<span class="c"># Check threshold status</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.HwmonTempSensor <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/temperature/CPU_Temp <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Threshold.Critical CriticalAlarmHigh
