## Configuration Methods

    

phosphor-pid-control supports two ways to load its configuration:

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Method | Config Location | When to Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Direct JSON** | `/usr/share/swampd/config.json` | Simple systems, single board, quick prototyping |
| **Entity Manager** | `/usr/share/entity-manager/configurations/*.json` | Multi-board support, dynamic hardware detection |

</div>

### Direct JSON

    

Place a `config.json` in `/usr/share/swampd/` (see [zone-config.json](https://github.com/MichaelTien8901/openbmc-guide-tutorial/blob/main/docs/examples/fan-control/zone-config.json) for a complete example). This file defines sensors, zones, and PIDs in a single flat structure.

The direct JSON format includes `sensors` (D-Bus paths for temperature and fan tach), `zones`, and `pid` arrays. phosphor-pid-control reads this file at startup.

### Entity Manager (Recommended)

    

Entity Manager is the preferred method for production systems. It separates hardware description from thermal policy and supports multiple board configurations.

**How it works:**

1. Entity Manager scans JSON files in `/usr/share/entity-manager/configurations/`
2. Each file has a `"Probe"` field that determines **when** the config applies (e.g., only when a specific board is detected via FRU data or GPIO)
3. When the probe matches, Entity Manager exposes the configuration on D-Bus
4. phosphor-pid-control reads its PID/zone config from D-Bus (not from the JSON file directly)

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
JSON file in configurations/     Entity Manager         phosphor-pid-control
┌──────────────────────┐     ┌──────────────────┐     ┌─────────────────┐
│ Probe: "board match" │────>│ Evaluates probe  │     │                 │
│ Exposes:             │     │ If match:        │     │ Reads PID config│
│   - Pid.Zone         │     │   publishes to   │────>│ from D-Bus      │
│   - Pid (temp)       │     │   D-Bus          │     │ Starts control  │
│   - Pid (fan)        │     │                  │     │ loop            │
└──────────────────────┘     └──────────────────┘     └─────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

## Entity Manager Integration

    

### Where to Put the JSON File

    

The Entity Manager configuration file goes in your machine layer:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># In your Yocto layer</span>
meta-myplatform/
  recipes-phosphor/
    configuration/
      entity-manager/
        files/
          my-board-fan-control.json    <span class="c"># <-- your fan config</span>
        entity-manager_%.bbappend

<span class="c"># bbappend to install the config</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> <span class="o">></span> entity-manager_%.bbappend <span class="o"><<</span> <span class="sh">'</span><span class="no">EOF</span><span class="sh">'
FILESEXTRAPATHS:prepend := "</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">THISDIR</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/files:"
SRC_URI += "file://my-board-fan-control.json"

do_install:append() {
    install -d </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">D</span><span class="k">}${</span><span class="nv">datadir</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/entity-manager/configurations
    install -m 0444 </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">WORKDIR</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/my-board-fan-control.json </span><span class="se">\</span><span class="sh">
        </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">D</span><span class="k">}${</span><span class="nv">datadir</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/entity-manager/configurations/
}
</span><span class="no">EOF
</span>
```

</div></div>

On the BMC filesystem, the file ends up at:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
/usr/share/entity-manager/configurations/my-board-fan-control.json
```

</div></div>

### The Probe Field

    

The `"Probe"` field tells Entity Manager **when** to activate this configuration. Common patterns:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="err">//</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">Always</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">active</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">(useful</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">for</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">development/QEMU)</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="nl">"Probe"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"TRUE"</span><span class="w">

</span><span class="err">//</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">Match</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">a</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">specific</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">board</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">by</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">FRU</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">product</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">name</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="nl">"Probe"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.FruDevice({'PRODUCT_PRODUCT_NAME': 'MyServer'})"</span><span class="w">

</span><span class="err">//</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">Match</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">by</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">board</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">ID</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">GPIO</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="nl">"Probe"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Decorator.Asset({'Model': 'X123'})"</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

### Complete Entity Manager Fan Config

    

A single JSON file defines the zone, thermal PIDs, and fan PIDs together. See [entity-manager-fan.json](https://github.com/MichaelTien8901/openbmc-guide-tutorial/blob/main/docs/examples/fan-control/entity-manager-fan.json) for the full working example.

The key `Exposes` entries:

**Zone definition** — sets minimum fan speed and failsafe behavior:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Zone 0"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Pid.Zone"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"MinThermalOutput"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">25.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"FailSafePercent"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">100.0</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

**Thermal PID** (`Class: "temp"`) — controls fan speed based on temperature:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"CPU Thermal PID"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Pid"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Class"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"temp"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Inputs"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"CPU_Temp"</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"SetPoint"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">80.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Zones"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"Zone 0"</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"PIDGains"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"P"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"I"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">-0.2</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"D"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"FF"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"ILimitMin"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"ILimitMax"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">100.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"OutLimitMin"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">25.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"OutLimitMax"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">100.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"SlewNeg"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">5.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"SlewPos"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">10.0</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

**Fan PID** (`Class: "fan"`) — converts zone PWM% to actual fan RPM using feed-forward:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Fan0 PID"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Pid"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Class"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"fan"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Inputs"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"Fan0"</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"SetPoint"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">7000.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Zones"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"Zone 0"</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"PIDGains"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"P"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"I"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"D"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"FF"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">1.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"ILimitMin"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"ILimitMax"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">100.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"OutLimitMin"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"OutLimitMax"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">100.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"SlewNeg"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"SlewPos"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

> The `Class` field is critical: `"temp"` PIDs calculate desired fan speed from temperature readings; `"fan"` PIDs translate the zone’s requested RPM into actual PWM output. A complete config needs **both** types.

### Verify on Running System

    

After deploying the config and rebooting:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check Entity Manager loaded the config</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.EntityManager | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> pid

<span class="c"># Check phosphor-pid-control is using the config</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> phosphor-pid-control | <span class="nb">head</span> <span class="nt">-20</span>

<span class="c"># Verify zones are active</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.State.FanCtrl
```

</div></div>
---

## D-Bus Interface

    

### Zone Control

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check zone status</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.State.FanCtrl

<span class="c"># Get current zone mode</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.State.FanCtrl <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/thermal/0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.ThermalMode Current

<span class="c"># Set manual mode</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.State.FanCtrl <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/thermal/0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.ThermalMode Current s <span class="s2">"Manual"</span>
```

</div></div>

### Manual Fan Control

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># When in Manual mode, set fan PWM directly</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.FanSensor <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/fanpwm/Fan0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.FanPwm Target t 75
```

</div></div>
---

## PID Tuning

    

### Step 1: Baseline Measurements

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Record temperatures at fixed fan speeds</span>
<span class="k">for </span>pwm <span class="k">in </span>30 50 70 100<span class="p">;</span> <span class="k">do
    </span><span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"Testing at </span><span class="nv">$pwm</span><span class="s2">% PWM"</span>
    <span class="c"># Set manual mode and fixed PWM</span>
    <span class="c"># Record temperatures after stabilization (5-10 minutes)</span>
<span class="k">done</span>
```

</div></div>

### Step 2: Start Conservative

    

Begin with conservative PID values:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"proportionalCoeff"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"integralCoeff"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">-0.1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"outLim_min"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">30.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"outLim_max"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">100.0</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

### Step 3: Tune Integral Gain

    

* **Too slow**: Increase `integralCoeff` magnitude (e.g., -0.1 → -0.2)
* **Oscillating**: Decrease `integralCoeff` magnitude
* **Not reaching setpoint**: Check `outLim_max` allows sufficient cooling

### Step 4: Add Rate Limiting

    

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"slewNeg"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">5.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"slewPos"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">10.0</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

* `slewPos`: Max PWM increase per second
* `slewNeg`: Max PWM decrease per second

### Step 5: Verify Failsafe

    

Test failsafe behavior:

1. Disconnect a temperature sensor
2. Verify fans go to `failsafePercent`
3. Reconnect and verify normal operation resumes

---

## Multiple Zones

    

For systems with multiple thermal zones:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"zones"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"id"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"minThermalOutput"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">25.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"failsafePercent"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">100.0</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"id"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"minThermalOutput"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">30.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"failsafePercent"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">100.0</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"fans"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"CPU_Fan"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"zone"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"sensors"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"CPU_Fan"</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"output"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"CPU_Fan"</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Sys_Fan"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"zone"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"sensors"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"Sys_Fan"</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"output"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Sys_Fan"</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>
---

## Exit-Air Temperature and Airflow (CFM)

    

The `exitairtempsensor` daemon (part of dbus-sensors) publishes two *calculated*
sensors that let thermal control reason about airflow, not just temperature.

**Airflow (CFM).** A `CFMSensor` estimates airflow in cubic feet per minute from
fan tachometer readings, using per-fan coefficients (`c1`, `c2`,
`tachMinPercent`, `tachMaxPercent`, `maxCFM`). It also publishes `PWMLimit` /
`CFMLimit` values that phosphor-pid-control can consume to cap fan PWM against a
system-wide airflow ceiling.

**Exit-air temperature.** An `ExitAirTempSensor` derives the chassis exit-air
temperature from total CFM, the inlet temperature, and system power, smoothed by
an exponential moving average. Its tuning constants (`powerFactorMin`/
`powerFactorMax`, `qMin`/`qMax`, `alphaS`, `alphaF`, `pOffset`) are supplied
through Entity Manager configuration. (Verify the exact key names against your
dbus-sensors version.)

Both sensors appear on D-Bus like any other sensor, so they can feed a PID zone
as an input or drive thresholds. Configure them with Entity Manager `Exposes`
entries of type `ExitAirTempSensor` / `CFMSensor` on the relevant chassis.

These are computed sensors with no backing hardware device. If either reads
`NaN`, confirm that its input sensors (fan tachs, inlet temperature, system
power) are present and that the coefficient set matches your chassis.

---

## Stepwise Control

    

For simple table-based control instead of PID:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Inlet Stepwise"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"stepwise"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"inputs"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"Inlet_Temp"</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"reading"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"positiveHysteresis"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">2.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"negativeHysteresis"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">2.0</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"output"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"0"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"25"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">40</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"30"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"35"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">70</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"40"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

The `output` map defines PWM percentage at each temperature threshold.

## Troubleshooting

    

### Fans at Maximum Speed

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check if in failsafe</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> phosphor-pid-control | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> failsafe

<span class="c"># Verify sensors are responding</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.HwmonTempSensor

<span class="c"># Check PID controller status</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> phosphor-pid-control <span class="nt">-f</span>
```

</div></div>

### Fans Not Responding

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Verify PWM control works manually</span>
<span class="nb">echo </span>128 <span class="o">></span> /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon0/pwm1

<span class="c"># Check fan sensor service</span>
systemctl status xyz.openbmc_project.fansensor

<span class="c"># Verify D-Bus fan objects exist</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.FanSensor
```

</div></div>

### Temperature Oscillating

    

Reduce integral gain or add slew rate limiting:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"integralCoeff"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">-0.1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"slewNeg"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">3.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"slewPos"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">5.0</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

### Debug Logging

    

Enable verbose logging:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
systemctl stop phosphor-pid-control
/usr/bin/swampd <span class="nt">-d</span>
```

</div></div>

## Deep Dive

    

Advanced implementation details for thermal control developers.

### PID Mathematics

    

The PID controller in phosphor-pid-control uses discrete-time calculations:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    PID Control Loop (per sample period)                  │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                          │
│   error = setpoint - current_temperature                                 │
│                                                                          │
│   ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐                │
│   │ Proportional│     │  Integral   │     │ Derivative  │                │
│   │             │     │             │     │             │                │
│   │  P = Kp × e │     │ I += Ki × e │     │ D = Kd × Δe │                │
│   │             │     │   × dt      │     │     / dt    │                │
│   └──────┬──────┘     └──────┬──────┘     └──────┬──────┘                │
│          │                   │                   │                       │
│          └───────────────────┼───────────────────┘                       │
│                              │                                           │
│                              ▼                                           │
│                    output = P + I + D + FF                               │
│                              │                                           │
│                              ▼                                           │
│                    output = clamp(output, outLim_min, outLim_max)        │
│                              │                                           │
│                              ▼                                           │
│                    output = apply_slew_rate(output, previous_output)     │
│                              │                                           │
│                              ▼                                           │
│                         Fan PWM %                                        │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

**Why negative integral coefficient?**

For cooling control, we want:

* Temperature **above** setpoint → **increase** fan speed
* `error = setpoint - temperature` is **negative** when too hot
* Negative `Ki` × negative `error` = **positive** output increase

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
Example:
  setpoint = 80°C, temperature = 85°C
  error = 80 - 85 = -5
  Ki = -0.2
  I contribution = -0.2 × -5 = +1.0  (increases PWM)
```

</div></div>

### Anti-Windup Implementation

    

**Integral windup** occurs when the integral term accumulates excessively during sustained error, causing overshoot when the system finally responds.

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     Integral Windup Prevention                          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   Without Anti-Windup:           With Anti-Windup:                      │
│                                                                         │
│   Integral                       Integral                               │
│      ▲                              ▲                                   │
│      │    ╱──────                   │    ╱──── integralLimit_max        │
│      │   ╱                          │   ╱                               │
│      │  ╱  (accumulates             │  ╱  (clamped at limit)            │
│      │ ╱    indefinitely)           │ ╱                                 │
│      │╱                             │╱                                  │
│   ───┼────────► time             ───┼────────► time                     │
│      │                              │                                   │
│                                                                         │
│   Code implementation (pid/ec/pid.cpp):                                 │
│                                                                         │
│   integral += Ki * error * dt;                                          │
│   integral = std::clamp(integral, integralLimit_min, integralLimit_max);│
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

**Configuration guidelines:**

* `integralLimit_max`: Should match `outLim_max` (typically 100.0)
* `integralLimit_min`: Usually 0.0 for cooling-only systems

### Slew Rate Limiting

    

Slew rate limits prevent sudden fan speed changes that cause acoustic disturbance:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      Slew Rate Limiting                                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   PWM %                                                                 │
│    100 ┤                    ╭───────────── Target                       │
│        │                  ╱                                             │
│     80 ┤                ╱   ← slewPos limits ramp-up rate               │
│        │              ╱                                                 │
│     60 ┤            ╱                                                   │
│        │          ╱                                                     │
│     40 ┤        ╱                                                       │
│        │      ╱                                                         │
│     20 ┤────╱                                                           │
│        │                                                                │
│        └────────────────────────────────────────────────────► time      │
│                                                                         │
│   Algorithm:                                                            │
│                                                                         │
│   delta = new_output - previous_output;                                 │
│   if (delta > 0 && slewPos > 0) {                                       │
│       delta = min(delta, slewPos * samplePeriod);                       │
│   } else if (delta < 0 && slewNeg > 0) {                                │
│       delta = max(delta, -slewNeg * samplePeriod);                      │
│   }                                                                     │
│   output = previous_output + delta;                                     │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

**Example calculation:**

* Current PWM: 40%, Target: 80%
* `slewPos`: 10.0 (%/second)
* `samplePeriod`: 1.0 second
* Max change per cycle: 10% → Output: 50% (not 80%)
* After 4 cycles: 40% → 50% → 60% → 70% → 80%

### Failsafe Trigger Conditions

    

Failsafe mode sets all fans to `failsafePercent` (typically 100%) when:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     Failsafe Trigger Conditions                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   1. SENSOR TIMEOUT                                                     │
│      └─ Sensor value not updated within timeout period                  │
│      └─ Default: 2 × samplePeriod                                       │
│      └─ Check: sensor returns NaN or error on D-Bus read                │
│                                                                         │
│   2. SENSOR MISSING                                                     │
│      └─ Required input sensor not found on D-Bus                        │
│      └─ Occurs during startup or sensor service crash                   │
│                                                                         │
│   3. FAN FAILURE                                                        │
│      └─ Tachometer reads 0 RPM when PWM > minimum                       │
│      └─ Indicates stuck or disconnected fan                             │
│                                                                         │
│   4. THERMAL RUNAWAY                                                    │
│      └─ Temperature exceeds critical threshold                          │
│      └─ Fans cannot maintain setpoint at 100% PWM                       │
│                                                                         │
│   Recovery:                                                             │
│   └─ Automatic when all sensors return to normal                        │
│   └─ Requires valid readings for "recovery delay" period                │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

**Source reference**: [pid/zone.cpp](https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-pid-control/blob/master/pid/zone.cpp)

### Control Loop Timing

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Control Loop Execution                               │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐          │
│   │  t=0s    │    │  t=1s    │    │  t=2s    │    │  t=3s    │          │
│   └────┬─────┘    └────┬─────┘    └────┬─────┘    └────┬─────┘          │
│        │               │               │               │                │
│        ▼               ▼               ▼               ▼                │
│   ┌─────────┐     ┌─────────┐     ┌─────────┐     ┌─────────┐           │
│   │Read     │     │Read     │     │Read     │     │Read     │           │
│   │Sensors  │     │Sensors  │     │Sensors  │     │Sensors  │           │
│   └────┬────┘     └────┬────┘     └────┬────┘     └────┬────┘           │
│        │               │               │               │                │
│        ▼               ▼               ▼               ▼                │
│   ┌─────────┐     ┌─────────┐     ┌─────────┐     ┌─────────┐           │
│   │Run PID  │     │Run PID  │     │Run PID  │     │Run PID  │           │
│   │Calc     │     │Calc     │     │Calc     │     │Calc     │           │
│   └────┬────┘     └────┬────┘     └────┬────┘     └────┬────┘           │
│        │               │               │               │                │
│        ▼               ▼               ▼               ▼                │
│   ┌─────────┐     ┌─────────┐     ┌─────────┐     ┌─────────┐           │
│   │Write    │     │Write    │     │Write    │     │Write    │           │
│   │PWM      │     │PWM      │     │PWM      │     │PWM      │           │
│   └─────────┘     └─────────┘     └─────────┘     └─────────┘           │
│                                                                         │
│   samplePeriod = 1.0s (configurable per PID)                            │
│   Zones may have different sample periods                               │
│   Shorter period = faster response, more CPU usage                      │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### Multi-Sensor Zone Arbitration

    

When multiple PID controllers exist in a zone, outputs are arbitrated:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Multi-Sensor Arbitration                             │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   Zone 0 contains:                                                      │
│   ├── CPU_Temp PID    → output: 45%                                     │
│   ├── DIMM_Temp PID   → output: 60%                                     │
│   └── Inlet_Temp PID  → output: 35%                                     │
│                                                                         │
│   Arbitration: MAX(all outputs)                                         │
│   └── Final zone output: 60% (highest demand wins)                      │
│                                                                         │
│   All fans in zone receive this output:                                 │
│   ├── Fan0 PWM = 60%                                                    │
│   ├── Fan1 PWM = 60%                                                    │
│   └── Fan2 PWM = 60%                                                    │
│                                                                         │
│   Rationale: Prevents any component from overheating                    │
│   Trade-off: May over-cool some components                              │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

## Overview

    

OpenBMC power management includes several components:

* **phosphor-power**: PSU management, power supply monitoring
* **phosphor-regulators**: Voltage regulator configuration
* **Power sequencing**: GPIO-based power control
* **Power capping**: System power limiting

```mermaid
---
title:  Power Management Architecture  
---

flowchart TB
    state["phosphor-state-manager  
(Chassis/Host state control)"]

    state --> power & regulators & sequencer

    subgraph services["Power Control Services"]
        direction LR
        power["phosphor-power  
(PSU mgmt)"]
        regulators["phosphor-regulators  
(VRM cfg)"]
        sequencer["Power Sequencer  
(GPIO)"]
    end

    subgraph hw["Hardware Interfaces"]
        direction LR
        pmbus["PMBus PSUs"]
        i2c["I2C/VID Regulators"]
        gpio["GPIO Control"]
    end

    power --> pmbus
    regulators --> i2c
    sequencer --> gpio
```

## Setup & Configuration

    

### Build-Time Configuration (Yocto)

    

Include power management components:

```bitbake
# In your machine .conf or image recipe

# Core power management
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " phosphor-power"

# Include specific components
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " \
    phosphor-power-psu-monitor \
    phosphor-power-regulators \
    phosphor-power-sequencer \
    phosphor-power-utils \
"

# Exclude components you don't need
IMAGE_INSTALL:remove = "phosphor-power-regulators"
```

### Meson Build Options

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># phosphor-power build options</span>
meson setup build <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-Dpsu-monitor</span><span class="o">=</span>enabled <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-Dregulators</span><span class="o">=</span>enabled <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-Dsequencer</span><span class="o">=</span>enabled <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-Dutils</span><span class="o">=</span>enabled <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-Dtests</span><span class="o">=</span>disabled
```

</div></div>

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `psu-monitor` | enabled | PSU monitoring daemon |
| `regulators` | enabled | Voltage regulator control |
| `sequencer` | enabled | Power sequencing |
| `utils` | enabled | Command-line utilities |

</div>

### Runtime Enable/Disable

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check power services status</span>
systemctl status phosphor-psu-monitor
systemctl status phosphor-regulators

<span class="c"># Disable PSU monitoring</span>
systemctl stop phosphor-psu-monitor
systemctl disable phosphor-psu-monitor

<span class="c"># Enable regulators service</span>
systemctl <span class="nb">enable </span>phosphor-regulators
systemctl start phosphor-regulators
```

</div></div>

### Configuration Files

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Config File | Install Path | Format | Read By |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PSU config | `/usr/share/entity-manager/configurations/psu.json` | Entity Manager JSON | Entity Manager → D-Bus → psu-monitor |
| Regulators config | `/usr/share/phosphor-regulators/config.json` | phosphor-regulators JSON | phosphor-regulators directly |
| Power sequencer | `/usr/share/phosphor-power-sequencer/config.json` | Sequencer JSON | phosphor-power-sequencer directly |

</div>

### Deploying Configuration via Yocto

    

Each config file needs a bbappend recipe to install it into the image.

#### Regulators Config

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># meta-myplatform/recipes-phosphor/power/phosphor-regulators/</span>
<span class="c"># └── files/</span>
<span class="c"># │   └── my-regulators-config.json</span>
<span class="c"># └── phosphor-regulators_%.bbappend</span>

<span class="nb">cat</span> <span class="o">></span> phosphor-regulators_%.bbappend <span class="o"><<</span> <span class="sh">'</span><span class="no">EOF</span><span class="sh">'
FILESEXTRAPATHS:prepend := "</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">THISDIR</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/files:"
SRC_URI += "file://my-regulators-config.json"

do_install:append() {
    install -d </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">D</span><span class="k">}${</span><span class="nv">datadir</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/phosphor-regulators
    install -m 0644 </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">WORKDIR</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/my-regulators-config.json </span><span class="se">\</span><span class="sh">
        </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">D</span><span class="k">}${</span><span class="nv">datadir</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/phosphor-regulators/config.json
}
</span><span class="no">EOF
</span>
```

</div></div>

#### PSU Entity Manager Config

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># meta-myplatform/recipes-phosphor/configuration/entity-manager/</span>
<span class="c"># └── files/</span>
<span class="c"># │   └── my-psu-config.json</span>
<span class="c"># └── entity-manager_%.bbappend</span>

<span class="nb">cat</span> <span class="o">></span> entity-manager_%.bbappend <span class="o"><<</span> <span class="sh">'</span><span class="no">EOF</span><span class="sh">'
FILESEXTRAPATHS:prepend := "</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">THISDIR</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/files:"
SRC_URI += "file://my-psu-config.json"

do_install:append() {
    install -d </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">D</span><span class="k">}${</span><span class="nv">datadir</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/entity-manager/configurations
    install -m 0444 </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">WORKDIR</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/my-psu-config.json </span><span class="se">\</span><span class="sh">
        </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">D</span><span class="k">}${</span><span class="nv">datadir</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/entity-manager/configurations/
}
</span><span class="no">EOF
</span>
```

</div></div>

#### Verification

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Verify regulators config loaded</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> phosphor-regulators | <span class="nb">head</span> <span class="nt">-20</span>

```

### Power Restore Policy Configuration

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get current policy</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.Settings <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/power_restore_policy <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Power.RestorePolicy PowerRestorePolicy

<span class="c"># Set policy via D-Bus</span>
<span class="c"># Options: AlwaysOn, AlwaysOff, Restore</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Settings <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/power_restore_policy <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Power.RestorePolicy PowerRestorePolicy s <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Power.RestorePolicy.Policy.AlwaysOn"</span>

<span class="c"># Configure via Redfish</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{"PowerRestorePolicy": "AlwaysOn"}'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system
```

</div></div>

### Power Capping Configuration

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Enable power capping</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Settings <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/power_cap <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Power.Cap PowerCapEnable b <span class="nb">true</span>

<span class="c"># Set power cap value (watts)</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Settings <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/power_cap <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Power.Cap PowerCap u 500

<span class="c"># Via Redfish</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{"PowerControl":[{"PowerLimit":{"LimitInWatts":500,"LimitException":"LogEventOnly"}}]}'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Chassis/chassis/Power
```

</div></div>

### PSU Redundancy Configuration

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get redundancy status</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.Power.PSU <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/power_supply_redundancy <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.PowerSupplyRedundancy PowerSupplyRedundancyEnabled

<span class="c"># Enable redundancy monitoring</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Power.PSU <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/power_supply_redundancy <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.PowerSupplyRedundancy PowerSupplyRedundancyEnabled b <span class="nb">true</span>
```

</div></div>

### GPIO Configuration for Power Control

    

Define GPIO pins in your machine’s device tree:

```dts
// Example device tree fragment
gpio-keys {
    compatible = "gpio-keys";

    power-button {
        label = "power-button";
        gpios = <&gpio0 ASPEED_GPIO(E, 0) GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW>;
        linux,code = <KEY_POWER>;
    };

    power-ok {
        label = "power-ok";
        gpios = <&gpio0 ASPEED_GPIO(E, 1) GPIO_ACTIVE_HIGH>;
        linux,code = <KEY_BATTERY>;
    };
};
```

Configure in JSON:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"gpio_configs"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"POWER_BUTTON"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"direction"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"out"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"polarity"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"active_low"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"line"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">32</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"POWER_OK"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"direction"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"in"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"polarity"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"active_high"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"line"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">33</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

## PSU Management (phosphor-power)

    

### PSU Monitoring

    

The `psu-monitor` service monitors PMBus power supplies for:

* Input/output voltage and current
* Temperature
* Fan speed
* Fault conditions

### D-Bus Interface

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># List PSU inventory</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Manager | <span class="nb">grep </span>powersupply

<span class="c"># Get PSU properties</span>
busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Manager <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/chassis/powersupply0

<span class="c"># Check PSU present</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Manager <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/chassis/powersupply0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item Present
```

</div></div>

### Entity Manager PSU Configuration

    

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"PSU0"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Board"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Probe"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.FruDevice({'PRODUCT_PRODUCT_NAME': 'PSU-1000W'})"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">

    </span><span class="nl">"Exposes"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"PSU0"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"pmbus"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Bus"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Address"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"0x58"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Labels"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
                </span><span class="s2">"vin"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                </span><span class="s2">"vout1"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                </span><span class="s2">"iout1"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                </span><span class="s2">"pin"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                </span><span class="s2">"pout1"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                </span><span class="s2">"temp1"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                </span><span class="s2">"temp2"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                </span><span class="s2">"fan1"</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w">

    </span><span class="nl">"xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"Present"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kc">true</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"PrettyName"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Power Supply 0"</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">

    </span><span class="nl">"xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Decorator.Asset"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"Manufacturer"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"$PRODUCT_MANUFACTURER"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"Model"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"$PRODUCT_PRODUCT_NAME"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
```

### PSU Redundancy

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get current redundancy mode</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.Power.PSU <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/power_supply_redundancy <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.PowerSupplyRedundancy PowerSupplyRedundancyEnabled

<span class="c"># Set redundancy mode</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Power.PSU <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/power_supply_redundancy <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.PowerSupplyRedundancy PowerSupplyRedundancyEnabled b <span class="nb">true</span>
```

## Voltage Regulators (phosphor-regulators)

    

### Overview

    

phosphor-regulators manages voltage regulators on the system:

* Configuration during power-on
* Voltage level monitoring
* Regulator fault detection

### JSON Configuration

    

Configuration file: `/usr/share/phosphor-regulators/config.json`

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"rules"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"id"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"set_voltage_rule"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"actions"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
                </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="nl">"pmbus_write_vout_command"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
                        </span><span class="nl">"format"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"linear"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                        </span><span class="nl">"exponent"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">-8</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
                </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"chassis"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"number"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"inventory_path"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"/xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/chassis"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"devices"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
                </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="nl">"id"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"vdd_cpu0"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="nl">"is_regulator"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kc">true</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="nl">"fru"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"/xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/chassis/motherboard/cpu0"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="nl">"i2c_interface"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
                        </span><span class="nl">"bus"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                        </span><span class="nl">"address"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"0x40"</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="nl">"configuration"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
                        </span><span class="nl">"volts"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">1.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                        </span><span class="nl">"rule_id"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"set_voltage_rule"</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="nl">"rails"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
                        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
                            </span><span class="nl">"id"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"vdd_cpu0"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
                            </span><span class="nl">"sensor_monitoring"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
                                </span><span class="nl">"rule_id"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"read_sensors_rule"</span><span class="w">
                            </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
                        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
                    </span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
                </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

## Power Sequencing

    

### GPIO-Based Sequencing

    

Power sequencing is typically handled by systemd targets and GPIO control.

#### Device Tree GPIO Configuration

    

```dts
gpio-keys {
    compatible = "gpio-keys";

    power-good {
        label = "power-good";
        gpios = <&gpio0 ASPEED_GPIO(B, 2) GPIO_ACTIVE_HIGH>;
        linux,code = <KEY_POWER>;
    };
};

leds {
    compatible = "gpio-leds";

    power-button {
        gpios = <&gpio0 ASPEED_GPIO(D, 3) GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW>;
    };
};
```

#### Power Control Service

    

<div class="language-ini highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># /lib/systemd/system/power-control.service
</span><span class="nn">[Unit]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Description</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">Power Control</span>
<span class="py">After</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">xyz.openbmc_project.State.Chassis.service</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="nn">[Service]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Type</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">oneshot</span>
<span class="py">ExecStart</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">/usr/bin/power-control.sh on</span>
<span class="py">RemainAfterExit</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">yes</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="nn">[Install]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">WantedBy</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">obmc-host-start@0.target</span>
```

</div></div>

### Power Button Handling

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Monitor power button</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> xyz.openbmc_project.Chassis.Buttons <span class="nt">-f</span>

<span class="c"># Check button state</span>
busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.Chassis.Buttons <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/chassis/buttons/power
```

## Power Capping

    

### Overview

    

Power capping limits total system power consumption.

### D-Bus Interface

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get current power cap</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.Settings <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/power_cap <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Power.Cap PowerCap

<span class="c"># Set power cap (watts)</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Settings <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/power_cap <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Power.Cap PowerCap u 500

<span class="c"># Enable power cap</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Settings <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/power_cap <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Power.Cap PowerCapEnable b <span class="nb">true</span>
```

</div></div>

### Via Redfish

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get power limit</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Chassis/chassis/Power

<span class="c"># Set power limit</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{"PowerControl":[{"PowerLimit":{"LimitInWatts":500}}]}'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Chassis/chassis/Power
```

</div></div>
---

## Power Restore Policy

    

Configure behavior after AC power loss.

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get policy</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.Settings <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/power_restore_policy <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Power.RestorePolicy PowerRestorePolicy

<span class="c"># Set to AlwaysOn</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Settings <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/power_restore_policy <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Power.RestorePolicy PowerRestorePolicy s <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Power.RestorePolicy.Policy.AlwaysOn"</span>
```

</div></div>

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Policy | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `AlwaysOn` | Power on after AC restore |
| `AlwaysOff` | Stay off after AC restore |
| `Restore` | Return to previous state |

</div>
---

## Porting Considerations

    

### Required Configuration

    

1. **PSU I2C addresses**: Identify PMBus addresses
2. **GPIO mapping**: Power button, power good signals
3. **Sequencing requirements**: Timing constraints
4. **Redundancy mode**: N+1 or N+N configuration

### Device Tree Example

    

```dts
&i2c3 {
    status = "okay";

    psu0: psu@58 {
        compatible = "pmbus";
        reg = <0x58>;
    };

    psu1: psu@59 {
        compatible = "pmbus";
        reg = <0x59>;
    };
};
```

### Machine Layer Integration

    

```bitbake
# In your machine .conf
PREFERRED_PROVIDER_virtual/phosphor-power = "phosphor-power"

# Include power-related packages
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " \
    phosphor-power \
    phosphor-regulators \
    "
```

---

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
