```
<span class="c"># Check I2C bus</span>
i2cdetect <span class="nt">-y</span> 3

<span class="c"># Verify PMBus communication</span>
i2cget <span class="nt">-y</span> 3 0x58 0x99 w  <span class="c"># Read MFR_ID</span>

<span class="c"># Check Entity Manager logs</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> xyz.openbmc_project.EntityManager | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> psu
```

</div></div>

### Power On Failure

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check power state</span>
obmcutil state

<span class="c"># Check power good GPIO</span>
gpioget gpiochip0 
# Check systemd targets
systemctl list-dependencies obmc-host-start@0.target
```

### PSU Fault

    

```
# Check PSU status
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.PSUSensor \
    /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/power/PSU0_Input_Power \
    xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value Value

# Read PMBus status
i2cget -y 3 0x58 0x79 w  # STATUS_WORD
```

## Deep Dive

    

Advanced implementation details for power management developers.

### PMBus Protocol Overview

    

PMBus is an I2C-based protocol for power supply communication:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    PMBus Communication                                  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   BMC                                    PSU (PMBus Device)             │
│    │                                           │                        │
│    │  I2C Write: [Addr] [Cmd] [Data...]        │                        │
│    │──────────────────────────────────────────▶│                        │
│    │                                           │                        │
│    │  I2C Read: [Addr] [Cmd]                   │                        │
│    │──────────────────────────────────────────▶│                        │
│    │◀──────────────────────────────────────────│ [Data...]              │
│    │                                           │                        │
│                                                                         │
│   Common PMBus Commands:                                                │
│   ┌──────────┬────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ Command  │  Code  │ Description                                 │   │
│   ├──────────┼────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────┤   │
│   │ PAGE     │  0x00  │ Select output page                          │   │
│   │ OPERATION│  0x01  │ Turn output on/off, margin                  │   │
│   │ ON_OFF   │  0x02  │ Soft on/off control                         │   │
│   │ CLEAR_FAULT│ 0x03 │ Clear all faults                            │   │
│   │ VOUT_MODE│  0x20  │ Voltage output mode/exponent                │   │
│   │ VOUT_CMD │  0x21  │ Commanded output voltage                    │   │
│   │ READ_VIN │  0x88  │ Input voltage                               │   │
│   │ READ_IIN │  0x89  │ Input current                               │   │
│   │ READ_VOUT│  0x8B  │ Output voltage                              │   │
│   │ READ_IOUT│  0x8C  │ Output current                              │   │
│   │ READ_TEMP│  0x8D  │ Temperature (various)                       │   │
│   │ READ_POUT│  0x96  │ Output power                                │   │
│   │ READ_PIN │  0x97  │ Input power                                 │   │
│   │ STATUS_WD│  0x79  │ Status word (all faults summary)            │   │
│   │ MFR_ID   │  0x99  │ Manufacturer ID                             │   │
│   │ MFR_MODEL│  0x9A  │ Manufacturer model                          │   │
│   └──────────┴────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
│   Linear11 Format (used for most readings):                             │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ 16-bit value: [YYYYYYYYYY XXXXX]                                │   │
│   │ Y = 11-bit mantissa (two's complement)                          │   │
│   │ X = 5-bit exponent (two's complement)                           │   │
│   │ Real value = Y × 2^X                                            │   │
│   │                                                                 │   │
│   │ Example: 0x0B20 = 0000101 10010 0000                            │   │
│   │   Y = 0x164 = 356, X = 0x00 = 0                                 │   │
│   │   Value = 356 × 2^0 = 356 (e.g., 35.6 Amps with scaling)        │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

**Source reference**: [phosphor-power/tools/power-utils](https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-power)

### Power Sequencing

    

Power sequencing ensures voltages come up in the correct order:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Power Sequencing Timeline                            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   Time ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────▶  │
│                                                                         │
│   STDBY_3V3 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────   │
│   (always on)                                                           │
│                                                                         │
│   ATX_PS_ON ───────────────────┐                                        │
│                                └─────────────────────────────────────   │
│                                │                                        │
│   P12V_MAIN ───────────────────┼──┐                                     │
│                                   └──────────────────────────────────   │
│                                   │                                     │
│   P3V3_MAIN ──────────────────────┼──┐                                  │
│                                      └───────────────────────────────   │
│                                      │                                  │
│   P1V8      ─────────────────────────┼──┐                               │
│                                         └────────────────────────────   │
│                                         │                               │
│   VCORE     ────────────────────────────┼──┐                            │
│   (VR output)                              └─────────────────────────   │
│                                            │                            │
│   POWER_GOOD ─────────────────────────────────┐                         │
│                                               └──────────────────────   │
│                                                                         │
│   Timing Constraints:                                                   │
│   ├── t1: PS_ON to 12V stable: < 500ms                                  │
│   ├── t2: 12V to 3.3V stable: 1-10ms                                    │
│   ├── t3: 3.3V to VR enable: 5-20ms                                     │
│   ├── t4: VR stable to POWER_GOOD: 10-100ms                             │
│   └── Total sequence time: typically 100-500ms                          │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### Voltage Regulator (VR) Configuration

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Voltage Regulator Control                            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   phosphor-regulators JSON Configuration:                               │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ {                                                               │   │
│   │   "chassis": [{                                                 │   │
│   │     "number": 1,                                                │   │
│   │     "devices": [{                                               │   │
│   │       "id": "vdd_cpu0",                                         │   │
│   │       "is_regulator": true,                                     │   │
│   │       "fru": "/system/chassis/motherboard/cpu0",                │   │
│   │       "i2c_interface": {                                        │   │
│   │         "bus": 5,                                               │   │
│   │         "address": "0x40"                                       │   │
│   │       },                                                        │   │
│   │       "configuration": {                                        │   │
│   │         "volts": 1.0,                                           │   │
│   │         "rule_id": "set_voltage_rule"                           │   │
│   │       },                                                        │   │
│   │       "rails": [{                                               │   │
│   │         "id": "vdd_cpu0_rail",                                  │   │
│   │         "sensor_monitoring": {                                  │   │
│   │           "rule_id": "read_sensors_rule"                        │   │
│   │         }                                                       │   │
│   │       }]                                                        │   │
│   │     }]                                                          │   │
│   │   }]                                                            │   │
│   │ }                                                               │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
│   VR Sensor Mapping:                                                    │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ D-Bus Path: /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/voltage/VDD_CPU0       │   │
│   │ PMBus Cmd: READ_VOUT (0x8B)                                     │   │
│   │ Conversion: Linear16 with VOUT_MODE exponent                    │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### Power Capping Implementation

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Power Capping (DCMI)                                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   Power Cap Control Flow:                                               │
│   ┌────────────────┐    ┌────────────────┐    ┌────────────────┐        │
│   │  User sets     │───▶│  BMC enforces  │───▶│  Host CPU      │        │
│   │  power cap     │    │  via DCMI/OOB  │    │  throttles     │        │
│   │  (Redfish/IPMI)│    │                │    │                │        │
│   └────────────────┘    └────────────────┘    └────────────────┘        │
│                                                                         │
│   D-Bus Interface:                                                      │
│   Path: /xyz/openbmc_project/control/host0/power_cap                    │
│   Interface: xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Power.Cap                      │
│   ├── PowerCap (uint32) - Target power in watts                         │
│   ├── PowerCapEnable (bool) - Cap enforcement enabled                   │
│   └── ExceptionAction - Action on cap violation                         │
│                                                                         │
│   Implementation:                                                       │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ 1. Redfish PATCH to /redfish/v1/Chassis/chassis0/Power          │   │
│   │    { "PowerControl": [{ "PowerLimit": {"LimitInWatts": 500}}] } │   │
│   │                                                                 │   │
│   │ 2. bmcweb writes to D-Bus PowerCap property                     │   │
│   │                                                                 │   │
│   │ 3. phosphor-host-ipmid sends DCMI Set Power Limit to host       │   │
│   │                                                                 │   │
│   │ 4. Host BIOS/ME enforces cap via CPU P-state throttling         │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

</div>

## Overview

    

OpenBMC user management is handled by **phosphor-user-manager**, providing local accounts, role-based access control, and LDAP integration.

```mermaid
---
title: User Manager Architecture
---
flowchart TB
    subgraph access["Access Methods"]
        direction TB
        redfish["Redfish API"]
        ipmi["IPMI Users"]
        ssh["SSH Login"]
        webui["WebUI Login"]
    end

    access --> usermgr

    subgraph usermgr["phosphor-user-manager"]
        direction TB
        local["Local Accounts  
/etc/passwd"]
        ldap["LDAP/AD Config  
nslcd/sssd"]
        priv["Privilege  
Management"]
    end

    usermgr --> pam["PAM  
(Pluggable Authentication Modules)"]
```

> **ASCII-art version (for comparison)**

  <div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   User Manager Architecture                     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                 │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐│
│  │                    Access Methods                           ││
│  │                                                             ││
│  │   ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────┐    ││
│  │   │ Redfish  │  │  IPMI    │  │   SSH    │  │  WebUI   │    ││
│  │   │ API      │  │  Users   │  │ Login    │  │  Login   │    ││
│  │   └────┬─────┘  └────┬─────┘  └────┬─────┘  └────┬─────┘    ││
│  └────────┼─────────────┼─────────────┼─────────────┼──────────┘│
│           └─────────────┴──────┬──────┴─────────────┘           │
│                                │                                │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┐│
│  │                   phosphor-user-manager                     ││
│  │                                                             ││
│  │   ┌────────────────┐  ┌────────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ││
│  │   │ Local Accounts │  │ LDAP/AD Config │  │ Privilege    │  ││
│  │   │ /etc/passwd    │  │ nslcd/sssd     │  │ Management   │  ││
│  │   └────────────────┘  └────────────────┘  └──────────────┘  ││
│  └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘│
│                             │                                   │
│  ┌──────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┐│
│  │                          PAM                                ││
│  │              (Pluggable Authentication Modules)             ││
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘│
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Setup & Configuration

    

### Build-Time Configuration (Yocto)

    

```bitbake
# In your machine .conf or local.conf

# Include user management
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " \
    phosphor-user-manager \
"

# For LDAP support
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " \
    nss-pam-ldapd \
    pam-plugin-ldap \
"

# Configure Meson options
EXTRA_OEMESON:pn-phosphor-user-manager = " \
    -Dldap=enabled \
"
```

### Configuration Files

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Config File | Install Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PAM auth config | `/etc/pam.d/common-auth` | Authentication module stack |
| PAM password config | `/etc/pam.d/common-password` | Password change rules |
| PAM account config | `/etc/pam.d/common-account` | Account validation |
| LDAP client config | `/etc/nslcd.conf` | nslcd LDAP client settings |
| LDAP NSS config | `/etc/nsswitch.conf` | Name service switch (adds ldap) |
| D-Bus policy | `/etc/dbus-1/system.d/phosphor-user-manager.conf` | D-Bus access control |

</div>

### Deploying Custom PAM Configuration via Yocto

    

To customize PAM authentication (e.g., add stricter password policies or modify the auth
module order), create a bbappend for the pam recipe:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># meta-myplatform/recipes-phosphor/users/phosphor-user-manager/</span>
<span class="c"># └── files/</span>
<span class="c"># │   └── common-auth</span>
<span class="c"># │   └── common-password</span>
<span class="c"># └── phosphor-user-manager_%.bbappend</span>

<span class="nb">cat</span> <span class="o">></span> phosphor-user-manager_%.bbappend <span class="o"><<</span> <span class="sh">'</span><span class="no">EOF</span><span class="sh">'
FILESEXTRAPATHS:prepend := "</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">THISDIR</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/files:"
SRC_URI += " </span><span class="se">\</span><span class="sh">
    file://common-auth </span><span class="se">\</span><span class="sh">
    file://common-password </span><span class="se">\</span><span class="sh">
"

do_install:append() {
    # Deploy custom PAM configuration
    install -d </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">D</span><span class="k">}${</span><span class="nv">sysconfdir</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/pam.d
    install -m 0644 </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">WORKDIR</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/common-auth </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">D</span><span class="k">}${</span><span class="nv">sysconfdir</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/pam.d/
    install -m 0644 </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">WORKDIR</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/common-password </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">D</span><span class="k">}${</span><span class="nv">sysconfdir</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/pam.d/
}
</span><span class="no">EOF
</span>
```

</div></div>

Example `common-auth` with lockout policy:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
# /etc/pam.d/common-auth
auth required   pam_tally2.so deny=5 unlock_time=300 onerr=fail
auth sufficient pam_unix.so nullok try_first_pass
auth sufficient pam_ldap.so use_first_pass
auth required   pam_deny.so
```

</div></div>

### LDAP Configuration Persistence

    

LDAP configuration set via Redfish/D-Bus is persisted to:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># LDAP config persistence (managed by phosphor-user-manager)</span>
/var/lib/phosphor-user-manager/ldap.conf

<span class="c"># nslcd runtime config (generated from D-Bus settings)</span>
/etc/nslcd.conf
```

</div></div>

To bake default LDAP settings into the image:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># meta-myplatform/recipes-phosphor/users/nss-pam-ldapd/</span>
<span class="c"># └── files/</span>
<span class="c"># │   └── nslcd.conf</span>
<span class="c"># └── nss-pam-ldapd_%.bbappend</span>

<span class="nb">cat</span> <span class="o">></span> nss-pam-ldapd_%.bbappend <span class="o"><<</span> <span class="sh">'</span><span class="no">EOF</span><span class="sh">'
FILESEXTRAPATHS:prepend := "</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">THISDIR</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/files:"
SRC_URI += "file://nslcd.conf"

do_install:append() {
    install -m 0600 </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">WORKDIR</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/nslcd.conf </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">D</span><span class="k">}${</span><span class="nv">sysconfdir</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/
}
</span><span class="no">EOF
</span>
```

</div></div>

### Runtime Configuration

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check user manager service</span>
systemctl status phosphor-user-manager

<span class="c"># View logs</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> phosphor-user-manager <span class="nt">-f</span>

<span class="c"># User configuration files</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /etc/passwd
<span class="nb">cat</span> /etc/group

<span class="c"># Verify PAM config</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /etc/pam.d/common-auth

<span class="c"># Verify LDAP client config</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /etc/nslcd.conf
```

</div></div>
---

## Local User Management

    

### Default Users

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Username | Default Password | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| root | 0penBmc | Administrator |

</div>

### Create User via Redfish

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Create new user</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> POST <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{
        "UserName": "operator1",
        "Password": "SecurePass123!",
        "RoleId": "Operator",
        "Enabled": true
    }'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService/Accounts
```

</div></div>

### Create User via D-Bus

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Create user</span>
busctl call xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/user <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager <span class="se">\</span>
    CreateUser ssasbs <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"newuser"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    3 <span class="s2">"ipmi"</span> <span class="s2">"redfish"</span> <span class="s2">"ssh"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"priv-admin"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nb">true</span>
```

</div></div>

### Modify User

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Change password via Redfish</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{"Password": "NewPassword123!"}'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService/Accounts/operator1

<span class="c"># Change role</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{"RoleId": "Administrator"}'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService/Accounts/operator1

<span class="c"># Enable/disable user</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{"Enabled": false}'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService/Accounts/operator1
```

</div></div>

### Delete User

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Via Redfish</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> DELETE <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService/Accounts/operator1

<span class="c"># Via IPMI</span>
ipmitool <span class="nt">-I</span> lanplus <span class="nt">-H</span> bmc-ip <span class="nt">-U</span> root <span class="nt">-P</span> 0penBmc user <span class="nb">set </span>name 3 <span class="s2">""</span>
```

</div></div>
---

## Privilege Roles

    

### Available Roles

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Role | Redfish | IPMI Priv | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Administrator | Administrator | 4 (admin) | Full access |
| Operator | Operator | 3 (operator) | Operations, no user mgmt |
| ReadOnly | ReadOnly | 2 (user) | Read-only access |
| Callback | Callback | 1 | Limited callback access |

</div>

### Role Permissions

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># View available roles</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService/Roles

<span class="c"># Get role details</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService/Roles/Operator
```

</div></div>

### D-Bus Privilege Mapping

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># View user privileges</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/user/newuser <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.User.Attributes <span class="se">\</span>
    UserPrivilege
```

</div></div>
---

## IPMI User Management

    

### Configure IPMI Users

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># List users</span>
ipmitool user list

<span class="c"># Create user</span>
ipmitool user <span class="nb">set </span>name 3 operator1
ipmitool user <span class="nb">set </span>password 3 Password123!
ipmitool user priv 3 3 1  <span class="c"># operator privilege, channel 1</span>
ipmitool user <span class="nb">enable </span>3

<span class="c"># Disable user</span>
ipmitool user disable 3

<span class="c"># Delete user</span>
ipmitool user <span class="nb">set </span>name 3 <span class="s2">""</span>
```

</div></div>

### IPMI User Privileges

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Level | Name | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Callback | Minimal access |
| 2 | User | Read sensors, view logs |
| 3 | Operator | Power control, sensor config |
| 4 | Administrator | Full access |
| 5 | OEM | Vendor-specific |

</div>

## LDAP Configuration

    

### Enable LDAP Authentication

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Configure LDAP via Redfish</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{
        "LDAP": {

            "ServiceAddresses": ["ldap://ldap.example.com"],
            "Authentication": {
```

## Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)

    

Beyond passwords, LDAP, and Active Directory, **phosphor-user-manager** supports
**multi-factor authentication (MFA)** using **TOTP** (Time-based One-Time
Password), which is compatible with Google Authenticator and equivalent
authenticator apps. When MFA is enabled for a user, login requires both the
account password and a current one-time passcode (OTP).

### How TOTP Enrollment Works

    

1. **Secret generation** — enabling TOTP for a user runs the
`google-authenticator` utility to produce a per-user secret. OpenBMC invokes it
non-interactively in time-based mode
(`google-authenticator -s  -u -W -Q NONE -t -f -d -C`), so no QR code or
interactive prompt is generated.
2. **Provisional secret** — the new secret is first written to a temporary file
(a `.google_authenticator.tmp` under the user’s home) and is **not yet active**.
3. **Verification makes it permanent** — the user must submit one valid OTP. Only
after that OTP verifies successfully is the secret promoted (renamed) to its
live location, `~/.google_authenticator`. A failed verification — or disabling
MFA — removes the temporary secret, so a half-finished enrollment never locks
the account.

### OTP Verification

    

One-time passcodes are checked through a **dedicated PAM service**, `mfa_pam`
(installed to `/etc/pam.d/mfa_pam`). The internal `Totp::verify(username, token)`
helper opens a PAM conversation against that service, answers its
`Verification code:` prompt with the supplied token, and reports success only when
PAM accepts the code. Isolating OTP checks in their own PAM stack lets MFA layer
on top of the existing `common-auth` password flow without modifying it.

### MFA State and D-Bus

    

MFA configuration lives on the `xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager` service, exposed
through the `xyz.openbmc_project.User.MultiFactorAuthConfiguration` interface —
whose `Enabled` property selects the active MFA type (for example
`GoogleAuthenticator` or `None`) — and is mirrored to the Redfish `AccountService`.
The selected MFA type and related state are **persisted as JSON** (via the
manager’s `JsonSerializer`), so the setting survives a BMC reboot.

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Inspect the user manager object and its MFA-related interfaces</span>
busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/user
```

</div></div>

### Per-User Bypass

    

For temporary exceptions — a break-glass account, or a user who has lost their
authenticator — phosphor-user-manager supports a per-user **bypass protocol**.
Bypassing a protocol (such as `GoogleAuthenticator`) exempts that user from the
corresponding factor and clears their stored secret. The bypass selection is
itself persisted as JSON, so it too survives a reboot.

> **MFA secrets are sensitive.** A user’s `~/.google_authenticator` secret is the
> shared key for their second factor. It is stored with restricted permissions
> under the user’s home directory and must never be logged, exported, or copied
> off the BMC — treat it with the same care as a private key or password hash.

## Deep Dive

    

Advanced implementation details for user management developers.

### PAM Integration

    

OpenBMC uses PAM (Pluggable Authentication Modules) for authentication:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    PAM Authentication Flow                              │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   Login Request (Redfish/IPMI/SSH)                                      │
│          │                                                              │
│          ▼                                                              │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │                    PAM Stack                                    │   │
│   │   /etc/pam.d/common-auth                                        │   │
│   └────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                │                                        │
│          ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐                  │
│          │                     │                     │                  │
│          ▼                     ▼                     ▼                  │
│   ┌────────────┐        ┌────────────┐        ┌────────────┐            │
│   │ pam_unix   │        │ pam_ldap   │        │ pam_radius │            │
│   │ (local)    │        │ (LDAP/AD)  │        │ (RADIUS)   │            │
│   └─────┬──────┘        └─────┬──────┘        └─────┬──────┘            │
│         │                     │                     │                   │
│         ▼                     ▼                     ▼                   │
│   /etc/shadow           LDAP Server           RADIUS Server             │
│                                                                         │
│   PAM Configuration (/etc/pam.d/common-auth):                           │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ auth sufficient pam_unix.so nullok try_first_pass               │   │
│   │ auth sufficient pam_ldap.so use_first_pass                      │   │
│   │ auth required   pam_deny.so                                     │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

**PAM module flow:**

* `sufficient`: If module succeeds, skip remaining; if fails, continue
* `required`: Must pass, but continue checking other modules
* `requisite`: Must pass, fail immediately if not

### LDAP Authentication Flow

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    LDAP Authentication Sequence                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   BMC (phosphor-user-manager)              LDAP Server                  │
│          │                                      │                       │
│          │  1. Bind (service account)           │                       │
│          │─────────────────────────────────────▶│                       │
│          │◀─────────────────────────────────────│ Bind success          │
│          │                                      │                       │
│          │  2. Search (find user DN)            │                       │
│          │  filter: (uid=username)              │                       │
│          │─────────────────────────────────────▶│                       │
│          │◀─────────────────────────────────────│ User DN returned      │
│          │                                      │                       │
│          │  3. Bind (user DN + password)        │                       │
│          │─────────────────────────────────────▶│                       │
│          │◀─────────────────────────────────────│ Auth success/fail     │
│          │                                      │                       │
│          │  4. Search (get group membership)    │                       │
│          │  filter: (member=userDN)             │                       │
│          │─────────────────────────────────────▶│                       │
│          │◀─────────────────────────────────────│ Group list            │
│          │                                      │                       │
│                                                                         │
│   Group to Privilege Mapping:                                           │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ LDAP Group          │ OpenBMC Role      │ IPMI Privilege        │   │
│   ├─────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────────┤   │
│   │ cn=bmc-admins       │ Administrator     │ 4 (Administrator)     │   │
│   │ cn=bmc-operators    │ Operator          │ 3 (Operator)          │   │
│   │ cn=bmc-users        │ User              │ 2 (User)              │   │
│   │ cn=bmc-readonly     │ ReadOnly          │ 1 (Callback)          │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### Password Hashing

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Password Storage                                     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   /etc/shadow format:                                                   │
│   username:$6$salt$hash:lastchange:min:max:warn:inactive:expire:        │
│                                                                         │
│   Hash Types:                                                           │
│   ├── $1$ = MD5 (deprecated, insecure)                                  │
│   ├── $5$ = SHA-256                                                     │
│   └── $6$ = SHA-512 (default, recommended)                              │
│                                                                         │
│   Password Change Flow:                                                 │
│   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│   │ 1. Redfish PATCH /AccountService/Accounts/{id}                   │  │
│   │    { "Password": "newPassword" }                                 │  │
│   │                                                                  │  │
│   │ 2. bmcweb calls D-Bus:                                           │  │
│   │    xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager.RenameUser() or              │  │
│   │    org.freedesktop.Accounts.User.SetPassword()                   │  │
│   │                                                                  │  │
│   │ 3. phosphor-user-manager:                                        │  │
│   │    - Validates password policy (length, complexity)              │  │
│   │    - Calls pam_chauthtok() to update /etc/shadow                 │  │
│   │    - Emits PropertiesChanged signal                              │  │
│   └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### D-Bus Permission Enforcement

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    D-Bus Access Control                                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   /etc/dbus-1/system.d/ policy files control D-Bus access:              │
│                                                                         │
│   Example: phosphor-user-manager.conf                                   │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ 
│   │
│   │                  │   │
│   │     │   │
│   │                                                        │   │
│   │                                                                 │   │
│   │                                       │   │
│   │        │   │
│   │                                        │   │
│   │                                                        │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
│   Privilege Enforcement in bmcweb:                                      │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ // Route with privilege requirement                             │   │
│   │ BMCWEB_ROUTE(app, "/redfish/v1/AccountService/Accounts//") │   │
│   │     .privileges(redfish::privileges::patchAccount)              │   │
│   │     .methods(boost::beast::http::verb::patch)(handlePatch);     │   │
│   │                                                                 │   │
│   │ // privileges::patchAccount requires ConfigureUsers             │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Overview

    

**phosphor-networkd** manages BMC network configuration, providing D-Bus interfaces for IP configuration, VLAN, DNS, and network settings.

```mermaid
---
title: Network Architecture
---
flowchart TB
    subgraph apis["Configuration APIs"]
        direction LR
        redfish["Redfish**API"]
        ipmi["IPMI  
Network"]
        dbus["D-Bus  
busctl"]
        webui["WebUI  
Config"]
    end

    subgraph networkd["phosphor-networkd"]
        direction LR
        iface["Interface Mgmt  
eth0, eth1"]
        ipvlan["IP/VLAN Config  
static, dhcp"]
        dns["DNS/DHCP  
Hostname"]
    end

    systemd["systemd-networkd  
(.network files)"]

    apis --> networkd --> systemd
```

## Setup & Configuration

    

### Build-Time Configuration (Yocto)

    

```bitbake
# In your machine .conf or local.conf

# Include network management
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " \
    phosphor-network \
"

# Configure Meson options
EXTRA_OEMESON:pn-phosphor-network = " \
    -Ddefault-link-local-autoconf=true \
    -Ddefault-ipv6-accept-ra=true \
"
```

### Meson Build Options

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default-link-local-autoconf` | true | Enable link-local IPv4 |
| `default-ipv6-accept-ra` | true | Accept IPv6 router advertisements |
| `sync-mac` | true | Sync MAC with hardware |
| `persist-mac` | false | Persist MAC across reboots |

</div>

### Configuration Files

    

phosphor-networkd translates D-Bus settings to systemd-networkd `.network` files.
Runtime configuration is persisted automatically. To bake default settings into
the image, deploy `.network` files via Yocto.

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Config File | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Network config | `/etc/systemd/network/00-bmc-eth0.network` | Main BMC interface (DHCP or static) |
| VLAN netdev | `/etc/systemd/network/00-bmc-eth0.100.netdev` | VLAN device definition |
| VLAN config | `/etc/systemd/network/10-bmc-eth0.100.network` | VLAN interface config |
| Resolved config | `/etc/systemd/resolved.conf` | DNS resolver settings |

</div>

### Deploying Default Network Configuration via Yocto

    

To bake a default static IP or DHCP configuration into the image:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># meta-myplatform/recipes-phosphor/network/phosphor-network/</span>
<span class="c"># └── files/</span>
<span class="c"># │   └── 00-bmc-eth0.network</span>
<span class="c"># └── phosphor-network_%.bbappend</span>

<span class="nb">cat</span> <span class="o">></span> phosphor-network_%.bbappend <span class="o"><<</span> <span class="sh">'</span><span class="no">EOF</span><span class="sh">'
FILESEXTRAPATHS:prepend := "</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">THISDIR</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/files:"
SRC_URI += "file://00-bmc-eth0.network"

do_install:append() {
    install -d </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">D</span><span class="k">}${</span><span class="nv">sysconfdir</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/systemd/network
    install -m 0644 </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">WORKDIR</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/00-bmc-eth0.network </span><span class="se">\</span><span class="sh">
        </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">D</span><span class="k">}${</span><span class="nv">sysconfdir</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/systemd/network/
}
</span><span class="no">EOF
</span>
```

</div></div>

Example `00-bmc-eth0.network` for DHCP:

<div class="language-ini highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="nn">[Match]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Name</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">eth0</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="nn">[Network]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">DHCP</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">ipv4</span>
<span class="py">LinkLocalAddressing</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">yes</span>
<span class="py">IPv6AcceptRA</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">true</span>
```

</div></div>

Example for static IP:

<div class="language-ini highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="nn">[Match]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Name</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">eth0</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="nn">[Network]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Address</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">192.168.1.100/24</span>
<span class="py">Gateway</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">192.168.1.1</span>
<span class="py">DNS</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">8.8.8.8</span>
<span class="py">DNS</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">8.8.4.4</span>
<span class="py">LinkLocalAddressing</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">no</span>
```

</div></div>

Runtime changes via Redfish or D-Bus will overwrite these files. The Yocto-deployed
file serves as the factory default. After a factory reset (`/usr/share/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/scripts/factory-reset.sh`),
the image-baked config is restored.

### Runtime Configuration

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check network service</span>
systemctl status systemd-networkd
systemctl status phosphor-network

<span class="c"># View network configuration files</span>
<span class="nb">ls</span> /etc/systemd/network/

<span class="c"># View current network state</span>
networkctl status

<span class="c"># View active config for eth0</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /etc/systemd/network/00-bmc-eth0.network
```

</div></div>

## IP Address Configuration

    

### View Current Configuration

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Via D-Bus</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.Network

<span class="c"># Get interface info</span>
busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.Network <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/network/eth0

<span class="c"># Via ip command</span>
ip addr show eth0
```

</div></div>

### Via Redfish

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get ethernet interfaces</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/EthernetInterfaces

<span class="c"># Get specific interface</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/EthernetInterfaces/eth0
```

</div></div>

### Configure Static IP

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Via Redfish</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{
        "IPv4Addresses": [
            {
                "Address": "192.168.1.100",
                "SubnetMask": "255.255.255.0",
                "Gateway": "192.168.1.1",
                "AddressOrigin": "Static"
            }
        ]
    }'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/EthernetInterfaces/eth0

<span class="c"># Via D-Bus</span>
busctl call xyz.openbmc_project.Network <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/network/eth0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Network.IP.Create <span class="se">\</span>
    IP ssys <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.Network.IP.Protocol.IPv4"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"192.168.1.100"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    24 <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"192.168.1.1"</span>
```

</div></div>

### Configure DHCP

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Enable DHCP via Redfish</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{"DHCPv4": {"DHCPEnabled": true}}'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/EthernetInterfaces/eth0

<span class="c"># Via D-Bus</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Network <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/network/eth0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Network.EthernetInterface <span class="se">\</span>
    DHCPEnabled s <span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.Network.EthernetInterface.DHCPConf.v4"</span>
```

</div></div>

### Delete IP Address

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get IP address object path</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.Network | <span class="nb">grep </span>ipv4

<span class="c"># Delete via D-Bus</span>
busctl call xyz.openbmc_project.Network <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/network/eth0/ipv4/abc123 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Object.Delete <span class="se">\</span>
    Delete
```

</div></div>

**Static neighbors and static gateways** follow the same child-object pattern as
IP addresses. A static ARP/NDP neighbor entry (`neighbor.cpp`) and a static
default gateway (`static_gateway.cpp`) each appear as their own D-Bus object
beneath `/xyz/openbmc_project/network/eth0`, and each exposes
`xyz.openbmc_project.Object.Delete`. Remove one exactly like an IP address: use
`busctl tree` to find its object path, then call `Delete` on it.

### Enable IPv6

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Configure IPv6 static address</span>

```

## VLAN Configuration

    

### Create VLAN

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Via Redfish</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> POST <span class="se">\</span>

<span class="c"># Via D-Bus</span>

    /xyz/openbmc_project/network <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Network.VLAN.Create <span class="se">\</span>

```

</div></div>

```
        "IPv4Addresses": [
            {
                "Address": "10.0.100.10",

                "AddressOrigin": "Static"
```

## Hostname Configuration

    

### Set Hostname

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Via Redfish</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{"HostName": "my-bmc"}'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/NetworkProtocol

<span class="c"># Via D-Bus</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Network <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/network/config <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Network.SystemConfiguration <span class="se">\</span>
    HostName s <span class="s2">"my-bmc"</span>
```

</div></div>

### Set Domain Name

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Network <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/network/config <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Network.SystemConfiguration <span class="se">\</span>
    DefaultGateway s <span class="s2">"192.168.1.1"</span>
```

</div></div>

**First-boot unique hostname.** On first boot the hostname manager
(`hostname_manager.cpp`) derives a unique suffix from the BMC serial number —
read from the inventory `xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item.Bmc` /
`Decorator.Asset` `SerialNumber` property — and falls back to the MAC address
when no serial is available. It applies the result once as `-`
via `org.freedesktop.hostname1` `SetStaticHostname`, then writes a marker file so
later boots leave any user-set hostname untouched.

---

## MAC Address Configuration

    

### View MAC Address

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Via ip command</span>
ip <span class="nb">link </span>show eth0

<span class="c"># Via D-Bus</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.Network <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/network/eth0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Network.MACAddress <span class="se">\</span>
    MACAddress
```

</div></div>

### Set MAC Address

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Via Redfish</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{"MACAddress": "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF"}'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/EthernetInterfaces/eth0
```

</div></div>

**Inventory-assigned MAC.** Where a platform stores a MAC address in inventory,
`inventory_mac.cpp` copies it onto the matching interface on first boot. It reads
the `MACAddress` property from
`xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item.NetworkInterface`, maps inventory paths to
interfaces via `/usr/share/network/config.json`, and records completion with a
`/var/lib/network/firstBoot_` marker so the assignment runs only once.

---

## NCSI Management

    

Network Controller Sideband Interface (NC-SI) lets the BMC share a network
controller with the host over a sideband channel (RBT, or increasingly MCTP).
phosphor-networkd ships two command-line helpers for talking to NC-SI-capable
NICs:

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Tool | Backend | Typical use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ncsi-netlink` | Netlink only | Package/channel selection through the kernel NC-SI driver |
| `ncsi-cmd` | Netlink **or** MCTP | Discovery, raw/OEM commands, and firmware dumps |

</div>

### Discover Packages and Channels

    

`ncsi-cmd discover` walks every package (0-7) and channel (0-31), issuing
*Clear Initial State* and *Get Capabilities* to enumerate what the NIC exposes:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Discover over the kernel netlink backend (NIC selected by interface)</span>
ncsi-cmd <span class="nt">-i</span> eth0 discover

<span class="c"># Discover over MCTP (endpoint ID 10 on the default network)</span>
ncsi-cmd <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 discover
```

</div></div>

### Common Options

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-p, --package ` | Target package index (required for non-discovery commands) |
| `-c, --channel ` | Target channel index |
| `-i, --interface ` | Select the NIC by network interface (netlink backend) |
| `-m, --mctp [NET,]` | Select the NIC by MCTP endpoint (MCTP backend) |
| `-v, --verbose` | Verbose output |

</div>

Every subcommand except `discover` needs a `--package`/`-p` value plus exactly
one interface type — `-i` (netlink) **or** `-m` (MCTP), never both.

### Send Raw, OEM, and Dump Commands

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># raw <type> [hex payload...] — send an arbitrary NC-SI command</span>
ncsi-cmd <span class="nt">-p</span> 0 <span class="nt">-c</span> 0 <span class="nt">-i</span> eth0 raw 0x15

<span class="c"># oem [hex payload...] — send an OEM command (NC-SI type 0x50)</span>
ncsi-cmd <span class="nt">-p</span> 0 <span class="nt">-c</span> 0 <span class="nt">-i</span> eth0 oem 0x00 0x00 0x00

<span class="c"># Capture NC-SI core/crash dumps to a file</span>
ncsi-cmd <span class="nt">-p</span> 0 <span class="nt">-i</span> eth0 core-dump /tmp/ncsi-core.bin
ncsi-cmd <span class="nt">-p</span> 0 <span class="nt">-i</span> eth0 crash-dump /tmp/ncsi-crash.bin
```

</div></div>

The netlink backend drives the in-kernel NC-SI driver, so `-i` takes a normal
interface. The MCTP backend instead talks to the NIC as an MCTP endpoint (`-m`),
reusing the MCTP stack rather than the network driver. `ncsi-netlink` is the
older, netlink-only helper (for example `ncsi-netlink -x 3 -p 0 -i`); `ncsi-cmd`
supersedes it and adds the MCTP path.

## IPMI LAN Configuration

    

### View LAN Configuration

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
ipmitool lan print
```

</div></div>

### Configure LAN Channel

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Set static IP</span>
ipmitool lan <span class="nb">set </span>1 ipsrc static
ipmitool lan <span class="nb">set </span>1 ipaddr 192.168.1.100
ipmitool lan <span class="nb">set </span>1 netmask 255.255.255.0
ipmitool lan <span class="nb">set </span>1 defgw ipaddr 192.168.1.1

<span class="c"># Enable DHCP</span>
ipmitool lan <span class="nb">set </span>1 ipsrc dhcp
```

</div></div>
---

## Hypervisor Network Synchronization

    

This feature is **IBM / PowerVM-specific**. It lives under
`src/ibm/hypervisor-network-mgr-src/` in phosphor-networkd and is built only for
IBM Power systems, where the BMC stages network settings on behalf of the
PowerVM hypervisor (its “virtual management interface”, VMI). It is not present
on typical x86 or generic ARM platforms.

On IBM Power systems a second daemon, **HypNetworkMgr**, publishes the D-Bus
service `xyz.openbmc_project.Network.Hypervisor`. It mirrors the familiar network
object model for the hypervisor’s own interfaces so management tooling can
pre-stage the hypervisor’s IP configuration before the host boots:

<div class="table-wrapper">
| D-Bus object | Interface class | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hypervisor ethernet interface (`eth0`, `eth1`) | `HypEthInterface` | Per-interface container for staged hypervisor IP addresses |
| Hypervisor IP address | `HypIPAddress` | A single staged IPv4 address / gateway / prefix |
| Hypervisor system config | `HypSysConfig` | Hostname and other system-wide settings |

</div>

### Backed by BIOS Attributes

    

Instead of writing `systemd-networkd` files, HypNetworkMgr persists every value
as a **BIOS attribute** through `xyz.openbmc_project.BIOSConfigManager`
(interface `xyz.openbmc_project.BIOSConfig.Manager`). The attributes use a
`vmi_`-prefixed naming scheme, for example:

<div class="table-wrapper">
| BIOS attribute | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `vmi__ipv4_ipaddr` | Staged IPv4 address |
| `vmi__ipv4_gateway` | Staged default gateway |
| `vmi__ipv4_prefix_length` | Prefix length |
| `vmi__ipv4_method` | Addressing method (e.g. `IPv4Static`) |
| `vmi_hostname` | Hypervisor hostname |

</div>

The hypervisor reads these attributes as it initializes, so the BMC and
hypervisor stay in sync without a running host.

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># List the hypervisor network objects (interfaces, staged IPs, system config)</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.Network.Hypervisor

<span class="c"># Introspect one of the objects listed above</span>
busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.Network.Hypervisor <object-path>
```

</div></div>

`HypIPAddress` properties (address, gateway, prefix length, origin, type) are
**immutable after the object is created** — every setter rejects updates with a
`NotAllowed` error (“Property update is not allowed”). To change a staged
address, delete the object via `xyz.openbmc_project.Object.Delete` and create a
new one rather than patching it in place.

## Troubleshooting

    

### No Network Connectivity

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check interface status</span>
ip <span class="nb">link </span>show eth0
networkctl status eth0

<span class="c"># Check for IP address</span>
ip addr show eth0

<span class="c"># Check routing table</span>
ip route

<span class="c"># Ping gateway</span>
ping <span class="nt">-c</span> 3 192.168.1.1
```

</div></div>

### DHCP Not Working

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check DHCP client</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> systemd-networkd | <span class="nb">grep </span>DHCP

<span class="c"># Force DHCP renewal</span>
networkctl renew eth0
```

</div></div>

### DNS Resolution Issues

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check DNS configuration</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /etc/resolv.conf

<span class="c"># Test DNS resolution</span>
nslookup example.com
```

</div></div>

### Configuration Not Persisting

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check network configuration files</span>
<span class="nb">ls</span> <span class="nt">-la</span> /etc/systemd/network/

<span class="c"># Verify phosphor-network service</span>
systemctl status phosphor-network

<span class="c"># Check for errors</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> phosphor-network
```

</div></div>

## Configuration Persistence

    

Network configuration is stored in:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># systemd-networkd files</span>
/etc/systemd/network/00-bmc-eth0.network

<span class="c"># Example content:</span>
<span class="o">[</span>Match]
<span class="nv">Name</span><span class="o">=</span>eth0

<span class="o">[</span>Network]
<span class="nv">Address</span><span class="o">=</span>192.168.1.100/24
<span class="nv">Gateway</span><span class="o">=</span>192.168.1.1
<span class="nv">DNS</span><span class="o">=</span>8.8.8.8
```

</div></div>

## Deep Dive

    

Advanced implementation details for network configuration developers.

### systemd-networkd Integration

    

phosphor-networkd translates D-Bus calls to systemd-networkd configuration:

```mermaid
---
title: Network Configuration Flow
---
flowchart TB
    request["Redfish/D-Bus Request"]

    networkd["phosphor-networkd  
xyz.openbmc_project.Network"]

    config["<b>/etc/systemd/network/*.network****[Match] Name=eth0  
[Network]  
Address=192.168.1.100/24  
Gateway=192.168.1.1  
DNS=8.8.8.8  
DHCP=no"]

    systemd["systemd-networkd  
Applies configuration to kernel network stack"]

    files["<b>File Naming Convention:**  
/etc/systemd/network/  
├── 00-bmc-eth0.network (Static/DHCP)  
├── 00-bmc-eth0.netdev (VLAN defs)  
└── 10-bmc-eth0.1.network (VLAN config)"]

    request --> networkd --> config --> systemd
    config -.- files
```

> **ASCII-art version (for comparison)**

  <div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Network Configuration Flow                           │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   Redfish/D-Bus Request                                                 │
│          │                                                              │
│          ▼                                                              │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │                    phosphor-networkd                            │   │
│   │   xyz.openbmc_project.Network                                   │   │
│   └────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                │                                        │
│                                ▼                                        │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │               /etc/systemd/network/*.network                    │   │
│   │                                                                 │   │
│   │   [Match]                                                       │   │
│   │   Name=eth0                                                     │   │
│   │                                                                 │   │
│   │   [Network]                                                     │   │
│   │   Address=192.168.1.100/24                                      │   │
│   │   Gateway=192.168.1.1                                           │   │
│   │   DNS=8.8.8.8                                                   │   │
│   │   DHCP=no                                                       │   │
│   └────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                │                                        │
│                                ▼                                        │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │                    systemd-networkd                             │   │
│   │   Applies configuration to kernel network stack                 │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
│   File Naming Convention:                                               │
│   /etc/systemd/network/                                                 │
│   ├── 00-bmc-eth0.network      ← Static/DHCP config                     │
│   ├── 00-bmc-eth0.netdev       ← VLAN definitions                       │
│   └── 10-bmc-eth0.1.network    ← VLAN interface config                  │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div>  </div>

### DHCP Transaction Flow

    

```mermaid
---
title: DHCP Client Operation
---
sequenceDiagram
    participant BMC as BMC (systemd-networkd)
    participant Server as DHCP Server

    BMC->>Server: 1. DHCPDISCOVER (broadcast)
    Server->>BMC: 2. DHCPOFFER (IP, Mask, Gateway, DNS)
    BMC->>Server: 3. DHCPREQUEST (Requesting offered IP)
    Server->>BMC: 4. DHCPACK (Lease confirmed)

    Note over BMC: Lease stored in:  
/run/systemd/netif/leases/
    Note over BMC: D-Bus Properties Updated:  
- Network.IP (Address, Gateway)  
- DHCPEnabled=true
```

**DHCP Options Handled:**

* Option 1: Subnet Mask
* Option 3: Router (Gateway)
* Option 6: DNS Servers
* Option 12: Hostname
* Option 15: Domain Name
* Option 42: NTP Servers

> **ASCII-art version (for comparison)**

  <div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    DHCP Client Operation                                │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   BMC (systemd-networkd)              DHCP Server                       │
│          │                                  │                           │
│          │  1. DHCPDISCOVER (broadcast)     │                           │
│          │─────────────────────────────────▶│                           │
│          │                                  │                           │
│          │  2. DHCPOFFER                    │                           │
│          │◀─────────────────────────────────│ IP, Mask, Gateway, DNS    │
│          │                                  │                           │
│          │  3. DHCPREQUEST                  │                           │
│          │─────────────────────────────────▶│ Requesting offered IP     │
│          │                                  │                           │
│          │  4. DHCPACK                      │                           │
│          │◀─────────────────────────────────│ Lease confirmed           │
│          │                                  │                           │
│                                                                         │
│   Lease stored in: /run/systemd/netif/leases/                           │
│                                                                         │
│   D-Bus Properties Updated:                                             │
│   ├── xyz.openbmc_project.Network.IP                                    │
│   │   └── Address, PrefixLength, Gateway, Origin=DHCP                   │
│   └── xyz.openbmc_project.Network.EthernetInterface                     │
│       └── DHCPEnabled=true                                              │
│                                                                         │
│   DHCP Options Handled:                                                 │
│   ├── Option 1: Subnet Mask                                             │
│   ├── Option 3: Router (Gateway)                                        │
│   ├── Option 6: DNS Servers                                             │
│   ├── Option 12: Hostname                                               │
│   ├── Option 15: Domain Name                                            │
│   └── Option 42: NTP Servers                                            │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div>  </div>

**VLAN .netdev file** (`/etc/systemd/network/00-eth0.100.netdev`):

<div class="language-ini highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="nn">[NetDev]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Name</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">eth0.100</span>
<span class="py">Kind</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">vlan</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="nn">[VLAN]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">Id</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">100</span>
```

</div></div>

**D-Bus VLAN Creation:**

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
busctl call xyz.openbmc_project.Network <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/network/eth0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Network.VLAN.Create <span class="se">\</span>
    VLAN sq <span class="s2">"eth0.100"</span> 100
```

### Link State Monitoring

    

```mermaid
---
title: Link State Detection
---
flowchart TB
    netlink["Kernel Netlink Events"]
    networkd["phosphor-networkd  
Subscribes to RTM_NEWLINK / RTM_DELLINK"]

    linkup["Link Up  
Set D-Bus LinkUp=true"]
    linkdown["Link Down  
Set D-Bus LinkUp=false"]
    speedchange["Link Speed Change  
Update Speed prop"]

    netlink --> networkd
    networkd --> linkup
    networkd --> linkdown
    networkd --> speedchange
```

**D-Bus Properties** (`/xyz/openbmc_project/network/eth0`):

* `LinkUp` (bool) - Physical link state
* `Speed` (uint32) - Link speed in Mbps
* `AutoNeg` (bool) - Auto-negotiation enabled
* `MTU` (uint32) - Maximum transmission unit

**Redfish Mapping:**

* `LinkUp` → `LinkStatus` (“LinkUp” / “LinkDown”)
* `Speed` → `SpeedMbps`
* `AutoNeg` → `AutoNeg`

> **ASCII-art version (for comparison)**

  <div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Link State Detection                                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   Kernel Netlink Events                                                 │
│          │                                                              │
│          ▼                                                              │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │                    phosphor-networkd                            │   │
│   │   Subscribes to RTM_NEWLINK / RTM_DELLINK                       │   │
│   └────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                │                                        │
│          ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐                  │
│          │                     │                     │                  │
│          ▼                     ▼                     ▼                  │
│   Link Up              Link Down             Link Speed Change          │
│   ┌────────────┐       ┌────────────┐       ┌────────────┐              │
│   │ Set D-Bus  │       │ Set D-Bus  │       │ Update     │              │
│   │ LinkUp=true│       │ LinkUp=    │       │ Speed prop │              │
│   │            │       │    false   │       │            │              │
│   └────────────┘       └────────────┘       └────────────┘              │
│                                                                         │
│   D-Bus Properties:                                                     │
│   /xyz/openbmc_project/network/eth0                                     │
│   ├── LinkUp (bool) - Physical link state                               │
│   ├── Speed (uint32) - Link speed in Mbps                               │
│   ├── AutoNeg (bool) - Auto-negotiation enabled                         │
│   └── MTU (uint32) - Maximum transmission unit                          │
│                                                                         │
│   Redfish Mapping:                                                      │
│   ├── LinkUp → LinkStatus ("LinkUp" / "LinkDown")                       │
│   ├── Speed → SpeedMbps                                                 │
│   └── AutoNeg → AutoNeg                                                 │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Overview

    

**phosphor-led-manager** provides LED control and group management, supporting identify, fault, and status LEDs through D-Bus interfaces.

```mermaid
---
title: LED Architecture
---
flowchart TB
    subgraph access["Access Methods"]
        direction TB
        redfish["Redfish  
Indicator"]
        ipmi["IPMI  
Identify"]
        dbus["D-Bus  
busctl"]
        button["Physical  
Button"]
    end

    subgraph manager["phosphor-led-manager"]
        direction TB
        groups["LED Groups  
(logical)"]
        actions["LED Actions  
(on/off/blink)"]
        lamptest["Lamp Test  
(all LEDs)"]
    end

    subgraph sysfs["phosphor-led-sysfs"]
        interface["Linux LED sysfs interface"]
    end

    subgraph physical["Physical LEDs"]
        leds["/sys/class/leds/*  
(power, identify, fault, etc.)"]
    end

    access --> manager
    manager --> sysfs
    sysfs --> physical
```
