## Porting Guide

    

Follow these steps to bring up PSU monitoring on a new platform.

### Step 1: Identify PSU Hardware

    

Determine the following from your platform schematic:

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Parameter | Example | How to find |
| --- | --- | --- |
| I2C bus number | 3 | Schematic, trace from BMC I2C controller to PSU connector |
| PSU I2C address | 0x58 | PSU datasheet or `i2cdetect -y ` |
| Number of PSUs | 2 | Platform design (N+1 redundancy) |
| PMBus commands supported | See datasheet | PSU vendor documentation |
| Vendor-specific driver | `"delta,dps800"` | Kernel driver list or `"pmbus"` for generic |

</div>

### Step 2: Add Device Tree Entries

    

```dts
// In your platform device tree (aspeed-bmc-myplatform.dts)
&i2c3 {
    status = "okay";

    psu0: psu@58 {
        compatible = "pmbus";
        reg = <0x58>;
    };

    psu1: psu@59 {
        compatible = "pmbus";
        reg = <0x59>;
    };
};
```

### Step 3: Verify Kernel Binding

    

After booting with the updated device tree:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Confirm devices appear on the bus</span>
i2cdetect <span class="nt">-y</span> 3

<span class="c"># Verify driver bound</span>
<span class="nb">ls</span> /sys/bus/i2c/devices/3-0058/driver

<span class="c"># List hwmon attributes to determine which Labels to use</span>
<span class="nb">ls</span> /sys/bus/i2c/devices/3-0058/hwmon/hwmon<span class="k">*</span>/
<span class="c"># in1_input  in2_input  curr1_input  curr2_input</span>
<span class="c"># power1_input  power2_input  temp1_input  fan1_input</span>
```

</div></div>

### Step 4: Create Entity Manager JSON

    

Map each hwmon attribute to a Label in your JSON configuration. Only include labels that exist in sysfs.

### Step 5: Add Yocto bbappend Files

    

Install your Entity Manager JSON and, if applicable, your phosphor-regulators config through bbappend files as shown in the Configuration section.

### Step 6: Verify End-to-End

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check Entity Manager detected the PSU</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.EntityManager | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> psu

<span class="c"># Verify PSU sensors on D-Bus</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.PSUSensor

<span class="c"># Read a sensor value</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.PSUSensor <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/voltage/PSU0_Input_Voltage <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value Value

<span class="c"># Check via Redfish</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost:2443/redfish/v1/Chassis/chassis/Power
```

</div></div>
---

## Code Examples

    

Working examples are available in the [examples/psu-pmbus](https://github.com/MichaelTien8901/openbmc-guide-tutorial/tree/main/docs/examples/psu-pmbus) directory:

* `psu-entity-manager.json` – Entity Manager configuration for a dual-PSU platform
* `regulators-config.json` – phosphor-regulators configuration with VRM rules
* `psu-status-check.sh` – Shell script to read PMBus STATUS_WORD and decode fault bits

### Reading PSU Sensors from D-Bus

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c">#!/bin/bash</span>
<span class="c"># Read all PSU sensors and display a summary</span>

<span class="nv">PSU_SERVICE</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.PSUSensor"</span>
<span class="nv">SENSOR_BASE</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"/xyz/openbmc_project/sensors"</span>

<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"=== PSU Sensor Readings ==="</span>

<span class="k">for </span><span class="nb">type </span><span class="k">in </span>voltage current power temperature<span class="p">;</span> <span class="k">do
    </span><span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">""</span>
    <span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"--- </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">type</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2"> ---"</span>
    busctl tree <span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">PSU_SERVICE</span><span class="k">}</span> 2>/dev/null <span class="se">\</span>
        | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">type</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
        | <span class="k">while </span><span class="nb">read</span> <span class="nt">-r</span> path<span class="p">;</span> <span class="k">do
            </span><span class="nv">value</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="si">$(</span>busctl get-property <span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">PSU_SERVICE</span><span class="k">}</span> <span class="se">\</span>
                <span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">path</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
                xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value Value 2>/dev/null <span class="se">\</span>
                | <span class="nb">awk</span> <span class="s1">'{print $2}'</span><span class="si">)</span>
            <span class="nv">name</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="si">$(</span><span class="nb">basename</span> <span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">path</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span><span class="si">)</span>
            <span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"  </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">name</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">: </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">value</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span>
        <span class="k">done
done</span>
```

</div></div>

### Querying PSU Inventory via D-Bus

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># List PSU inventory objects</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Manager | <span class="nb">grep </span>powersupply

<span class="c"># Get PSU presence</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Manager <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/chassis/powersupply0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item Present

<span class="c"># Get PSU asset information (manufacturer, model, serial)</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Manager <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/chassis/powersupply0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Decorator.Asset Manufacturer

busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Manager <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/chassis/powersupply0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Decorator.Asset SerialNumber
```

</div></div>

### Querying PSU Data via Redfish

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get power supply collection</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost:2443/redfish/v1/Chassis/chassis/Power <span class="se">\</span>
    | jq <span class="s1">'.PowerSupplies'</span>

<span class="c"># Get specific sensor reading</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost:2443/redfish/v1/Chassis/chassis/Sensors/PSU0_Input_Voltage

<span class="c"># Get power supply inventory with FRU data</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost:2443/redfish/v1/Chassis/chassis/Power <span class="se">\</span>
    | jq <span class="s1">'.PowerSupplies[] | {Name, Model, Manufacturer, SerialNumber, Status}'</span>
```

</div></div>

## Troubleshooting

    

### PSU Not Detected on I2C

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Scan the I2C bus</span>
i2cdetect <span class="nt">-y</span> 3
<span class="c"># If address 0x58 shows "--", the PSU is not responding</span>

<span class="c"># Check device tree</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/firmware/devicetree/base/ahb/apb/bus@1e78a000/i2c-bus@180/psu@58/compatible

<span class="c"># Try reading MFR_ID to confirm PMBus communication</span>
i2cget <span class="nt">-y</span> 3 0x58 0x99 s   <span class="c"># MFR_ID (block read)</span>
i2cget <span class="nt">-y</span> 3 0x58 0x79 w   <span class="c"># STATUS_WORD</span>
```

</div></div>

If `i2cdetect` shows the address but the pmbus driver does not bind, you may need to manually instantiate the device: `echo pmbus 0x58 > /sys/bus/i2c/devices/i2c-3/new_device`

### No Sensors Appearing on D-Bus

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check PSUSensor daemon status</span>
systemctl status xyz.openbmc_project.psusensor
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> xyz.openbmc_project.psusensor <span class="nt">-f</span>

<span class="c"># Check Entity Manager found the PSU configuration</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> xyz.openbmc_project.EntityManager | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> psu

<span class="c"># Verify the hwmon sysfs path exists</span>
<span class="nb">ls</span> /sys/bus/i2c/devices/3-0058/hwmon/

<span class="c"># Check if Labels in Entity Manager config match actual hwmon attributes</span>
<span class="nb">ls</span> /sys/bus/i2c/devices/3-0058/hwmon/hwmon<span class="k">*</span>/
```

</div></div>

A common failure is mismatched Labels. If your Entity Manager config lists `"vout1"` but the hwmon driver only creates `in2_input` (without a label file), PSUSensor may not find the sensor. Check the hwmon attribute names and adjust Labels accordingly.

### Incorrect Sensor Readings

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Compare D-Bus value with raw hwmon value</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon5/in1_input
<span class="c"># 229800 (millivolts = 229.8 V)</span>

busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.PSUSensor <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/voltage/PSU0_Input_Voltage <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value Value
<span class="c"># d 229.8</span>

<span class="c"># If values differ, check for scaling issues in the kernel driver</span>
<span class="c"># or Entity Manager ScaleFactor/Offset properties</span>
```

</div></div>

### PSU Fault Detected

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Read STATUS_WORD to identify the fault type</span>
i2cget <span class="nt">-y</span> 3 0x58 0x79 w

<span class="c"># Decode individual status registers for details</span>
i2cget <span class="nt">-y</span> 3 0x58 0x7A b   <span class="c"># STATUS_VOUT</span>
i2cget <span class="nt">-y</span> 3 0x58 0x7B b   <span class="c"># STATUS_IOUT</span>
i2cget <span class="nt">-y</span> 3 0x58 0x7C b   <span class="c"># STATUS_INPUT</span>
i2cget <span class="nt">-y</span> 3 0x58 0x7D b   <span class="c"># STATUS_TEMPERATURE</span>
i2cget <span class="nt">-y</span> 3 0x58 0x81 b   <span class="c"># STATUS_FANS_1_2</span>

<span class="c"># Clear faults after resolving the issue</span>
i2cset <span class="nt">-y</span> 3 0x58 0x03     <span class="c"># CLEAR_FAULTS command</span>

<span class="c"># Check PSU operational status on D-Bus</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Manager <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/chassis/powersupply0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.State.Decorator.OperationalStatus Functional
```

</div></div>

### Regulators Service Fails to Start

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check service status</span>
systemctl status phosphor-regulators
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> phosphor-regulators <span class="nt">--no-pager</span> | <span class="nb">tail</span> <span class="nt">-30</span>

<span class="c"># Validate JSON configuration syntax</span>
python3 <span class="nt">-m</span> json.tool /usr/share/phosphor-regulators/config.json <span class="o">></span> /dev/null

<span class="c"># Common issues:</span>
<span class="c"># - Invalid I2C bus/address in config (device not present)</span>
<span class="c"># - Missing rule_id reference (typo in rule name)</span>
<span class="c"># - Incorrect PMBus format (linear_11 vs linear_16)</span>
```

</div></div>

### PSU Threshold Alarms Not Triggering

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Verify thresholds are set on D-Bus</span>
busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.PSUSensor <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/temperature/PSU0_Temperature_1 <span class="se">\</span>
    | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> threshold

<span class="c"># Check that sel-logger is running (required for SEL entries)</span>
systemctl status xyz.openbmc_project.sel-logger

<span class="c"># Monitor threshold events in real time</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> xyz.openbmc_project.sel-logger <span class="nt">-f</span> | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> threshold
```

</div></div>
---

## Overview

    

OpenBMC supports centralized user authentication through LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol). Instead of managing accounts locally on every BMC, you can point the BMC at an existing LDAP or Active Directory server so that users authenticate with their enterprise credentials.

**phosphor-user-manager** implements the LDAP client configuration, while **nslcd** (Name Service LDAP Connection Daemon) handles the actual LDAP communication. The Redfish `AccountService` resource exposes LDAP and Active Directory configuration, and D-Bus interfaces provide the underlying control layer.

**Key concepts covered:**

* Configuring LDAP and Active Directory authentication via Redfish and D-Bus
* Setting up LDAPS (LDAP over TLS) with trusted certificates
* Mapping LDAP groups to OpenBMC privilege roles (RoleMapping)
* Differences between OpenLDAP and Active Directory configurations
* Troubleshooting authentication failures with ldapsearch and debug logging

---

### D-Bus Interfaces

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Interface | Object Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `xyz.openbmc_project.User.Ldap.Create` | `/xyz/openbmc_project/user/ldap` | Create LDAP configuration |
| `xyz.openbmc_project.User.Ldap.Config` | `/xyz/openbmc_project/user/ldap/config` | LDAP server settings |
| `xyz.openbmc_project.User.PrivilegeMapper.Create` | `/xyz/openbmc_project/user/ldap/config` | Create group-to-role mappings |
| `xyz.openbmc_project.User.PrivilegeMapperEntry` | `/xyz/openbmc_project/user/ldap/config/role_map/` | Individual role mapping entry |

</div>

### Key Dependencies

    

* **phosphor-user-manager**: Manages LDAP configuration and group-to-role mapping on D-Bus
* **nss-pam-ldapd (nslcd)**: Performs actual LDAP queries and PAM authentication
* **phosphor-certificate-manager**: Manages LDAP CA certificates for LDAPS connections
* **bmcweb**: Exposes Redfish AccountService endpoints for LDAP/AD configuration

## Configuration

    

### Build-Time Configuration (Yocto)

    

```bitbake
# In your machine .conf or local.conf

# Include LDAP support packages
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " \
    phosphor-user-manager \
    nss-pam-ldapd \
    pam-plugin-ldap \
    openldap-bin \
"

# Enable LDAP in phosphor-user-manager
EXTRA_OEMESON:pn-phosphor-user-manager = " \
    -Dldap=enabled \
"
```

The `openldap-bin` package provides the `ldapsearch` command-line tool, which is valuable for testing LDAP connectivity directly from the BMC.

### Configuration Files

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Config File | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PAM auth config | `/etc/pam.d/common-auth` | Authentication module stack (includes pam_ldap) |
| LDAP client config | `/etc/nslcd.conf` | nslcd LDAP client settings (auto-generated) |
| NSS config | `/etc/nsswitch.conf` | Name service switch (adds ldap lookup) |
| LDAP persistence | `/var/lib/phosphor-user-manager/ldap.conf` | Persisted LDAP configuration |
| LDAP CA certs | `/etc/ssl/certs/ldap/` | Trusted CA certificates for LDAPS |

</div>

### Runtime Verification

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Verify LDAP-related services are running</span>
systemctl status phosphor-user-manager
systemctl status nslcd

<span class="c"># View current LDAP configuration via D-Bus</span>
busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/user/ldap

<span class="c"># Check nslcd configuration</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /etc/nslcd.conf

<span class="c"># Check PAM is configured for LDAP</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /etc/pam.d/common-auth
```

</div></div>

## LDAP Client Configuration

    

### Configure OpenLDAP via Redfish

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Enable OpenLDAP authentication</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{
        "LDAP": {
            "ServiceEnabled": true,
            "ServiceAddresses": ["ldap://ldap.example.com"],
            "Authentication": {
                "AuthenticationType": "UsernameAndPassword",
                "Username": "cn=readonly,dc=example,dc=com",
                "Password": "bindpassword"
            },
            "LDAPService": {
                "SearchSettings": {
                    "BaseDistinguishedNames": ["dc=example,dc=com"],
                    "UsernameAttribute": "uid",
                    "GroupsAttribute": "memberOf"
                }
            }
        }
    }'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService
```

</div></div>

### Configure OpenLDAP via D-Bus (busctl)

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Create LDAP configuration</span>
busctl call xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/user/ldap <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.User.Ldap.Create <span class="se">\</span>
    Create sssssa<span class="o">{</span>ss<span class="o">}</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"ldap://ldap.example.com"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"cn=readonly,dc=example,dc=com"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"dc=example,dc=com"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"uid"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"OpenLDAP"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    0

<span class="c"># Verify the configuration</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/user/ldap/config <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.User.Ldap.Config <span class="se">\</span>
    LDAPServerURI

<span class="c"># Check if LDAP is enabled</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/user/ldap/config <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.User.Ldap.Config <span class="se">\</span>
    LDAPEnabled
```

</div></div>

### View Current LDAP Configuration

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># View full LDAP settings via Redfish</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService | <span class="se">\</span>
    python3 <span class="nt">-m</span> json.tool

<span class="c"># Check LDAP-specific properties</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService | <span class="se">\</span>
    python3 <span class="nt">-c</span> <span class="s2">"
import sys, json
data = json.load(sys.stdin)
print(json.dumps(data.get('LDAP', {}), indent=2))
"</span>
```

</div></div>

### Disable LDAP

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Disable via Redfish</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{"LDAP": {"ServiceEnabled": false}}'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService
```

</div></div>

## LDAPS Certificate Setup

    

Using plain `ldap://` transmits credentials in cleartext. Always use `ldaps://` (LDAP over TLS) in production environments.

### Install the LDAP Server CA Certificate

    

The BMC must trust the CA that signed the LDAP server certificate. Upload the CA certificate through Redfish or the certificate manager.

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Upload LDAP CA certificate via Redfish</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> POST <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{
        "CertificateType": "PEM",
        "CertificateString": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIDrzCCApeg...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
    }'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService/LDAP/Certificates
```

</div></div>

### Switch to LDAPS

    

After installing the CA certificate, update the service address to use `ldaps://`:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Update LDAP URI to use TLS</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{
        "LDAP": {
            "ServiceAddresses": ["ldaps://ldap.example.com"]
        }
    }'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService
```

</div></div>

### Verify TLS Connection

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Test TLS handshake to the LDAP server</span>
openssl s_client <span class="nt">-connect</span> ldap.example.com:636 <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-CAfile</span> /etc/ssl/certs/ldap/ca.pem

<span class="c"># Test LDAPS with ldapsearch</span>
ldapsearch <span class="nt">-x</span> <span class="nt">-H</span> ldaps://ldap.example.com <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-D</span> <span class="s2">"cn=readonly,dc=example,dc=com"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-w</span> bindpassword <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-b</span> <span class="s2">"dc=example,dc=com"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"(uid=testuser)"</span>
```

</div></div>

If the LDAP server uses a self-signed certificate, you must upload that specific certificate as the CA cert. For certificates signed by an internal CA, upload the root CA certificate (and any intermediates) that form the trust chain.

---

## Group-to-Privilege Mapping (RoleMapping)

    

LDAP group membership determines the OpenBMC privilege level. You create role mappings that associate an LDAP group distinguished name (DN) with a local role.

### Available Roles

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Local Role | Redfish RoleId | IPMI Privilege | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| priv-admin | Administrator | 4 (admin) | Full access, user management |
| priv-operator | Operator | 3 (operator) | Operations, no user management |
| priv-user | ReadOnly | 2 (user) | Read-only access |
| priv-callback | Callback | 1 (callback) | Limited callback access |

</div>

### Create Role Mappings via Redfish

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Map "bmc-admins" LDAP group to Administrator role</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> POST <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{
        "RemoteGroup": "cn=bmc-admins,ou=groups,dc=example,dc=com",
        "LocalRole": "Administrator"
    }'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService/LDAP/RemoteRoleMapping

<span class="c"># Map "bmc-operators" LDAP group to Operator role</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> POST <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{
        "RemoteGroup": "cn=bmc-operators,ou=groups,dc=example,dc=com",
        "LocalRole": "Operator"
    }'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService/LDAP/RemoteRoleMapping

<span class="c"># Map "bmc-readonly" LDAP group to ReadOnly role</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> POST <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{
        "RemoteGroup": "cn=bmc-readonly,ou=groups,dc=example,dc=com",
        "LocalRole": "ReadOnly"
    }'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService/LDAP/RemoteRoleMapping
```

</div></div>

### Create Role Mappings via D-Bus

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Create a privilege mapping entry</span>
busctl call xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/user/ldap/config <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.User.PrivilegeMapper.Create <span class="se">\</span>
    Create ss <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"cn=bmc-admins,ou=groups,dc=example,dc=com"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"priv-admin"</span>
```

</div></div>

### View Existing Mappings

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># List role mappings via Redfish</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService | <span class="se">\</span>
    python3 <span class="nt">-c</span> <span class="s2">"
import sys, json
data = json.load(sys.stdin)
ldap = data.get('LDAP', {})
for mapping in ldap.get('RemoteRoleMapping', []):
    print(f</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">Group: {mapping['RemoteGroup']} -> Role: {mapping['LocalRole']}</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">)
"</span>

<span class="c"># List mappings via D-Bus</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager | <span class="nb">grep </span>role_map
```

</div></div>

### Delete a Role Mapping

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Delete via D-Bus (replace <id> with the mapping ID)</span>
busctl call xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/user/ldap/config/role_map/<<span class="nb">id</span><span class="o">></span> <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Object.Delete <span class="se">\</span>
    Delete
```

</div></div>

## Active Directory vs OpenLDAP

    

OpenBMC supports both Active Directory and OpenLDAP. The Redfish AccountService provides separate configuration objects for each.

### Key Differences

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Attribute | OpenLDAP | Active Directory |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Redfish property | `LDAP` | `ActiveDirectory` |
| D-Bus server type | `OpenLDAP` | `ActiveDirectory` |
| Username attribute | `uid` | `sAMAccountName` |
| Groups attribute | `memberOf` | `memberOf` |
| Bind DN format | `cn=admin,dc=example,dc=com` | `admin@example.com` or `DOMAIN\admin` |
| Base DN format | `dc=example,dc=com` | `DC=example,DC=com` |
| Default port (TLS) | 636 | 636 |
| Default port (plain) | 389 | 389 |
| Group DN format | `cn=group,ou=groups,dc=example,dc=com` | `CN=group,OU=Groups,DC=example,DC=com` |

</div>

You can enable either LDAP or Active Directory, but not both simultaneously. Enabling one disables the other.

### Configure Active Directory via Redfish

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Configure Active Directory</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{
        "ActiveDirectory": {
            "ServiceEnabled": true,
            "ServiceAddresses": ["ldaps://ad.example.com"],
            "Authentication": {
                "AuthenticationType": "UsernameAndPassword",
                "Username": "svc-bmc@example.com",
                "Password": "ServiceAccountPassword"
            },
            "LDAPService": {
                "SearchSettings": {
                    "BaseDistinguishedNames": ["DC=example,DC=com"],
                    "UsernameAttribute": "sAMAccountName",
                    "GroupsAttribute": "memberOf"
                }
            }
        }
    }'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService
```

</div></div>

### Active Directory Role Mapping

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Map AD security group to Administrator</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> POST <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{
        "RemoteGroup": "CN=BMC-Admins,OU=Security Groups,DC=example,DC=com",
        "LocalRole": "Administrator"
    }'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService/ActiveDirectory/RemoteRoleMapping
```

</div></div>

When using Active Directory, the bind account (`Username`) should be a dedicated service account with read-only access to the directory. Use the UPN format (`user@domain.com`) for the bind DN, as it works across all AD forests.

---

## Porting Guide

    

Follow these steps to enable LDAP authentication on your platform.

### Step 1: Prerequisites

    

Ensure you have:

* A working OpenBMC build for your platform
* An accessible LDAP or Active Directory server
* A bind/service account with read permissions on the directory
* The CA certificate for the LDAP server (for LDAPS)

### Step 2: Add LDAP Packages to Your Image

    

```bitbake
# meta-myplatform/conf/machine/myplatform.conf (or local.conf)
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " \
    phosphor-user-manager \
    nss-pam-ldapd \
    pam-plugin-ldap \
    openldap-bin \
"

EXTRA_OEMESON:pn-phosphor-user-manager = " \
    -Dldap=enabled \
"
```

### Step 3: Configure Default PAM Stack

    

Create a bbappend to deploy a PAM configuration that includes LDAP:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># meta-myplatform/recipes-phosphor/users/phosphor-user-manager/</span>
<span class="c"># └── files/</span>
<span class="c"># │   └── common-auth</span>
<span class="c"># └── phosphor-user-manager_%.bbappend</span>

<span class="nb">cat</span> <span class="o">></span> phosphor-user-manager_%.bbappend <span class="o"><<</span> <span class="sh">'</span><span class="no">EOF</span><span class="sh">'
FILESEXTRAPATHS:prepend := "</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">THISDIR</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/files:"
SRC_URI += "file://common-auth"

do_install:append() {
    install -d </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">D</span><span class="k">}${</span><span class="nv">sysconfdir</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/pam.d
    install -m 0644 </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">WORKDIR</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/common-auth </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">D</span><span class="k">}${</span><span class="nv">sysconfdir</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/pam.d/
}
</span><span class="no">EOF
</span>
```

</div></div>

Example `common-auth` with LDAP:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
# /etc/pam.d/common-auth
auth sufficient pam_unix.so nullok try_first_pass
auth sufficient pam_ldap.so use_first_pass
auth required   pam_deny.so
```

</div></div>

### Step 4: Bake Default nslcd Configuration (Optional)

    

To include a factory-default LDAP configuration:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># meta-myplatform/recipes-phosphor/users/nss-pam-ldapd/</span>
<span class="c"># └── files/</span>
<span class="c"># │   └── nslcd.conf</span>
<span class="c"># └── nss-pam-ldapd_%.bbappend</span>

<span class="nb">cat</span> <span class="o">></span> nss-pam-ldapd_%.bbappend <span class="o"><<</span> <span class="sh">'</span><span class="no">EOF</span><span class="sh">'
FILESEXTRAPATHS:prepend := "</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">THISDIR</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/files:"
SRC_URI += "file://nslcd.conf"

do_install:append() {
    install -m 0600 </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">WORKDIR</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/nslcd.conf </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">D</span><span class="k">}${</span><span class="nv">sysconfdir</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/
}
</span><span class="no">EOF
</span>
```

</div></div>

### Step 5: Build, Flash, and Verify

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Build the image</span>
bitbake obmc-phosphor-image

<span class="c"># After flashing, verify services are running</span>
systemctl status phosphor-user-manager
systemctl status nslcd

<span class="c"># Configure LDAP via Redfish (see Configuration section above)</span>
<span class="c"># Then test authentication</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> ldapuser:ldappassword <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions
```

</div></div>

## Code Examples

    

### Example 1: LDAP Configuration Script

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c">#!/bin/bash</span>
<span class="c"># configure-ldap.sh - Configure LDAP authentication on OpenBMC</span>
<span class="c"># Usage: ./configure-ldap.sh <bmc-host> <ldap-server> <bind-dn> <base-dn></span>

<span class="nv">BMC_HOST</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">1</span><span class="k">:-</span><span class="nv">localhost</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span>
<span class="nv">LDAP_SERVER</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">2</span><span class="k">:-</span><span class="nv">ldaps</span>://ldap.example.com<span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span>
<span class="nv">BIND_DN</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">3</span><span class="k">:-</span><span class="nv">cn</span><span class="p">=readonly,dc=example,dc=com</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span>
<span class="nv">BASE_DN</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">4</span><span class="k">:-</span><span class="nv">dc</span><span class="p">=example,dc=com</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span>
<span class="nv">BMC_USER</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"root"</span>
<span class="nv">BMC_PASS</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"0penBmc"</span>

<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"Configuring LDAP on </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BMC_HOST</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">..."</span>

<span class="c"># Step 1: Enable LDAP</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> <span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BMC_USER</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">:</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BMC_PASS</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span> <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s2">"{
        </span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">LDAP</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">: {
            </span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">ServiceEnabled</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">: true,
            </span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">ServiceAddresses</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">: [</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">LDAP_SERVER</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">],
            </span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">Authentication</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">: {
                </span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">AuthenticationType</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">: </span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">UsernameAndPassword</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">,
                </span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">Username</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">: </span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BIND_DN</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">,
                </span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">Password</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">: </span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">changeme</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">
            },
            </span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">LDAPService</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">: {
                </span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">SearchSettings</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">: {
                    </span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">BaseDistinguishedNames</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">: [</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BASE_DN</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">],
                    </span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">UsernameAttribute</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">: </span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">uid</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">,
                    </span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">GroupsAttribute</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">: </span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">memberOf</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">
                }
            }
        }
    }"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"https://</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BMC_HOST</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">/redfish/v1/AccountService"</span>

<span class="c"># Step 2: Add role mappings</span>
<span class="k">for </span>role_pair <span class="k">in</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"cn=bmc-admins,ou=groups,</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BASE_DN</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">:Administrator"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"cn=bmc-operators,ou=groups,</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BASE_DN</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">:Operator"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"cn=bmc-readonly,ou=groups,</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BASE_DN</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">:ReadOnly"</span><span class="p">;</span> <span class="k">do

    </span><span class="nv">group</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">role_pair</span><span class="p">%%</span>:<span class="p">*</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span>
    <span class="nv">role</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">role_pair</span><span class="p">##*</span>:<span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span>

    <span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"Mapping group '</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">group</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">' to role '</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">role</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">'..."</span>
    curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> <span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BMC_USER</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">:</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BMC_PASS</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span> <span class="nt">-X</span> POST <span class="se">\</span>
        <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
        <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s2">"{
            </span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">RemoteGroup</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">: </span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">group</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">,
            </span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">LocalRole</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">: </span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">role</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s2">
        }"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
        <span class="s2">"https://</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BMC_HOST</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">/redfish/v1/AccountService/LDAP/RemoteRoleMapping"</span>
<span class="k">done

</span><span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"LDAP configuration complete."</span>
```

```
<span class="c">#!/bin/bash</span>
<span class="c"># test-ldap.sh - Test LDAP connectivity and authentication from BMC</span>
<span class="c"># Usage: ./test-ldap.sh <ldap-server> <bind-dn> <base-dn> <test-user></span>

<span class="nv">LDAP_SERVER</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">1</span><span class="k">:-</span><span class="nv">ldaps</span>://ldap.example.com<span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span>
<span class="nv">BIND_DN</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">2</span><span class="k">:-</span><span class="nv">cn</span><span class="p">=readonly,dc=example,dc=com</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span>
<span class="nv">BASE_DN</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">3</span><span class="k">:-</span><span class="nv">dc</span><span class="p">=example,dc=com</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span>
<span class="nv">TEST_USER</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">4</span><span class="k">:-</span><span class="nv">testuser</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span>

<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"=== Testing LDAP connection ==="</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"Server: </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">LDAP_SERVER</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"Bind DN: </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BIND_DN</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"Base DN: </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BASE_DN</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">""</span>

<span class="c"># Test 1: Anonymous bind (if allowed)</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"--- Test 1: Server reachability ---"</span>
ldapsearch <span class="nt">-x</span> <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">LDAP_SERVER</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-b</span> <span class="s2">""</span> <span class="nt">-s</span> base <span class="s2">"(objectClass=*)"</span> namingContexts 2>&1
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">""</span>

<span class="c"># Test 2: Authenticated bind</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"--- Test 2: Bind authentication ---"</span>
<span class="nb">read</span> <span class="nt">-s</span> <span class="nt">-p</span> <span class="s2">"Enter bind password: "</span> BIND_PASS
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">""</span>
ldapsearch <span class="nt">-x</span> <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">LDAP_SERVER</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-D</span> <span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BIND_DN</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-w</span> <span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BIND_PASS</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-b</span> <span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BASE_DN</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"(uid=</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">TEST_USER</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">)"</span> uid cn memberOf 2>&1
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">""</span>

<span class="c"># Test 3: Check group membership</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"--- Test 3: Group membership ---"</span>
ldapsearch <span class="nt">-x</span> <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">LDAP_SERVER</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-D</span> <span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BIND_DN</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-w</span> <span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BIND_PASS</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-b</span> <span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BASE_DN</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"(uid=</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">TEST_USER</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">)"</span> memberOf 2>&1
```

## Troubleshooting

    

### Issue: LDAP Authentication Fails

    

**Symptom**: Users cannot log in with LDAP credentials. Redfish returns 401 Unauthorized.

**Cause**: LDAP configuration may be incorrect, the bind account may lack permissions, or the server may be unreachable.

**Solution**:

1. Verify LDAP is enabled:
    
```
curl -k -u root:0penBmc \
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService | \
    python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('LDAP',{}).get('ServiceEnabled'))"
```
2. Test LDAP connectivity from the BMC:
    
```
ldapsearch -x -H ldap://ldap.example.com \
    -D "cn=readonly,dc=example,dc=com" \
    -w bindpassword \
    -b "dc=example,dc=com" \
    "(uid=testuser)"
```
3. Check nslcd logs:
    
```
journalctl -u nslcd -f
```

### Issue: LDAPS Certificate Not Trusted

    

**Symptom**: LDAPS connections fail with “TLS handshake failure” or “certificate verify failed”.

**Cause**: The BMC does not trust the CA that signed the LDAP server certificate.

**Solution**:

1. Verify the LDAP server certificate:
    
```
openssl s_client -connect ldap.example.com:636 \
    -CAfile /etc/ssl/certs/ldap/ca.pem
```
2. Upload the CA certificate:
    
```
curl -k -u root:0penBmc -X POST \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "CertificateType": "PEM",
        "CertificateString": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
    }' \
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService/LDAP/Certificates
```
3. Restart nslcd after installing the certificate:
    
```
systemctl restart nslcd
```

If the LDAP server certificate has expired or uses an untrusted CA, authentication will fail silently. Always check certificate validity dates with `openssl x509 -in cert.pem -noout -dates`.

### Issue: Role Mapping Not Applied

    

**Symptom**: LDAP users authenticate successfully but receive no privileges or the wrong privilege level.

**Cause**: Group-to-role mappings are missing, or the LDAP group DN in the mapping does not match the group DN returned by the server.

**Solution**:

1. Verify the user’s group membership on the LDAP server:
    
```
ldapsearch -x -H ldap://ldap.example.com \
    -D "cn=readonly,dc=example,dc=com" \
    -w bindpassword \
    -b "dc=example,dc=com" \
    "(uid=testuser)" memberOf
```
2. Compare the returned group DN with your role mapping. The DN must match exactly (case-sensitive for OpenLDAP):
    
```
curl -k -u root:0penBmc \
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService | \
    python3 -c "
import sys, json
data = json.load(sys.stdin)
for m in data.get('LDAP',{}).get('RemoteRoleMapping',[]):
    print(f\"{m['RemoteGroup']} -> {m['LocalRole']}\")
"
```
3. If the DNs do not match, delete the incorrect mapping and create a new one with the correct group DN.

### Issue: nslcd Service Not Running

    

**Symptom**: All LDAP authentication attempts fail. The `nslcd` service shows as inactive.

**Cause**: The nslcd service may have failed to start due to a bad configuration or missing dependencies.

**Solution**:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check nslcd status</span>
systemctl status nslcd

<span class="c"># View startup logs</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> nslcd <span class="nt">--no-pager</span>

<span class="c"># Restart the service</span>
systemctl restart nslcd

<span class="c"># Verify nslcd config is valid</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /etc/nslcd.conf
```

</div></div>

### Debug Commands

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Enable debug logging for phosphor-user-manager</span>
<span class="c"># (Requires recompile with debug flags or environment override)</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> phosphor-user-manager <span class="nt">-f</span>

<span class="c"># Check nslcd debug output</span>
systemctl stop nslcd
nslcd <span class="nt">-d</span>  <span class="c"># Run in foreground with debug output</span>

<span class="c"># Test PAM authentication directly</span>
pamtester common-auth testuser authenticate

<span class="c"># Inspect D-Bus LDAP objects</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager
busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/user/ldap/config

<span class="c"># List all role mapping entries</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager | <span class="nb">grep </span>role_map
```

</div></div>

Running `nslcd -d` in the foreground shows detailed LDAP communication traces, including bind attempts, search filters, and TLS negotiation. This is the single most useful debugging tool for LDAP issues.

## Deep Dive

    

Advanced implementation details for LDAP integration developers.

### LDAP Authentication Flow

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    LDAP Authentication Sequence                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   Client (Redfish/SSH)       BMC                    LDAP Server         │
│          │                    │                          │              │
│   1. Login request            │                          │              │
│   (user + password)           │                          │              │
│   ──────────────────────────▶ │                          │              │
│                               │                          │              │
│          PAM Stack            │                          │              │
│          ┌────────────────────┤                          │              │
│          │ pam_unix: check    │                          │              │
│          │ /etc/shadow        │                          │              │
│          │ -> NOT FOUND       │                          │              │
│          ├────────────────────┤                          │              │
│          │ pam_ldap: try LDAP │                          │              │
│          └────────────────────┤                          │              │
│                               │                          │              │
│                               │  2. Bind (service acct)  │              │
│                               │─────────────────────────▶│              │
│                               │◀─────────────────────────│ Bind OK     │
│                               │                          │              │
│                               │  3. Search (find user)   │              │
│                               │  filter: (uid=username)  │              │
│                               │─────────────────────────▶│              │
│                               │◀─────────────────────────│ User DN     │
│                               │                          │              │
│                               │  4. Bind (user DN + pw)  │              │
│                               │─────────────────────────▶│              │
│                               │◀─────────────────────────│ Auth OK     │
│                               │                          │              │
│                               │  5. Search (groups)      │              │
│                               │  filter: (member=userDN) │              │
│                               │─────────────────────────▶│              │
│                               │◀─────────────────────────│ Group list  │
│                               │                          │              │
│          6. Map groups to     │                          │              │
│             OpenBMC roles     │                          │              │
│          (role_map entries)   │                          │              │
│                               │                          │              │
│   7. Session created with     │                          │              │
│      mapped privilege level   │                          │              │
│   ◀────────────────────────── │                          │              │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### LDAP Configuration Persistence

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Configuration Persistence Flow                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   Redfish PATCH /AccountService                                         │
│          │                                                              │
│          ▼                                                              │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │  bmcweb                                                         │   │
│   │  Translates Redfish to D-Bus calls                              │   │
│   └────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                │                                        │
│                                ▼                                        │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │  phosphor-user-manager                                          │   │
│   │                                                                 │   │
│   │  1. Validate configuration parameters                           │   │
│   │  2. Persist to /var/lib/phosphor-user-manager/ldap.conf         │   │
│   │  3. Generate /etc/nslcd.conf from D-Bus properties              │   │
│   │  4. Restart nslcd service                                       │   │
│   │  5. Emit D-Bus PropertiesChanged signal                         │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
│   Persisted Files:                                                      │
│   ├── /var/lib/phosphor-user-manager/ldap.conf  (D-Bus state)          │
│   ├── /etc/nslcd.conf                           (runtime config)       │
│   └── /etc/ssl/certs/ldap/                      (CA certificates)      │
│                                                                         │
│   After BMC reboot:                                                     │
│   phosphor-user-manager reads /var/lib/.../ldap.conf                    │
│   and regenerates /etc/nslcd.conf                                       │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>
