## Mounting Images

    

### Via WebUI

    

1. Login to WebUI at `https:///`
2. Navigate to **Operations** → **Virtual Media**
3. Select device type: **CD/DVD** or **USB**
4. Choose mount method:
    
* **From URL**: Enter HTTP/HTTPS/NFS/CIFS path
* **Upload**: Upload local file
5. Click **Mount**

### Via Redfish API

    

#### List Virtual Media Devices

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/VirtualMedia
```

</div></div>

#### Mount from URL

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Mount ISO from HTTPS server</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{
        "Image": "https://example.com/images/ubuntu-22.04.iso",
        "TransferProtocolType": "HTTPS",
        "UserName": "",
        "Password": "",
        "WriteProtected": true,
        "Inserted": true
    }'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/VirtualMedia/Slot_0

<span class="c"># Mount from NFS</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{
        "Image": "nfs://192.168.1.100/exports/images/boot.iso",
        "Inserted": true
    }'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/VirtualMedia/Slot_0

<span class="c"># Mount from CIFS/SMB</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{
        "Image": "smb://192.168.1.100/share/images/install.iso",
        "UserName": "user",
        "Password": "password",
        "Inserted": true
    }'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/VirtualMedia/Slot_0
```

</div></div>

#### Check Mount Status

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">

## Boot from Virtual Media

    

### Configure Boot Order

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Set boot source override to CD</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{
        "Boot": {
            "BootSourceOverrideTarget": "Cd",
            "BootSourceOverrideEnabled": "Once"
        }
    }'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system
```

</div></div>

### One-Time Boot Sequence

    

1. Mount installation ISO
2. Set boot override to CD
3. Reset/power on system
4. System boots from virtual CD

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Complete workflow</span>
<span class="c"># 1. Mount ISO</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{"Image": "https://server/ubuntu.iso", "Inserted": true}'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/VirtualMedia/Slot_0

<span class="c"># 2. Set boot source</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{"Boot": {"BootSourceOverrideTarget": "Cd", "BootSourceOverrideEnabled": "Once"}}'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system

<span class="c"># 3. Power cycle</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> POST <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{"ResetType": "ForceRestart"}'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system/Actions/ComputerSystem.Reset
```

</div></div>

## WebSocket Mode

    

### Connecting via WebSocket

    

For direct file streaming:

<div class="language-javascript highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c1">// JavaScript example</span>
<span class="kd">const</span> <span class="nx">ws</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">WebSocket</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="dl">'</span><span class="s1">wss://bmc-ip/nbd/0</span><span class="dl">'</span><span class="p">);</span>

<span class="c1">// Handle binary data streaming</span>
<span class="nx">ws</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">binaryType</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="dl">'</span><span class="s1">arraybuffer</span><span class="dl">'</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="nx">ws</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">onmessage</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kd">function</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nx">event</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="c1">// Handle NBD protocol messages</span>
<span class="p">};</span>
```

</div></div>

### NBD Protocol

    

Network Block Device protocol for efficient streaming:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check NBD devices</span>
<span class="nb">ls</span> /dev/nbd<span class="k">*</span>

<span class="c"># NBD proxy handles protocol translation</span>
<span class="c"># WebSocket → NBD → USB mass storage</span>
```

</div></div>

## Troubleshooting

    

### Image Not Mounting

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check virtual media service</span>
systemctl status virtual-media
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> virtual-media <span class="nt">-f</span>

<span class="c"># Verify URL is accessible from BMC</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> https://example.com/image.iso <span class="nt">-o</span> /dev/null

<span class="c"># Check USB gadget</span>
<span class="nb">ls</span> /sys/kernel/config/usb_gadget/
```

</div></div>

### Host Not Seeing USB Device

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check USB connection</span>
lsusb <span class="nt">-t</span>   <span class="c"># On host if possible</span>

<span class="c"># Verify USB gadget is bound</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/kernel/config/usb_gadget/<span class="k">*</span>/UDC

<span class="c"># Check USB device controller</span>
<span class="nb">ls</span> /sys/class/udc/

<span class="c"># Rebind gadget</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">""</span> <span class="o">></span> /sys/kernel/config/usb_gadget/virtual_media/UDC
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"1e6a0000.usb-vhub:p1"</span> <span class="o">></span> /sys/kernel/config/usb_gadget/virtual_media/UDC
```

</div></div>

### Slow Transfer Speed

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check network connection</span>
iftop <span class="nt">-i</span> eth0

<span class="c"># Monitor image streaming</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> virtual-media <span class="nt">-f</span>

<span class="c"># For large images, consider:</span>
<span class="c"># - Local caching</span>
<span class="c"># - Faster network link</span>
<span class="c"># - Proximity of image server</span>
```

### Boot Fails

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Verify boot order in BIOS</span>
<span class="c"># USB boot may need to be enabled</span>

<span class="c"># Check image integrity</span>
curl https://server/image.iso | <span class="nb">sha256sum</span>

<span class="c"># Verify image is bootable</span>
<span class="c"># May need to test image locally first</span>
```

</div></div>

### Authentication Errors

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># For CIFS/SMB shares</span>
<span class="c"># Verify credentials</span>
smbclient //server/share <span class="nt">-U</span> username

<span class="c"># For HTTPS with client cert</span>

```

## Deep Dive

    

Advanced implementation details for virtual media developers.

### NBD (Network Block Device) Protocol

    

```mermaid
---
title: NBD Handshake (Newstyle)
---
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Server

    Server->>Client: NBDMAGIC (8 bytes)  
0x4e42444d41474943 "NBDMAGIC"
    Server->>Client: IHAVEOPT (8 bytes)  
0x49484156454F5054 "IHAVEOPT"
    Server->>Client: Global flags (2 bytes)  
NBD_FLAG_FIXED_NEWSTYLE | NBD_FLAG_NO_ZEROES

    Client->>Server: Client flags (4 bytes)  
NBD_FLAG_C_FIXED_NEWSTYLE | NBD_FLAG_C_NO_ZEROES
    Client->>Server: NBD_OPT_GO (export name)  
option: 7 (GO), export_name: "vm0"

    Server->>Client: NBD_REP_INFO (size, flags)  
size: 4700000000, flags: READ_ONLY
    Server->>Client: NBD_REP_ACK

    Note over Client,Server: Transmission phase begins
```

**NBD Request Format (28 bytes):**

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Field | Size | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Magic | 4 bytes | 0x25609513 |
| Flags | 2 bytes | 0x0000 |
| Type | 2 bytes | NBD_CMD_* |
| Handle | 8 bytes | request_id |
| Offset | 8 bytes | byte_offset |
| Length | 4 bytes | bytes_to_read |

</div>

**NBD Commands:**

* `NBD_CMD_READ` (0) - Read data from export
* `NBD_CMD_WRITE` (1) - Write data to export
* `NBD_CMD_DISC` (2) - Disconnect gracefully
* `NBD_CMD_FLUSH` (3) - Flush writes to storage
* `NBD_CMD_TRIM` (4) - Discard blocks (sparse)

**NBD Reply Format (16 bytes + data):**

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Field | Size | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Magic | 4 bytes | 0x67446698 |
| Error | 4 bytes | 0 (OK) |
| Handle | 8 bytes | request_id (matches request) |

</div>

Data payload follows for READ responses.

### USB Mass Storage Gadget Architecture

    

**ConfigFS Gadget Setup:**

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
/sys/kernel/config/usb_gadget/virtual_media/
├── idVendor           # 0x1d6b (Linux Foundation)
├── idProduct          # 0x0104 (Composite Gadget)
├── bcdDevice          # 0x0100
├── bcdUSB             # 0x0200 (USB 2.0)
├── strings/0x409/
│   ├── manufacturer   # "OpenBMC"
│   ├── product        # "Virtual Media"
│   └── serialnumber   # BMC serial
├── configs/c.1/
│   ├── MaxPower       # 500 mA
│   └── mass_storage.0 -> ../../functions/mass_storage.0
└── functions/
    └── mass_storage.0/
        └── lun.0/
            ├── cdrom        # 1 (CD-ROM mode for ISO)
            ├── ro           # 1 (read-only)
            ├── removable    # 1 (removable media)
            ├── nofua        # 0 (respect FUA bit)
            └── file         # /dev/nbd0 or /path/to/image.iso
```

</div></div>

**Command Block Wrapper (CBW) - 31 bytes:**

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Field | Value | Size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dCBWSignature | 0x43425355 “USBC” | 4 bytes |
| dCBWTag | Transaction identifier | 4 bytes |
| dCBWDataLength | Expected data transfer length | 4 bytes |
| bmCBWFlags | Direction (0x80=IN, 0x00=OUT) | 1 byte |
| bCBWLUN | Logical Unit Number (0) | 1 byte |
| bCBWCBLength | SCSI command length (6-16) | 1 byte |
| CBWCB[16] | SCSI command block | 16 bytes |

</div>

**Common SCSI Commands for CD-ROM:**

* `INQUIRY` (0x12) - Device identification
* `TEST_UNIT_READY` (0x00) - Check if media present
* `READ_CAPACITY` (0x25) - Get media size
* `READ_10` (0x28) - Read data blocks
* `MODE_SENSE_10` (0x5A) - Get device parameters
* `GET_CONFIGURATION` (0x46) - Get multimedia features

**Command Status Wrapper (CSW) - 13 bytes:**

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Field | Value | Size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dCSWSignature | 0x53425355 “USBS” | 4 bytes |
| dCSWTag | Matches CBW tag | 4 bytes |
| dCSWDataResidue | Bytes not transferred | 4 bytes |
| bCSWStatus | 0=OK, 1=Failed, 2=Phase Error | 1 byte |

</div>

### Proxy Mode Data Flow

    

```mermaid
---
title: Virtual Media Proxy Mode Data Flow
---
flowchart TB
    https["HTTPS Server  
(ISO image)"]

    subgraph daemon["virtual-media daemon"]
        direction TB
        httpclient["HTTP Client (HTTPS fetch)  
Fetch 1MB chunks on demand"]
        nbdserver["NBD Server (local)  
Handle READ requests  
Check cache → fetch if needed"]
        httpclient -->|"Data chunks"| nbdserver
    end

    https -->|"HTTPS/TLS  
(image chunks)"| httpclient

    subgraph gadget["USB Mass Storage Gadget"]
        direction TB
        lun["lun.0/file = /dev/nbd0"]
        flow["SCSI READ_10 → nbd_read() → NBD → HTTP fetch"]
    end

    nbdserver -->|"/dev/nbd0"| gadget

    subgraph host["Host System"]
        direction LR
        dev["/dev/sr0 (CD-ROM)"]
        mount["mount /dev/sr0 /mnt/cdrom"]
        boot["BIOS → USB CDROM → Boot"]
    end

    gadget -->|"USB"| host
```

**Caching Strategy:**

* **Read-ahead caching**: When block N is requested, prefetch blocks N+1 to N+K. Reduces latency for sequential reads (common during boot).
* **LRU cache eviction**: Limited BMC memory (e.g., 64MB cache). Evict least recently used chunks when full.
* **Sparse image support**: Only fetch blocks actually read by host. Zero-fill unread blocks (improves mount speed).

## Overview

    

**Serial Console** provides text-mode access to the host system through the BMC, enabling boot monitoring, BIOS configuration, and command-line access when graphical interfaces are unavailable.

```mermaid
---
title: Console Architecture
---
flowchart TB
    subgraph clients["Clients"]
        direction LR
        webui["WebUI  
Console"]
        ssh["SSH  
Console"]
        sol["IPMI SOL  
ipmitool"]
    end

    bmcweb["bmcweb  
WebSocket: /console/default"]

    subgraph console["obmc-console"]
        direction LR
        server["Console Server  
(multiplexer)"]
        hostlogger["hostlogger  
(persistent logging)"]
    end

    serial["/dev/ttyS*, /dev/ttyVUART*"]

    host["Host System  
(Serial console)"]

    clients --> bmcweb --> console --> serial --> host
```

## Components

    

### obmc-console-server

    

* Multiplexes serial port to multiple clients
* Provides Unix socket interface
* Handles console access control

### obmc-console-client

    

* Command-line console access
* Connects to console-server socket

### hostlogger

    

* Captures console output persistently
* Stores in rotating log files
* Available via Redfish API

---

## Hardware Configuration

    

### Serial Port Types

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Type | Description | Device Path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Physical UART | Hardware serial port | /dev/ttyS0, /dev/ttyS1 |
| Virtual UART | LPC/VUART interface | /dev/ttyVUART0 |
| PTY | Pseudo-terminal (testing) | /dev/pts/* |

</div>

### ASPEED VUART

    

ASPEED BMCs use Virtual UART for LPC-based console:

```dts
// Device tree configuration
&vuart {
    status = "okay";
};
```

### Nuvoton Serial

    

```dts
// Device tree for serial ports
&serial1 {
    status = "okay";
};
```

---

## Setup & Configuration

    

### Build-Time Configuration (Yocto)

    

```bitbake
# In your machine .conf or local.conf

# Include console packages
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " \
    obmc-console \
    phosphor-hostlogger \
"

# Configure console device in machine config
OBMC_CONSOLE_HOST_TTY ?= "ttyVUART0"

# For physical serial port:
# OBMC_CONSOLE_HOST_TTY ?= "ttyS2"
```

### Console Server Configuration

    

Configuration file: `/etc/obmc-console/server.ttyVUART0.conf`

<div class="language-ini highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Console server configuration
</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="c"># Socket directory
</span><span class="py">socket-id</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">default</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="c"># Console device
</span><span class="py">console-id</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">default</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="c"># Baud rate
</span><span class="py">baud</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">115200</span>
<span class="w">
```

## Accessing the Console

    

### Via WebUI

    

1. Login to WebUI at `https:///`
2. Navigate to **Operations** → **Serial over LAN Console**
3. Terminal opens in browser window
4. Type commands to interact with host

### Via SSH

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Direct console access via SSH</span>
ssh <span class="nt">-t</span> root@bmc-ip /usr/bin/obmc-console-client

<span class="c"># With specific console ID</span>
ssh <span class="nt">-t</span> root@bmc-ip /usr/bin/obmc-console-client <span class="nt">-i</span> host0
```

</div></div>

### Via IPMI SOL

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Activate SOL session</span>
ipmitool <span class="nt">-I</span> lanplus <span class="nt">-H</span> bmc-ip <span class="nt">-U</span> root <span class="nt">-P</span> 0penBmc sol activate

<span class="c"># Deactivate SOL session</span>
ipmitool <span class="nt">-I</span> lanplus <span class="nt">-H</span> bmc-ip <span class="nt">-U</span> root <span class="nt">-P</span> 0penBmc sol deactivate

<span class="c"># SOL configuration</span>
ipmitool <span class="nt">-I</span> lanplus <span class="nt">-H</span> bmc-ip <span class="nt">-U</span> root <span class="nt">-P</span> 0penBmc sol info
```

</div></div>

### Via Redfish

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get console URL</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc

<span class="c"># Look for SerialConsole property</span>
<span class="c"># WebSocket endpoint: wss://bmc-ip/console/default</span>
```

</div></div>

### Via obmc-console-client

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># On the BMC directly</span>
obmc-console-client

<span class="c"># Specify console ID</span>
obmc-console-client <span class="nt">-i</span> default

<span class="c"># Exit: Ctrl+] or ~.</span>
```

</div></div>

## Multi-UART Muxing

    

Unlike [Multiple Host Consoles](#multiple-host-consoles) – which gives each host its own dedicated serial port – multi-UART muxing shares **one physical port** between several UARTs that sit behind a GPIO mux, exposing only one of them at a time. A single `obmc-console-server` process drives the shared tty and switches the mux GPIOs to select the active console.

Use **Multiple Host Consoles** when each host has independent wiring; use **Multi-UART Muxing** when several UARTs share the same BMC port and a mux chip selects between them.

### Mux Configuration

    

Two configuration keys control muxing (see the upstream [mux-support.md](https://github.com/openbmc/obmc-console/blob/master/docs/mux-support.md)):

* **`mux-gpios`** (global, top of the config file) – the GPIO line name(s) that drive the mux. The order of the listed GPIOs forms the LSB-first bit representation of the number taken from each console’s `mux-index`.
* **`mux-index`** (per console) – the numeric mux value that selects this console. Each console lives in a section whose name matches its `console-id`.

<div class="language-ini highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># /etc/obmc-console/server.conf  (started as: obmc-console-server --config server.conf /dev/ttyS0)
</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="c"># Global: GPIO(s) that select which UART is active
</span><span class="py">mux-gpios</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">MUX_CTL</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="nn">[host1]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">mux-index</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">0</span>
<span class="py">logfile</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">/var/log/console-host1.log</span>
<span class="w">
</span><span class="nn">[host2]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="py">mux-index</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">1</span>
<span class="py">logfile</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">/var/log/console-host2.log</span>
```

</div></div>

### Per-Console D-Bus Interface

    

Each muxed console is published as its own D-Bus service named after the console-id:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
busctl list | <span class="nb">grep </span>xyz.openbmc_project.Console
<span class="c"># xyz.openbmc_project.Console.host1  ...  obmc-console-server  root ...</span>
<span class="c"># xyz.openbmc_project.Console.host2  ...  obmc-console-server  root ...</span>

busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.Console.host1 <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/console/host1
<span class="c"># xyz.openbmc_project.Console.Access  interface  -  -</span>
<span class="c"># .Connect                            method     -  h</span>
```

</div></div>

### Mux Switching via Connect()

    

Mux control is **implicit**: switching happens when a client connects. Calling `Connect()` on a console (or simply attaching `obmc-console-client -i host1`) makes the server switch the mux GPIOs to that console’s `mux-index`, then start forwarding bytes. Any client attached to another console is disconnected.

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Selecting host1 asserts the mux GPIOs for host1 and drops host2</span>
busctl call xyz.openbmc_project.Console.host1 <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/console/host1 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Console.Access Connect
```

</div></div>

Concretely, connecting to `host1` causes the previously active `host2` to (1) stop forwarding bytes and (2) print a disconnect log to its clients; then `host1` (1) switches the mux via the GPIOs, (2) prints a connect log to its clients, and (3) resumes forwarding.

### Connect/Disconnect Log Markers

    

So a log reader can see why a console went quiet, the server writes a marker line to all clients of a console whenever the mux switches:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
[obmc-console] %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S UTC CONNECTED
[obmc-console] %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S UTC DISCONNECTED
```

</div></div>

These markers are a convenience only – anything on the other side of the UART could print the same text, and the exact format is not guaranteed to stay fixed. Do not parse them as a reliable connection signal.

### D-Bus Console Interface

    

Beyond the muxing `Access` interface, `obmc-console-server` (in `console-dbus.c`) exposes a `xyz.openbmc_project.Console.UART` interface on `/xyz/openbmc_project/console/` with a **writable `Baud` property** (type `t`, uint64). Writing it re-applies the tty’s termios at runtime – no service restart needed:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Read the current baud rate</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.Console.default <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/console/default <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Console.UART Baud

<span class="c"># Change baud rate live (re-applies termios on the underlying tty)</span>
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Console.default <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/console/default <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Console.UART Baud t 57600
```

</div></div>

The `xyz.openbmc_project.Console.Access` interface’s **`Connect()`** method takes no arguments and returns a Unix file descriptor (`h`). The server creates a socket pair, hands the client end back over D-Bus, and closes its own end – giving the caller a direct byte stream to the console without going through the on-disk Unix socket path.

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Returns a connected fd for the default console</span>
busctl call xyz.openbmc_project.Console.default <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/console/default <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Console.Access Connect
```

</div></div>
---

## Troubleshooting

    

### No Console Output

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check if console server is running</span>
systemctl status obmc-console-server@ttyVUART0

<span class="c"># Check device exists</span>
<span class="nb">ls</span> <span class="nt">-la</span> /dev/ttyVUART0

<span class="c"># Check permissions</span>
<span class="nb">stat</span> /dev/ttyVUART0

<span class="c"># Check serial port configuration</span>
<span class="nb">stty</span> <span class="nt">-F</span> /dev/ttyVUART0 <span class="nt">-a</span>

<span class="c"># Verify baud rate matches host</span>
<span class="nb">stty</span> <span class="nt">-F</span> /dev/ttyVUART0 115200
```

</div></div>

### Console Frozen

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Restart console server</span>
systemctl restart obmc-console-server@ttyVUART0

<span class="c"># Kill stuck clients</span>
pkill obmc-console-client

<span class="c"># Check for hardware issues</span>
dmesg | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> uart
```

</div></div>

### Garbled Text

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Baud rate mismatch - verify settings match</span>
<span class="c"># Host BIOS/OS must use same baud rate as BMC</span>

<span class="c"># Common baud rates to try:</span>
<span class="nb">stty</span> <span class="nt">-F</span> /dev/ttyVUART0 9600
<span class="nb">stty</span> <span class="nt">-F</span> /dev/ttyVUART0 19200
<span class="nb">stty</span> <span class="nt">-F</span> /dev/ttyVUART0 38400
<span class="nb">stty</span> <span class="nt">-F</span> /dev/ttyVUART0 57600
<span class="nb">stty</span> <span class="nt">-F</span> /dev/ttyVUART0 115200
```

</div></div>

### SOL Connection Failed

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check IPMI service</span>
systemctl status phosphor-ipmi-net

<span class="c"># Verify SOL is enabled</span>
ipmitool <span class="nt">-I</span> lanplus <span class="nt">-H</span> bmc-ip <span class="nt">-U</span> root <span class="nt">-P</span> 0penBmc sol info

<span class="c"># Check for active sessions</span>
ipmitool <span class="nt">-I</span> lanplus <span class="nt">-H</span> bmc-ip <span class="nt">-U</span> root <span class="nt">-P</span> 0penBmc session info all

<span class="c"># Force deactivate stale session</span>
ipmitool <span class="nt">-I</span> lanplus <span class="nt">-H</span> bmc-ip <span class="nt">-U</span> root <span class="nt">-P</span> 0penBmc sol deactivate
```

</div></div>

### Permission Denied

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check user permissions</span>
<span class="c"># User needs Operator or Administrator role</span>

<span class="c"># Verify via Redfish</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> user:password <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService/Accounts/user
```

</div></div>

## Security Considerations

    

### Access Control

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Console access requires authentication</span>
<span class="c"># Recommended role: Operator or Administrator</span>

<span class="c"># View user roles</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService/Accounts
```

</div></div>

### SOL Encryption

    

IPMI SOL uses RMCP+ encryption:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check cipher suite</span>
ipmitool <span class="nt">-I</span> lanplus <span class="nt">-H</span> bmc-ip <span class="nt">-U</span> root <span class="nt">-P</span> 0penBmc <span class="nt">-C</span> 17 sol activate

<span class="c"># Cipher 17 = AES-CBC-128 + HMAC-SHA256 (recommended)</span>
```

</div></div>

### Console Logging Security

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Console logs may contain sensitive data</span>
<span class="c"># Configure retention policy</span>
<span class="c"># Restrict access to log files</span>

<span class="c"># File permissions</span>
<span class="nb">chmod </span>600 /var/log/hostlogger/<span class="k">*</span>
```

</div></div>

## Deep Dive

    

Advanced implementation details for console developers.

### Console Server Multiplexing Architecture

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   obmc-console Multiplexer Architecture                    │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                            │
│  SERIAL DEVICE                                                             │
│  ─────────────                                                             │
│  /dev/ttyVUART0 (or /dev/ttyS*)                                            │
│        │                                                                   │
│        │ termios settings: 115200 8N1                                      │
│        v                                                                   │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │                    obmc-console-server                              │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │   │
│  │  │  TTY Handler                                                  │  │   │
│  │  │                                                               │  │   │
│  │  │  // Open serial port with correct settings                    │  │   │
│  │  │  fd = open("/dev/ttyVUART0", O_RDWR | O_NOCTTY);              │  │   │
│  │  │  tcgetattr(fd, &termios);                                     │  │   │
│  │  │  cfsetispeed(&termios, B115200);                              │  │   │
│  │  │  cfsetospeed(&termios, B115200);                              │  │   │
│  │  │  termios.c_cflag = CS8 | CREAD | CLOCAL;  // 8N1              │  │   │
│  │  │  tcsetattr(fd, TCSANOW, &termios);                            │  │   │
│  │  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │   │
│  │                          │                                          │   │
│  │                          │ epoll multiplexing                       │   │
│  │                          v                                          │   │
│  │  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │   │
│  │  │  Event Loop (main.c)                                          │  │   │
│  │  │                                                               │  │   │
│  │  │  epoll_fd = epoll_create1(0);                                 │  │   │
│  │  │  epoll_ctl(epoll_fd, EPOLL_CTL_ADD, tty_fd, &ev_tty);         │  │   │
│  │  │  epoll_ctl(epoll_fd, EPOLL_CTL_ADD, socket_fd, &ev_sock);     │  │   │
│  │  │                                                               │  │   │
│  │  │  while (running) {                                            │  │   │
│  │  │      n = epoll_wait(epoll_fd, events, MAX_EVENTS, -1);        │  │   │
│  │  │      for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {                                │  │   │
│  │  │          if (events[i].data.fd == tty_fd) {                   │  │   │
│  │  │              // Data from host → broadcast to all clients     │  │   │
│  │  │              handle_tty_data();                               │  │   │
│  │  │          } else if (events[i].data.fd == socket_fd) {         │  │   │
│  │  │              // New client connection                         │  │   │
│  │  │              accept_client();                                 │  │   │
│  │  │          } else {                                             │  │   │
│  │  │              // Data from client → write to tty               │  │   │
│  │  │              handle_client_data(events[i].data.fd);           │  │   │
│  │  │          }                                                    │  │   │
│  │  │      }                                                        │  │   │
│  │  │  }                                                            │  │   │
│  │  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │   │
│  │                          │                                          │   │
│  │            ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐                            │   │
│  │            │             │             │                            │   │
│  │            v             v             v                            │   │
│  │  ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐                 │   │
│  │  │ Unix Socket  │ │ Unix Socket  │ │ Unix Socket  │                 │   │
│  │  │ Client 1     │ │ Client 2     │ │ Client 3     │                 │   │
│  │  │ (SSH)        │ │ (WebUI)      │ │ (hostlogger) │                 │   │
│  │  └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘                 │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                            │
│  UNIX SOCKET: /var/run/obmc-console.sock (or /run/obmc-console/ttyVUART0)  │
│                                                                            │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### IPMI SOL Protocol Details

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                          IPMI SOL Packet Format                            │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                            │
│  SOL PAYLOAD FORMAT (within RMCP+ session)                                 │
│  ─────────────────────────────────────────                                 │
│                                                                            │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │  RMCP+ Session Header                                              │    │
│  │  ┌─────────────┬─────────────┬─────────────┬────────────────────┐  │    │
│  │  │ Auth Type   │ Payload Type│ Session ID  │ Sequence Number    │  │    │
│  │  │ (1 byte)    │ (1 byte)    │ (4 bytes)   │ (4 bytes)          │  │    │
│  │  │ 0x06 (RMCP+)│ 0x01 (SOL)  │             │                    │  │    │
│  │  └─────────────┴─────────────┴─────────────┴────────────────────┘  │    │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                            │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │  SOL Payload Header (4 bytes)                                      │    │
│  │                                                                    │    │
│  │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │    │
│  │  │ Byte 0: Packet Sequence Number (4 bits ack, 4 bits send)    │   │    │
│  │  │         ┌───┬───┬───┬───┬───┬───┬───┬───┐                   │   │    │
│  │  │         │ 7 │ 6 │ 5 │ 4 │ 3 │ 2 │ 1 │ 0 │                   │   │    │
│  │  │         ├───┴───┴───┴───┼───┴───┴───┴───┤                   │   │    │
│  │  │         │  Ack Seq Num  │ Packet Seq Num│                   │   │    │
│  │  │         └───────────────┴───────────────┘                   │   │    │
│  │  │                                                             │   │    │
│  │  │ Byte 1: Accepted Character Count                            │   │    │
│  │  │         Number of characters accepted from last packet      │   │    │
│  │  │                                                             │   │    │
│  │  │ Byte 2: Operation/Status                                    │   │    │
│  │  │         ┌───┬───┬───┬───┬───┬───┬───┬───┐                   │   │    │
│  │  │         │ 7 │ 6 │ 5 │ 4 │ 3 │ 2 │ 1 │ 0 │                   │   │    │
│  │  │         └───┴───┴───┴───┴───┴───┴───┴───┘                   │   │    │
│  │  │         Bit 0: Nack packet                                  │   │    │
│  │  │         Bit 1: Ring WOR (Wake on Ring)                      │   │    │
│  │  │         Bit 2: Break detected                               │   │    │
│  │  │         Bit 3: Transmit overrun                             │   │    │
│  │  │         Bit 4: SOL deactivating                             │   │    │
│  │  │         Bit 5: Character transfer unavail                   │   │    │
│  │  │         Bit 6: SOL deactivating                             │   │    │
│  │  │         Bit 7: Reserved                                     │   │    │
│  │  │                                                             │   │    │
│  │  │ Byte 3: Reserved                                            │   │    │
│  │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │    │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                            │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │  SOL Character Data (variable length, max ~255 bytes)              │    │
│  │                                                                    │    │
│  │  Serial console data (text from/to host)                           │    │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                            │
│  SOL FLOW CONTROL:                                                         │
│  ─────────────────                                                         │
│                                                                            │
│  Client                                       BMC                          │
│     │                                          │                           │
│     │  Activate SOL (payload type 0x01)        │                           │
│     │  ──────────────────────────────────────> │                           │
│     │                                          │                           │
│     │  SOL Data (seq=1, console output)        │                           │
│     │  <────────────────────────────────────── │                           │
│     │                                          │                           │
│     │  SOL Ack (ack_seq=1, accepted=N)         │                           │
│     │  ──────────────────────────────────────> │                           │
│     │                                          │                           │
│     │  SOL Data (seq=1, keyboard input)        │                           │
│     │  ──────────────────────────────────────> │                           │
│     │                                          │                           │
│     │  SOL Ack (ack_seq=1)                     │                           │
│     │  <────────────────────────────────────── │                           │
│     │                                          │                           │
│                                                                            │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### Escape Sequence Processing

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      Console Escape Sequence Handling                      │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                            │
│  ESCAPE SEQUENCE STATE MACHINE                                             │
│  ─────────────────────────────                                             │
│                                                                            │
│  ┌──────────────┐       '~'        ┌──────────────┐                        │
│  │              │─────────────────>│              │                        │
│  │    NORMAL    │                  │ ESCAPE_START │                        │
│  │              │<─────────────────│              │                        │
│  └──────┬───────┘    other char    └──────┬───────┘                        │
│         │                                 │                                │
│         │ all other                       │ '.'                            │
│         │ characters                      v                                │
│         │                          ┌──────────────┐                        │
│         │                          │  DISCONNECT  │                        │
│         │                          │              │                        │
│         │                          │  Close conn  │                        │
│         v                          └──────────────┘                        │
│  ┌──────────────┐                                                          │
│  │   FORWARD    │                  ┌──────────────┐                        │
│  │  TO SERIAL   │                  │    BREAK     │<─── '~' then 'B'       │
│  └──────────────┘                  │              │                        │
│                                    │  Send break  │                        │
│                                    │  to serial   │                        │
│                                    └──────────────┘                        │
│                                                                            │
│  ESCAPE SEQUENCES (obmc-console-client):                                   │
│  ──────────────────────────────────────                                    │
│                                                                            │
│  │ Sequence │ Action                                      │                │
│  │──────────│─────────────────────────────────────────────│                │
│  │ ~.       │ Disconnect from console                     │                │
│  │ ~B       │ Send serial break signal                    │                │
│  │ ~?       │ Show help message                           │                │
│  │ ~~       │ Send literal '~' character                  │                │
│  │ ~^Z      │ Suspend client (if in terminal)             │                │
│                                                                            │
│  IMPLEMENTATION (console-client.c):                                        │
│  ─────────────────────────────────                                         │
│                                                                            │
│  enum escape_state { ESC_NONE, ESC_TILDE };                                │
│                                                                            │
│  void process_input(char *buf, size_t len) {                               │
│      for (i = 0; i < len; i++) {                                           │
│          char c = buf[i];                                                  │
│                                                                            │
│          if (escape_state == ESC_NONE) {                                   │
│              if (c == '~' && last_was_newline) {                           │
│                  escape_state = ESC_TILDE;                                 │
│                  continue;                                                 │
│              }                                                             │
│          } else if (escape_state == ESC_TILDE) {                           │
│              escape_state = ESC_NONE;                                      │
│              switch (c) {                                                  │
│                  case '.':                                                 │
│                      disconnect();                                         │
│                      return;                                               │
│                  case 'B':                                                 │
│                      send_break();                                         │
│                      continue;                                             │
│                  case '~':                                                 │
│                      // Forward literal ~                                  │
│                      break;                                                │
│                  default:                                                  │
│                      // Not escape, forward ~ and char                     │
│                      forward_char('~');                                    │
│                      break;                                                │
│              }                                                             │
│          }                                                                 │
│          forward_char(c);                                                  │
│          last_was_newline = (c == '\n' || c == '\r');                      │
│      }                                                                     │
│  }                                                                         │
│                                                                            │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### Host Logger Ring Buffer

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    phosphor-hostlogger Implementation                      │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                            │
│  RING BUFFER ARCHITECTURE                                                  │
│  ───────────────────────                                                   │
│                                                                            │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │  Console Data Stream                                                │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │  obmc-console-server → Unix socket → hostlogger                     │   │
│  └────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                   │                                        │
│                                   v                                        │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │  Ring Buffer (in memory)                                            │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │  struct RingBuffer {                                                │   │
│  │      char data[BUFFER_SIZE];    // e.g., 64KB                       │   │
│  │      size_t write_pos;          // Next write position              │   │
│  │      size_t read_pos;           // Current read position            │   │
│  │      size_t total_written;      // Total bytes ever written         │   │
│  │  };                                                                 │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │   │
│  │  │ ... old data ... │ write_pos │ ... space ... │ read_pos ...   │  │   │
│  │  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │   │
│  │                         ↑                            │              │   │
│  │                         │                            │              │   │
│  │                    New data appended            Oldest data         │   │
│  │                    (wraps around)               (overwritten)       │   │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                   │                                        │
│                                   │ Periodic flush / rotation              │
│                                   v                                        │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │  Persistent Log Files                                               │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │  /var/log/hostlogger/                                               │   │
│  │  ├── host_console.log        (current, up to 100KB)                 │   │
│  │  ├── host_console.log.1      (rotated)                              │   │
│  │  ├── host_console.log.2      (rotated)                              │   │
│  │  └── host_console.log.3      (oldest, deleted when 4 created)       │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │  Rotation policy:                                                   │   │
│  │    - Max file size: 100KB (configurable)                            │   │
│  │    - Max files: 4 (configurable)                                    │   │
│  │    - Rotate on size limit reached                                   │   │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                            │
│  REDFISH LOG ENTRIES                                                       │
│  ───────────────────                                                       │
│                                                                            │
│  GET /redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/HostLogger/Entries             │
│                                                                            │
│  {                                                                         │
│      "@odata.id": ".../Entries/1",                                         │
│      "EntryType": "Oem",                                                   │
│      "OemRecordFormat": "Host Logger Entry",                               │
│      "Message": "Linux version 5.10.0 (gcc version 10.2.0)...",            │
│      "Created": "2024-01-15T10:30:00+00:00",                               │
│      "Severity": "OK"                                                      │
│  }                                                                         │
│                                                                            │
│  Line parsing:                                                             │
│    - Split on newline                                                      │
│    - Each line becomes one Redfish entry                                   │
│    - Timestamp from when line was received                                 │
│    - Severity: OK for normal, Warning for errors                           │
│                                                                            │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

## Overview

    

OpenBMC uses **Dropbear** as its SSH server, a lightweight alternative to OpenSSH optimized for embedded systems. This guide covers SSH configuration, PAM integration, and security hardening.

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     SSH Architecture                            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                 │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐│
│  │                   SSH Client                                ││
│  │            (ssh, PuTTY, scripts)                            ││
│  └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘│
│                             │                                   │
│                          TCP/22                                 │
│                             │                                   │
│  ┌──────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┐│
│  │                       Dropbear                              ││
│  │                  (SSH Server Daemon)                        ││
│  │                                                             ││
│  │   ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    ││
│  │   │  Features: SSH2, RSA/DSS/ECDSA, SCP, SFTP proxy    │    ││
│  │   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    ││
│  └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘│
│                             │                                   │
│  ┌──────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┐│
│  │                         PAM                                 ││
│  │              (Pluggable Authentication Modules)             ││
│  │                                                             ││
│  │   ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────┐    ││
│  │   │pam_unix  │  │pam_ldap  │  │pam_tally2│  │pam_limits│    ││
│  │   └──────────┘  └──────────┘  └──────────┘  └──────────┘    ││
│  └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘│
│                             │                                   │
│  ┌──────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┐│
│  │                    User Database                            ││
│  │         (/etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, LDAP)                    ││
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘│
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

```mermaid
---
title: SSH Architecture
---
flowchart TB
    Client["SSH Client  
(ssh, PuTTY, scripts)"]
    Client -->|"TCP/22"| Dropbear
    Dropbear["Dropbear SSH Server  
SSH2, RSA/DSS/ECDSA, SCP, SFTP"]
    Dropbear --> PAM

    PAM["PAM (Pluggable Authentication)  
pam_unix, pam_ldap, pam_tally2, pam_limits"]

    PAM --> UserDB
    UserDB["User Database  
(/etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, LDAP)"]
```

## Setup & Configuration

    

### Build-Time Configuration (Yocto)

    

Configure SSH packages in your build:

```bitbake
# In your machine .conf or local.conf

# Include Dropbear (default SSH server)
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " dropbear"

# For OpenSSH instead of Dropbear (larger, more features)
# IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " openssh-server openssh-client"
# IMAGE_INSTALL:remove = "dropbear"

# Include SSH-related utilities
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " \
    openssh-sftp-server \
    openssh-scp \
"

# Configure dropbear options
DROPBEAR_EXTRA_ARGS ?= "-w -s"
```

### Dropbear Configuration Options

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-p [address:]port` | Listen on specified port (default 22) |
| `-w` | Disallow root logins |
| `-s` | Disable password logins (key only) |
| `-g` | Disable password logins for root |
| `-j` | Disable local port forwarding |
| `-k` | Disable remote port forwarding |
| `-a` | Allow connections to forwarded ports from any host |
| `-W` | Window size (performance tuning) |
| `-K` | Keepalive interval (seconds) |
| `-I` | Idle timeout (seconds, 0 = no timeout) |

</div>

### Runtime Configuration

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check dropbear status</span>
systemctl status dropbear

<span class="c"># View current configuration</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /etc/default/dropbear

<span class="c"># Modify dropbear arguments</span>
vi /etc/default/dropbear

<span class="c"># Restart after changes</span>
systemctl restart dropbear
```

</div></div>

### /etc/default/dropbear

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Dropbear configuration</span>
<span class="c"># DROPBEAR_EXTRA_ARGS contains additional arguments</span>

<span class="c"># Default: allow root, password auth</span>
<span class="nv">DROPBEAR_EXTRA_ARGS</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">""</span>

<span class="c"># Secure: no root login, key only</span>
<span class="nv">DROPBEAR_EXTRA_ARGS</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"-w -s"</span>

<span class="c"># Custom port</span>
<span class="nv">DROPBEAR_EXTRA_ARGS</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"-p 2222"</span>

<span class="c"># Disable port forwarding</span>
<span class="nv">DROPBEAR_EXTRA_ARGS</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"-j -k"</span>
```

</div></div>

## Authentication Configuration

    

### Password Authentication

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Enable password authentication (default)</span>
<span class="c"># Remove -s from DROPBEAR_EXTRA_ARGS</span>

<span class="c"># Change user password</span>
passwd root
passwd username

<span class="c"># Password hashes stored in /etc/shadow</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /etc/shadow
```

</div></div>

### SSH Key Authentication

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Generate host keys (done automatically)</span>
dropbearkey <span class="nt">-t</span> rsa <span class="nt">-f</span> /etc/dropbear/dropbear_rsa_host_key
dropbearkey <span class="nt">-t</span> ecdsa <span class="nt">-f</span> /etc/dropbear/dropbear_ecdsa_host_key
dropbearkey <span class="nt">-t</span> ed25519 <span class="nt">-f</span> /etc/dropbear/dropbear_ed25519_host_key

<span class="c"># User authorized keys location</span>
<span class="nb">mkdir</span> <span class="nt">-p</span> ~/.ssh
<span class="nb">chmod </span>700 ~/.ssh
<span class="nb">touch</span> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
<span class="nb">chmod </span>600 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys

<span class="c"># Add public key to authorized_keys</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"ssh-rsa AAAA...= user@host"</span> <span class="o">>></span> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
```

</div></div>

### Key-Only Authentication

    

For security, disable password authentication:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Edit dropbear defaults</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s1">'DROPBEAR_EXTRA_ARGS="-s"'</span> <span class="o">></span> /etc/default/dropbear

<span class="c"># Restart dropbear</span>
systemctl restart dropbear

<span class="c"># Test key-based login</span>
ssh <span class="nt">-i</span> ~/.ssh/id_rsa root@bmc-ip
```

</div></div>

## PAM Configuration

    

### PAM Overview

    

OpenBMC uses PAM for authentication. Configuration files are in `/etc/pam.d/`.

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># View PAM configuration for dropbear</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /etc/pam.d/dropbear
```

</div></div>

### Default PAM Configuration

    

```pam
# /etc/pam.d/dropbear
auth       include      common-auth
account    include      common-account
password   include      common-password
session    include      common-session
```

### Common Auth Configuration

    

```pam
# /etc/pam.d/common-auth
auth    [success=1 default=ignore]  pam_unix.so nullok
auth    requisite                   pam_deny.so
auth    required                    pam_permit.so
```

### Enable Account Lockout

    

```pam
# /etc/pam.d/common-auth with tally
auth    required    pam_tally2.so deny=3 unlock_time=300 onerr=fail
auth    [success=1 default=ignore]  pam_unix.so nullok
auth    requisite   pam_deny.so
auth    required    pam_permit.so
```

### LDAP Authentication

    

```bitbake
# Include LDAP PAM module
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " pam-plugin-ldap"
```

```pam
# /etc/pam.d/common-auth with LDAP
auth    sufficient  pam_ldap.so
auth    required    pam_unix.so nullok try_first_pass
```

---

## Security Hardening

    

### Disable Root SSH Login

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Option 1: Dropbear -w flag</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s1">'DROPBEAR_EXTRA_ARGS="-w"'</span> <span class="o">></span> /etc/default/dropbear
systemctl restart dropbear

<span class="c"># Option 2: PAM configuration</span>
<span class="c"># Add to /etc/pam.d/dropbear:</span>
auth    required    pam_listfile.so <span class="nv">item</span><span class="o">=</span>user <span class="nv">sense</span><span class="o">=</span>deny <span class="nv">file</span><span class="o">=</span>/etc/ssh/denied_users <span class="nv">onerr</span><span class="o">=</span>succeed
```

</div></div>

### Restrict SSH to Specific Users

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Create allowed users file</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"operator"</span> <span class="o">></span> /etc/ssh/allowed_users
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"admin"</span> <span class="o">>></span> /etc/ssh/allowed_users

<span class="c"># Add to /etc/pam.d/dropbear</span>
auth    required    pam_listfile.so <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nv">item</span><span class="o">=</span>user <span class="nv">sense</span><span class="o">=</span>allow <span class="nv">file</span><span class="o">=</span>/etc/ssh/allowed_users <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nv">onerr</span><span class="o">=</span>fail
```

</div></div>

### Change Default Port

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Edit dropbear config</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s1">'DROPBEAR_EXTRA_ARGS="-p 2222"'</span> <span class="o">></span> /etc/default/dropbear

<span class="c"># Restart service</span>
systemctl restart dropbear

<span class="c"># Connect on new port</span>
ssh <span class="nt">-p</span> 2222 root@bmc-ip
```

</div></div>

### Disable Port Forwarding

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Disable both local and remote port forwarding</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s1">'DROPBEAR_EXTRA_ARGS="-j -k"'</span> <span class="o">></span> /etc/default/dropbear
systemctl restart dropbear
```

</div></div>

### Set Connection Timeout

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Set idle timeout (300 seconds = 5 minutes)</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s1">'DROPBEAR_EXTRA_ARGS="-I 300"'</span> <span class="o">></span> /etc/default/dropbear
systemctl restart dropbear
```

</div></div>

### Host Key Verification

    

Ensure consistent host keys across updates:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Backup host keys</span>
<span class="nb">cp</span> /etc/dropbear/dropbear_<span class="k">*</span> /path/to/backup/

<span class="c"># Include in image build (recipe)</span>
SRC_URI +<span class="o">=</span> <span class="s2">"file://dropbear_rsa_host_key"</span>

do_install:append<span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="nb">install</span> <span class="nt">-m</span> 0600 <span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">WORKDIR</span><span class="k">}</span>/dropbear_rsa_host_key <span class="se">\</span>
        <span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">D</span><span class="k">}${</span><span class="nv">sysconfdir</span><span class="k">}</span>/dropbear/
<span class="o">}</span>
```

</div></div>

## Recommended Secure Configuration

    

### Production Hardening Checklist

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># 1. Key-only authentication</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s1">'DROPBEAR_EXTRA_ARGS="-s"'</span> <span class="o">></span> /etc/default/dropbear

<span class="c"># 2. Disable root password login (allow key)</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s1">'DROPBEAR_EXTRA_ARGS="-g"'</span> <span class="o">></span> /etc/default/dropbear

<span class="c"># 3. Complete lockdown (no root at all)</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s1">'DROPBEAR_EXTRA_ARGS="-w -s"'</span> <span class="o">></span> /etc/default/dropbear

<span class="c"># 4. Set idle timeout</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s1">'DROPBEAR_EXTRA_ARGS="-s -I 300"'</span> <span class="o">></span> /etc/default/dropbear

<span class="c"># 5. Apply changes</span>
systemctl restart dropbear
```

</div></div>

### Secure Dropbear Recipe

    

```bitbake
# In your machine layer
# recipes-connectivity/dropbear/dropbear_%.bbappend

FILESEXTRAPATHS:prepend := "${THISDIR}/files:"

SRC_URI += " \
    file://dropbear.default \
    file://authorized_keys \
"

do_install:append() {
    # Secure defaults
    install -m 0644 ${WORKDIR}/dropbear.default \
        ${D}${sysconfdir}/default/dropbear

    # Pre-authorized keys
    install -d ${D}/home/root/.ssh
    install -m 0600 ${WORKDIR}/authorized_keys \
        ${D}/home/root/.ssh/authorized_keys
}
```

## Managing SSH Access

    

### User Management

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Create non-root user</span>
useradd <span class="nt">-m</span> operator
passwd operator

<span class="c"># Add to admin group for sudo</span>
usermod <span class="nt">-aG</span> admin operator

<span class="c"># Add SSH key for user</span>
<span class="nb">mkdir</span> <span class="nt">-p</span> /home/operator/.ssh
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"ssh-rsa AAAA...="</span> <span class="o">></span> /home/operator/.ssh/authorized_keys
<span class="nb">chmod </span>700 /home/operator/.ssh
<span class="nb">chmod </span>600 /home/operator/.ssh/authorized_keys
<span class="nb">chown</span> <span class="nt">-R</span> operator:operator /home/operator/.ssh
```

</div></div>

### View Active Sessions

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># List SSH connections</span>
<span class="nb">who</span>

<span class="c"># Detailed connection info</span>
ss <span class="nt">-tnp</span> | <span class="nb">grep </span>ssh

<span class="c"># Kill specific session (by PID)</span>
pkill <span class="nt">-9</span> <span class="nt">-t</span> pts/0
```

### Connection Logging

```
<span class="c"># View SSH authentication logs</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> dropbear

<span class="c"># Failed login attempts</span>

<span class="c"># Successful logins</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> dropbear | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> <span class="s2">"password auth succeeded</span><span class="se">\|</span><span class="s2">pubkey auth succeeded"</span>
```

## Enabling/Disabling SSH

    

### Build-Time Disable

    

```bitbake
# Remove dropbear from image
IMAGE_INSTALL:remove = "dropbear"
```

### Runtime Disable

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Stop SSH service</span>
systemctl stop dropbear

<span class="c"># Disable SSH permanently</span>
systemctl disable dropbear

<span class="c"># Re-enable SSH</span>
systemctl <span class="nb">enable </span>dropbear
systemctl start dropbear
```

</div></div>

### Redfish Control

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Enable/disable SSH via Redfish</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> PATCH <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{"SSH": {"ProtocolEnabled": false}}'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/NetworkProtocol
```

## Troubleshooting

    

### Connection Refused

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check if dropbear is running</span>
systemctl status dropbear

<span class="c"># Check listening ports</span>
ss <span class="nt">-tlnp</span> | <span class="nb">grep </span>22

<span class="c"># Start dropbear</span>
systemctl start dropbear
```

</div></div>

### Authentication Failures

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check logs for specific errors</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> dropbear <span class="nt">-f</span>

<span class="c"># Common issues:</span>
<span class="c"># - Wrong password</span>
<span class="c"># - Key permissions (must be 600)</span>
<span class="c"># - authorized_keys format</span>
<span class="c"># - PAM configuration</span>

<span class="c"># Test with verbose client</span>
ssh <span class="nt">-vvv</span> root@bmc-ip
```

</div></div>

### Key Not Accepted

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check key permissions</span>
<span class="nb">ls</span> <span class="nt">-la</span> ~/.ssh/
<span class="c"># Should be: drwx------ .ssh</span>
<span class="c"># Should be: -rw------- authorized_keys</span>

<span class="c"># Fix permissions</span>
<span class="nb">chmod </span>700 ~/.ssh
<span class="nb">chmod </span>600 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys

<span class="c"># Check key format in authorized_keys</span>
<span class="c"># Must be single line: ssh-rsa AAAA... user@host</span>
```

</div></div>

### PAM Errors

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check PAM configuration syntax</span>
pamtester dropbear root authenticate

<span class="c"># View PAM debug output</span>
<span class="c"># Add to /etc/pam.d/dropbear:</span>
auth    required    pam_warn.so
```

</div></div>

### Host Key Changed Warning

    

When reinstalling or updating BMC:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Client side - remove old key</span>
ssh-keygen <span class="nt">-R</span> bmc-ip

<span class="c"># Or edit known_hosts manually</span>
vi ~/.ssh/known_hosts
```

</div></div>

## Security Comparison

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Feature | Dropbear | OpenSSH |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Binary size | ~110KB | ~900KB |
| Memory usage | Lower | Higher |
| SFTP | Via openssh-sftp-server | Built-in |
| Port forwarding | Supported | Full support |
| X11 forwarding | Limited | Full support |
| Key types | RSA, DSS, ECDSA, Ed25519 | All |
| Configuration | Command-line flags | sshd_config file |
| Chroot | Not built-in | Supported |

</div>
---

## Using OpenSSH Instead of Dropbear

    

While Dropbear is the default SSH server in OpenBMC, you can optionally use OpenSSH for environments requiring additional features or enterprise integration.

### Switching to OpenSSH

    

#### Build-Time Configuration

    

```bitbake
# In your machine .conf or local.conf

# Remove Dropbear and add OpenSSH
IMAGE_FEATURES += "ssh-server-openssh"
IMAGE_FEATURES:remove = "ssh-server-dropbear"

# Or manually in IMAGE_INSTALL
IMAGE_INSTALL:remove = "dropbear"
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " openssh-server openssh-client openssh-sftp-server"
```

#### OpenSSH Configuration File

    

Unlike Dropbear’s command-line flags, OpenSSH uses `/etc/ssh/sshd_config`:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># /etc/ssh/sshd_config</span>

<span class="c"># Security settings</span>
PermitRootLogin prohibit-password
PasswordAuthentication no
PubkeyAuthentication <span class="nb">yes
</span>PermitEmptyPasswords no

<span class="c"># Connection settings</span>
Port 22
AddressFamily any
ListenAddress 0.0.0.0

<span class="c"># Timeout and limits</span>
ClientAliveInterval 300
ClientAliveCountMax 3
MaxAuthTries 3
MaxSessions 10

<span class="c"># Disable unnecessary features</span>
X11Forwarding no
AllowTcpForwarding no
AllowAgentForwarding no

<span class="c"># Logging</span>
SyslogFacility AUTH
LogLevel INFO

<span class="c"># Allowed users (optional)</span>
AllowUsers root admin operator
```

</div></div>

#### Runtime Management

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check OpenSSH status</span>
systemctl status sshd

<span class="c"># Restart after config changes</span>
systemctl restart sshd

<span class="c"># Test configuration before restart</span>
sshd <span class="nt">-t</span>

<span class="c"># View logs</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> sshd
```

</div></div>

### Pros and Cons Comparison

    

#### Dropbear Advantages

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Advantage | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Smaller footprint** | ~110KB binary vs ~900KB for OpenSSH; critical for flash-constrained BMCs |
| **Lower memory usage** | Uses less RAM per connection; important for BMCs with limited memory (typically 256-512MB) |
| **Faster startup** | Quicker service initialization; relevant for BMC boot time |
| **Simpler configuration** | Command-line flags are straightforward for basic setups |
| **Battle-tested in embedded** | Widely used in routers, IoT, and embedded Linux systems |
| **Default in OpenBMC** | Well-integrated and tested with the OpenBMC ecosystem |

</div>

#### Dropbear Disadvantages

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Disadvantage | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Limited features** | No Match blocks, no chroot, limited forwarding options |
| **No sshd_config** | Configuration via flags can be awkward for complex setups |
| **Fewer cipher options** | Smaller set of supported algorithms |
| **Limited logging** | Less detailed audit logging compared to OpenSSH |
| **No certificate authentication** | Does not support OpenSSH certificate-based auth |

</div>

#### OpenSSH Advantages

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Advantage | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Rich feature set** | Full SSH specification support including all forwarding modes |
| **Flexible configuration** | `/etc/ssh/sshd_config` with Match blocks for per-user/host settings |
| **Certificate authentication** | Supports SSH certificates for scalable key management |
| **Chroot/SFTP jail** | Built-in chroot support for restricted SFTP-only users |
| **Extensive logging** | Detailed audit logs for compliance requirements |
| **Wider compatibility** | Better interoperability with enterprise SSH clients and tools |
| **Active development** | Frequent security updates from OpenBSD team |
| **FIDO2/U2F support** | Hardware security key authentication |

</div>

#### OpenSSH Disadvantages

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Disadvantage | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Larger size** | ~900KB binary; may be problematic for space-constrained BMCs |
| **Higher memory usage** | More RAM per connection (~1-2MB vs ~100KB for Dropbear) |
| **More complex** | Configuration file can be overwhelming for simple use cases |
| **Not OpenBMC default** | May require additional testing and validation |
| **Slower startup** | Slightly longer service initialization time |

</div>

### When to Use Each

    

#### Choose Dropbear When

    

* Flash storage is limited (< 32MB)
* Memory is constrained (< 256MB)
* Simple SSH access is sufficient
* Using standard OpenBMC configuration
* Boot time is critical
* No enterprise compliance requirements

#### Choose OpenSSH When

    

* Enterprise security compliance required (SOX, PCI-DSS, HIPAA)
* Need SSH certificate authentication for fleet management
* Require detailed audit logging
* Need chroot/jail for restricted users
* Using FIDO2/hardware security keys
* Advanced features like Match blocks needed
* Integrating with enterprise identity management

### OpenSSH Hardening Recipe

    

```bitbake
# recipes-connectivity/openssh/openssh_%.bbappend

FILESEXTRAPATHS:prepend := "${THISDIR}/files:"

SRC_URI += " \
    file://sshd_config \
    file://ssh_host_ed25519_key \
    file://ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub \
"

do_install:append() {
    # Install hardened sshd_config
    install -m 0644 ${WORKDIR}/sshd_config ${D}${sysconfdir}/ssh/sshd_config

    # Install pre-generated host keys (for consistent fingerprint)
    install -m 0600 ${WORKDIR}/ssh_host_ed25519_key ${D}${sysconfdir}/ssh/
    install -m 0644 ${WORKDIR}/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub ${D}${sysconfdir}/ssh/

    # Remove weak key types
    rm -f ${D}${sysconfdir}/ssh/ssh_host_dsa_key*
}
```

### Migration Checklist

    

When switching from Dropbear to OpenSSH:

* Back up existing host keys and authorized_keys
* Update Yocto configuration to include OpenSSH
* Create and test sshd_config
* Regenerate or convert host keys
* Test authentication methods (password, key)
* Verify PAM integration works correctly
* Test SFTP functionality
* Update firewall rules if port changed
* Document the change for operations team
* Update monitoring/alerting for new service name (sshd vs dropbear)
