## Overview

    

The Redfish standard provides a well-defined mechanism for vendors to expose platform-specific functionality through **OEM extensions**. In OpenBMC, OEM extensions are implemented in **bmcweb** and follow the `/Oem/` namespace pattern defined by the DMTF Redfish specification.

This guide covers the complete lifecycle: designing the namespace, creating schemas, implementing C++ route handlers with D-Bus backends, and validating with the Redfish Service Validator.

```mermaid
---
title: Redfish OEM Extension Architecture
---
flowchart TB
    client["Redfish Client"]
    client -->|"GET /redfish/v1/Oem/MyVendor/..."| bmcweb
    subgraph bmcweb["bmcweb"]
        direction LR
        router["OEM Router"]
        handler["OEM Handler  
(C++ route)"]
        router --> handler
    end
    handler -->|"D-Bus call"| dbus["D-Bus Backend  
(phosphor-* or custom service)"]
    handler -->|"JSON response"| client
```

> **ASCII-art version (for comparison)**

  <div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                 Redfish OEM Extension Architecture                    |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
|   +-----------------+                                                 |
|   | Redfish Client  |                                                 |
|   +--------+--------+                                                 |
|            | GET /redfish/v1/Oem/MyVendor/...                         |
|            v                                                          |
|   +--------+------------------------------------------+               |
|   |                     bmcweb                         |               |
|   |   +--------------+       +--------------------+    |               |
|   |   |  OEM Router  | ----> |  OEM Handler       |    |               |
|   |   +--------------+       +---------+----------+    |               |
|   +------------------------------------+---------------+               |
|                                        | D-Bus call                   |
|   +------------------------------------v---------------+               |
|   |              D-Bus Backend                          |               |
|   |     (phosphor-* services or custom daemon)          |               |
|   +----------------------------------------------------+               |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

</div>  </div>

---

## OEM Namespace Design

    

### The /Oem/ Pattern

    

Redfish uses a structured namespace to prevent collisions between vendor extensions. OEM extensions live either under the `Oem` property of a standard resource or under a dedicated `/redfish/v1/Oem//` top-level route.

> The DMTF requires that vendors use a unique identifier (typically your company name) as the `` portion. This prevents conflicts between different vendors’ extensions on the same BMC.

**Approach 1: Embedded OEM properties** – Add vendor-specific properties to an existing resource:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"@odata.id"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"/redfish/v1/Systems/system"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Oem"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"MyVendor"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"@odata.type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"#OemComputerSystem.v1_0_0.MyVendor"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"FirmwareProvisioning"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nl">"ProvisioningStatus"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Provisioned"</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

**Approach 2: Standalone OEM resources** – Create new resource trees:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
/redfish/v1/Oem/MyVendor/
    BoardInfo                              # Hardware details
    DiagnosticService/                     # Diagnostics
        Actions/
            DiagnosticService.RunTest      # Run a test (POST)
```

</div></div>

### bmcweb OEM Router

    

bmcweb uses the `BMCWEB_ROUTE` macro to register HTTP routes. The routing flow for an OEM request:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
GET /redfish/v1/Oem/MyVendor/BoardInfo
  --> Route match: "/redfish/v1/Oem/<str>/BoardInfo"
  --> Privilege check: privileges::getManager
  --> Vendor validation: reject if vendorName != oemVendorName
  --> D-Bus queries (async) --> JSON response
```

</div></div>

> Always validate the vendor name in your handler. The route pattern `/redfish/v1/Oem//...` matches any string, so your handler must reject unknown vendor namespaces with a 404 response.

### Namespace Design Guidelines

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Guideline | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| Use your company name as `` | Avoids collisions with other vendors |
| Version your schema types (e.g., `v1_0_0`) | Enables backward-compatible evolution |
| Group related resources logically | Improves discoverability |
| Follow Redfish naming conventions | `PascalCase` for properties |
| Define actions under standard `Actions` property | Consistent with Redfish patterns |

</div>
---

## CSDL and OpenAPI Schema Creation

    

OEM schemas document your extensions and enable automated validation.

### JSON Schema

    

> **Source Reference**: The example schema follows the pattern from the examples/redfish/oem-schema.json file in this repository.

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"$schema"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"$id"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"http://myvendor.com/schemas/v1/OemBoardInfo.v1_0_0.json"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"title"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"#OemBoardInfo.v1_0_0.BoardInfo"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"description"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"MyVendor OEM Board Information Resource"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"object"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"properties"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"@odata.type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nl">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"string"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nl">"const"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"#OemBoardInfo.v1_0_0.BoardInfo"</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"@odata.id"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nl">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"string"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nl">"format"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"uri"</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"Id"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nl">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"string"</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nl">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"string"</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"BoardType"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nl">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"string"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nl">"enum"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"Server"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Workstation"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Storage"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Network"</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"BoardRevision"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nl">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"string"</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"MaxPowerWatts"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nl">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"integer"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nl">"minimum"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"Status"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nl">"$ref"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"http://redfish.dmtf.org/schemas/v1/Resource.json#/definitions/Status"</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"required"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"@odata.type"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"@odata.id"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Id"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Name"</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

### CSDL Schema

    

CSDL (Common Schema Definition Language) is the XML format used by the DMTF. The Redfish Service Validator uses CSDL to validate OEM resources.

<div class="language-xml highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="cp"><?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?></span>
<span class="nt"><edmx:Edmx</span> <span class="na">xmlns:edmx=</span><span class="s">"http://docs.oasis-open.org/odata/ns/edmx"</span> <span class="na">Version=</span><span class="s">"4.0"</span><span class="nt">></span>
  <span class="nt"><edmx:Reference</span> <span class="na">Uri=</span><span class="s">"http://redfish.dmtf.org/schemas/v1/Resource_v1.xml"</span><span class="nt">></span>
    <span class="nt"><edmx:Include</span> <span class="na">Namespace=</span><span class="s">"Resource"</span><span class="nt">/></span>
    <span class="nt"><edmx:Include</span> <span class="na">Namespace=</span><span class="s">"Resource.v1_0_0"</span><span class="nt">/></span>
  <span class="nt"></edmx:Reference></span>
  <span class="nt"><edmx:DataServices></span>
    <span class="nt"><Schema</span> <span class="na">xmlns=</span><span class="s">"http://docs.oasis-open.org/odata/ns/edm"</span> <span class="na">Namespace=</span><span class="s">"OemBoardInfo"</span><span class="nt">></span>
      <span class="nt"><EntityType</span> <span class="na">Name=</span><span class="s">"BoardInfo"</span> <span class="na">BaseType=</span><span class="s">"Resource.v1_0_0.Resource"</span> <span class="na">Abstract=</span><span class="s">"true"</span><span class="nt">></span>
        <span class="nt"><Annotation</span> <span class="na">Term=</span><span class="s">"OData.Description"</span> <span class="na">String=</span><span class="s">"MyVendor board information resource."</span><span class="nt">/></span>
      <span class="nt"></EntityType></span>
    <span class="nt"></Schema></span>
    <span class="nt"><Schema</span> <span class="na">xmlns=</span><span class="s">"http://docs.oasis-open.org/odata/ns/edm"</span> <span class="na">Namespace=</span><span class="s">"OemBoardInfo.v1_0_0"</span><span class="nt">></span>
      <span class="nt"><EntityType</span> <span class="na">Name=</span><span class="s">"BoardInfo"</span> <span class="na">BaseType=</span><span class="s">"OemBoardInfo.BoardInfo"</span><span class="nt">></span>
        <span class="nt">
Name="BoardType" Type="OemBoardInfo.v1_0_0.BoardType"/>
         Name="BoardRevision" Type="Edm.String"/>
         Name="MaxPowerWatts" Type="Edm.Int64"/>
      
       Name="BoardType">
         Name="Server"/> Name="Workstation"/>
         Name="Storage"/> Name="Network"/>
      
    
  

```

### Hosting Schemas in bmcweb

    

Place schema files in the bmcweb source tree so clients can discover them:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
bmcweb/
  static/redfish/v1/schema/
    OemBoardInfo_v1.xml          # CSDL schema
  static/redfish/v1/JsonSchemas/
    OemBoardInfo.v1_0_0.json     # JSON schema
```

</div></div>

> You can host schemas externally if you prefer not to embed them in the BMC image. Set the `@odata.type` to reference your external schema URL instead.

---

## Regenerating Redfish Schemas and Generated Code

    

Much of bmcweb is **generated** from DMTF schema files rather than hand-written: C++ enums, the aggregation collection table, and the message/privilege registries are all produced from CSDL/JSON by scripts in bmcweb’s `scripts/` directory. Run this workflow after you **add or upgrade a standard schema** or **author an OEM CSDL extension**, then rebuild bmcweb so the generated headers pick up your changes.

### The Generation Pipeline

    

Run these from the root of the bmcweb source tree, in order:

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Step | Script | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `scripts/update_schemas.py` | Clones the DMTF **Redfish-Publications** repo at a pinned tag, copies the CSDL/JSON schemas in, selects the newest version of each schema with a semantic `SchemaVersion` sort, and refreshes the symlinks for the installed schemas. |
| 2 | `scripts/generate_schema_enums.py` | Parses CSDL `EnumType` definitions into C++ `enum class` types under `redfish-core/include/generated/enums/`, emitting a `NLOHMANN_JSON_SERIALIZE_ENUM` macro for each so values (de)serialize to/from JSON automatically. |
| 3 | `scripts/generate_schema_collections.py` | Extracts the top-level collection URIs and writes them to `redfish-core/include/aggregation_utils.hpp`, which Redfish Aggregation uses. |
| 4 | `scripts/parse_registries.py` | Generates the message-registry headers (for example `base_message_registry.hpp`) and `privilege_registry.hpp` from the DMTF message registries and the privilege registry. |
| 5 | `scripts/csdl-to-json-converter/` | Holds the OpenBMC config (`openbmc-config.json`) for the DMTF `csdl-to-json.py` converter, which turns OEM/local CSDL into JSON schema so your OEM types are served as JSON. See the directory’s `README.md`. |

</div>

`scripts/update_schemas.py` runs the downstream generators for you after it refreshes the schemas, so a full upgrade is usually a single command. Run the individual generators only when you are iterating on one artifact (for example, regenerating just the enums after editing an `EnumType`).

A separate helper, `scripts/generate_auth_certificates.py`, creates mTLS **test** certificates (a CA plus server and client certificates) for exercising client-certificate authentication against bmcweb – handy when validating OEM routes that require mTLS.

### Running the Workflow

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="nb">cd </span>bmcweb

<span class="c"># 1. Pull the latest DMTF schemas, re-select versions, refresh symlinks</span>
<span class="c">#    (this also invokes the generators below on your behalf)</span>
python3 scripts/update_schemas.py

<span class="c"># 2-4. Regenerate individual artifacts while iterating</span>
python3 scripts/generate_schema_enums.py
python3 scripts/generate_schema_collections.py
python3 scripts/parse_registries.py

<span class="c"># 5. (OEM) Convert your OEM CSDL to JSON with the DMTF converter,</span>
<span class="c">#    using OpenBMC's config -- see scripts/csdl-to-json-converter/README.md</span>
<span class="c">#    csdl-to-json.py --input <oem-csdl> --output <json-out> \</span>
<span class="c">#                    --config scripts/csdl-to-json-converter/openbmc-config.json</span>

<span class="c"># Rebuild so the regenerated headers are compiled in</span>
bitbake bmcweb <span class="nt">-c</span> cleansstate <span class="o">&&</span> bitbake bmcweb
```

</div></div>

> When adding an **OEM CSDL** schema, add it to the input consumed by `scripts/csdl-to-json-converter/openbmc-config.json`, then re-run the pipeline. The generated JSON is what the Redfish Service Validator (below) uses to validate your OEM resources against their schema.

> The generated headers under `redfish-core/include/generated/` are checked into the bmcweb tree. Regenerate them with these scripts rather than editing them by hand – manual edits are overwritten the next time anyone runs the pipeline.

---

## OEM Route Implementation

    

### C++ Handler Structure

    

OEM handlers in bmcweb follow the same async pattern as standard Redfish routes. Each handler receives a request, queries D-Bus for data, and populates a JSON response.

> **Source Reference**: Pattern based on bmcweb
>   
>     Route patterns: redfish-core/lib/managers.hpp
>     Privilege definitions: registries/privilege_registry.hpp

#### Step 1: Create the OEM Header File

    

Create `redfish-core/lib/oem_myvendor.hpp`:

<div class="language-cpp highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="cp">#pragma once
#include</span> <span class="cpf">"app.hpp"</span><span class="cp">
#include</span> <span class="cpf">"dbus_utility.hpp"</span><span class="cp">
#include</span> <span class="cpf">"query.hpp"</span><span class="cp">
#include</span> <span class="cpf">"registries/privilege_registry.hpp"</span><span class="cp">
#include</span> <span class="cpf">"utils/dbus_utils.hpp"</span><span class="cp">
#include</span> <span class="cpf"><nlohmann/json.hpp></span><span class="cp">
#include</span> <span class="cpf"><sdbusplus/asio/property.hpp></span><span class="cp">
</span>
<span class="k">namespace</span> <span class="n">redfish</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
<span class="k">constexpr</span> <span class="k">const</span> <span class="kt">char</span><span class="o">*</span> <span class="n">oemVendorName</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">"MyVendor"</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="c1">// OEM Root: GET /redfish/v1/Oem/MyVendor/</span>
<span class="kr">inline</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="n">requestRoutesOemRoot</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">App</span><span class="o">&</span> <span class="n">app</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="n">BMCWEB_ROUTE</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">app</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="s">"/redfish/v1/Oem/<str>/"</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="p">.</span><span class="n">privileges</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">redfish</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">privileges</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">getManager</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="p">.</span><span class="n">methods</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">boost</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">beast</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">http</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">verb</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">get</span><span class="p">)(</span>
            <span class="p">[](</span><span class="k">const</span> <span class="n">crow</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">Request</span><span class="o">&</span><span class="p">,</span>
               <span class="k">const</span> <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">shared_ptr</span><span class="o"><</span><span class="n">bmcweb</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">AsyncResp</span><span class="o">>&</span> <span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="p">,</span>
               <span class="k">const</span> <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">string</span><span class="o">&</span> <span class="n">vendorName</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">{</span>
                <span class="k">if</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="n">vendorName</span> <span class="o">!=</span> <span class="n">oemVendorName</span><span class="p">)</span>
                <span class="p">{</span>
                    <span class="n">messages</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">resourceNotFound</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">,</span>
                                               <span class="s">"OemRoot"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">vendorName</span><span class="p">);</span>
                    <span class="k">return</span><span class="p">;</span>
                <span class="p">}</span>
                <span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">jsonValue</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s">"@odata.type"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span>
                    <span class="s">"#OemServiceRoot.v1_0_0.OemServiceRoot"</span><span class="p">;</span>
                <span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">jsonValue</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s">"@odata.id"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span>
                    <span class="s">"/redfish/v1/Oem/MyVendor"</span><span class="p">;</span>
                <span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">jsonValue</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s">"Id"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">"MyVendor"</span><span class="p">;</span>
                <span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">jsonValue</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s">"Name"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span>
                    <span class="s">"MyVendor OEM Extensions"</span><span class="p">;</span>
                <span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">jsonValue</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s">"BoardInfo"</span><span class="p">][</span><span class="s">"@odata.id"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span>
                    <span class="s">"/redfish/v1/Oem/MyVendor/BoardInfo"</span><span class="p">;</span>
            <span class="p">});</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
<span class="p">}</span> <span class="c1">// namespace redfish</span>
```

</div></div>

#### Step 2: Implement a Resource with D-Bus Backend

    

Read properties from a D-Bus service and map them to JSON:

<div class="language-cpp highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c1">// Board Info: GET /redfish/v1/Oem/MyVendor/BoardInfo</span>
<span class="kr">inline</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">requestRoutesBoardInfo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">App</span><span class="o">&</span> <span class="n">app</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="n">BMCWEB_ROUTE</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">app</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="s">"/redfish/v1/Oem/<str>/BoardInfo"</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="p">.</span><span class="n">privileges</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">redfish</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">privileges</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">getManager</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="p">.</span><span class="n">methods</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">boost</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">beast</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">http</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">verb</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">get</span><span class="p">)(</span>
            <span class="p">[](</span><span class="k">const</span> <span class="n">crow</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">Request</span><span class="o">&</span><span class="p">,</span>
               <span class="k">const</span> <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">shared_ptr</span><span class="o"><</span><span class="n">bmcweb</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">AsyncResp</span><span class="o">>&</span> <span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="p">,</span>
               <span class="k">const</span> <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">string</span><span class="o">&</span> <span class="n">vendorName</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">{</span>
                <span class="k">if</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="n">vendorName</span> <span class="o">!=</span> <span class="n">oemVendorName</span><span class="p">)</span>
                <span class="p">{</span>
                    <span class="n">messages</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">resourceNotFound</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">,</span>
                                               <span class="s">"BoardInfo"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">vendorName</span><span class="p">);</span>
                    <span class="k">return</span><span class="p">;</span>
                <span class="p">}</span>
                <span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">jsonValue</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s">"@odata.type"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span>
                    <span class="s">"#OemBoardInfo.v1_0_0.BoardInfo"</span><span class="p">;</span>
                <span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">jsonValue</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s">"@odata.id"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span>
                    <span class="s">"/redfish/v1/Oem/MyVendor/BoardInfo"</span><span class="p">;</span>
                <span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">jsonValue</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s">"Id"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">"BoardInfo"</span><span class="p">;</span>
                <span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">jsonValue</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s">"Name"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">"Board Information"</span><span class="p">;</span>

                <span class="c1">// Async D-Bus query for manufacturer</span>
                <span class="n">sdbusplus</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">asio</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">getProperty</span><span class="o"><</span><span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">string</span><span class="o">></span><span class="p">(</span>
                    <span class="o">*</span><span class="n">crow</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">connections</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">systemBus</span><span class="p">,</span>
                    <span class="s">"xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Manager"</span><span class="p">,</span>
                    <span class="s">"/xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/board"</span><span class="p">,</span>
                    <span class="s">"xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Decorator.Asset"</span><span class="p">,</span>
                    <span class="s">"Manufacturer"</span><span class="p">,</span>
                    <span class="p">[</span><span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="p">](</span><span class="k">const</span> <span class="n">boost</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">system</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">error_code</span><span class="o">&</span> <span class="n">ec</span><span class="p">,</span>
                                <span class="k">const</span> <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">string</span><span class="o">&</span> <span class="n">manufacturer</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">{</span>
                        <span class="k">if</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ec</span><span class="p">)</span>
                        <span class="p">{</span>
                            <span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">jsonValue</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s">"Manufacturer"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">"Unknown"</span><span class="p">;</span>
                            <span class="k">return</span><span class="p">;</span>
                        <span class="p">}</span>
                        <span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">jsonValue</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s">"Manufacturer"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">manufacturer</span><span class="p">;</span>
                    <span class="p">});</span>

                <span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">jsonValue</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s">"BoardType"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">"Server"</span><span class="p">;</span>
                <span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">jsonValue</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s">"Status"</span><span class="p">][</span><span class="s">"State"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">"Enabled"</span><span class="p">;</span>
                <span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">jsonValue</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s">"Status"</span><span class="p">][</span><span class="s">"Health"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">"OK"</span><span class="p">;</span>
            <span class="p">});</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
```

</div></div>

#### Step 3: Implement a POST Action

    

Actions allow clients to trigger operations on the BMC:

<div class="language-cpp highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c1">// POST /redfish/v1/Oem/MyVendor/DiagnosticService/Actions/DiagnosticService.RunTest</span>
<span class="kr">inline</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">requestRoutesRunTest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">App</span><span class="o">&</span> <span class="n">app</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="n">BMCWEB_ROUTE</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">app</span><span class="p">,</span>
        <span class="s">"/redfish/v1/Oem/<str>/DiagnosticService/Actions/"</span>
        <span class="s">"DiagnosticService.RunTest"</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="p">.</span><span class="n">privileges</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">redfish</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">privileges</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">postManager</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="p">.</span><span class="n">methods</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">boost</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">beast</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">http</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">verb</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">post</span><span class="p">)(</span>
            <span class="p">[](</span><span class="k">const</span> <span class="n">crow</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">Request</span><span class="o">&</span> <span class="n">req</span><span class="p">,</span>
               <span class="k">const</span> <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">shared_ptr</span><span class="o"><</span><span class="n">bmcweb</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">AsyncResp</span><span class="o">>&</span> <span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="p">,</span>
               <span class="k">const</span> <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">string</span><span class="o">&</span> <span class="n">vendorName</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">{</span>
                <span class="k">if</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="n">vendorName</span> <span class="o">!=</span> <span class="n">oemVendorName</span><span class="p">)</span>
                <span class="p">{</span>
                    <span class="n">messages</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">resourceNotFound</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="s">"Action"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="s">"RunTest"</span><span class="p">);</span>
                    <span class="k">return</span><span class="p">;</span>
                <span class="p">}</span>
                <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">optional</span><span class="o"><</span><span class="kt">uint32_t</span><span class="o">></span> <span class="n">testId</span><span class="p">;</span>
                <span class="k">if</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="o">!</span><span class="n">json_util</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">readJsonAction</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">req</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="s">"TestId"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">testId</span><span class="p">))</span>
                <span class="p">{</span>
                    <span class="k">return</span><span class="p">;</span>
                <span class="p">}</span>
                <span class="k">if</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="o">!</span><span class="n">testId</span> <span class="o">||</span> <span class="o">*</span><span class="n">testId</span> <span class="o"><</span> <span class="mi">1</span> <span class="o">||</span> <span class="o">*</span><span class="n">testId</span> <span class="o">></span> <span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">)</span>
                <span class="p">{</span>
                    <span class="n">messages</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">actionParameterValueError</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">,</span>
                        <span class="n">testId</span> <span class="o">?</span> <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">to_string</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="n">testId</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">:</span> <span class="s">"null"</span><span class="p">,</span>
                        <span class="s">"TestId"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="s">"DiagnosticService.RunTest"</span><span class="p">);</span>
                    <span class="k">return</span><span class="p">;</span>
                <span class="p">}</span>
                <span class="n">crow</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">connections</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">systemBus</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">async_method_call</span><span class="p">(</span>
                    <span class="p">[</span><span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="p">](</span><span class="k">const</span> <span class="n">boost</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">system</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">error_code</span><span class="o">&</span> <span class="n">ec</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">{</span>
                        <span class="k">if</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ec</span><span class="p">)</span>
                        <span class="p">{</span>
                            <span class="n">messages</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">internalError</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">);</span>
                            <span class="k">return</span><span class="p">;</span>
                        <span class="p">}</span>
                        <span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">result</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">boost</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">beast</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">http</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">status</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">accepted</span><span class="p">);</span>
                        <span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">jsonValue</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s">"TaskState"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">"Running"</span><span class="p">;</span>
                    <span class="p">},</span>
                    <span class="s">"xyz.openbmc_project.OEM.DiagService"</span><span class="p">,</span>
                    <span class="s">"/xyz/openbmc_project/oem/diag"</span><span class="p">,</span>
                    <span class="s">"xyz.openbmc_project.OEM.DiagService"</span><span class="p">,</span>
                    <span class="s">"RunTest"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="o">*</span><span class="n">testId</span><span class="p">);</span>
            <span class="p">});</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
```

</div></div>

### Register Routes in bmcweb

    

<div class="language-cpp highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c1">// In src/webserver_main.cpp</span>
<span class="cp">#include</span> <span class="cpf">"oem_myvendor.hpp"</span><span class="cp">
</span>
<span class="c1">// In the route registration section:</span>
<span class="n">redfish</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">requestRoutesOemRoot</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">app</span><span class="p">);</span>
<span class="n">redfish</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">requestRoutesBoardInfo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">app</span><span class="p">);</span>
<span class="n">redfish</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">requestRoutesRunTest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">app</span><span class="p">);</span>
```

</div></div>

### D-Bus Backend

    

Your OEM handler reads from or writes to a D-Bus service. You can use an existing phosphor-* service or create a custom daemon:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
bmcweb OEM Handler  <-- D-Bus -->  Backend Service (xyz.openbmc_project.OEM.MyService)
  sdbusplus::asio::getProperty()                    |
  async_method_call()                               v
                                            Hardware / sysfs / devmem
```

</div></div>

> For simple OEM properties that map to existing inventory or sensor D-Bus objects, you do not need a custom D-Bus service. Use `xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Manager` or sensor services directly.

### JSON Response Best Practices

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Property | Requirement | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@odata.type` | Required. Versioned type. | `#OemBoardInfo.v1_0_0.BoardInfo` |
| `@odata.id` | Required. Full URI. | `/redfish/v1/Oem/MyVendor/BoardInfo` |
| `Id` | Required. Short identifier. | `BoardInfo` |
| `Name` | Required. Human-readable. | `Board Information` |
| `Status` | Recommended. Standard Redfish. | `{"State":"Enabled","Health":"OK"}` |
| `Actions` | If applicable. | `{"#MyAction.Do":{"target":"..."}}` |

</div>
---

## Building and Deploying

    

### Yocto Integration

    

Create a bbappend to include your OEM handler in the bmcweb build:

```bitbake
# recipes-phosphor/bmcweb/bmcweb_%.bbappend
FILESEXTRAPATHS:prepend := "${THISDIR}/files:"

SRC_URI += " \
    file://oem_myvendor.hpp \
    file://0001-Add-MyVendor-OEM-routes.patch \
"

do_configure:prepend() {
    cp ${WORKDIR}/oem_myvendor.hpp ${S}/redfish-core/lib/oem_myvendor.hpp
}
```

The patch file registers your routes in `webserver_main.cpp`.

### Build and Test

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Build bmcweb with OEM changes</span>
bitbake bmcweb <span class="nt">-c</span> cleansstate <span class="o">&&</span> bitbake bmcweb

<span class="c"># Full image build for QEMU</span>
bitbake obmc-phosphor-image

<span class="c"># Or copy binary directly for quick testing</span>
scp build/tmp/work/<span class="k">*</span>/bmcweb/<span class="k">*</span>/build/bmcweb root@<bmc-ip>:/usr/bin/
ssh root@<bmc-ip> systemctl restart bmcweb
```

</div></div>
---

## Redfish Service Validator Testing

    

The DMTF Redfish Service Validator verifies that your Redfish implementation conforms to the specification.

### Install and Run

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
git clone https://github.com/DMTF/Redfish-Service-Validator.git
<span class="nb">cd </span>Redfish-Service-Validator
pip3 <span class="nb">install</span> <span class="nt">-r</span> requirements.txt

<span class="c"># Validate the entire service</span>
python3 RedfishServiceValidator.py <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">--ip</span> https://<bmc-ip> <span class="nt">--authtype</span> Basic <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">--username</span> root <span class="nt">--password</span> 0penBmc <span class="nt">--nochkcert</span>

<span class="c"># Validate a specific OEM resource</span>
python3 RedfishServiceValidator.py <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">--ip</span> https://<bmc-ip> <span class="nt">--authtype</span> Basic <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">--username</span> root <span class="nt">--password</span> 0penBmc <span class="nt">--nochkcert</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">--uri</span> /redfish/v1/Oem/MyVendor/BoardInfo
```

</div></div>

### Validating with Custom OEM Schemas

    

Provide a local schema directory to validate OEM resources against your custom schemas:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="nb">mkdir</span> <span class="nt">-p</span> oem-schemas/
<span class="nb">cp </span>OemBoardInfo_v1.xml oem-schemas/

python3 RedfishServiceValidator.py <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">--ip</span> https://<bmc-ip> <span class="nt">--authtype</span> Basic <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">--username</span> root <span class="nt">--password</span> 0penBmc <span class="nt">--nochkcert</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">--schemadir</span> ./oem-schemas/ <span class="nt">--logdir</span> ./validation-results/
```

</div></div>

> The validator reports OEM resources as “unknown type” if you do not provide custom schemas. This is expected. Supply your CSDL schemas via `--schemadir` to get full property validation.

### Interpreting Results

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Check | What It Validates |
| --- | --- |
| `@odata.type` present | Every resource must declare its type |
| `@odata.id` matches URI | The `@odata.id` value must match the request URI |
| Required properties | All `required` properties in the schema are present |
| Property types | Values match declared types (string, integer, etc.) |
| Enum values | Enum properties contain only allowed values |
| Links resolve | Navigation properties return valid resources |

</div>

### Manual Curl Validation

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="nb">alias </span><span class="nv">bmcurl</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s1">'curl -k -s -u root:0penBmc'</span>

<span class="c"># Test OEM root</span>
bmcurl https://localhost/redfish/v1/Oem/MyVendor/ | jq <span class="nb">.</span>

<span class="c"># Test a specific resource</span>
bmcurl https://localhost/redfish/v1/Oem/MyVendor/BoardInfo | jq <span class="nb">.</span>

<span class="c"># Test an action</span>
bmcurl <span class="nt">-X</span> POST <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{"TestId": 1}'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Oem/MyVendor/DiagnosticService/Actions/DiagnosticService.RunTest | jq <span class="nb">.</span>
```

</div></div>

### Automated Test Script

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="nb">cd </span>docs/examples/redfish/
./test_oem_resource.sh <bmc-ip> root 0penBmc
```

</div></div>

## Extending Existing Resources with OEM Properties

    

You can add OEM properties to existing standard Redfish resources by patching the handler:

<div class="language-cpp highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c1">// In redfish-core/lib/systems.cpp (or via bbappend patch)</span>
<span class="c1">// Inside handleSystemsGet, after standard properties:</span>

<span class="n">nlohmann</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">json</span><span class="o">&</span> <span class="n">oem</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">jsonValue</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s">"Oem"</span><span class="p">][</span><span class="s">"MyVendor"</span><span class="p">];</span>
<span class="n">oem</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s">"@odata.type"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">"#OemComputerSystem.v1_0_0.MyVendor"</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="n">sdbusplus</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">asio</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">getProperty</span><span class="o"><</span><span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">string</span><span class="o">></span><span class="p">(</span>
    <span class="o">*</span><span class="n">crow</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">connections</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">systemBus</span><span class="p">,</span>
    <span class="s">"xyz.openbmc_project.OEM.MyService"</span><span class="p">,</span>
    <span class="s">"/xyz/openbmc_project/oem/system"</span><span class="p">,</span>
    <span class="s">"xyz.openbmc_project.OEM.SystemInfo"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="s">"ProvisioningStatus"</span><span class="p">,</span>
    <span class="p">[</span><span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="p">](</span><span class="k">const</span> <span class="n">boost</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">system</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">error_code</span><span class="o">&</span> <span class="n">ec</span><span class="p">,</span>
                <span class="k">const</span> <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">string</span><span class="o">&</span> <span class="n">status</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">{</span>
        <span class="k">if</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="o">!</span><span class="n">ec</span><span class="p">)</span>
            <span class="n">asyncResp</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">jsonValue</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s">"Oem"</span><span class="p">][</span><span class="s">"MyVendor"</span><span class="p">]</span>
                <span class="p">[</span><span class="s">"FirmwareProvisioning"</span><span class="p">][</span><span class="s">"ProvisioningStatus"</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">status</span><span class="p">;</span>
    <span class="p">});</span>
```

</div></div>

## Troubleshooting

    

### Route Not Found (404)

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
systemctl status bmcweb
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> bmcweb | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> <span class="s2">"route</span><span class="se">\|</span><span class="s2">oem"</span>
bmcurl https://localhost/redfish/v1/Oem/MyVendor/    <span class="c"># trailing slash matters</span>
```

</div></div>

### D-Bus Errors

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
busctl list | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> oem
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.OEM.MyService
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Manager <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/board <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Decorator.Asset Manufacturer
```

</div></div>

### Debug Logging

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Edit /lib/systemd/system/bmcweb.service, add:</span>
<span class="c"># Environment="BMCWEB_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG"</span>
systemctl daemon-reload <span class="o">&&</span> systemctl restart bmcweb
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> bmcweb <span class="nt">-f</span>
```

</div></div>

### Common Mistakes

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Issue | Cause | Solution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 404 on OEM route | Route not registered | Add registration in `webserver_main.cpp` |
| Empty JSON response | Handler returns before async callbacks | Use `asyncResp` shared_ptr pattern |
| 500 Internal Server Error | D-Bus service not running | Verify with `busctl` |
| Missing `@odata.type` | Forgot to set type in handler | Always set `@odata.type` first |
| Validator warns “unknown type” | No custom schema provided | Supply CSDL via `--schemadir` |

</div>
---

## Examples

    

Working examples are available in the [examples/redfish](https://github.com/MichaelTien8901/openbmc-guide-tutorial/tree/main/docs/examples/redfish) directory:

* `oem_resource.hpp` – Complete OEM handler with root, BoardInfo, DiagnosticService, and RunTest action
* `oem-schema.json` – JSON Schema for the OEM BoardInfo resource
* `test_oem_resource.sh` – Automated test script for validating OEM endpoints

> Use the example files as a starting point. Copy `oem_resource.hpp`, replace `MyVendor` with your vendor name, and modify the resource properties and D-Bus paths to match your hardware platform.

## Overview

    

**MCTP (Management Component Transport Protocol)** and **PLDM (Platform Level Data Model)** are DMTF standards for platform management communication. They provide a modern, scalable alternative to IPMI for device-to-device management in data center environments.

### Why MCTP/PLDM?

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Feature | IPMI | MCTP/PLDM |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Message size | 256 bytes max | 64KB+ |
| Transport | KCS, BT, IPMB | I2C, PCIe, SMBus, USB, Serial |
| Extensibility | OEM codes | Typed messages with PDR |
| Discovery | Manual | Automatic endpoint discovery |
| Sensors | SDR-based | PDR with rich metadata |
| Security | Limited | SPDM integration |

</div>

## MCTP Protocol Deep Dive

    

### MCTP Packet Format

    

Every MCTP packet follows this structure:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+
| Byte 0        | Byte 1        | Byte 2        | Byte 3        |
+---------------+---------------+---------------+---------------+
| Header Ver(4) | Dest EID (8)  | Source EID(8) | SOM|EOM|PktSeq|
| Rsvd (4)      |               |               | TO |Tag (3)   |
+---------------+---------------+---------------+---------------+
|                    Message Payload                            |
|                    (variable length)                          |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|                    Integrity Check (optional)                 |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
```

</div></div>

#### Header Fields

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Field | Bits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Header Version | 4 | Always 0x1 for MCTP v1.x |
| Reserved | 4 | Must be 0 |
| Destination EID | 8 | Target endpoint ID (0x00-0xFF) |
| Source EID | 8 | Sender endpoint ID |
| SOM | 1 | Start of Message flag |
| EOM | 1 | End of Message flag |
| Packet Sequence | 2 | Sequence number for fragmentation |
| TO | 1 | Tag Owner (1=requester, 0=responder) |
| Message Tag | 3 | Unique tag per outstanding request |

</div>

#### Special Endpoint IDs

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| EID | Name | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0x00 | Null EID | Unassigned endpoint |
| 0x01-0x07 | Reserved | Reserved by DMTF |
| 0x08 | Default BMC | Common BMC address |
| 0x09-0xFE | General | Assignable to endpoints |
| 0xFF | Broadcast | All endpoints on network |

</div>

### MCTP Message Types

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Type | Value | Description | Specification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MCTP Control | 0x00 | Endpoint management | DSP0236 |
| PLDM | 0x01 | Platform management | DSP0240 |
| NCSI | 0x02 | Network controller | DSP0222 |
| Ethernet | 0x03 | Ethernet frames | DSP0236 |
| NVMe-MI | 0x04 | NVMe management | NVM Express |
| SPDM | 0x05 | Security protocol | DSP0274 |
| Secure SPDM | 0x06 | Secured SPDM | DSP0277 |
| Vendor Defined (PCI) | 0x7E | PCI vendor ID | DSP0236 |
| Vendor Defined (IANA) | 0x7F | IANA enterprise | DSP0236 |

</div>

### MCTP Control Messages

    

MCTP Control (type 0x00) manages the MCTP network:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
MCTP Control Message Format:
+-------+-------+-------+-------+
| IC|MsgType(7)| RqDI| Command |
| (1)          | (1) |Instance |
|              |     | ID (5)  |
+-------+-------+-------+-------+
|          Command Data         |
+-------------------------------+
```

</div></div>

#### Control Commands

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Command | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Set Endpoint ID | 0x01 | Assign EID to endpoint |
| Get Endpoint ID | 0x02 | Query endpoint’s EID |
| Get Endpoint UUID | 0x03 | Get unique identifier |
| Get MCTP Version | 0x04 | Query MCTP version support |
| Get Message Type Support | 0x05 | Query supported message types |
| Get Vendor Defined Message Support | 0x06 | Query vendor extensions |
| Resolve Endpoint ID | 0x07 | Map EID to physical address |
| Allocate Endpoint IDs | 0x08 | Request EID pool |
| Routing Information Update | 0x09 | Update routing tables |
| Get Routing Table Entries | 0x0A | Query routing table |
| Prepare Endpoint Discovery | 0x0B | Reset discovery state |
| Endpoint Discovery | 0x0C | Discover endpoints |
| Discovery Notify | 0x0D | Notify discovery complete |

</div>

### Message Fragmentation

    

MCTP fragments large messages across multiple packets:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
Large Message (> MTU):
+------------------+------------------+------------------+
|  Packet 1        |  Packet 2        |  Packet 3        |
|  SOM=1, EOM=0    |  SOM=0, EOM=0    |  SOM=0, EOM=1    |
|  Seq=0           |  Seq=1           |  Seq=2           |
|  [Payload 1]     |  [Payload 2]     |  [Payload 3]     |
+------------------+------------------+------------------+

Reassembled at receiver:
+----------------------------------------------------------+
|  Complete Message = Payload 1 + Payload 2 + Payload 3    |
+----------------------------------------------------------+
```

</div></div>

#### MTU by Transport

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Transport | Minimum MTU | Typical MTU |
| --- | --- | --- |
| I2C/SMBus | 64 bytes | 64-256 bytes |
| PCIe VDM | 64 bytes | 64-4096 bytes |
| Serial | 64 bytes | 64-256 bytes |
| USB | 64 bytes | 512 bytes |

</div>
---

## MCTP Transport Bindings

    

### I2C/SMBus Binding (DSP0237)

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
I2C MCTP Packet Structure:
+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+
| Slave | Cmd   | Byte  | Src   | Hdr   | MCTP Header   |
| Addr  | Code  | Count | Addr  | Ver   | + Payload     |
| (7+1) | 0x0F  | (8)   | (7+1) | (4+4) |               |
+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+---------------+
|                    Payload Data                       |
+-------------------------------------------------------+
| PEC (optional)                                        |
+-------------------------------------------------------+
```

</div></div>

#### I2C Configuration

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Create MCTP I2C interface</span>
mctp <span class="nb">link </span>add mctpi2c1 <span class="nb">type </span>i2c bus 1

<span class="c"># Set interface up</span>
mctp <span class="nb">link set </span>mctpi2c1 up

<span class="c"># Set local address</span>
mctp addr add 8 dev mctpi2c1

<span class="c"># Verify configuration</span>
mctp <span class="nb">link </span>show
mctp addr show
```

</div></div>

#### Device Tree for I2C MCTP

    

```dts
&i2c1 {
    status = "okay";

    /* MCTP-capable device at address 0x50 */
    mctp_device@50 {
        compatible = "mctp-i2c-controller";
        reg = <0x50>;
    };
};
```

### PCIe VDM Binding (DSP0238)

    

PCIe Vendor Defined Messages carry MCTP over PCIe:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
PCIe VDM TLP Format:
+-------+-------+-------+-------+
| Fmt   | Type  | TC    | Attr  |  <- TLP Header
| (3)   | (5)   | (3)   | (2)   |
+-------+-------+-------+-------+
| Length        | Requester ID  |
+---------------+---------------+
| Tag   | Message Code          |  <- VDM Header
| (8)   | Vendor ID (16)        |
+-------+-----------------------+
| MCTP Transport Header         |  <- MCTP Packet
+-------------------------------+
| MCTP Payload                  |
+-------------------------------+
```

</div></div>

#### PCIe VDM Configuration

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># PCIe MCTP typically auto-discovered</span>
<span class="c"># Check for PCIe MCTP devices</span>
lspci <span class="nt">-vvv</span> | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> mctp

<span class="c"># MCTP over PCIe uses kernel MCTP stack</span>
mctp <span class="nb">link</span>
```

</div></div>

### Serial Binding (DSP0239)

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
Serial MCTP Frame:
+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+
| Sync  | Rev   | Byte  | MCTP Packet   |
| 0x7E  | (8)   | Count |               |
+-------+-------+-------+---------------+
| FCS (16-bit CRC)                      |
+---------------------------------------+
```

</div></div>
---

## PLDM Protocol Deep Dive

    

### PLDM Message Format

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
PLDM Message Structure:
+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+
| MCTP  |PLDM Hdr       | PLDM Payload                  |
| Msg   |               |                               |
| Type  |               |                               |
| 0x01  |               |                               |
+-------+-------+-------+-------------------------------+

PLDM Header:
+-------+-------+-------+-------+
| Rq|D|IID(5)   | Hdr   | PLDM  |
| (1)(1)        | Ver(2)| Type  |
|               |       | (6)   |
+---------------+-------+-------+
| Command Code (8)              |
+-------------------------------+
```

</div></div>

#### Header Fields

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Field | Bits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rq (Request) | 1 | 1=Request, 0=Response |
| D (Datagram) | 1 | 1=No response expected |
| Instance ID | 5 | Request/response correlation |
| Header Version | 2 | Always 0b00 |
| PLDM Type | 6 | Message type (0-63) |
| Command Code | 8 | Type-specific command |

</div>

### PLDM Types

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Type | Name | Specification | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Base | DSP0240 | Discovery, TID, versions |
| 1 | SMBIOS | DSP0246 | SMBIOS table transfer |
| 2 | Monitoring & Control | DSP0248 | Sensors, effecters, events |
| 3 | BIOS Control | DSP0247 | BIOS attributes |
| 4 | FRU Data | DSP0257 | Field Replaceable Unit data |
| 5 | Firmware Update | DSP0267 | Firmware update protocol |
| 6 | Redfish Device Enablement | DSP0218 | Redfish over PLDM |
| 63 | OEM | - | Vendor-specific |

</div>

### PLDM Type 0: Base Commands

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Command | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SetTID | 0x01 | Set Terminus ID |
| GetTID | 0x02 | Get Terminus ID |
| GetPLDMVersion | 0x03 | Query PLDM type versions |
| GetPLDMTypes | 0x04 | Query supported PLDM types |
| GetPLDMCommands | 0x05 | Query commands for a type |
| SelectPLDMVersion | 0x06 | Negotiate version |
| NegotiateTransferParameters | 0x07 | Set transfer sizes |
| MultipartSend | 0x08 | Send large data |
| MultipartReceive | 0x09 | Receive large data |

</div>

#### Example: Get TID

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Request GetTID (Command 0x02)</span>
pldmtool raw <span class="nt">-m</span> 9 <span class="nt">-d</span> 0x80 0x00 0x02

<span class="c"># Response format:</span>
<span class="c"># [0]: Completion Code (0x00 = success)</span>
<span class="c"># [1]: TID value</span>
```

</div></div>

### PLDM Type 2: Monitoring & Control

    

This type handles sensors, effecters, and events.

#### Sensor Commands

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Command | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GetSensorReading | 0x11 | Read numeric sensor |
| GetSensorThresholds | 0x12 | Get threshold values |
| SetSensorThresholds | 0x13 | Set threshold values |
| RestoreSensorThresholds | 0x14 | Restore defaults |
| GetSensorHysteresis | 0x15 | Get hysteresis value |
| SetSensorHysteresis | 0x16 | Set hysteresis value |
| InitNumericSensor | 0x17 | Initialize sensor |
| GetStateSensorReading | 0x21 | Read state sensor |

</div>

#### Effecter Commands

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Command | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SetNumericEffecterValue | 0x31 | Set numeric effecter |
| GetNumericEffecterValue | 0x32 | Get numeric effecter value |
| SetStateEffecterStates | 0x39 | Set state effecter |
| GetStateEffecterStates | 0x3A | Get state effecter |

</div>

#### Event Commands

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Command | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PlatformEventMessage | 0x0A | Send platform event |
| PollForPlatformEventMessage | 0x0B | Poll for events |
| EventMessageSupported | 0x0C | Query event support |
| EventMessageBufferSize | 0x0D | Query buffer size |

</div>

### PLDM Type 5: Firmware Update

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Command | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| QueryDeviceIdentifiers | 0x01 | Get device IDs |
| GetFirmwareParameters | 0x02 | Get FW info |
| RequestUpdate | 0x10 | Start update |
| PassComponentTable | 0x13 | Send component list |
| UpdateComponent | 0x14 | Update single component |
| RequestFirmwareData | 0x15 | Request FW chunk |
| TransferComplete | 0x16 | Transfer done |
| VerifyComplete | 0x17 | Verification done |
| ApplyComplete | 0x18 | Application done |
| ActivateFirmware | 0x1A | Activate new FW |
| GetStatus | 0x1B | Query update status |
| CancelUpdateComponent | 0x1C | Cancel component update |
| CancelUpdate | 0x1D | Cancel entire update |

</div>

## Platform Data Records (PDR)

    

PDRs describe the platform’s sensors, effecters, and associations.

### PDR Structure

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
PDR Header (common to all PDRs):
+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+
| Record Handle (32 bits)                                       |
+---------------+---------------+---------------+---------------+
| PDR Hdr Ver(8)| PDR Type (8)  | Record Change#| Data Len (16) |
+---------------+---------------+---------------+---------------+
|                    PDR-specific data                          |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
```

</div></div>

### PDR Types

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Type | Name | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Terminus Locator | Maps TID to MCTP EID |
| 2 | Numeric Sensor | Numeric sensor definition |
| 3 | Numeric Sensor Initialization | Init parameters |
| 4 | State Sensor | State sensor definition |
| 5 | State Sensor Initialization | Init parameters |
| 6 | Sensor Auxiliary Names | Sensor name strings |
| 9 | OEM Device | Vendor-specific device |
| 10 | OEM | Vendor-specific PDR |
| 11 | Numeric Effecter | Numeric effecter definition |
| 12 | Numeric Effecter Initialization | Init parameters |
| 13 | State Effecter | State effecter definition |
| 14 | State Effecter Initialization | Init parameters |
| 15 | Effecter Auxiliary Names | Effecter name strings |
| 20 | Entity Association | Entity hierarchy |
| 21 | Entity Auxiliary Names | Entity name strings |
| 22 | OEM Entity ID | Vendor entity types |

</div>

### Numeric Sensor PDR Example

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
Numeric Sensor PDR (Type 2):
+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+
| Terminus Handle (16) | Sensor ID (16)                         |
+---------------+---------------+---------------+---------------+
| Entity Type(16)       | Entity Instance (16)                  |
+---------------+---------------+---------------+---------------+
| Container ID (16)     | Sensor Init | Auxiliary Names         |
+---------------+---------------+---------------+---------------+
| Base Unit (8)         | Unit Modifier (8) | Rate Unit (8)     |
+-----------------------+-----------------------+---------------+
| ... additional fields for ranges, thresholds, etc.            |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
```

</div></div>

### State Sets

    

State sensors/effecters use predefined state sets:

<div class="table-wrapper">
| State Set ID | Name | Example States |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Health State | Normal, Warning, Critical |
| 2 | Availability | Available, Unavailable |
| 3 | Operational Status | Enabled, Disabled |
| 4 | Configuration State | Valid, Invalid |
| 11 | Link State | Up, Down |
| 15 | Power Device | On, Off, Powering On, Powering Off |
| 192 | Boot Progress | Primary Processor Init, Memory Init, PCI Init |
| 196 | System Power State | Off, On, Standby |

</div>

### Querying PDRs

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get all PDRs</span>
pldmtool platform getpdr <span class="nt">-t</span> all <span class="nt">-m</span> 9

<span class="c"># Get specific PDR types</span>
pldmtool platform getpdr <span class="nt">-t</span> numericSensorPDR <span class="nt">-m</span> 9
pldmtool platform getpdr <span class="nt">-t</span> stateSensorPDR <span class="nt">-m</span> 9
pldmtool platform getpdr <span class="nt">-t</span> numericEffecterPDR <span class="nt">-m</span> 9
pldmtool platform getpdr <span class="nt">-t</span> stateEffecterPDR <span class="nt">-m</span> 9
pldmtool platform getpdr <span class="nt">-t</span> terminusLocatorPDR <span class="nt">-m</span> 9
pldmtool platform getpdr <span class="nt">-t</span> entityAssociationPDR <span class="nt">-m</span> 9

<span class="c"># Get PDR by record handle</span>
pldmtool platform getpdr <span class="nt">-d</span> 1 <span class="nt">-m</span> 9
pldmtool platform getpdr <span class="nt">-d</span> 2 <span class="nt">-m</span> 9
```

### libmctp

    

Low-level MCTP packet handling:

<div class="language-c highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c1">// Key libmctp structures</span>
<span class="k">struct</span> <span class="n">mctp</span><span class="p">;</span>                    <span class="c1">// MCTP context</span>
<span class="k">struct</span> <span class="n">mctp_binding</span><span class="p">;</span>            <span class="c1">// Transport binding</span>
<span class="k">struct</span> <span class="n">mctp_pktbuf</span><span class="p">;</span>             <span class="c1">// Packet buffer</span>

<span class="c1">// Transport bindings</span>
<span class="k">struct</span> <span class="n">mctp_binding_i2c</span><span class="p">;</span>        <span class="c1">// I2C/SMBus</span>
<span class="k">struct</span> <span class="n">mctp_binding_astlpc</span><span class="p">;</span>     <span class="c1">// ASPEED LPC</span>
<span class="k">struct</span> <span class="n">mctp_binding_serial</span><span class="p">;</span>     <span class="c1">// Serial</span>

<span class="c1">// Key functions</span>
<span class="n">mctp_init</span><span class="p">();</span>                    <span class="c1">// Initialize context</span>
<span class="n">mctp_set_rx_all</span><span class="p">();</span>              <span class="c1">// Set receive callback</span>
<span class="n">mctp_message_tx</span><span class="p">();</span>              <span class="c1">// Transmit message</span>
<span class="n">mctp_binding_set_tx_enabled</span><span class="p">();</span>  <span class="c1">// Enable transmission</span>
```

</div></div>

### libpldm

    

PLDM message encoding and decoding:

<div class="language-c highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c1">// Request encoding</span>
<span class="n">encode_get_tid_req</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">instance_id</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="o">&</span><span class="n">request</span><span class="p">);</span>
<span class="n">encode_get_sensor_reading_req</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">instance_id</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">sensor_id</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="o">&</span><span class="n">request</span><span class="p">);</span>
<span class="n">encode_set_state_effecter_states_req</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">instance_id</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">effecter_id</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="p">...);</span>

<span class="c1">// Response decoding</span>
<span class="n">decode_get_tid_resp</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">response</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="o">&</span><span class="n">tid</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="o">&</span><span class="n">completion_code</span><span class="p">);</span>
<span class="n">decode_get_sensor_reading_resp</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">response</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="o">&</span><span class="n">reading</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="o">&</span><span class="n">status</span><span class="p">);</span>

<span class="c1">// PDR handling</span>
<span class="n">pldm_pdr_init</span><span class="p">();</span>                    <span class="c1">// Initialize PDR repository</span>
<span class="n">pldm_pdr_add</span><span class="p">();</span>                     <span class="c1">// Add PDR record</span>
<span class="n">pldm_pdr_find_record</span><span class="p">();</span>             <span class="c1">// Find PDR by handle</span>
<span class="n">pldm_entity_association_tree_init</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="c1">// Entity tree</span>
```

</div></div>

## Setup & Configuration

    

### Build-Time Configuration (Yocto)

    

```bitbake
# In your machine .conf or local.conf

# Include MCTP/PLDM components
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " \
    mctp \
    mctpd \
    libpldm \
    pldm \
"

# Configure MCTP transport options
EXTRA_OEMESON:pn-mctpd = " \
    -Di2c=enabled \
    -Dastlpc=enabled \
    -Dserial=disabled \
"

# Configure PLDM options
EXTRA_OEMESON:pn-pldm = " \
    -Dtransport-implementation=af-mctp \
    -Doem-ibm=disabled \
    -Dsoftoff=enabled \
    -Dhost-eid=9 \
    -Dlibpldmresponder=enabled \
"
```

### Meson Build Options (pldm)

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `transport-implementation` | af-mctp | Transport (af-mctp or mctp-demux) |
| `oem-ibm` | disabled | IBM OEM PLDM extensions |
| `softoff` | enabled | Host soft power off via PLDM |
| `host-eid` | 9 | Default host endpoint ID |
| `libpldmresponder` | enabled | BMC as PLDM responder |
| `system-specific-bios-json` | disabled | Custom BIOS JSON location |

</div>

### Meson Build Options (mctpd)

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `i2c` | enabled | I2C/SMBus transport |
| `astlpc` | enabled | ASPEED LPC transport |
| `serial` | disabled | Serial transport |
| `tests` | disabled | Build unit tests |

</div>

### Kernel Configuration

    

```kconfig
# Enable MCTP in kernel
CONFIG_MCTP=y
CONFIG_MCTP_FLOWS=y

# Transport drivers
CONFIG_I2C_MCTP=m
CONFIG_MCTP_SERIAL=m
```

### Runtime Configuration

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check MCTP daemon status</span>
systemctl status mctpd

<span class="c"># Check PLDM daemon status</span>
systemctl status pldmd

<span class="c"># View logs</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> mctpd <span class="nt">-f</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> pldmd <span class="nt">-f</span>

<span class="c"># Enable debug logging</span>
systemctl edit pldmd
<span class="c"># Add: Environment="PLDM_VERBOSITY=debug"</span>
```

</div></div>

## MCTP Configuration

    

### Managing MCTP Networks

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># List all MCTP interfaces</span>
mctp <span class="nb">link</span>

<span class="c"># Example output:</span>
<span class="c"># dev        net  eid    up</span>
<span class="c"># mctpi2c1   1    8      yes</span>
<span class="c"># mctplpc0   2    8      yes</span>

<span class="c"># Set interface up</span>
mctp <span class="nb">link set </span>mctpi2c1 up

<span class="c"># Set interface down</span>
mctp <span class="nb">link set </span>mctpi2c1 down

<span class="c"># View interface details</span>
ip <span class="nb">link </span>show <span class="nb">type </span>mctp
```

</div></div>

### Endpoint Management

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># List all endpoints</span>
mctp endpoint

<span class="c"># Add local endpoint address</span>
mctp addr add 8 dev mctpi2c1

<span class="c"># Remove endpoint address</span>
mctp addr del 8 dev mctpi2c1

<span class="c"># View endpoint routing</span>
mctp route
```

</div></div>
