## PLDM Configuration

    

### PDR Repository

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># List all PDRs</span>
pldmtool platform getpdr <span class="nt">-t</span> all

<span class="c"># Count PDRs</span>
pldmtool platform getpdr <span class="nt">-t</span> all | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-c</span> <span class="s2">"recordHandle"</span>

<span class="c"># Export PDRs to file</span>
pldmtool platform getpdr <span class="nt">-t</span> all <span class="o">></span> /tmp/pdr_dump.txt
```

</div></div>

### Common PLDM Commands

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># === Base Commands (Type 0) ===</span>

<span class="c"># Get terminus ID</span>
pldmtool base getTID <span class="nt">-m</span> 9

<span class="c"># Get PLDM version for type 0</span>
pldmtool base getPLDMVersion <span class="nt">-m</span> 9 <span class="nt">-t</span> 0

<span class="c"># Get supported PLDM types</span>
pldmtool base getPLDMTypes <span class="nt">-m</span> 9

<span class="c"># Get commands for a PLDM type</span>
pldmtool base getPLDMCommands <span class="nt">-m</span> 9 <span class="nt">-t</span> 0
pldmtool base getPLDMCommands <span class="nt">-m</span> 9 <span class="nt">-t</span> 2

<span class="c"># === Platform Commands (Type 2) ===</span>

<span class="c"># Get numeric sensor reading</span>
pldmtool platform getSensorReading <span class="nt">-m</span> 9 <span class="nt">-i</span> 1

<span class="c"># Get state sensor reading</span>
pldmtool platform getStateSensorReadings <span class="nt">-m</span> 9 <span class="nt">-i</span> 5

<span class="c"># Set state effecter</span>
pldmtool platform setStateEffecterStates <span class="nt">-m</span> 9 <span class="nt">-i</span> 1 <span class="nt">-c</span> 1 <span class="nt">-d</span> 1

<span class="c"># Get PDR by type</span>
pldmtool platform getPDR <span class="nt">-m</span> 9 <span class="nt">-t</span> sensorPDR
pldmtool platform getPDR <span class="nt">-m</span> 9 <span class="nt">-t</span> effecterPDR

<span class="c"># === Firmware Update Commands (Type 5) ===</span>

<span class="c"># Get firmware parameters</span>
pldmtool fw_update GetFirmwareParameters <span class="nt">-m</span> 9

<span class="c"># Query device identifiers</span>
pldmtool fw_update QueryDeviceIdentifiers <span class="nt">-m</span> 9
```

</div></div>

### Raw PLDM Commands

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Send raw PLDM command</span>
<span class="c"># Format: pldmtool raw -m <eid> -d <byte1> <byte2> ...</span>
<span class="c"># Byte format: 0xRR 0xTT 0xCC [payload...]</span>
<span class="c">#   RR = Request/Instance (0x80 for request, IID=0)</span>
<span class="c">#   TT = PLDM Type</span>
<span class="c">#   CC = Command Code</span>

<span class="c"># GetTID (Type 0, Command 0x02)</span>
pldmtool raw <span class="nt">-m</span> 9 <span class="nt">-d</span> 0x80 0x00 0x02

<span class="c"># GetPLDMTypes (Type 0, Command 0x04)</span>
pldmtool raw <span class="nt">-m</span> 9 <span class="nt">-d</span> 0x80 0x00 0x04

<span class="c"># GetSensorReading (Type 2, Command 0x11) for sensor ID 1</span>
pldmtool raw <span class="nt">-m</span> 9 <span class="nt">-d</span> 0x80 0x02 0x11 0x01 0x00 0x00
```

</div></div>

## Device Integration Examples

    

### NVMe over MCTP

    

NVMe-MI (Management Interface) uses MCTP for out-of-band management:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Discover NVMe endpoints</span>
mctp endpoint

<span class="c"># NVMe-MI over MCTP uses message type 0x04</span>
<span class="c"># Query via pldmtool if device supports PLDM</span>
pldmtool base getPLDMTypes <span class="nt">-m</span> 11

<span class="c"># For native NVMe-MI, use nvme-cli with MCTP transport</span>
nvme list <span class="nt">--mctp</span>
```

</div></div>

### GPU Management

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Configure GPU endpoint (I2C bus 3, address 0x51)</span>
mctp addr add 10 dev mctpi2c3

<span class="c"># Verify endpoint responds</span>
pldmtool base getTID <span class="nt">-m</span> 10

<span class="c"># Query GPU sensors</span>
pldmtool platform getSensorReading <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">-i</span> 1   <span class="c"># Temperature</span>
pldmtool platform getSensorReading <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">-i</span> 2   <span class="c"># Power</span>

<span class="c"># Query GPU capabilities</span>
pldmtool base getPLDMTypes <span class="nt">-m</span> 10
```

</div></div>

### PSU Management

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Configure PSU endpoint</span>
mctp addr add 11 dev mctpi2c4

<span class="c"># Read PSU telemetry via PLDM sensors</span>
pldmtool platform getSensorReading <span class="nt">-m</span> 11 <span class="nt">-i</span> 1   <span class="c"># Input voltage</span>
pldmtool platform getSensorReading <span class="nt">-m</span> 11 <span class="nt">-i</span> 2   <span class="c"># Output voltage</span>
pldmtool platform getSensorReading <span class="nt">-m</span> 11 <span class="nt">-i</span> 3   <span class="c"># Output current</span>
pldmtool platform getSensorReading <span class="nt">-m</span> 11 <span class="nt">-i</span> 4   <span class="c"># Temperature</span>
```

</div></div>

### Host CPU/BIOS Communication

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Host typically at EID 9</span>
<span class="c"># PLDM for BIOS attributes (Type 3)</span>
pldmtool bios GetBIOSTable <span class="nt">-m</span> 9 <span class="nt">-t</span> StringTable
pldmtool bios GetBIOSTable <span class="nt">-m</span> 9 <span class="nt">-t</span> AttributeTable
pldmtool bios GetBIOSTable <span class="nt">-m</span> 9 <span class="nt">-t</span> AttributeValueTable

<span class="c"># Get specific BIOS attribute</span>
pldmtool bios GetBIOSAttributeCurrentValueByHandle <span class="nt">-m</span> 9 <span class="nt">-a</span> <span class="s2">"boot_order"</span>
```

## PLDM Firmware Update

    

### Firmware Update Flow

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
BMC (Update Agent)                    Device (FD)
      |                                    |
      |  1. QueryDeviceIdentifiers         |
      |------------------------------------>|
      |  <------ Device IDs ---------------|
      |                                    |
      |  2. GetFirmwareParameters          |
      |------------------------------------>|
      |  <------ Component info ------------|
      |                                    |
      |  3. RequestUpdate                  |
      |------------------------------------>|
      |  <------ RequestUpdateResponse -----|
      |                                    |
      |  4. PassComponentTable             |
      |------------------------------------>|
      |  <------ PassComponentTableResp ----|
      |                                    |
      |  5. UpdateComponent (repeat)       |
      |------------------------------------>|
      |                                    |
      |  6. RequestFirmwareData            |
      |<------------------------------------|
      |  ------ Firmware chunk ------------>|
      |     (repeat until complete)        |
      |                                    |
      |  7. TransferComplete               |
      |<------------------------------------|
      |  ------ Acknowledgment ------------>|
      |                                    |
      |  8. VerifyComplete                 |
      |<------------------------------------|
      |  ------ Acknowledgment ------------>|
      |                                    |
      |  9. ApplyComplete                  |
      |<------------------------------------|
      |  ------ Acknowledgment ------------>|
      |                                    |
      |  10. ActivateFirmware              |
      |------------------------------------>|
      |  <------ ActivateResponse ---------|
      |                                    |
```

</div></div>

### Firmware Update Commands

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Query device capabilities</span>
pldmtool fw_update QueryDeviceIdentifiers <span class="nt">-m</span> 9
pldmtool fw_update GetFirmwareParameters <span class="nt">-m</span> 9

<span class="c"># Start update process</span>
pldmtool fw_update RequestUpdate <span class="nt">-m</span> 9 <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-c</span> 1000 <span class="se">\ </span>     <span class="c"># max_transfer_size</span>
    <span class="nt">-n</span> 1 <span class="se">\ </span>        <span class="c"># number of components</span>
    <span class="nt">-m</span> 0 <span class="se">\ </span>        <span class="c"># max_outstanding_requests</span>
    <span class="nt">-s</span> 1           <span class="c"># package_data_length</span>

<span class="c"># The actual update is typically handled by pldmd</span>
<span class="c"># or a dedicated update agent</span>
```

</div></div>

## Event Handling

    

### PLDM Event Types

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Event Class | ID | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sensor Event | 0x00 | Sensor threshold/state changed |
| Effecter Event | 0x01 | Effecter state changed |
| Redfish Task Executed | 0x02 | Redfish task complete |
| Redfish Message | 0x03 | Redfish log message |
| PDR Repository Changed | 0x04 | PDR update |
| Message Poll | 0x05 | Async message waiting |
| Heartbeat | 0x06 | Keepalive |

</div>

### Sensor Event Format

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
Sensor Event Data:
+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+
| Sensor ID (16)        | Sensor Event Class (8)        |
+-----------------------+-------------------------------+
| Event Data (variable based on class)                  |
+-------------------------------------------------------+
```

</div></div>

### Event Monitoring

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Subscribe to PLDM events via D-Bus</span>
busctl monitor xyz.openbmc_project.PLDM

<span class="c"># Poll for platform events</span>
pldmtool platform pollForPlatformEventMessage <span class="nt">-m</span> 9

<span class="c"># Check event message buffer size</span>
pldmtool platform getEventMessageBufferSize <span class="nt">-m</span> 9
```

</div></div>

## Host-BMC PLDM Coordination

    

On platforms where the host runs its own PLDM stack, `pldmd` coordinates state
and inventory with it:

* **PDR exchange** — `HostPDRHandler` issues `GetPDR` when the host powers on, folds the host’s entity-association PDRs into the BMC entity tree, and creates D-Bus inventory objects (for example `xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item.CpuCore`) through `CustomDBus`.
* **Event forwarding** — `DbusToPLDMEvent` converts D-Bus state-sensor `PropertiesChanged` signals into PLDM `PlatformEventMessage`s sent to the host.
* **Graceful shutdown** — `pldmSoftPowerOff.service` (`SoftPowerOff`) reads `softoff_config.json` (TID / entity type / state-set ID), sends `SetStateEffecterStates`, then waits for the host’s PLDM state-sensor event with a timeout before a hard power-off.

(Verify class/service names against your `pldm` version.)

---

```
<span class="c"># Service: xyz.openbmc_project.MCTP</span>
<span class="c"># Path: /xyz/openbmc_project/mctp/<network>/<eid></span>

busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.MCTP

<span class="c"># Example output:</span>
<span class="c"># └─/xyz/openbmc_project</span>
<span class="c">#   └─/xyz/openbmc_project/mctp</span>

<span class="c">#       ├─/xyz/openbmc_project/mctp/1/8</span>
<span class="c">#       └─/xyz/openbmc_project/mctp/1/9</span>

<span class="c"># Inspect endpoint</span>
busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.MCTP <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/mctp/1/9

<span class="c"># Properties:</span>
<span class="c">#   .Address          - Physical address</span>
<span class="c">#   .NetworkId        - MCTP network ID</span>
<span class="c">#   .EID              - Endpoint ID</span>
```

## Troubleshooting

    

### MCTP Connectivity Issues

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># 1. Check kernel MCTP support</span>
lsmod | <span class="nb">grep </span>mctp
modprobe mctp

<span class="c"># 2. Verify I2C bus</span>
i2cdetect <span class="nt">-l</span>
i2cdetect <span class="nt">-y</span> 1   <span class="c"># Check bus 1</span>

<span class="c"># 3. Check MCTP link status</span>
mctp <span class="nb">link
</span>mctp addr

<span class="c"># 4. View mctpd logs</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> mctpd <span class="nt">-f</span>

<span class="c"># 5. Enable debug logging</span>
systemctl edit mctpd
<span class="c"># Add: Environment="MCTP_LOG_LEVEL=debug"</span>
systemctl restart mctpd

<span class="c"># 6. Check MCTP network device</span>
ip <span class="nb">link </span>show <span class="nb">type </span>mctp
ip <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="nb">link </span>show mctpi2c1
```

</div></div>

### PLDM Communication Issues

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># 1. Verify endpoint responds</span>
pldmtool base getTID <span class="nt">-m</span> 9

<span class="c"># 2. Check PLDM daemon status</span>
systemctl status pldmd

<span class="c"># 3. View PLDM logs</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> pldmd <span class="nt">-f</span>

<span class="c"># 4. Test raw PLDM command</span>
pldmtool raw <span class="nt">-m</span> 9 <span class="nt">-d</span> 0x80 0x00 0x04  <span class="c"># GetPLDMTypes</span>

<span class="c"># 5. Increase timeout</span>
pldmtool <span class="nt">--timeout</span> 30000 base getTID <span class="nt">-m</span> 9
```

</div></div>

### No Endpoints Discovered

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># 1. Check static configuration</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /etc/mctp/static-endpoints.json

<span class="c"># 2. Manually add endpoint</span>
mctp addr add 9 dev mctpi2c1

<span class="c"># 3. Verify I2C device responds</span>
i2cdetect <span class="nt">-y</span> 1
i2ctransfer <span class="nt">-y</span> 1 w1@0x50 0x00

<span class="c"># 4. Check discovery</span>
mctp ctrl discover mctpi2c1
```

</div></div>

### Command Timeouts

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># 1. Check endpoint health</span>
mctp stats

<span class="c"># 2. Increase command timeout</span>
pldmtool <span class="nt">--timeout</span> 60000 <<span class="nb">command</span><span class="o">></span>

<span class="c"># 3. Check for I2C bus contention</span>
dmesg | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> i2c

<span class="c"># 4. Verify clock speed</span>
<span class="c"># Some devices need slower I2C clock</span>
```

</div></div>

### PDR Issues

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># 1. Check PDR repository</span>
pldmtool platform getpdr <span class="nt">-t</span> all

<span class="c"># 2. Verify terminus locator</span>
pldmtool platform getpdr <span class="nt">-t</span> terminusLocatorPDR

<span class="c"># 3. Check PDR JSON configuration</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /usr/share/pldm/pdr/<span class="k">*</span>.json

<span class="c"># 4. Rebuild PDR repository</span>
systemctl restart pldmd
```

</div></div>

## Security Considerations

    

### Authentication with SPDM

    

MCTP/PLDM integrates with SPDM for device authentication:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># SPDM runs over MCTP (message type 0x05)</span>
<span class="c"># See the SPDM Guide for details</span>

<span class="c"># Verify device certificate</span>
<span class="c"># Challenge device</span>
<span class="c"># Establish secure session</span>
```

</div></div>

### Access Control

    

<div class="language-xml highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"><!-- /etc/dbus-1/system.d/pldm.conf --></span>
<span class="cp"><!DOCTYPE busconfig PUBLIC
 "-//freedesktop//DTD D-BUS Bus Configuration 1.0//EN"
 "http://www.freedesktop.org/standards/dbus/1.0/busconfig.dtd"></span>
<span class="nt"><busconfig></span>
    <span class="nt">
user="root">
         own="xyz.openbmc_project.PLDM"/>
         send_destination="xyz.openbmc_project.PLDM"/>
    
     context="default">
         send_destination="xyz.openbmc_project.PLDM"
               send_interface="org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties"
               send_member="Get"/>
         send_destination="xyz.openbmc_project.PLDM"
               send_interface="org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties"
               send_member="GetAll"/>
    

```

### Network Isolation

    

```
# MCTP networks are isolated by network ID
# EIDs are only unique within a network

# Use separate networks for different security domains
# Network 1: Host communication
# Network 2: Peripheral devices
```

## Enabling/Disabling

    

### Build-Time Disable

    

```bitbake
# Remove MCTP/PLDM packages
IMAGE_INSTALL:remove = "mctp mctpd pldm libpldm"
```

### Runtime Disable

    

```
# Stop PLDM daemon
systemctl stop pldmd
systemctl disable pldmd

# Stop MCTP daemon
systemctl stop mctpd
systemctl disable mctpd

# Verify stopped
systemctl status pldmd mctpd
```

## Examples

    

Working examples are available in the [examples/mctp-pldm](https://github.com/MichaelTien8901/openbmc-guide-tutorial/tree/main/docs/examples/mctp-pldm) directory:

* `mctp_health_check.sh` - Verify MCTP/PLDM stack connectivity
* `pldm_discovery.sh` - Discover and characterize PLDM endpoints
* `pldm_sensors.sh` - Read numeric and state sensors
* `pldm_pdr_dump.sh` - Dump Platform Descriptor Records
* `pldm_bios.sh` - Read BIOS tables and attributes (Type 3)
* `pldm_fwupdate.sh` - Query firmware update capabilities (Type 5)
* `config/static-endpoints.json` - Static MCTP endpoint configuration
* `config/pdr.json` - PDR repository definition
* `config/pldm-dbus.conf` - D-Bus access policy for PLDM

---

The `pldm` repo carries vendor OEM extensions under `oem/`, conditionally compiled
per platform: **IBM** (DMA-based file I/O for PELs / LIDs / dumps / certificates,
in-band code update, PCIe-slot VPD, host lamp test), **Ampere** (CPER and
sensor-event decoding to SEL/Redfish), **Meta** (system / BIOS-SEL / memory /
POST-error decoding, power-control file I/O), and **NVIDIA**. When porting to one
of these platforms, enable the matching `oem` build option. (Verify against your
`pldm` version.)

## Deep Dive

    

Advanced implementation details for MCTP/PLDM developers.

### MCTP Message Fragmentation

    

Large PLDM messages are fragmented across multiple MCTP packets:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    MCTP Message Fragmentation                           │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   PLDM Message (e.g., 500 bytes):                                       │
│   ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│   │                    PLDM Request/Response Data                  │    │
│   │                         (500 bytes)                            │    │
│   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                   │                                     │
│                                   ▼                                     │
│   MCTP Fragmentation (MTU = 64 bytes per binding):                      │
│                                                                         │
│   Packet 1 (SOM=1, EOM=0):                                              │
│   ┌────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ Header │ Data[0:63]                                             │   │
│   │ SOM=1  │                                                        │   │
│   │ EOM=0  │                                                        │   │
│   │ Seq=0  │                                                        │   │
│   └────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
│   Packet 2 (SOM=0, EOM=0):                                              │
│   ┌────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ Header │ Data[64:127]                                           │   │
│   │ SOM=0  │                                                        │   │
│   │ EOM=0  │                                                        │   │
│   │ Seq=1  │                                                        │   │
│   └────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                          ...                                            │
│   Packet N (SOM=0, EOM=1):                                              │
│   ┌────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ Header │ Data[remaining]                                        │   │
│   │ SOM=0  │                                                        │   │
│   │ EOM=1  │ ← End of Message                                       │   │
│   │ Seq=7  │                                                        │   │
│   └────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
│   Header Flags:                                                         │
│   ├── SOM (Start of Message) - First fragment                           │
│   ├── EOM (End of Message) - Last fragment                              │
│   ├── Seq (Sequence) - 2-bit, wraps 0-3                                 │
│   └── Tag - Correlates request/response                                 │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### PLDM Message Type Encoding

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    PLDM Message Structure                               │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   Request Message Format:                                               │
│   ┌────────┬──────────┬──────────┬─────────────────────────────────┐    │
│   │ Byte 0 │  Byte 1  │  Byte 2  │        Bytes 3-N                │    │
│   ├────────┼──────────┼──────────┼─────────────────────────────────┤    │
│   │Instance│   Type   │ Command  │       Request Data              │    │
│   │ ID/Rq  │(0-6 DMTF)│          │                                 │    │
│   └────────┴──────────┴──────────┴─────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                         │
│   Byte 0 breakdown:                                                     │
│   ┌─────┬─────┬──────────────┐                                          │
│   │ D/Rq│ Rsvd│ Instance ID  │                                          │
│   │ 1b  │ 1b  │    5 bits    │                                          │
│   └─────┴─────┴──────────────┘                                          │
│   D=0: Request, D=1: Response                                           │
│   Rq=1: Request message, Rq=0: Response message                         │
│                                                                         │
│   Response Message Format:                                              │
│   ┌────────┬──────────┬──────────┬───────────┬──────────────────┐       │
│   │Instance│   Type   │ Command  │Completion │   Response Data  │       │
│   │ ID/D=1 │          │          │   Code    │                  │       │
│   └────────┴──────────┴──────────┴───────────┴──────────────────┘       │
│                                                                         │
│   PLDM Types:                                                           │
│   ┌──────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│   │ Type │ Description                                            │     │
│   ├──────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤     │
│   │  0   │ PLDM Messaging Control and Discovery                   │     │
│   │  1   │ SMBIOS (not commonly used)                             │     │
│   │  2   │ Platform Monitoring and Control (sensors, PDRs)        │     │
│   │  3   │ BIOS Control and Configuration                         │     │
│   │  4   │ FRU Data                                               │     │
│   │  5   │ Firmware Update                                        │     │
│   │  6   │ Redfish Device Enablement                              │     │
│   └──────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">

## Overview

    

**SPDM (Security Protocol and Data Model)** is a DMTF standard (DSP0274) that provides device identity verification and firmware attestation through certificate-based authentication and cryptographic measurements. It enables the BMC to verify that platform components (GPUs, NICs, storage devices, power supplies) are authentic and running trusted firmware.

### Why SPDM?

    

Modern data centers face supply chain security threats including:

* Counterfeit components
* Firmware tampering
* Hardware implants
* Unauthorized firmware modifications

SPDM addresses these by providing:

* **Device Identity**: X.509 certificate chains prove device authenticity
* **Firmware Attestation**: Cryptographic measurements verify firmware integrity
* **Secure Communication**: Encrypted sessions protect management traffic
* **Mutual Authentication**: Both BMC and device can verify each other

### SPDM Versions

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Version | DSP0274 | Key Features |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1.0 | 2019 | Base attestation, challenge-response |
| 1.1 | 2020 | Mutual authentication, key exchange |
| 1.2 | 2022 | Chunking, multi-key, extended algorithms |
| 1.3 | 2024 | Event notifications, measurement extensions |

</div>

### Component Roles

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Component | Role |
| --- | --- |
| **Requester** | Initiates SPDM exchanges (BMC is typically the requester) |
| **Responder** | Responds to SPDM requests (devices being attested) |
| **spdmd** | OpenBMC daemon managing SPDM sessions and attestation |
| **libspdm** | DMTF reference implementation library |
| **mctpd** | MCTP transport daemon providing message delivery |

## SPDM Protocol Deep Dive

    

### Message Format

    

Every SPDM message follows a common header structure:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+
|  Byte 0       |  Byte 1       |  Byte 2       |  Byte 3       |
+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+
| SPDMVersion   | RequestResCode|   Param1      |   Param2      |
+---------------+---------------+---------------+---------------+
|                    Payload (variable length)                  |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
```

</div></div>

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Field | Size | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SPDMVersion` | 1 byte | Major.Minor version (e.g., 0x12 = v1.2) |
| `RequestResponseCode` | 1 byte | Message type identifier |
| `Param1` | 1 byte | Message-specific parameter |
| `Param2` | 1 byte | Message-specific parameter |
| `Payload` | Variable | Message-specific data |

</div>

### Request/Response Codes

    

#### Base Commands (0x01-0x0F)

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Code | Request | Response | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0x04 | GET_VERSION | VERSION (0x04) | Query supported SPDM versions |
| 0x61 | GET_CAPABILITIES | CAPABILITIES (0x61) | Query device capabilities |
| 0x63 | NEGOTIATE_ALGORITHMS | ALGORITHMS (0x63) | Negotiate crypto algorithms |
| 0x01 | GET_DIGESTS | DIGESTS (0x01) | Get certificate chain digests |
| 0x02 | GET_CERTIFICATE | CERTIFICATE (0x02) | Retrieve certificate chain |
| 0x03 | CHALLENGE | CHALLENGE_AUTH (0x03) | Challenge-response auth |

</div>

#### Measurement Commands (0x60-0x6F)

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Code | Request | Response | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0x60 | GET_MEASUREMENTS | MEASUREMENTS (0x60) | Retrieve firmware measurements |

</div>

#### Session Commands (0xE0-0xEF)

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Code | Request | Response | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0xE4 | KEY_EXCHANGE | KEY_EXCHANGE_RSP (0xE4) | Establish session key |
| 0xE5 | FINISH | FINISH_RSP (0xE5) | Complete session establishment |
| 0xE6 | PSK_EXCHANGE | PSK_EXCHANGE_RSP (0xE6) | Pre-shared key exchange |
| 0xE7 | PSK_FINISH | PSK_FINISH_RSP (0xE7) | Complete PSK session |
| 0xEC | END_SESSION | END_SESSION_ACK (0xEC) | Terminate session |
| 0xEE | HEARTBEAT | HEARTBEAT_ACK (0xEE) | Keep session alive |
| 0xEF | KEY_UPDATE | KEY_UPDATE_ACK (0xEF) | Rotate session keys |

</div>

#### Error Response (0x7F)

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Error Code | Name | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0x01 | InvalidRequest | Request format invalid |
| 0x02 | Busy | Device temporarily unavailable |
| 0x03 | UnexpectedRequest | Request out of sequence |
| 0x04 | Unspecified | Generic error |
| 0x05 | DecryptError | Session decryption failed |
| 0x06 | UnsupportedRequest | Request not supported |
| 0x07 | RequestInFlight | Previous request pending |
| 0x41 | InvalidSession | Session ID invalid |
| 0x42 | SessionLimitExceeded | Too many active sessions |

</div>
---

## Protocol Flow

    

### Discovery and Capability Negotiation

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
BMC (Requester)                              Device (Responder)
      |                                              |
      |  1. GET_VERSION                              |
      |--------------------------------------------->|
      |  Version = 0x10 (request v1.0 base)          |
      |                                              |
      |  VERSION                                     |
      |<---------------------------------------------|
      |  VersionNumberEntryCount = 3                 |
      |  Entries: [0x10, 0x11, 0x12]  (v1.0-1.2)     |
      |                                              |
      |  2. GET_CAPABILITIES                         |
      |--------------------------------------------->|
      |  CTExponent = 12 (timeout = 2^12 µs)         |
      |  Flags = CERT_CAP | CHAL_CAP | MEAS_CAP      |
      |                                              |
      |  CAPABILITIES                                |
      |<---------------------------------------------|
      |  CTExponent = 14                             |
      |  Flags = CERT_CAP | CHAL_CAP | MEAS_CAP |    |
      |          KEY_EX_CAP | ENCRYPT_CAP            |
      |                                              |
      |  3. NEGOTIATE_ALGORITHMS                     |
      |--------------------------------------------->|
      |  MeasurementSpec = DMTF                      |
      |  BaseAsymSel = RSASSA_3072, ECDSA_P384       |
      |  BaseHashSel = SHA2_384, SHA2_256            |
      |                                              |
      |  ALGORITHMS                                  |
      |<---------------------------------------------|
      |  MeasurementHashAlgo = SHA2_384              |
      |  BaseAsymAlgo = ECDSA_P384                   |
      |  BaseHashAlgo = SHA2_384                     |
      |                                              |
```

</div></div>

### Capability Flags

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Flag | Bit | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CACHE_CAP` | 0 | Supports caching of negotiated state |
| `CERT_CAP` | 1 | Has certificate chain(s) |
| `CHAL_CAP` | 2 | Supports challenge authentication |
| `MEAS_CAP` | 3-4 | Measurement capability (0=none, 1=no sig, 2=with sig) |
| `MEAS_FRESH_CAP` | 5 | Generates fresh measurements on request |
| `ENCRYPT_CAP` | 6 | Supports encrypted messages |
| `MAC_CAP` | 7 | Supports message authentication codes |
| `MUT_AUTH_CAP` | 8 | Supports mutual authentication |
| `KEY_EX_CAP` | 9 | Supports key exchange |
| `PSK_CAP` | 10-11 | Pre-shared key capability |
| `ENCAP_CAP` | 12 | Supports encapsulated requests |
| `HBEAT_CAP` | 13 | Supports heartbeat |
| `KEY_UPD_CAP` | 14 | Supports key update |
| `HANDSHAKE_ITC_CAP` | 15 | Handshake in-the-clear support |
| `PUB_KEY_ID_CAP` | 16 | Public key ID instead of certificate |
| `CHUNK_CAP` | 17 | Supports message chunking |
| `ALIAS_CERT_CAP` | 18 | Has alias certificate model |

</div>
---

## Certificate Chain Structure

    

### Chain Format

    

SPDM uses DER-encoded X.509 certificate chains:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|                    Certificate Chain                          |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Length (2 bytes)     |  Reserved (2 bytes)                   |
+-----------------------+---------------------------------------+
|  Root Hash (0 or HashSize bytes)                              |
|  - Only present if RootHash is non-zero                       |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Certificate[0] - Root CA or Intermediate (DER)               |
|  +-----------------------------------------------------------+|
|  |  TBSCertificate                                           ||
|  |    - Version, Serial, Signature Algorithm                 ||
|  |    - Issuer, Validity, Subject                            ||
|  |    - SubjectPublicKeyInfo                                 ||
|  |    - Extensions (Key Usage, Basic Constraints, etc.)      ||
|  +-----------------------------------------------------------+|
|  |  SignatureAlgorithm                                       ||
|  +-----------------------------------------------------------+|
|  |  SignatureValue                                           ||
|  +-----------------------------------------------------------+|
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Certificate[1] - Intermediate CA (DER) - if present          |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Certificate[N] - Device/Leaf Certificate (DER)               |
|  +-----------------------------------------------------------+|
|  |  Subject: CN=DeviceSerial, O=Vendor                       ||
|  |  Key Usage: Digital Signature                             ||
|  |  Extended Key Usage: id-kp-cmcRA (SPDM signing)           ||
|  +-----------------------------------------------------------+|
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
```

</div></div>

### Certificate Slot Model

    

SPDM supports up to 8 certificate slots (0-7):

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Slot | Typical Use |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Device identity certificate (required) |
| 1-7 | Alternative certificates (optional) |

</div>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get certificate digests for all slots</span>
spdmtool getcert <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">--digests</span>

<span class="c"># Get certificate from specific slot</span>
spdmtool getcert <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">-s</span> 0  <span class="c"># Slot 0</span>
spdmtool getcert <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">-s</span> 1  <span class="c"># Slot 1</span>
```

</div></div>

### Certificate Requirements

    

For SPDM device certificates:

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Requirement | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Key Usage | digitalSignature must be set |
| Key Size | RSA ≥ 2048, ECDSA P-256/P-384/P-521 |
| Hash Algorithm | SHA-256 or stronger |
| Chain Depth | Typically 2-4 certificates |
| OID Extensions | May include SPDM-specific OIDs |

</div>
---

## Measurements

    

### Measurement Concept

    

Measurements are cryptographic digests of device firmware, configuration, and state. They allow the requester to verify device integrity.

### Measurement Block Format

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|                     Measurement Block                         |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
| Index (1 byte) | MeasurementSpec (1 byte) | Size (2 bytes)    |
+----------------+------------------------+--------------------+
|                    Measurement Data                           |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+

Measurement Data (DMTF format):
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
| DMTFSpecMeasurementValueType (1 byte) | Size (2 bytes)        |
+---------------------------------------+-----------------------+
|                    Measurement Value                          |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
```

</div></div>

### Measurement Types (DMTF)

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Type | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ImmutableROM` | 0x00 | Boot ROM, immutable code |
| `MutableFirmware` | 0x01 | Updateable firmware |
| `HardwareConfig` | 0x02 | Hardware configuration |
| `FirmwareConfig` | 0x03 | Firmware configuration |
| `MeasurementManifest` | 0x04 | Measurement manifest |
| `DebugMode` | 0x05 | Debug/manufacturing mode indication |
| `MutableFirmwareVersion` | 0x06 | Firmware version string |
| `MutableFirmwareSecurityVersion` | 0x07 | Security version number |
| `HashExtendMeasurement` | 0x08-0x7F | Extended hash measurements |
| `InformationalMeasurement` | 0x80-0xEF | Informational data |
| `Vendor` | 0xF0-0xFF | Vendor-defined |

</div>

### Measurement Operations

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get all measurements (unsigned)</span>
spdmtool measurements <span class="nt">-m</span> 10

<span class="c"># Get measurements with signature</span>
spdmtool measurements <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">--signed</span>

<span class="c"># Get specific measurement index</span>
spdmtool measurements <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">-i</span> 1

<span class="c"># Get raw measurement data</span>
spdmtool measurements <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">-i</span> 1 <span class="nt">--raw</span> <span class="nt">-o</span> measurement_1.bin

<span class="c"># Example output:</span>
<span class="c"># Index 1: Type=MutableFirmware, Size=48, Hash=SHA384:abc123...</span>
<span class="c"># Index 2: Type=FirmwareConfig, Size=48, Hash=SHA384:def456...</span>
<span class="c"># Index 3: Type=HardwareConfig, Size=48, Hash=SHA384:789abc...</span>
```

</div></div>

### Measurement Response Attributes

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Attribute | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `NUMBER_OF_BLOCKS` | Number of measurement blocks |
| `MEASUREMENT_RECORD_LENGTH` | Total length of measurement data |
| `NONCE` | 32-byte random value (when signed) |
| `OPAQUE_DATA` | Optional vendor-specific data |
| `SIGNATURE` | Response signature (when signed) |

</div>
---

## Challenge-Response Authentication

    

### Challenge Flow

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
BMC (Requester)                              Device (Responder)
      |                                              |
      |  CHALLENGE                                   |
      |--------------------------------------------->|
      |  Param1 = SlotID (0-7)                       |
      |  Param2 = MeasurementSummaryHashType         |
      |  Nonce = 32 random bytes                     |
      |                                              |
      |  CHALLENGE_AUTH                              |
      |<---------------------------------------------|
      |  CertChainHash = SHA384(CertificateChain)    |
      |  Nonce = 32 random bytes (responder)         |
      |  MeasurementSummaryHash = SHA384(all meas)   |
      |  OpaqueDataLength + OpaqueData               |
      |  Signature = Sign(Transcript)                |
      |                                              |
```

</div></div>

### Transcript Hash

    

The signature covers a transcript of the entire exchange:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
TranscriptHash = Hash(
    GET_VERSION || VERSION ||
    GET_CAPABILITIES || CAPABILITIES ||
    NEGOTIATE_ALGORITHMS || ALGORITHMS ||
    GET_DIGESTS || DIGESTS ||
    GET_CERTIFICATE[0..N] || CERTIFICATE[0..N] ||
    CHALLENGE || CHALLENGE_AUTH (without signature)
)

Signature = Sign(PrivateKey, TranscriptHash)
```

</div></div>
---

## Secure Session Establishment

    

### Key Exchange Flow

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
BMC (Requester)                              Device (Responder)
      |                                              |
      | [After authentication via CHALLENGE]         |
      |                                              |
      |  KEY_EXCHANGE                                |
      |--------------------------------------------->|
      |  Param1 = MeasurementSummaryHashType         |
      |  Param2 = SlotID                             |
      |  ReqSessionID = random 16-bit                |
      |  DHE_Pub_Key = Requester's ECDH public key   |
      |  RequesterVerifyData (optional)              |
      |                                              |
      |  KEY_EXCHANGE_RSP                            |
      |<---------------------------------------------|
      |  RspSessionID = random 16-bit                |
      |  MutAuthRequested = flags                    |
      |  DHE_Pub_Key = Responder's ECDH public key   |
      |  MeasurementSummaryHash                      |
      |  OpaqueData                                  |
      |  Signature = Sign(Transcript)                |
      |  ResponderVerifyData = HMAC(HandshakeSecret) |
      |                                              |
      |  [Derive session keys from shared secret]    |
      |                                              |
      |  FINISH                                      |
      |--------------------------------------------->|
      |  Signature = Sign(Transcript) [if mut auth]  |
      |  RequesterVerifyData = HMAC(HandshakeSecret) |
      |                                              |
      |  FINISH_RSP                                  |
      |<---------------------------------------------|
      |  ResponderVerifyData = HMAC(HandshakeSecret) |
      |                                              |
      | [Session established - encrypted messages]   |
```

</div></div>

### Session Key Derivation

    

Keys are derived using HKDF:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
SharedSecret = ECDH(RequesterPrivKey, ResponderPubKey)

HandshakeSecret = HKDF-Extract(Salt=0, IKM=SharedSecret)

RequesterHandshakeKey = HKDF-Expand(HandshakeSecret, "req hs key", KeyLen)
ResponderHandshakeKey = HKDF-Expand(HandshakeSecret, "rsp hs key", KeyLen)

MasterSecret = HKDF-Extract(HandshakeSecret, 0)

RequesterDataKey = HKDF-Expand(MasterSecret, "req data key", KeyLen)
ResponderDataKey = HKDF-Expand(MasterSecret, "rsp data key", KeyLen)
```

</div></div>

### Encrypted Message Format

    

Within a secure session, messages use AEAD encryption:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|                    Secured Message                            |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
| SessionID (4 bytes) | SeqNum (2-8 bytes)                      |
+-----------------------+---------------------------------------+
|                                                               |
|  AEAD Encrypted Payload:                                      |
|  +----------------------------------------------------------+ |
|  |  Application Data Length (2 bytes)                       | |
|  +----------------------------------------------------------+ |
|  |  Application Data (SPDM message)                         | |
|  +----------------------------------------------------------+ |
|  |  Random Padding (variable)                               | |
|  +----------------------------------------------------------+ |
|                                                               |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
| MAC/Tag (16 bytes for AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305)             |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
```

</div></div>
---

## Cryptographic Algorithms

    

### Supported Algorithms

    

#### Asymmetric Signature

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Algorithm | OID | Key Size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RSASSA_2048` | 1.2.840.113549.1.1.11 | 2048 bits |
| `RSASSA_3072` | 1.2.840.113549.1.1.11 | 3072 bits |
| `RSASSA_4096` | 1.2.840.113549.1.1.11 | 4096 bits |
| `RSAPSS_2048` | 1.2.840.113549.1.1.10 | 2048 bits |
| `RSAPSS_3072` | 1.2.840.113549.1.1.10 | 3072 bits |
| `RSAPSS_4096` | 1.2.840.113549.1.1.10 | 4096 bits |
| `ECDSA_P256` | 1.2.840.10045.4.3.2 | 256 bits |
| `ECDSA_P384` | 1.2.840.10045.4.3.3 | 384 bits |
| `ECDSA_P521` | 1.2.840.10045.4.3.4 | 521 bits |
| `EDDSA_25519` | 1.3.101.112 | 255 bits |
| `EDDSA_448` | 1.3.101.113 | 448 bits |

</div>

#### Hash Algorithms

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Algorithm | Digest Size |
| --- | --- |
| `SHA2_256` | 32 bytes |
| `SHA2_384` | 48 bytes |
| `SHA2_512` | 64 bytes |
| `SHA3_256` | 32 bytes |
| `SHA3_384` | 48 bytes |
| `SHA3_512` | 64 bytes |

</div>

#### DHE (Diffie-Hellman Ephemeral)

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Named Group | Key Size |
| --- | --- |
| `FFDHE_2048` | 2048 bits |
| `FFDHE_3072` | 3072 bits |
| `FFDHE_4096` | 4096 bits |
| `SECP_256_R1` | 256 bits |
| `SECP_384_R1` | 384 bits |
| `SECP_521_R1` | 521 bits |
| `X25519` | 255 bits |
| `X448` | 448 bits |

</div>

#### AEAD (Session Encryption)

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Algorithm | Key Size | Tag Size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AES_128_GCM` | 128 bits | 128 bits |
| `AES_256_GCM` | 256 bits | 128 bits |
| `CHACHA20_POLY1305` | 256 bits | 128 bits |

</div>

## Setup & Configuration

    

### Build-Time Configuration (Yocto)

    

```bitbake
# In your machine .conf or local.conf

# Include SPDM support
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " \
    libspdm \
    spdm-emu \
    phosphor-spdm \
"

# Enable SPDM in relevant components
EXTRA_OEMESON:pn-bmcweb = " \
    -Dredfish-component-integrity=enabled \
"

# libspdm build configuration
EXTRA_OECMAKE:pn-libspdm = " \
    -DLIBSPDM_ENABLE_CAPABILITY_CERT_CAP=ON \
    -DLIBSPDM_ENABLE_CAPABILITY_CHAL_CAP=ON \
    -DLIBSPDM_ENABLE_CAPABILITY_MEAS_CAP=ON \
    -DLIBSPDM_ENABLE_CAPABILITY_KEY_EX_CAP=ON \
    -DLIBSPDM_ENABLE_CAPABILITY_PSK_EX_CAP=OFF \
    -DLIBSPDM_ENABLE_CAPABILITY_HBEAT_CAP=ON \
    -DLIBSPDM_ENABLE_CAPABILITY_MUT_AUTH_CAP=ON \
    -DLIBSPDM_ENABLE_CAPABILITY_CHUNK_CAP=ON \
"
```

### libspdm Build Options

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LIBSPDM_ENABLE_CAPABILITY_CERT_CAP` | ON | Certificate capability |
| `LIBSPDM_ENABLE_CAPABILITY_CHAL_CAP` | ON | Challenge capability |
| `LIBSPDM_ENABLE_CAPABILITY_MEAS_CAP` | ON | Measurement capability |
| `LIBSPDM_ENABLE_CAPABILITY_KEY_EX_CAP` | ON | Key exchange (sessions) |
| `LIBSPDM_ENABLE_CAPABILITY_PSK_EX_CAP` | OFF | Pre-shared key exchange |
| `LIBSPDM_ENABLE_CAPABILITY_HBEAT_CAP` | ON | Session heartbeat |
| `LIBSPDM_ENABLE_CAPABILITY_MUT_AUTH_CAP` | ON | Mutual authentication |
| `LIBSPDM_ENABLE_CAPABILITY_CHUNK_CAP` | ON | Large message chunking |
| `LIBSPDM_ENABLE_CAPABILITY_ENCAP_CAP` | OFF | Encapsulated requests |
| `LIBSPDM_RECORD_TRANSCRIPT_DATA_SUPPORT` | ON | Transcript for debugging |

</div>

### Runtime Configuration

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">

```
<span class="c"># Check SPDM daemon status</span>
systemctl status spdmd

<span class="nb">cat</span> /etc/spdm/spdm.conf
```

```
</span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">

        </span><span class="s2">"RSASSA_3072"</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w">

    </span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w">

    </span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w">

    </span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w">

</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
```

## Certificate Management

    

### Certificate Chain

    

SPDM uses X.509 certificate chains for device authentication:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
Root CA (Self-signed, Trusted by BMC)
   │
   └── Intermediate CA (Optional)
          │
          └── Device Certificate (Leaf)
                - Contains device public key
                - Signed by Intermediate/Root CA
                - Used for challenge signature
```

</div></div>

### Provisioning Trust Anchors

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Root CA certificates location</span>
/etc/spdm/certs/trust/

<span class="c"># Add trusted root CA</span>
<span class="nb">cp </span>vendor_root_ca.pem /etc/spdm/certs/trust/

<span class="c"># Convert DER to PEM if needed</span>
openssl x509 <span class="nt">-inform</span> DER <span class="nt">-in</span> vendor_root_ca.der <span class="nt">-out</span> vendor_root_ca.pem

<span class="c"># Verify certificate</span>
openssl x509 <span class="nt">-in</span> vendor_root_ca.pem <span class="nt">-text</span> <span class="nt">-noout</span>

<span class="c"># Restart SPDM daemon to load new trust anchors</span>
systemctl restart spdmd
```

</div></div>

### BMC Certificate (for Mutual Auth)

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># BMC certificate location</span>
/etc/spdm/certs/bmc/

<span class="c"># Generate BMC keypair (ECDSA P-384 recommended)</span>
openssl ecparam <span class="nt">-name</span> secp384r1 <span class="nt">-genkey</span> <span class="nt">-noout</span> <span class="nt">-out</span> /etc/spdm/certs/bmc/key.pem

<span class="c"># Generate CSR</span>
openssl req <span class="nt">-new</span> <span class="nt">-key</span> /etc/spdm/certs/bmc/key.pem <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-out</span> /etc/spdm/certs/bmc/csr.pem <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-subj</span> <span class="s2">"/CN=BMC-</span><span class="si">$(</span><span class="nb">hostname</span><span class="si">)</span><span class="s2">/O=MyOrg/OU=OpenBMC"</span>

<span class="c"># Install signed certificate (after CA signs the CSR)</span>
<span class="nb">cp </span>signed_bmc_cert.pem /etc/spdm/certs/bmc/cert.pem

<span class="c"># Set proper permissions</span>
<span class="nb">chmod </span>600 /etc/spdm/certs/bmc/key.pem
<span class="nb">chmod </span>644 /etc/spdm/certs/bmc/cert.pem
```

</div></div>

### Certificate Verification

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Verify certificate chain</span>
openssl verify <span class="nt">-CAfile</span> root_ca.pem <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-untrusted</span> intermediate.pem device_cert.pem

<span class="c"># Check certificate validity period</span>
openssl x509 <span class="nt">-in</span> device_cert.pem <span class="nt">-noout</span> <span class="nt">-dates</span>

<span class="c"># Check certificate key usage</span>
openssl x509 <span class="nt">-in</span> device_cert.pem <span class="nt">-noout</span> <span class="nt">-text</span> | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-A1</span> <span class="s2">"Key Usage"</span>

<span class="c"># Check certificate subject</span>
openssl x509 <span class="nt">-in</span> device_cert.pem <span class="nt">-noout</span> <span class="nt">-subject</span>
```

</div></div>
---

## SPDM Operations

    

### Device Discovery

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># List SPDM-capable endpoints</span>
spdmtool discover

<span class="c"># Get SPDM version from device</span>
spdmtool version <span class="nt">-m</span> 10

<span class="c"># Example output:</span>
<span class="c"># SPDM Version: 1.2.0</span>
<span class="c"># Supported Versions: 1.0.0, 1.1.0, 1.2.0</span>

<span class="c"># Get device capabilities</span>
spdmtool capabilities <span class="nt">-m</span> 10

<span class="c"># Example output:</span>
<span class="c"># Capabilities:</span>
<span class="c">#   CERT_CAP: Yes</span>
<span class="c">#   CHAL_CAP: Yes</span>
<span class="c">#   MEAS_CAP: Signature</span>
<span class="c">#   KEY_EX_CAP: Yes</span>
<span class="c">#   MUT_AUTH_CAP: Yes</span>
<span class="c">#   ENCRYPT_CAP: Yes</span>
```

</div></div>

### Get Device Certificate

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get certificate chain digest</span>
spdmtool getdigest <span class="nt">-m</span> 10

<span class="c"># Get certificate chain</span>
spdmtool getcert <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">-s</span> 0

<span class="c"># Save certificate chain to file</span>
spdmtool getcert <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">-s</span> 0 <span class="nt">-o</span> device_chain.pem

<span class="c"># Extract individual certificates</span>
openssl storeutl <span class="nt">-certs</span> device_chain.pem
```

</div></div>

### Challenge Authentication

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Send challenge to verify device</span>
spdmtool challenge <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">-s</span> 0

<span class="c"># Challenge with measurement summary</span>
spdmtool challenge <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">-s</span> 0 <span class="nt">--meas-summary</span> all

<span class="c"># Example output:</span>
<span class="c"># Challenge Response:</span>
<span class="c">#   Certificate Hash: SHA384:abc123...</span>
<span class="c">#   Nonce: 0x1234...</span>
<span class="c">#   Measurement Summary Hash: SHA384:def456...</span>
<span class="c">#   Signature: ECDSA_P384:789...</span>
<span class="c">#   Verification: SUCCESS</span>
```

</div></div>

### Get Measurements

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get all measurements</span>
spdmtool measurements <span class="nt">-m</span> 10

<span class="c"># Get signed measurements</span>
spdmtool measurements <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">--signed</span>

<span class="c"># Get specific measurement index</span>
spdmtool measurements <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">-i</span> 1

<span class="c"># Save measurements to JSON</span>
spdmtool measurements <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">-o</span> measurements.json

<span class="c"># Example output:</span>
<span class="c"># Measurement Record:</span>
<span class="c">#   Index 1: Type=MutableFirmware</span>
<span class="c">#            Hash=SHA384:abc123def456...</span>
<span class="c">#   Index 2: Type=FirmwareConfig</span>
<span class="c">#            Hash=SHA384:789abc012def...</span>
<span class="c">#   Index 3: Type=MutableFirmwareVersion</span>
<span class="c">#            Value="v2.1.0-rc3"</span>
```

</div></div>

## Redfish ComponentIntegrity

    

### Enable in bmcweb

    

```bitbake
EXTRA_OEMESON:pn-bmcweb = " \
    -Dredfish-component-integrity=enabled \
"
```

### Query Component Integrity

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get ComponentIntegrity collection</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/ComponentIntegrity

<span class="c"># Get specific component</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/ComponentIntegrity/GPU_0
```

</div></div>

### ComponentIntegrity Response

    

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
```

### Trigger New Attestation

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Force re-attestation via action</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> POST <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{"Nonce": "abc123", "MeasurementIndices": [1, 2, 3]}'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/ComponentIntegrity/GPU_0/Actions/ComponentIntegrity.SPDMGetSignedMeasurements

<span class="c"># Get certificate from component</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/ComponentIntegrity/GPU_0/Certificates/0
```

</div></div>

## Secure Session Operations

    

### Key Exchange

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Establish secure session</span>
spdmtool keyexchange <span class="nt">-m</span> 10

<span class="c"># Session provides:</span>
<span class="c"># - Encrypted communication</span>
<span class="c"># - Authenticated channel</span>
<span class="c"># - Replay protection</span>

<span class="c"># Session with mutual authentication</span>
spdmtool keyexchange <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">--mutual-auth</span>

<span class="c"># Example output:</span>
<span class="c"># Session Established:</span>
<span class="c">#   Session ID: 0xABCD1234</span>
<span class="c">#   Algorithm: AES_256_GCM</span>
<span class="c">#   DHE: SECP_384_R1</span>
```

</div></div>

### Session Management

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Send message over secure session</span>
spdmtool secured-message <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">-s</span> 0xABCD1234 <span class="nt">--data</span> <span class="s2">"..."</span>

<span class="c"># Heartbeat to keep session alive</span>
spdmtool heartbeat <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">-s</span> 0xABCD1234

<span class="c"># Update session keys</span>
spdmtool keyupdate <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">-s</span> 0xABCD1234

<span class="c"># End session</span>
spdmtool endsession <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">-s</span> 0xABCD1234
```

</div></div>

### Session Types

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Type | Description | Use Case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `KEY_EXCHANGE` | Asymmetric key exchange | Standard sessions |
| `PSK_EXCHANGE` | Pre-shared key | Devices without certificates |
| `PSK_FINISH` | PSK with challenge | Enhanced PSK security |

</div>
---

## Measurement Policy

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```

</span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"deviceType"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"GPU"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"vendorId"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"0x10DE"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"measurements"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"1"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"MutableFirmware"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"expectedHash"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"sha384:abc123def456789..."</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"description"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"GPU firmware v2.1.0"</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"2"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"FirmwareConfig"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"expectedHash"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"sha384:789abc012def345..."</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"description"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Factory configuration"</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"3"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"MutableFirmwareVersion"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"expectedValue"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"v2.1.0"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"description"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Firmware version string"</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"policy"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"requireAllMeasurements"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kc">true</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"actionOnMismatch"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"log_and_alert"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"allowFirmwareUpdate"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kc">true</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

### Policy Actions

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Action | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `log` | Log mismatch, continue operation |
| `alert` | Generate Redfish alert event |
| `log_and_alert` | Both log and alert |
| `reject` | Block device from operation |
| `quarantine` | Isolate device, require manual action |

</div>

## D-Bus Integration

    

### SPDM D-Bus Interface

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># List SPDM service</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.SPDM

<span class="c"># Object structure:</span>
<span class="c"># /xyz/openbmc_project/spdm</span>
<span class="c">#   /endpoint/<eid></span>
<span class="c">#     - xyz.openbmc_project.SPDM.Endpoint</span>
<span class="c">#     - xyz.openbmc_project.SPDM.Certificate</span>
<span class="c">#     - xyz.openbmc_project.SPDM.Measurement</span>

<span class="c"># Get endpoint properties</span>
busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.SPDM <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/spdm/endpoint/10

<span class="c"># Get measurements via D-Bus</span>
busctl call xyz.openbmc_project.SPDM <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/spdm/endpoint/10 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.SPDM.Measurement <span class="se">\</span>
    GetMeasurements u 0xFF
```

</div></div>

### Attestation Events

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Monitor SPDM events</span>
busctl monitor xyz.openbmc_project.SPDM

<span class="c"># Events include:</span>
<span class="c"># - EndpointDiscovered</span>
<span class="c"># - AuthenticationSuccess/Failure</span>
<span class="c"># - MeasurementMismatch</span>
<span class="c"># - SessionEstablished/Terminated</span>
```

</div></div>

## Troubleshooting

    

### Discovery Failures

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Verify MCTP connectivity first</span>
mctp endpoint

<span class="c"># Check SPDM version compatibility</span>
spdmtool version <span class="nt">-m</span> 10

<span class="c"># Enable debug logging</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"SPDM_DEBUG=1"</span> <span class="o">>></span> /etc/default/spdmd
systemctl restart spdmd

<span class="c"># View detailed logs</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> spdmd <span class="nt">-f</span> <span class="nt">--no-pager</span>
```

</div></div>

### Certificate Verification Failed

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check trust anchor is installed</span>
<span class="nb">ls</span> <span class="nt">-la</span> /etc/spdm/certs/trust/

<span class="c"># Get device certificate chain</span>
spdmtool getcert <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">-s</span> 0 <span class="nt">-o</span> /tmp/device_chain.pem

<span class="c"># Verify certificate chain manually</span>
openssl verify <span class="nt">-CAfile</span> /etc/spdm/certs/trust/root.pem <span class="se">\</span>
    /tmp/device_chain.pem

<span class="c"># Check certificate validity</span>
openssl x509 <span class="nt">-in</span> /tmp/device_chain.pem <span class="nt">-checkend</span> 0

<span class="c"># Check certificate details</span>
openssl x509 <span class="nt">-in</span> /tmp/device_chain.pem <span class="nt">-text</span> <span class="nt">-noout</span> | <span class="nb">head</span> <span class="nt">-30</span>
```

</div></div>

### Measurement Mismatch

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get actual measurements</span>
spdmtool measurements <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">-o</span> /tmp/actual_meas.json

<span class="c"># Compare with expected</span>
diff /tmp/actual_meas.json /etc/spdm/policy/expected.json

<span class="c"># Check if firmware was updated</span>
<span class="c"># Measurements change with firmware updates</span>

<span class="c"># Verify measurement type</span>
spdmtool measurements <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 <span class="nt">-i</span> 1 <span class="nt">--verbose</span>
```

</div></div>

### Session Failures

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check algorithm compatibility</span>
spdmtool capabilities <span class="nt">-m</span> 10

<span class="c"># Verify key exchange support</span>
spdmtool algorithms <span class="nt">-m</span> 10

<span class="c"># Check session logs</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> spdmd | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> session

<span class="c"># Verify DHE is supported</span>
spdmtool capabilities <span class="nt">-m</span> 10 | <span class="nb">grep </span>KEY_EX
```

</div></div>

### Common Error Codes

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Error | Cause | Solution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `InvalidRequest` | Malformed message | Check message format |
| `Busy` | Device processing | Retry with backoff |
| `UnexpectedRequest` | Wrong state machine | Reset and restart |
| `DecryptError` | Session key mismatch | Re-establish session |
| `UnsupportedRequest` | Feature not supported | Check capabilities |
| `InvalidSession` | Session expired/invalid | Create new session |

</div>
---

## Security Best Practices

    

### Certificate Management

    

1. **Use strong keys**: RSA ≥ 3072 or ECDSA P-384
2. **Rotate certificates**: Before expiration, plan rotation
3. **Secure storage**: Protect private keys with HSM or secure enclave
4. **Monitor expiration**: Alert before certificate expires
5. **Revocation checking**: Implement CRL or OCSP if available

### Measurement Verification

    

1. **Store expected values securely**: Protect measurement database
2. **Update with firmware**: Expected values must match deployed firmware
3. **Alert on changes**: Any measurement change should trigger investigation
4. **Log all events**: Maintain audit trail of attestation attempts
5. **Regular re-attestation**: Periodically verify device integrity

### Access Control

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Limit SPDM administration access</span>
<span class="nb">chmod </span>600 /etc/spdm/spdm.conf
<span class="nb">chmod </span>600 /etc/spdm/policy/<span class="k">*</span>.json

<span class="c"># Use D-Bus policy for access control</span>
<span class="c"># /etc/dbus-1/system.d/spdm.conf</span>
```

</div></div>

### Production Recommendations

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Recommendation | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Enable mutual auth | Both BMC and device authenticate |
| Use secure sessions | Encrypt SPDM traffic |
| Require signed measurements | Don’t accept unsigned |
| Implement alerting | Notify on failures |
| Regular audits | Review attestation logs |
| Update policies | Keep expected measurements current |

</div>
---

## Enabling/Disabling SPDM

    

### Build-Time Disable

    

```bitbake
# Remove SPDM packages
IMAGE_INSTALL:remove = "libspdm phosphor-spdm"

# Disable in bmcweb
EXTRA_OEMESON:pn-bmcweb = " \
    -Dredfish-component-integrity=disabled \
"
```

### Runtime Disable

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Stop SPDM daemon</span>
systemctl stop spdmd
systemctl disable spdmd

<span class="c"># SPDM attestation will not be available</span>
<span class="c"># Existing sessions will close</span>
```

</div></div>
---

## Examples

    

Working examples are available in the [examples/spdm](https://github.com/MichaelTien8901/openbmc-guide-tutorial/tree/main/docs/examples/spdm) directory:

* `spdm_cert_setup.sh` - Generate test certificate chain (Root CA / Intermediate / BMC)
* `spdm_auth.sh` - Full SPDM authentication flow (version, capabilities, certs, challenge)
* `spdm_measurements.sh` - Collect and verify firmware measurements
* `spdm_redfish.sh` - Query Redfish ComponentIntegrity endpoints
* `config/algorithms.json` - Crypto algorithm preferences
* `config/gpu_expected.json` - Expected measurement policy for attestation
* `config/component_integrity.json` - Example Redfish ComponentIntegrity response

* [DMTF DSP0274 - SPDM Specification](https://www.dmtf.org/dsp/DSP0274) - Official SPDM protocol specification

* [OpenBMC Redfish SPDM Attestation Design](https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/designs/redfish-spdm-attestation.md) - OpenBMC integration design
* [OpenBMC SPDM Daemon](https://github.com/openbmc/spdm) - OpenBMC SPDM implementation
* [TCG DICE Attestation Architecture](https://trustedcomputinggroup.org/resource/dice-attestation-architecture/) - Related attestation architecture

## Overview

    

OpenBMC supports firmware updates for BMC, BIOS/UEFI, and other platform components through multiple interfaces including Redfish, IPMI, PLDM, and command-line tools. This guide provides a deep dive into the update architecture, image formats, flash layouts, and troubleshooting procedures.
