## Best Practices

    

### Pre-Update Checklist

    

1. **Verify backup image** - Ensure standby image is known-good
2. **Check storage space** - Minimum 2x image size in /tmp
3. **Verify network connectivity** - For network-based updates
4. **Document current version** - For rollback reference
5. **Schedule maintenance window** - BMC reboot affects management

### Update Procedure

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># 1. Record current version</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory/bmc_active <span class="se">\</span>
    | jq .Version <span class="o">></span> /tmp/before_version.txt

<span class="c"># 2. Verify backup image is bootable</span>
fw_printenv bootside
<span class="c"># Ensure alternate side has valid image</span>

<span class="c"># 3. Upload new image</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-X</span> POST <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/octet-stream"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">--data-binary</span> @firmware.tar <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/UpdateService

<span class="c"># 4. Monitor activation</span>
watch <span class="nt">-n</span> 5 <span class="s1">'curl -sk -u root:0penBmc \
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/TaskService/Tasks | jq'</span>

<span class="c"># 5. Verify after reboot</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory/bmc_active <span class="se">\</span>
    | jq .Version
```

</div></div>

### Post-Update Verification

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Verify boot success</span>
fw_printenv bootcount
<span class="c"># Should be 0</span>

<span class="c"># Check system health</span>
obmcutil state
<span class="c"># Should show Ready</span>

<span class="c"># Verify all services running</span>
systemctl <span class="nt">--failed</span>
<span class="c"># Should be empty</span>

<span class="c"># Test critical functionality</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system
ipmitool <span class="nt">-I</span> lanplus <span class="nt">-H</span> <bmc-ip> <span class="nt">-U</span> root <span class="nt">-P</span> 0penBmc chassis status
```

</div></div>

## Deep Dive

    

Advanced implementation details for firmware update developers.

### Flash Layout and MTD Partitions

    

* Typical BMC Flash Layout (32MB)

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Offset | Size | Partition | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0x0000000 | 512KB | u-boot | Bootloader |
| 0x0080000 | 128KB | u-boot-env | U-Boot environment |
| 0x00A0000 | 4.5MB | kernel | FIT image (kernel+dtb) |
| 0x0520000 | 25MB | rofs | Read-only rootfs |
| 0x1DC0000 | 2MB | rwfs | Persistent read-write |

</div>

* Dual-Flash Configuration (A/B):

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Flash 0 (Current) | Flash 1 (Alternate) |
| --- | --- |
| u-boot (shared) | (reserved) |
| u-boot-env |  |
| kernel-a (active) | kernel-b |
| rofs-a (active) | rofs-b |
| rwfs (shared) |  |

</div>

* Linux MTD Devices:
    
```
/dev/mtd0 = u-boot          
  /dev/mtd1 = u-boot-env      
  /dev/mtd2 = kernel          
  /dev/mtd3 = rofs            
  /dev/mtd4 = rwfs
```

> **ASCII-art version (for comparison)**

  <div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Typical BMC Flash Layout (32MB)                      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   Offset     Size        Partition        Description                   │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ 0x0000000│ 512KB     │ u-boot        │ Bootloader               │   │
│   ├──────────┼───────────┼───────────────┼──────────────────────────┤   │
│   │ 0x0080000│ 128KB     │ u-boot-env    │ U-Boot environment       │   │
│   ├──────────┼───────────┼───────────────┼──────────────────────────┤   │
│   │ 0x00A0000│ 4.5MB     │ kernel        │ FIT image (kernel+dtb)   │   │
│   ├──────────┼───────────┼───────────────┼──────────────────────────┤   │
│   │ 0x0520000│ 25MB      │ rofs          │ Read-only rootfs         │   │
│   ├──────────┼───────────┼───────────────┼──────────────────────────┤   │
│   │ 0x1DC0000│ 2MB       │ rwfs          │ Persistent read-write    │   │
│   └──────────┴───────────┴───────────────┴──────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
│   Dual-Flash Configuration (A/B):                                       │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ Flash 0 (Current)     │ Flash 1 (Alternate)                     │   │
│   ├───────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────┤   │
│   │ u-boot (shared)       │ (reserved)                              │   │
│   │ u-boot-env            │                                         │   │
│   │ kernel-a (active)     │ kernel-b                                │   │
│   │ rofs-a (active)       │ rofs-b                                  │   │
│   │ rwfs (shared)         │                                         │   │
│   └───────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
│   Linux MTD Devices:                                                    │
│   /dev/mtd0 = u-boot                                                    │
│   /dev/mtd1 = u-boot-env                                                │
│   /dev/mtd2 = kernel                                                    │
│   /dev/mtd3 = rofs                                                      │
│   /dev/mtd4 = rwfs                                                      │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div>  </div>

### Update Image Verification

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Image Verification Process                           │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   Update Image Structure:                                               │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ MANIFEST (text)        │ Version info, purpose, sha256 hashes   │   │
│   ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤   │
│   │ publickey (optional)   │ Public key for signature verification  │   │
│   ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤   │
│   │ image-kernel           │ FIT image with kernel and DTB          │   │
│   ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤   │
│   │ image-rofs             │ Read-only root filesystem (squashfs)   │   │
│   ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤   │
│   │ image-u-boot           │ U-Boot binary (optional)               │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
│   MANIFEST File Example:                                                │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ purpose=xyz.openbmc_project.Software.Version.VersionPurpose.BMC │   │
│   │ version=2.12.0                                                  │   │
│   │ MachineName=romulus                                             │   │
│   │ KeyType=OpenBMC                                                 │   │
│   │ HashType=RSA-SHA256                                             │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
│   Verification Flow:                                                    │
│   ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐          │
│   │ Receive  │───▶│ Verify   │───▶│ Verify   │───▶│ Verify   │          │
│   │ Image    │    │ MANIFEST │    │ Signature│    │ Hashes   │          │
│   └──────────┘    └──────────┘    └──────────┘    └──────────┘          │
│                        │              │               │                 │
│                        ▼              ▼               ▼                 │
│                   Check          RSA verify      SHA256 each            │
│                   required       against        component vs            │
│                   fields         pubkey         MANIFEST                │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### Flash Programming Internals

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Flash Write Process                                  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   MTD Write Operation:                                                  │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ 1. Erase sector (typically 64KB)                                │   │
│   │    ioctl(mtd_fd, MEMERASE, &erase_info)                         │   │
│   │    └─ Sector erased to 0xFF                                     │   │
│   │                                                                 │   │
│   │ 2. Write data (page-aligned, typically 256 bytes)               │   │
│   │    write(mtd_fd, data, page_size)                               │   │
│   │    └─ Data written to erased sector                             │   │
│   │                                                                 │   │
│   │ 3. Verify (optional, MEMVERIFY ioctl)                           │   │
│   │    read-back and compare                                        │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
│   Update Daemon (phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt) Flow:                          │
│   ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│   │ 1. Image uploaded to /tmp/images/                              │    │
│   │ 2. Item Updater detects new image via inotify                  │    │
│   │ 3. Verify signature and hashes                                 │    │
│   │ 4. Create D-Bus Version object (Ready)                         │    │
│   │ 5. User activates: RequestedActivation = Active                │    │
│   │ 6. Write image components to alternate flash                   │    │
│   │ 7. Update U-Boot env to boot from new image                    │    │
│   │ 8. Set Activation = Activating, then Active                    │    │
│   │ 9. Reboot (if requested)                                       │    │
│   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                         │
│   U-Boot Environment (dual-boot):                                       │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ bootside=a           # Currently running: a or b                │   │
│   │ bootcount=0          # Failed boot attempts                     │   │
│   │ bootlimit=3          # Max failures before fallback             │   │
│   │ bootcmd=             # Selects kernel-a or kernel-b             │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### Recovery Mechanism

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Boot Failure Recovery                                │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   Recovery Flow:                                                        │
│   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│   │                                                                  │  │
│   │  U-Boot Power On                                                 │  │
│   │       │                                                          │  │
│   │       ▼                                                          │  │
│   │  bootcount++                                                     │  │
│   │       │                                                          │  │
│   │       ▼                                                          │  │
│   │  bootcount > bootlimit? ───Yes──▶ Switch to alternate image      │  │
│   │       │                           Reset bootcount                │  │
│   │       No                          Boot alternate                 │  │
│   │       │                                                          │  │
│   │       ▼                                                          │  │
│   │  Boot current image                                              │  │
│   │       │                                                          │  │
│   │       ▼                                                          │  │
│   │  Linux boots successfully?                                       │  │
│   │       │                                                          │  │
│   │      Yes                                                         │  │
│   │       │                                                          │  │
│   │       ▼                                                          │  │
│   │  systemd reaches multi-user.target                               │  │
│   │       │                                                          │  │
│   │       ▼                                                          │  │
│   │  obmc-flash-bmc-setenv@bootcount=0.service                       │  │
│   │  (Reset bootcount to indicate successful boot)                   │  │
│   │                                                                  │  │
│   └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                                                         │
│   Manual Recovery Commands:                                             │
│   # From U-Boot prompt (serial console):                                │
│   => setenv bootside b        # Switch to alternate                     │
│   => saveenv                                                            │
│   => reset                                                              │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

## Overview

    

**ASD (At-Scale Debug)** and **ACD (Autonomous Crash Dump)** are Intel technologies for remote CPU debugging and crash analysis on Intel Xeon server platforms.

```mermaid
---
title: Intel Debug Architecture
---
flowchart TB
    subgraph client["Debug Client (Host)"]
        direction TB
        isd["Intel System  
Debugger (ISD)"]
        itpxdp["ITP-XDP  
(In-Target Probe)"]
        crash["Crash Analyzer  
Tool"]
    end

    subgraph network["Network (TCP/IP)"]
        ports["Port 5123 (ASD) / HTTPS (Redfish)"]
    end

    subgraph bmc["BMC"]
        direction TB
        asd["ASD  
Daemon"]
        crashdump["Crashdump  
Service"]
        jtag["JTAG Handler  
(jtag_handler.c)"]
        peci["PECI Interface  
(Platform Environment Control I/F)"]

        asd --> jtag
        crashdump --> jtag
        jtag --> peci
    end

    subgraph cpu["Intel Xeon CPU(s)"]
        direction TB
        xdp["XDP Port  
(Debug Port)"]
        tap["JTAG TAP  
Controller"]
        mca["MCA Banks  
(Error Regs)"]
    end

    client --> network
    network --> bmc
    bmc --> cpu
```

## ASD (At-Scale Debug)

    

### What is ASD?

    

At-Scale Debug provides remote JTAG-like access to Intel CPUs through the BMC, enabling:

* **Remote debugging** without physical access to the server
* **JTAG chain access** to CPU cores, uncore, and PCH
* **Run control** (halt, step, breakpoints)
* **Register access** (MSRs, GPRs, control registers)
* **Memory access** through the CPU debug interface

### ASD Architecture

    

```mermaid
---
title: ASD Components
---
flowchart LR
    subgraph host["Debug Host"]
        direction LR
        openipc["OpenIPC/ISD"]
        asdclient["ASD Client"]
    end

    subgraph bmc["BMC - ASD Daemon"]
        direction TB
        msghandler["Message Handler"]
        jtaghandler["JTAG Handler  
- Chain discovery  
- TAP state machine  
- IR/DR shifting"]
        targethandler["Target Handler  
- XDP interface  
- GPIO control"]

        msghandler --> jtaghandler
        jtaghandler --> targethandler
    end

    host -->|"TCP:5123"| bmc
```

### Build Configuration

    

```bitbake
# recipes-phosphor/debug/asd.bb or local.conf

# Include ASD daemon
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " asd"

# ASD build options
EXTRA_OEMESON:pn-asd = " \
    -Djtag-legacy-driver=disabled \
    -Dsafe-mode=enabled \
"
```

### Meson Build Options

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `jtag-legacy-driver` | disabled | Use legacy JTAG driver |
| `safe-mode` | enabled | Enable safe mode protections |
| `i2c-debug` | disabled | Enable I2C debug messages |
| `i3c-debug` | disabled | Enable I3C debug messages |

</div>

### GPIO Configuration

    

ASD requires specific GPIO pins for JTAG and control signals:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="err">//</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">/usr/share/asd/pin_config.json</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"MyPlatform"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Platform"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"jtag"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"tck"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="nl">"pin"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"GPIOA0"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nl">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"gpio"</span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"tdi"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="nl">"pin"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"GPIOA1"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nl">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"gpio"</span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"tdo"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="nl">"pin"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"GPIOA2"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nl">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"gpio"</span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"tms"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="nl">"pin"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"GPIOA3"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nl">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"gpio"</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="nl">"target"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"xdp_present"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="nl">"pin"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"GPIOB0"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nl">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"gpio"</span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"debug_enable"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="nl">"pin"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"GPIOB1"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nl">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"gpio"</span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"preq"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="nl">"pin"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"GPIOB2"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nl">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"gpio"</span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"prdy"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="nl">"pin"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"GPIOB3"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nl">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"gpio"</span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"reset"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="nl">"pin"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"GPIOB4"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nl">"type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"gpio"</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

### XDP (eXtended Debug Port) Interface

    

XDP provides enhanced debug access:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
XDP Signals:
+----------+----------------------------------+
| Signal   | Description                      |
+----------+----------------------------------+
| PREQ#    | Probe Request (BMC -> CPU)       |
| PRDY#    | Probe Ready (CPU -> BMC)         |
| RESET#   | Platform Reset control           |
| TCK      | JTAG Test Clock                  |
| TMS      | JTAG Test Mode Select            |
| TDI      | JTAG Test Data In                |
| TDO      | JTAG Test Data Out               |
| TRST#    | JTAG Test Reset                  |
+----------+----------------------------------+
```

</div></div>

## ACD (Autonomous Crash Dump)

    

### What is ACD?

    

Autonomous Crash Dump automatically collects CPU diagnostic data when critical errors occur:

* **Machine Check Exceptions (MCE)** capture
* **CPU register state** preservation
* **Memory controller errors** logging
* **PCIe errors** collection
* **Uncore state** dump

### Crash Dump Architecture

    

```mermaid
---
title: Crash Dump Collection Flow
---
flowchart TB
    subgraph step1["1. Error Occurs"]
        cpu["CPU Asserts  
CATERR# / IERR#"]
    end

    subgraph step2["2. BMC Detects Error"]
        gpio["GPIO Interrupt  
Handler"]
    end

    subgraph step3["3. Trigger Collection"]
        crashdump["Crashdump  
Service"]
    end

    subgraph step4["4. Collect Data via PECI"]
        peci["PECI Commands  
- RdPkgConfig  
- RdIAMSR  
- CrashDump"]
        mca["CPU MCA Banks  
- MC0-MCn  
- Uncore MSRs  
- Core State"]
        peci --> mca
    end

    subgraph step5["5. Store & Expose"]
        json["JSON Storage  
/var/lib/crashdump/"]
        redfish["Redfish API  
LogService"]
        json --> redfish
    end

    cpu --> gpio
    gpio --> crashdump
    crashdump --> peci
    peci --> json
```

> **ASCII-art version (for comparison)**

  <div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                   Crash Dump Collection Flow                      |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                   |
|  1. Error Occurs                                                  |
|     +------------------+                                          |
|     | CPU Asserts      |                                          |
|     | CATERR# / IERR#  |                                          |
|     +--------+---------+                                          |
|              |                                                    |
|  2. BMC Detects Error                                             |
|     +--------v---------+                                          |
|     | GPIO Interrupt   |                                          |
|     | Handler          |                                          |
|     +--------+---------+                                          |
|              |                                                    |
|  3. Trigger Collection                                            |
|     +--------v---------+                                          |
|     | Crashdump        |                                          |
|     | Service          |                                          |
|     +--------+---------+                                          |
|              |                                                    |
|  4. Collect Data via PECI                                         |
|     +--------v---------+     +------------------+                 |
|     | PECI Commands    |---->| CPU MCA Banks    |                 |
|     | - RdPkgConfig    |     | - MC0-MCn        |                 |
|     | - RdIAMSR        |     | - Uncore MSRs    |                 |
|     | - CrashDump      |     | - Core State     |                 |
|     +--------+---------+     +------------------+                 |
|              |                                                    |
|  5. Store & Expose                                                |
|     +--------v---------+                                          |
|     | JSON Storage     |                                          |
|     | /var/lib/        |                                          |
|     | crashdump/       |                                          |
|     +--------+---------+                                          |
|              |                                                    |
|     +--------v---------+                                          |
|     | Redfish API      |                                          |
|     | LogService       |                                          |
|     +------------------+                                          |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

</div>  </div>

### Build Configuration

    

```bitbake
# Include crashdump service
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " crashdump"

# Crashdump build options
EXTRA_OEMESON:pn-crashdump = " \
    -Dtests=disabled \
    -Dcrashdump-x86=enabled \
"
```

### Crash Dump Triggers

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Trigger | Signal | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CATERR# | GPIO | Catastrophic Error |
| IERR# | GPIO | Internal Error |
| MCERR# | GPIO | Machine Check Error |
| ERR2# | GPIO | Error Signal 2 |
| Manual | Redfish/IPMI | User-initiated collection |

</div>

### GPIO Configuration for Error Detection

    

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="err">//</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">Entity</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">Manager</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">configuration</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">

    </span><span class="nl">"Exposes"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"CATERR"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"gpio"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Index"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">45</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Polarity"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Low"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Direction"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Input"</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">},</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"ERR2"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"gpio"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Index"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">46</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Polarity"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Low"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Direction"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Input"</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

### PECI Interface

    

PECI (Platform Environment Control Interface) is used to collect crash data:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># PECI commands used by crashdump:</span>

<span class="c"># Read Package Config</span>
peci_cmds RdPkgConfig <address> <index> 
# Read IA MSR
peci_cmds RdIAMSR   

# Crashdump command
peci_cmds Crashdump  command> 
```

### Crash Dump Data Sections

    

  
    
      Section
      Content
    
  
  
    
      `metadata`
      Timestamp, trigger, platform info
    
    
      `MCA`
      Machine Check Architecture banks
    
    
      `uncore`
      Uncore MSRs and registers
    
    
      `TOR`
      Transaction Outstanding Registers
    
    
      `PM_Info`
      Power management state
    
    
      `address_map`
      Memory address mapping
    
    
      `big_core`
      CPU core registers
    
    
      `crashlog`
      Hardware crash log
    
  

### Manual Crash Dump Collection

    

#### Via Redfish

    

```
# Trigger crash dump collection
curl -k -u root:0penBmc -X POST \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"DiagnosticDataType": "OEM", "OEMDiagnosticDataType": "OnDemand"}' \
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/Crashdump/Actions/LogService.CollectDiagnosticData

# List collected dumps
curl -k -u root:0penBmc \
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/Crashdump/Entries

# Get specific dump
curl -k -u root:0penBmc \
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/Crashdump/Entries/1

# Download raw dump data
curl -k -u root:0penBmc -o crashdump.json \
    "https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/Crashdump/Entries/1/attachment"
```

#### Via IPMI

    

```
# Trigger crash dump (Intel OEM command)
ipmitool -I lanplus -H  -U root -P 0penBmc \
    raw 0x30 0x74  # Intel OEM crashdump trigger

# Get crash dump status
ipmitool -I lanplus -H  -U root -P 0penBmc \
    raw 0x30 0x75  # Intel OEM crashdump status
```

### Crash Dump JSON Format

    

```
{
    "crash_data": {
        "METADATA": {
            "timestamp": "2024-01-15T10:30:45Z",
            "trigger_type": "CATERR",
            "platform": "Intel Xeon 4th Gen",
            "cpu_count": 2
        },
        "CPU0": {
            "MCA": {
                "MC0_CTL": "0x0000000000000001",
                "MC0_STATUS": "0xBE00000000800400",
                "MC0_ADDR": "0x000000007F400000",
                "MC0_MISC": "0x0000000000000000",
                "MC0_CTL2": "0x0000000000000001"
            },
            "uncore": {
                "UNCORE_MC0_STATUS": "0x0000000000000000",
                "UNCORE_CHA0_STATUS": "0x0000000000000000"
            },
            "TOR": {
                "TOR_0_SAD": "0x0000000000000000",
                "TOR_0_TAD": "0x0000000000000000"
            }
        },
        "CPU1": {
            "MCA": {
                "...": "..."
            }
        }
    }
}

```

### Analyzing Crash Dumps

    

```
# Use Intel Crash Analyzer Tool (proprietary)
# Or parse JSON manually:

# Extract MCA status
cat crashdump.json | jq '.crash_data.CPU0.MCA.MC0_STATUS'

# Check for valid error
# Bit 63 (VAL) = 1 indicates valid error
# Bit 61 (UC) = 1 indicates uncorrected error
# Bit 60 (EN) = 1 indicates error reporting enabled

# Decode MCACOD (bits 15:0) for error type
cat crashdump.json | jq -r '.crash_data.CPU0.MCA | to_entries[] |
    select(.key | endswith("_STATUS")) |
    "\(.key): \(.value)"'
```

### Storage Location

    

```
# Crash dumps stored at:
ls /var/lib/crashdump/

# Format: crashdump_.json
# Example: crashdump_20240115_103045.json

# Check available space
df -h /var/lib/crashdump/

# Cleanup old dumps
# Managed by crashdump service based on retention policy
```

### D-Bus Interface

    

```
# Crashdump D-Bus service
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.CrashDump

# Get last crash dump status
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.CrashDump \
    /xyz/openbmc_project/crashdump \
    xyz.openbmc_project.CrashDump.Manager \
    LastCrashDumpTime

# Trigger collection via D-Bus
busctl call xyz.openbmc_project.CrashDump \
    /xyz/openbmc_project/crashdump \
    xyz.openbmc_project.CrashDump.Manager \
    GenerateCrashDump s "OnDemand"
```

## Integration with Intel Tools

    

### Intel System Debugger (ISD)

    

```
Prerequisites:
- Intel System Studio or standalone ISD
- Network connectivity to BMC
- BMC credentials with debug privileges

Connection Steps:
1. Launch Intel System Debugger
2. Create new target connection:
   - Type: At-Scale Debug
   - Host: 
   - Port: 5123
3. Authenticate with BMC credentials
4. Discover JTAG chain
5. Connect to CPU target
```

### OpenIPC Configuration

    

```
# OpenIPC is part of Intel System Studio
# Configuration file: openipc.cfg

[connection]
type = asd
host = 192.168.1.100
port = 5123
username = root
password = 0penBmc

[target]
cpu_type = SPR  # Sapphire Rapids
num_cpus = 2

[debug]
log_level = info
```

## Security Considerations

    

ASD provides deep system access equivalent to physical JTAG. Implement strict security controls.

### Access Control

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Restrict ASD access to specific users</span>
<span class="c"># Configure via Redfish AccountService</span>

<span class="c"># Create debug-only user</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> POST <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{
        "UserName": "debuguser",
        "Password": "SecureDebugPass123!",
        "RoleId": "Administrator"
    }'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/AccountService/Accounts
```

</div></div>

### Network Security

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Restrict ASD port access via firewall</span>
iptables <span class="nt">-A</span> INPUT <span class="nt">-p</span> tcp <span class="nt">--dport</span> 5123 <span class="nt">-s</span> 10.0.0.0/8 <span class="nt">-j</span> ACCEPT
iptables <span class="nt">-A</span> INPUT <span class="nt">-p</span> tcp <span class="nt">--dport</span> 5123 <span class="nt">-j</span> DROP

<span class="c"># Use VPN or isolated management network for debug access</span>
```

</div></div>

### Audit Logging

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Enable debug access logging</span>
<span class="c"># All ASD connections logged to journal</span>

<span class="c"># View ASD access logs</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> asd | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> <span class="s2">"connection</span><span class="se">\|</span><span class="s2">auth"</span>

<span class="c"># Integrate with SEL</span>
<span class="c"># ASD events appear in System Event Log</span>
ipmitool sel list | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> debug
```

</div></div>

### Production Recommendations

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Setting | Development | Production |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ASD Enabled | Yes | No (disable) |
| Debug Port | Open | Blocked |
| Crashdump | Enabled | Enabled |
| Auto-collection | Enabled | Enabled |
| Retention | 30 days | 7 days |

</div>

### Disabling ASD in Production

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Stop and disable ASD service</span>
systemctl stop asd
systemctl disable asd

<span class="c"># Or remove from build</span>
<span class="c"># IMAGE_INSTALL:remove = "asd"</span>

<span class="c"># Verify disabled</span>
systemctl status asd
ss <span class="nt">-tlnp</span> | <span class="nb">grep </span>5123  <span class="c"># Should show nothing</span>
```

</div></div>

## Troubleshooting

    

### ASD Connection Issues

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check ASD daemon is running</span>
systemctl status asd

<span class="c"># Verify port is listening</span>
ss <span class="nt">-tlnp</span> | <span class="nb">grep </span>5123

<span class="c"># Check authentication</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> asd | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> <span class="s2">"auth</span><span class="se">\|</span><span class="s2">fail"</span>

<span class="c"># Verify GPIO configuration</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/kernel/debug/gpio | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> jtag

<span class="c"># Test JTAG chain manually</span>
jtag_test <span class="nt">--scan</span>
```

</div></div>

### JTAG Chain Not Detected

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check XDP present signal</span>
gpioget gpiochip0 <xdp_present_pin>

<span class="c"># Verify CPU is powered</span>
obmcutil state

<span class="c"># Check JTAG signals</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/kernel/debug/pinctrl/<span class="k">*</span>/pins | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> jtag

<span class="c"># Reset JTAG state machine</span>
jtag_test <span class="nt">--reset</span>
```

</div></div>

### Crash Dump Collection Fails

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check crashdump service</span>
systemctl status crashdump

<span class="c"># View crash dump logs</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> crashdump <span class="nt">-f</span>

<span class="c"># Verify PECI connectivity</span>
peci_cmds Ping 0x30  <span class="c"># CPU0 address</span>

<span class="c"># Check GPIO error signals</span>
gpioget gpiochip0 <caterr_pin>
gpioget gpiochip0 <err2_pin>

<span class="c"># Manual PECI test</span>
peci_cmds RdPkgConfig 0x30 0 0
```

</div></div>

### Incomplete Crash Dump

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check storage space</span>
<span class="nb">df</span> <span class="nt">-h</span> /var/lib/crashdump/

<span class="c"># Verify PECI timeout</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> crashdump | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> <span class="s2">"timeout</span><span class="se">\|</span><span class="s2">peci"</span>

<span class="c"># Check CPU accessibility</span>
peci_cmds Ping 0x30
peci_cmds Ping 0x31  <span class="c"># CPU1 if present</span>

<span class="c"># Retry collection</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> POST <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{"DiagnosticDataType": "OEM", "OEMDiagnosticDataType": "OnDemand"}'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/Crashdump/Actions/LogService.CollectDiagnosticData
```

## Platform-Specific Notes

    

### Intel Xeon Scalable (Ice Lake, Sapphire Rapids)

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
- Supports enhanced crashdump features
- Multiple MCA banks per CPU
- Extended TOR dump capability
- Hardware crashlog support
```

</div></div>

### Intel Xeon D

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
- Reduced feature set
- Single-socket configuration typical
- Integrated PCH
```

</div></div>

### Supported Platforms

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Platform | ASD | ACD | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ice Lake-SP | Yes | Yes | Full support |
| Sapphire Rapids | Yes | Yes | Enhanced crashlog |
| Xeon D | Yes | Limited | Reduced MCA banks |
| Older Xeon | Limited | Limited | Legacy JTAG only |

</div>

## References

    

* [Intel At-Scale Debug (ASD)](https://github.com/Intel-BMC/asd) - Intel BMC debug access solution
* [Intel-BMC OpenBMC](https://github.com/Intel-BMC/openbmc) - Intel OpenBMC fork with crashdump support
* [bmcweb Crashdump Endpoints](https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/redfish-core/lib/log_services.hpp) - Redfish crashdump implementation
* [Intel IPMI OEM](https://github.com/openbmc/intel-ipmi-oem) - Intel-specific IPMI commands
* [PECI Specification](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-power-thermal-technologies.html) - Platform Environment Control Interface

OpenIPC (Open In-band Processor Communication) is part of Intel System Studio and is not publicly available on GitHub. Contact Intel for access.

## Error Injection

    

Error injection enables RAS (Reliability, Availability, Serviceability) validation by deliberately triggering hardware errors to verify detection and recovery mechanisms.

### Error Injection via ASD/ITP

    

When connected to a CPU via ASD, you can inject errors through the debug interface to test MCA handling:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Prerequisites:</span>
<span class="c"># - ASD daemon running and connected</span>
<span class="c"># - Intel System Debugger (ISD) or OpenIPC connected</span>
<span class="c"># - Host powered on and running OS</span>

<span class="c"># Via ISD scripting interface (Python):</span>
<span class="c"># Connect to target</span>
target <span class="o">=</span> debugger.connect<span class="o">(</span><span class="s2">"asd://bmc-ip:5123"</span><span class="o">)</span>

<span class="c"># Inject correctable memory error (CE)</span>
<span class="c"># Write to IA32_MCi_STATUS to simulate error</span>
target.write_msr<span class="o">(</span><span class="nv">thread</span><span class="o">=</span>0, <span class="nv">msr</span><span class="o">=</span>0x401,
    <span class="nv">value</span><span class="o">=</span>0x8C00004000010150<span class="o">)</span>  <span class="c"># Correctable ECC error</span>

<span class="c"># Inject uncorrectable error (UCE)</span>
target.write_msr<span class="o">(</span><span class="nv">thread</span><span class="o">=</span>0, <span class="nv">msr</span><span class="o">=</span>0x401,
    <span class="nv">value</span><span class="o">=</span>0xBE00000000800400<span class="o">)</span>  <span class="c"># Uncorrected, PCC set</span>

<span class="c"># Trigger machine check via APIC</span>
target.write_msr<span class="o">(</span><span class="nv">thread</span><span class="o">=</span>0, <span class="nv">msr</span><span class="o">=</span>0x79,  <span class="c"># MCG_STATUS</span>
    <span class="nv">value</span><span class="o">=</span>0x05<span class="o">)</span>  <span class="c"># MCIP + RIPV</span>
```

</div></div>

Error injection through ASD bypasses normal error reporting paths. Use only in isolated test environments with expendable hardware. Injecting UCE with PCC (Processor Context Corrupt) will crash the host.

### ACPI EINJ Interface

    

The ACPI Error INJection (EINJ) table provides a firmware-standard method to inject errors without requiring ASD debug access. This is the preferred method for production-like RAS testing.

#### EINJ Overview

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    EINJ Error Injection Flow                 │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                              │
│  BMC / Test Host                        Platform BIOS/UEFI   │
│  ┌──────────────────────┐               ┌──────────────────┐ │
│  │ Redfish / ipmitool   │               │ ACPI EINJ Table  │ │
│  │ or Linux einj driver │──── IPMI ────>│ Error Action     │ │
│  └──────────────────────┘               │ Table entries    │ │
│                                         └────────┬─────────┘ │
│                                                  │           │
│                                         ┌────────v─────────┐ │
│  Host OS (Linux)                        │ Platform HW      │ │
│  ┌──────────────────────┐               │ Error injection  │ │
│  │ /sys/kernel/debug/   │ ─── MMIO ───>│ registers         │ │
│  │   apei/einj/         │               └──────────────────┘ │
│  └──────────────────────┘                                    │
│                                                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

#### Using EINJ from the Host OS

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># On the host Linux OS (not the BMC):</span>

<span class="c"># Load EINJ support module</span>
modprobe einj

<span class="c"># Check available error types</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/kernel/debug/apei/einj/available_error_type
<span class="c"># Typical output:</span>
<span class="c"># 0x00000001  Processor Correctable</span>
<span class="c"># 0x00000002  Processor Uncorrectable non-fatal</span>
<span class="c"># 0x00000004  Processor Uncorrectable fatal</span>
<span class="c"># 0x00000008  Memory Correctable</span>
<span class="c"># 0x00000010  Memory Uncorrectable non-fatal</span>
<span class="c"># 0x00000020  Memory Uncorrectable fatal</span>
<span class="c"># 0x00000040  PCIe Correctable</span>
<span class="c"># 0x00000080  PCIe Uncorrectable non-fatal</span>
<span class="c"># 0x00000100  PCIe Uncorrectable fatal</span>

<span class="c"># Inject correctable memory error</span>
<span class="nb">echo </span>0x00000008 <span class="o">></span> /sys/kernel/debug/apei/einj/error_type
<span class="nb">echo </span>0x0 <span class="o">></span> /sys/kernel/debug/apei/einj/error_inject

<span class="c"># Inject PCIe correctable error</span>
<span class="nb">echo </span>0x00000040 <span class="o">></span> /sys/kernel/debug/apei/einj/error_type
<span class="nb">echo </span>0x0 <span class="o">></span> /sys/kernel/debug/apei/einj/error_inject

<span class="c"># Inject memory UCE at specific address</span>
<span class="nb">echo </span>0x00000010 <span class="o">></span> /sys/kernel/debug/apei/einj/error_type
<span class="nb">echo </span>0x7F400000 <span class="o">></span> /sys/kernel/debug/apei/einj/param1  <span class="c"># Physical address</span>
<span class="nb">echo </span>0xFFFFFFFFFFFFF000 <span class="o">></span> /sys/kernel/debug/apei/einj/param2  <span class="c"># Address mask</span>
<span class="nb">echo </span>0x0 <span class="o">></span> /sys/kernel/debug/apei/einj/error_inject
```

</div></div>

#### Monitoring Injected Errors from BMC

    

After injecting errors on the host, verify the BMC captures them:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># On the BMC:</span>

<span class="c"># Check for new crash dumps (for fatal errors)</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/Crashdump/Entries

<span class="c"># Check System Event Log for error records</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/EventLog/Entries

<span class="c"># Monitor PECI for MCA errors in real-time</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> crashdump <span class="nt">-f</span>

<span class="c"># Check if CATERR was asserted (for fatal errors)</span>
gpioget gpiochip0 <caterr_pin>
```

</div></div>

### RAS Validation Workflow

    

A structured approach to validating RAS features on an Intel platform with OpenBMC:

#### Step 1: Pre-Test Setup

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Verify BMC services are running</span>
systemctl status crashdump
systemctl status phosphor-host-state-manager

<span class="c"># Clear existing logs</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> POST <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/Crashdump/Actions/LogService.ClearLog

<span class="c"># Verify PECI connectivity to all CPUs</span>
peci_cmds Ping 0x30  <span class="c"># CPU0</span>
peci_cmds Ping 0x31  <span class="c"># CPU1 (if dual-socket)</span>

<span class="c"># Record baseline MCA state</span>
<span class="k">for </span>bank <span class="k">in </span>0 1 2 3 4 5<span class="p">;</span> <span class="k">do
    </span><span class="nv">msr</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="k">$((</span><span class="m">0</span>x401 <span class="o">+</span> bank <span class="o">*</span> <span class="m">4</span><span class="k">))</span>
    peci_cmds RdIAMSR 0x30 0 <span class="si">$(</span><span class="nb">printf</span> <span class="s2">"0x%x"</span> <span class="nv">$msr</span><span class="si">)</span>
<span class="k">done</span>
```

</div></div>

#### Step 2: Execute Test Matrix

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Test Case | Error Type | Injection Method | Expected BMC Response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CE-MEM-01 | Memory correctable | EINJ 0x08 | SEL entry, no crash dump |
| CE-PCIE-01 | PCIe correctable | EINJ 0x40 | SEL entry, AER log |
| UCE-MEM-01 | Memory uncorrectable | EINJ 0x10 | SEL + crash dump collected |
| UCE-FATAL-01 | Fatal processor | EINJ 0x04 | CATERR, full crash dump, host reset |
| MCA-ITP-01 | MCA via ASD | ISD MSR write | Crash dump if PCC set |

</div>

#### Step 3: Verify Collection

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># After each injection, verify BMC response:</span>

<span class="c"># 1. Check crash dump was collected (for UCE/fatal)</span>
<span class="nv">ENTRIES</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="si">$(</span>curl <span class="nt">-sk</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/Crashdump/Entries <span class="se">\</span>
    | python3 <span class="nt">-c</span> <span class="s2">"import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['Members@odata.count'])"</span><span class="si">)</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"Crash dump entries: </span><span class="nv">$ENTRIES</span><span class="s2">"</span>

<span class="c"># 2. Download and validate crash dump content</span>
curl <span class="nt">-sk</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-o</span> crashdump.json <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/Crashdump/Entries/1/attachment"</span>

<span class="c"># 3. Verify MCA banks contain expected error signature</span>
python3 <span class="nt">-c</span> <span class="s2">"
import json
with open('crashdump.json') as f:
    data = json.load(f)
for cpu in ['CPU0', 'CPU1']:
    if cpu in data.get('crash_data', {}):
        mca = data['crash_data'][cpu].get('MCA', {})
        for bank, val in mca.items():
            if bank.endswith('_STATUS') and int(val, 16) & (1 << 63):
                uc = 'UC' if int(val, 16) & (1 << 61) else 'CE'
                print(f'{cpu} {bank}: {val} [{uc}]')
"</span>

<span class="c"># 4. Verify host recovery (for non-fatal errors)</span>
obmcutil state  <span class="c"># Should show Running for non-fatal</span>
```

</div></div>

#### Step 4: Report Generation

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Collect all test artifacts</span>
<span class="nb">mkdir</span> <span class="nt">-p</span> /tmp/ras-validation-<span class="si">$(</span><span class="nb">date</span> +%Y%m%d<span class="si">)</span>
<span class="nb">cd</span> /tmp/ras-validation-<span class="si">$(</span><span class="nb">date</span> +%Y%m%d<span class="si">)</span>

<span class="c"># Export crash dumps</span>
<span class="k">for </span>i <span class="k">in</span> <span class="si">$(</span><span class="nb">seq </span>1 <span class="nv">$ENTRIES</span><span class="si">)</span><span class="p">;</span> <span class="k">do
    </span>curl <span class="nt">-sk</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-o</span> <span class="s2">"crashdump_</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">i</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">.json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
        <span class="s2">"https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/Crashdump/Entries/</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">i</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">/attachment"</span>
<span class="k">done</span>

<span class="c"># Export event log</span>
curl <span class="nt">-sk</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-o</span> event_log.json <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/EventLog/Entries

<span class="c"># Export BMC journal</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> crashdump <span class="nt">--since</span> <span class="s2">"today"</span> <span class="o">></span> crashdump_journal.log
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> phosphor-host-state-manager <span class="nt">--since</span> <span class="s2">"today"</span> <span class="o">></span> state_manager.log
```

</div></div>

For automated RAS validation, see the example scripts in `docs/examples/error-injection/` which automate the inject-verify-report cycle.

## Deep Dive

    

This section provides detailed technical information for developers who want to understand Intel ASD and crash dump internals.

### ASD Protocol Message Format

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      ASD Network Protocol Format                            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│  TCP Connection (Port 5123):                                                │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  1. Client connects to BMC:5123                                        │ │
│  │  2. TLS handshake (optional, depends on config)                        │ │
│  │  3. Authentication (BMC credentials via custom protocol)               │ │
│  │  4. Message exchange begins                                            │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
│  ASD Message Header:                                                        │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  Offset │ Size │ Field        │ Description                            │ │
│  │  ───────┼──────┼──────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────── │ │
│  │  0x00   │ 1    │ cmd_stat     │ Command/Status byte                    │ │
│  │  0x01   │ 1    │ cmd_type     │ Message type                           │ │
│  │  0x02   │ 2    │ size_lsb     │ Payload size (little-endian)           │ │
│  │  0x04   │ 2    │ size_msb     │                                        │ │
│  │  0x06   │ 1    │ tag          │ Sequence tag for request matching      │ │
│  │  0x07   │ 1    │ origin       │ Message origin ID                      │ │
│  │  0x08   │ N    │ payload      │ Variable-length payload                │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
│  Message Types (cmd_type):                                                  │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  Type   │ Name              │ Description                              │ │
│  │  ───────┼───────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────│ │
│  │  0x01   │ AGENT_CONTROL     │ Init, reset, status queries              │ │
│  │  0x02   │ JTAG_CHAIN        │ JTAG operations (scan, shift)            │ │
│  │  0x03   │ I2C_MSG           │ I2C read/write transactions              │ │
│  │  0x04   │ GPIO_MSG          │ GPIO control (XDP signals)               │ │
│  │  0x05   │ REMOTE_DEBUG      │ Enable/disable debug mode                │ │
│  │  0x06   │ HW_DEBUG          │ Hardware debug operations                │ │
│  │  0x07   │ I3C_MSG           │ I3C transactions (newer CPUs)            │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
│  JTAG Message Payload:                                                      │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  JTAG_CHAIN message structure:                                         │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  │  ┌──────────┬──────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │ │
│  │  │ JTAG Cmd │ Bit Count│ TDI/TMS Data                               │  │ │
│  │  │ (1 byte) │ (2 bytes)│ (N bytes, packed bits)                     │  │ │
│  │  └──────────┴──────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  │  JTAG Commands:                                                        │ │
│  │  0x00 - SET_TAP_STATE  (navigate TAP state machine)                    │ │
│  │  0x01 - WAIT_CYCLES    (idle cycles)                                   │ │
│  │  0x02 - SHIFT_TDI      (shift data into chain)                         │ │
│  │  0x03 - SHIFT_TDO      (shift data out of chain)                       │ │
│  │  0x04 - SHIFT_TDI_TDO  (bidirectional shift)                           │ │
│  │  0x05 - SCAN_CHAIN     (auto-discover JTAG chain)                      │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### JTAG TAP State Machine

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        JTAG TAP State Machine                               │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│                        ┌──────────────────┐                                 │
│                        │   Test-Logic-    │<──── TMS=1 (5+ clocks to reset) │
│              ┌────────>│     Reset        │                                 │
│              │         └────────┬─────────┘                                 │
│              │                  │ TMS=0                                     │
│              │                  v                                           │
│              │         ┌──────────────────┐                                 │
│              │         │   Run-Test/Idle  │<────────────────┐               │
│              │         └────────┬─────────┘                 │               │
│              │                  │ TMS=1                     │ TMS=0         │
│              │                  v                           │               │
│              │         ┌──────────────────┐                 │               │
│              │         │   Select-DR-Scan │─── TMS=1 ───────┼──┐            │
│              │         └────────┬─────────┘                 │  │            │
│              │                  │ TMS=0                     │  │            │
│              │                  v                           │  │            │
│              │         ┌──────────────────┐                 │  │            │
│              │         │    Capture-DR    │                 │  │            │
│              │         └────────┬─────────┘                 │  │            │
│              │                  │ TMS=0                     │  │            │
│              │                  v                           │  │            │
│              │         ┌──────────────────┐                 │  │            │
│    TMS=1     │   ┌────>│     Shift-DR     │───┐ TMS=0       │  │            │
│     │        │   │     └────────┬─────────┘   │ (loop)      │  │            │
│     │        │   │              │ TMS=1       │             │  │            │
│     │        │   │              v             │             │  │            │
│     │        │   │     ┌──────────────────┐   │             │  │            │
│     │        │   │     │     Exit1-DR     │<──┘             │  │            │
│     │        │   │     └────────┬─────────┘                 │  │            │
│     │        │   │ TMS=0        │ TMS=1                     │  │            │
│     │        │   │              v                           │  │            │
│     │        │   │     ┌──────────────────┐                 │  │            │
│     │        │   └─────│     Pause-DR     │                 │  │            │
│     │        │         └────────┬─────────┘                 │  │            │
│     │        │                  │ TMS=1                     │  │            │
│     │        │                  v                           │  │            │
│     │        │         ┌──────────────────┐                 │  │            │
│     │        │         │     Exit2-DR     │                 │  │            │
│     │        │         └────────┬─────────┘                 │  │            │
│     │        │                  │ TMS=1                     │  │            │
│     │        │                  v                           │  │            │
│     │        │         ┌──────────────────┐                 │  │            │
│     │        └─────────│    Update-DR     │─────────────────┘  │            │
│     │                  └──────────────────┘                    │            │
│     │                                                          │            │
│     │                  ┌──────────────────┐                    │            │
│     └──────────────────│  Select-IR-Scan  │<───────────────────┘            │
│                        └────────┬─────────┘                                 │
│                                 │                                           │
│                       (IR path mirrors DR path)                             │
│                                                                             │
│  Key States:                                                                │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  State       │ Purpose                                                 │ │
│  │  ────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │ │
│  │  Shift-DR    │ Shift data through Data Register (target registers)     │ │
│  │  Shift-IR    │ Shift instruction to select which DR to access          │ │
│  │  Update-DR   │ Latch shifted data into target register                 │ │
│  │  Capture-DR  │ Capture current register value for readout              │ │
│  │  Run-Test    │ Execute loaded instruction (run test, BIST, etc.)       │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### PECI Crash Dump Command Flow

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    PECI Crash Dump Collection Sequence                      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│  BMC (crashdump service)                    Intel CPU                       │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────┐           ┌──────────────────────────┐    │
│  │                              │           │                          │    │
│  │  1. Detect CATERR# GPIO      │           │  Error condition         │    │
│  │     (falling edge interrupt) │<──────────│  asserts CATERR#         │    │
│  │                              │           │                          │    │
│  │  2. PECI Ping (verify CPU)   │           │                          │    │
│  │     ┌────────────────────────┴───────────┴────────────────────────┐ │    │
│  │     │  Command: Ping                                              │ │    │
│  │     │  Address: 0x30 (CPU0) or 0x31 (CPU1)                        │ │    │
│  │     │  Response: Completion code 0x40 = success                   │ │    │
│  │     └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │    │
│  │                              │           │                          │    │
│  │  3. Read CPU ID              │           │                          │    │
│  │     ┌────────────────────────┴───────────┴────────────────────────┐ │    │
│  │     │  Command: RdPkgConfig                                       │ │    │
│  │     │  Index: 0x00 (CPU_ID)                                       │ │    │
│  │     │  Response: Family/Model/Stepping                            │ │    │
│  │     └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │    │
│  │                              │           │                          │    │
│  │  4. Read MCA Banks           │           │                          │    │
│  │     ┌────────────────────────┴───────────┴────────────────────────┐ │    │
│  │     │  For each MCA bank (0 to N):                                │ │    │
│  │     │    Command: RdIAMSR                                         │ │    │
│  │     │    Thread: 0 (or iterate all threads)                       │ │    │
│  │     │    MSR: IA32_MCi_STATUS (0x401, 0x405, 0x409, ...)          │ │    │
│  │     │    MSR: IA32_MCi_ADDR (0x402, 0x406, 0x40A, ...)            │ │    │
│  │     │    MSR: IA32_MCi_MISC (0x403, 0x407, 0x40B, ...)            │ │    │
│  │     └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │    │
│  │                              │           │                          │    │
│  │  5. Crashdump Discovery      │           │                          │    │
│  │     ┌────────────────────────┴───────────┴────────────────────────┐ │    │
│  │     │  Command: CrashDump Discovery                               │ │    │
│  │     │  Returns: Available crashdump sections and sizes            │ │    │
│  │     │  Sections: TOR, PM_Info, Address_Map, etc.                  │ │    │
│  │     └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │    │
│  │                              │           │                          │    │
│  │  6. Read Crashdump Data      │           │                          │    │
│  │     ┌────────────────────────┴───────────┴────────────────────────┐ │    │
│  │     │  Command: CrashDump GetFrame                                │ │    │
│  │     │  Section: (TOR, PM_Info, etc.)                              │ │    │
│  │     │  Frame: 0, 1, 2, ... (paginate through data)                │ │    │
│  │     │  Response: 64-byte frame of crash data                      │ │    │
│  │     └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │    │
│  │                              │           │                          │    │
│  │  7. Store JSON output        │           │                          │    │
│  │     /var/lib/crashdump/      │           │                          │    │
│  │                              │           │                          │    │
│  └──────────────────────────────┘           └──────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                             │
│  PECI Wire Protocol:                                                        │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  Single-wire, half-duplex bus (OD with pull-up)                        │ │
│  │  Clock: 1 MHz typical (variable negotiated)                            │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  │  Frame Format:                                                         │ │
│  │  ┌────────┬────────┬────────┬────────┬────────┬──────────┐             │ │
│  │  │  AWF   │ Target │ Write  │ Read   │ Cmd/   │  FCS     │             │ │
│  │  │(preamble)│ Addr │  Len   │  Len   │ Data   │(checksum)│             │ │
│  │  └────────┴────────┴────────┴────────┴────────┴──────────┘             │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### MCA Bank Status Register Format

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    IA32_MCi_STATUS Register (MSR)                           │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│  64-bit Machine Check Architecture Status Register:                         │
│                                                                             │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  Bit  │ Name    │ Description                                          │ │
│  │  ─────┼─────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────│ │
│  │  63   │ VAL     │ Valid - Error recorded in this bank                  │ │
│  │  62   │ OVER    │ Overflow - Multiple errors, some lost                │ │
│  │  61   │ UC      │ Uncorrected - Error not corrected                    │ │
│  │  60   │ EN      │ Enabled - Error reporting was enabled                │ │
│  │  59   │ MISCV   │ MISC Valid - MCi_MISC contains valid info            │ │
│  │  58   │ ADDRV   │ ADDR Valid - MCi_ADDR contains fault address         │ │
│  │  57   │ PCC     │ Processor Context Corrupt - restart required         │ │
│  │  56   │ S       │ Signaled - Error was signaled to software            │ │
│  │  55   │ AR      │ Action Required - Immediate action needed            │ │
│  │  54-53│ LSB     │ Corrected error local significance                   │ │
│  │  52-38│ Other   │ Model-specific error information                     │ │
│  │  37   │ FW      │ Firmware-corrected error                             │ │
│  │  36-32│ MSCOD   │ Model-specific error code                            │ │
│  │  31-16│ MCACOD  │ MCA error code (architecture-defined)                │ │
│  │  15-0 │ Reserved│ (varies by generation)                               │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
│  MCACOD (bits 15:0) Error Type Examples:                                    │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  Code   │ Meaning                                                      │ │
│  │  ───────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────│ │
│  │  0x0001 │ Unclassified error                                           │ │
│  │  0x0005 │ Internal parity error                                        │ │
│  │  0x000A │ Generic I/O error                                            │ │
│  │  0x010A │ Memory controller error (channel A)                          │ │
│  │  0x010C │ Memory controller error (channel C)                          │ │
│  │  0x0150 │ Memory ECC error                                             │ │
│  │  0x0400 │ Watchdog timer (internal)                                    │ │
│  │  0x0800 │ Internal timer error                                         │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
│  Decoding Example:                                                          │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  MC0_STATUS = 0xBE00000000800400                                       │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  │  Bit 63 (VAL) = 1   -> Error is valid                                  │ │
│  │  Bit 62 (OVER) = 0  -> No overflow                                     │ │
│  │  Bit 61 (UC) = 1    -> Uncorrected error                               │ │
│  │  Bit 60 (EN) = 1    -> Error reporting enabled                         │ │
│  │  Bit 59 (MISCV) = 1 -> MCi_MISC is valid                               │ │
│  │  Bit 58 (ADDRV) = 1 -> MCi_ADDR is valid                               │ │
│  │  Bit 57 (PCC) = 1   -> Processor context corrupt                       │ │
│  │  MCACOD = 0x0400    -> Watchdog timer error                            │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  │  Interpretation: Uncorrected watchdog error, context corrupt,          │ │
│  │                 system restart required                                │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

## Overview

    

AMD EPYC platforms provide system management and debug capabilities through **APML (Advanced Platform Management Link)** and **HDT (Hardware Debug Tool)**. This guide covers the BMC integration for AMD server platforms.

```mermaid
---
title: AMD Platform Management Architecture
---
flowchart TB
    subgraph bmcapps["BMC Applications"]
        direction LR
        telemetry["Telemetry  
Monitoring"]
        ras["RAS/Error  
Handling"]
        powermgmt["Power Mgmt  
Control"]
    end

    subgraph apml["APML Library"]
        apmllib["apml_sbrmi / apml_sbtsi drivers"]
    end

    subgraph bus["I2C / I3C Bus"]
        i2cbus["Communication Bus"]
    end

    subgraph cpu["AMD EPYC Processor"]
        direction LR
        sbrmi["SB-RMI  
(Remote Mgmt I/F)"]
        sbtsi["SB-TSI  
(Thermal Sensor)"]
        hdt["HDT Port  
(Hardware Debug)"]
    end

    bmcapps --> apml
    apml --> bus
    bus --> cpu
```
