## AMD Management Interfaces

    

### SB-RMI (Sideband Remote Management Interface)

    

Provides system management commands:

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Power Management | RAPL power limits, throttling |
| RAS | Machine check, error reporting |
| Mailbox Commands | CPU configuration, CPUID |
| Performance | Core boost, C-states |

</div>

### SB-TSI (Sideband Thermal Sensor Interface)

    

Provides thermal monitoring:

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| CPU Temperature | Die temperature reading |
| Thermal Alerts | High/low temperature thresholds |
| Thermal Throttling | PROCHOT status |

</div>

### HDT (Hardware Debug Tool)

    

Low-level debug access (requires special hardware/NDA):

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| JTAG Access | CPU debug via JTAG chain |
| Run Control | Halt, step, breakpoints |
| Register Access | MSR, GPR access |
| Trace | Instruction trace |

</div>
---

## APML Setup

    

### Build-Time Configuration (Yocto)

    

```bitbake
# In your machine .conf or local.conf

# Include APML support
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " \
    apml-modules \
    apml-library \
    esmi-oob-library \
"

# Kernel configuration
KERNEL_MODULE_AUTOLOAD:append = " apml_sbrmi apml_sbtsi"
```

### Kernel Modules

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Load APML modules</span>
modprobe apml_sbrmi
modprobe apml_sbtsi

<span class="c"># Verify modules loaded</span>
lsmod | <span class="nb">grep </span>apml

<span class="c"># Check I2C devices</span>
i2cdetect <span class="nt">-l</span>
i2cdetect <span class="nt">-y</span> <bus>  <span class="c"># Find SB-RMI/SB-TSI addresses</span>
```

</div></div>

### Device Tree Configuration

    

```dts
&i2c3 {
    status = "okay";

    /* SB-TSI - Thermal sensor */
    sbtsi@4c {
        compatible = "amd,sbtsi";
        reg = <0x4c>;
    };

    /* SB-RMI - Remote management */
    sbrmi@3c {
        compatible = "amd,sbrmi";
        reg = <0x3c>;
    };
};
```

---

## APML Library Usage

    

### Installation

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check APML library</span>
<span class="nb">ls</span> /usr/lib/libapml<span class="k">*</span>

<span class="c"># Check APML tools</span>
which esmi_oob_tool
```

</div></div>

### Reading CPU Temperature

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Via hwmon (SB-TSI driver)</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon<span class="k">*</span>/temp1_input

<span class="c"># Via APML library tool</span>
esmi_oob_tool <span class="nt">-s</span> 0 <span class="nt">--showtemprange</span>
```

</div></div>

### Power Management

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Read current power</span>
esmi_oob_tool <span class="nt">-s</span> 0 <span class="nt">--showpower</span>

<span class="c"># Read power limit</span>
esmi_oob_tool <span class="nt">-s</span> 0 <span class="nt">--showpowerlimit</span>

<span class="c"># Set power limit (in milliwatts)</span>
esmi_oob_tool <span class="nt">-s</span> 0 <span class="nt">--setpowerlimit</span> 200000

<span class="c"># Read TDP</span>
esmi_oob_tool <span class="nt">-s</span> 0 <span class="nt">--showtdp</span>
```

</div></div>

### RAS (Reliability, Availability, Serviceability)

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Read MCA (Machine Check Architecture) status</span>
esmi_oob_tool <span class="nt">-s</span> 0 <span class="nt">--showmcastatus</span>

<span class="c"># Read DIMM temperature</span>
esmi_oob_tool <span class="nt">-s</span> 0 <span class="nt">--showdimmtemp</span>

<span class="c"># Read DIMM power</span>
esmi_oob_tool <span class="nt">-s</span> 0 <span class="nt">--showdimmpower</span>

<span class="c"># Read DIMM thermal sensor</span>
esmi_oob_tool <span class="nt">-s</span> 0 <span class="nt">--showdimmthermal</span>
```

</div></div>

### Mailbox Commands

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Read CPUID</span>
esmi_oob_tool <span class="nt">-s</span> 0 <span class="nt">--showcpuid</span>

<span class="c"># Read processor info</span>
esmi_oob_tool <span class="nt">-s</span> 0 <span class="nt">--showprocinfo</span>

<span class="c"># Read boost limit</span>
esmi_oob_tool <span class="nt">-s</span> 0 <span class="nt">--showboostlimit</span>

<span class="c"># Set boost limit per core</span>
esmi_oob_tool <span class="nt">-s</span> 0 <span class="nt">--setboostlimit</span> <core> <limit>
```

</div></div>

## D-Bus Integration

    

### Sensor Integration

    

APML sensors integrate with OpenBMC’s sensor framework:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Temperature sensors from SB-TSI appear in D-Bus</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.HwmonTempSensor

<span class="c"># Example: CPU temperature</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.HwmonTempSensor <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/temperature/CPU0_Temp <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value Value
```

</div></div>

### Power Monitoring

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Power sensors via APML</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor

<span class="c"># Socket power reading</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/power/CPU0_Power <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value Value
```

</div></div>
---

## AMD OpenBMC Platform

    

### AMDESE OpenBMC

    

AMD maintains an OpenBMC distribution for EPYC platforms:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Clone AMD's OpenBMC</span>
git clone https://github.com/AMDESE/OpenBMC.git

<span class="c"># Build for Genoa platform</span>
<span class="nb">cd </span>OpenBMC
<span class="nb">.</span> setup onyx  <span class="c"># or other platform</span>
bitbake obmc-phosphor-image
```

</div></div>

### Supported Platforms

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Platform | Codename | Socket |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Onyx | Genoa | SP5 |
| Quartz | Genoa | SP5 |
| Ruby | Turin | SP5 |
| Chalupa | Genoa | SP5 |

</div>

## HDT Debug Access

    

HDT provides deep hardware access. Full documentation requires AMD NDA. Use only in controlled debug environments.

### HDT Overview

    

HDT (Hardware Debug Tool) is AMD’s JTAG-based debug interface:

* Accessed via dedicated debug header or BMC mux
* Requires specialized debug tools (AMD HDT software or third-party)
* Provides run-control (halt, step, breakpoints)
* Full register and memory access

### BMC JTAG Mux

    

Some platforms support JTAG muxing through BMC:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check for JTAG mux support</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/kernel/debug/gpio | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> jtag

<span class="c"># JTAG mux control (platform-specific)</span>
gpioset gpiochip0 <jtag_mux_gpio><span class="o">=</span>1  <span class="c"># Route JTAG to BMC</span>
```

</div></div>

### Commercial Solutions

    

For at-scale debug, commercial tools provide BMC-embedded debug:

* ASSET InterTech ScanWorks Embedded Diagnostics (SED)
* Lauterbach TRACE32 with remote access
* AMD HDT software (under NDA)

## Crash Dump Collection

    

### RAS Error Logging

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Machine Check errors are logged to SEL</span>
ipmitool sel list | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> <span class="s2">"Machine Check"</span>

<span class="c"># View via Redfish</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/EventLog/Entries
```

</div></div>

### BERT (Boot Error Record Table)

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># BERT records are available via ACPI</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/firmware/acpi/tables/BERT

<span class="c"># Decoded in system logs</span>
dmesg | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> <span class="s2">"BERT"</span>
journalctl | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> <span class="s2">"hardware error"</span>
```

</div></div>

### Collecting Debug Data

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Collect system state dump</span>
dreport <span class="nt">-d</span> /tmp/debug <span class="nt">-n</span> amd_debug <span class="nt">-t</span> user

<span class="c"># Include APML data</span>
esmi_oob_tool <span class="nt">-s</span> 0 <span class="nt">--showallinfo</span> <span class="o">></span> /tmp/apml_state.txt

<span class="c"># Read MCA banks</span>
esmi_oob_tool <span class="nt">-s</span> 0 <span class="nt">--showmcastatus</span> <span class="o">></span> /tmp/mca_status.txt
```

</div></div>

## Troubleshooting

    

### APML Not Working

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check I2C bus connectivity</span>
i2cdetect <span class="nt">-y</span> 3  <span class="c"># Replace with correct bus</span>

<span class="c"># Verify kernel modules</span>
lsmod | <span class="nb">grep </span>apml

<span class="c"># Check dmesg for errors</span>
dmesg | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> <span class="s2">"sbrmi</span><span class="se">\|</span><span class="s2">sbtsi</span><span class="se">\|</span><span class="s2">apml"</span>

<span class="c"># Verify device nodes</span>
<span class="nb">ls</span> <span class="nt">-la</span> /dev/sbrmi<span class="k">*</span> /dev/sbtsi<span class="k">*</span>
```

</div></div>

### Temperature Reading Fails

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check hwmon path</span>
<span class="nb">ls</span> /sys/class/hwmon/

<span class="c"># Find correct hwmon device</span>
<span class="k">for </span>h <span class="k">in</span> /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon<span class="k">*</span><span class="p">;</span> <span class="k">do
    </span><span class="nv">name</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="si">$(</span><span class="nb">cat</span> <span class="nv">$h</span>/name 2>/dev/null<span class="si">)</span>
    <span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"</span><span class="nv">$h</span><span class="s2">: </span><span class="nv">$name</span><span class="s2">"</span>
<span class="k">done</span>

<span class="c"># Read directly</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon<N>/temp1_input
```

</div></div>

### Command Timeouts

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># APML commands may timeout under heavy load</span>
<span class="c"># Increase timeout in library calls</span>

<span class="c"># Check SMBus errors</span>
dmesg | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> <span class="s2">"i2c</span><span class="se">\|</span><span class="s2">smbus"</span>

<span class="c"># Retry with delay</span>
<span class="nb">sleep </span>1 <span class="o">&&</span> esmi_oob_tool <span class="nt">-s</span> 0 <span class="nt">--showpower</span>
```

</div></div>

### Permission Issues

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># APML requires root or proper group membership</span>
<span class="nb">ls</span> <span class="nt">-la</span> /dev/sbrmi0 /dev/sbtsi0

<span class="c"># Add user to appropriate group</span>
usermod <span class="nt">-aG</span> i2c <username>
```

</div></div>

## Security Considerations

    

### Access Control

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Restrict APML access to administrators only</span>
<span class="nb">chmod </span>600 /dev/sbrmi<span class="k">*</span> /dev/sbtsi<span class="k">*</span>

<span class="c"># Use D-Bus policy for access control</span>
<span class="c"># /etc/dbus-1/system.d/apml.conf</span>
```

</div></div>

### Audit Logging

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Log APML access</span>
<span class="c"># Integrate with phosphor-logging for audit trail</span>
```

</div></div>

### Production Recommendations

    

* Disable HDT access in production (via fuses or GPIO)
* Restrict APML to essential operations
* Monitor for anomalous power/thermal changes
* Log all RAS events

## Deep Dive

    

This section provides detailed technical information for developers who want to understand AMD APML internals and SB-RMI/SB-TSI protocols.

### APML Communication Architecture

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      APML Sideband Interface Architecture                   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│  BMC                                        AMD EPYC Processor              │
│  ┌────────────────────────────┐             ┌────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │                            │             │                            │  │
│  │  ┌──────────────────────┐  │  I2C/I3C   │  ┌──────────────────────┐  │  │
│  │  │  APML Library        │  │  ──────────│──│  System Management   │  │  │
│  │  │  (esmi_oob_library)  │  │  Bus       │  │  Unit (SMU)          │  │  │
│  │  └──────────┬───────────┘  │             │  └──────────────────────┘  │  │
│  │             │              │             │             │              │  │
│  │  ┌──────────┴───────────┐  │             │  ┌──────────┴───────────┐  │  │
│  │  │  Kernel Driver       │  │             │  │  Sideband Interfaces │  │  │
│  │  │  ┌─────────────────┐ │  │             │  │                      │  │  │
│  │  │  │  apml_sbrmi.ko  │ │  │   I2C      │  │  SB-RMI (0x3C)       │  │  │
│  │  │  │  /dev/sbrmi0    │─│──│───────────>│──│  Remote Management   │  │  │
│  │  │  └─────────────────┘ │  │             │  │  Interface           │  │  │
│  │  │  ┌─────────────────┐ │  │             │  │                      │  │  │
│  │  │  │  apml_sbtsi.ko  │ │  │   I2C      │  │  SB-TSI (0x4C)       │  │  │
│  │  │  │  /dev/sbtsi0    │─│──│───────────>│──│  Thermal Sensor      │  │  │
│  │  │  └─────────────────┘ │  │             │  │  Interface           │  │  │
│  │  └──────────────────────┘  │             │  └──────────────────────┘  │  │
│  │                            │             │                            │  │
│  └────────────────────────────┘             └────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                                                             │
│  I2C Bus Configuration:                                                     │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  Address  │ Interface │ Function                                       │ │
│  │  ─────────┼───────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────── │ │
│  │  0x3C     │ SB-RMI    │ Remote management, mailbox commands             │ │
│  │  0x4C     │ SB-TSI    │ Thermal sensor, temperature alerts              │ │
│  │  0x3D     │ SB-RMI    │ Secondary socket (Socket 1)                     │ │
│  │  0x4D     │ SB-TSI    │ Secondary socket (Socket 1)                     │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
│  I2C Speed: Standard mode (100 kHz) or Fast mode (400 kHz)                  │
│  Pull-up: 2.2kΩ to 3.3V                                                     │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### SB-RMI Mailbox Protocol

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    SB-RMI Mailbox Command Sequence                          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│  Mailbox Architecture:                                                      │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  SMU (System Management Unit) processes mailbox commands               │ │
│  │  BMC writes command/data, waits for SMU to process, reads response     │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
│  Mailbox Transaction Flow:                                                  │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  │  Step 1: Check mailbox not busy                                        │ │
│  │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │ │
│  │  │  Read SB_RMI_STATUS (0x02)                                       │  │ │
│  │  │  Wait for SwAlertSts bit to clear                                │  │ │
│  │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │ │
│  │                              │                                         │ │
│  │                              v                                         │ │
│  │  Step 2: Write input arguments (if any)                                │ │
│  │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │ │
│  │  │  Write to InBndMsg registers (0x50-0x5F)                         │  │ │
│  │  │  Up to 16 bytes of input data                                    │  │ │
│  │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │ │
│  │                              │                                         │ │
│  │                              v                                         │ │
│  │  Step 3: Write command                                                 │ │
│  │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │ │
│  │  │  Write command ID to SB_RMI_SW_MAILBOX_CMD (0x3B)                │  │ │
│  │  │  This triggers SMU to process the command                        │  │ │
│  │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │ │
│  │                              │                                         │ │
│  │                              v                                         │ │
│  │  Step 4: Wait for completion                                           │ │
│  │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │ │
│  │  │  Poll SB_RMI_STATUS for SwAlertSts bit                           │  │ │
│  │  │  Timeout after ~100ms                                            │  │ │
│  │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │ │
│  │                              │                                         │ │
│  │                              v                                         │ │
│  │  Step 5: Read response                                                 │ │
│  │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │ │
│  │  │  Read OutBndMsg registers (0x60-0x6F)                            │  │ │
│  │  │  Read SB_RMI_SW_MAILBOX_STATUS (0x3F) for result code            │  │ │
│  │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
│  Common SB-RMI Mailbox Commands:                                            │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  Command ID │ Name               │ Description                         │ │
│  │  ───────────┼────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────── │ │
│  │  0x01       │ ReadPkgPowerLimit  │ Read socket power limit (TDP cap)   │ │
│  │  0x02       │ WritePkgPowerLimit │ Set socket power limit              │ │
│  │  0x03       │ ReadPkgPowerConsumption │ Read current power draw        │ │
│  │  0x04       │ ReadDDRBandwidth   │ Read memory bandwidth usage         │ │
│  │  0x05       │ ReadBoostLimit     │ Read boost frequency limit          │ │
│  │  0x06       │ WriteBoostLimit    │ Set boost frequency limit           │ │
│  │  0x10       │ ReadMcaData        │ Read Machine Check registers        │ │
│  │  0x11       │ ReadDimmTemp       │ Read DIMM temperature               │ │
│  │  0x12       │ ReadDimmPower      │ Read DIMM power consumption         │ │
│  │  0x20       │ ReadCpuId          │ Read CPU family/model/stepping      │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### SB-TSI Temperature Sensing

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    SB-TSI Thermal Interface Protocol                        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│  Register Map:                                                              │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  Offset │ Register          │ Access │ Description                     │ │
│  │  ───────┼───────────────────┼────────┼──────────────────────────────── │ │
│  │  0x00   │ CPU_TEMP_INT      │ R      │ CPU temp integer part (°C)      │ │
│  │  0x01   │ STATUS            │ R      │ Status and alert flags          │ │
│  │  0x02   │ CONFIG            │ R/W    │ Configuration register          │ │
│  │  0x03   │ UPDATE_RATE       │ R/W    │ Temperature update rate         │ │
│  │  0x04   │ HI_TEMP_INT       │ R/W    │ High temp threshold integer     │ │
│  │  0x05   │ LO_TEMP_INT       │ R/W    │ Low temp threshold integer      │ │
│  │  0x10   │ CPU_TEMP_DEC      │ R      │ CPU temp decimal part           │ │
│  │  0x11   │ CPU_TEMP_OFFSET_INT │ R/W  │ Temperature offset integer      │ │
│  │  0x13   │ HI_TEMP_DEC       │ R/W    │ High temp threshold decimal     │ │
│  │  0x14   │ LO_TEMP_DEC       │ R/W    │ Low temp threshold decimal      │ │
│  │  0x19   │ TIMEOUT_CONFIG    │ R/W    │ Alert timeout configuration     │ │
│  │  0xFE   │ VENDOR_ID         │ R      │ Vendor ID (0x00 = AMD)          │ │
│  │  0xFF   │ DEVICE_ID         │ R      │ Device ID                       │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
│  Temperature Reading:                                                       │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  Temperature = CPU_TEMP_INT + (CPU_TEMP_DEC × 0.125)                   │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  │  CPU_TEMP_DEC bits[7:5] represent 0.125°C increments:                  │ │
│  │    000 = 0.000°C                                                       │ │
│  │    001 = 0.125°C                                                       │ │
│  │    010 = 0.250°C                                                       │ │
│  │    011 = 0.375°C                                                       │ │
│  │    100 = 0.500°C                                                       │ │
│  │    101 = 0.625°C                                                       │ │
│  │    110 = 0.750°C                                                       │ │
│  │    111 = 0.875°C                                                       │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  │  Example: INT=55, DEC=0x40 (010 in bits[7:5])                          │ │
│  │           Temperature = 55 + 0.250 = 55.25°C                           │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
│  Threshold Alert Mechanism:                                                 │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  │  Temperature                                                           │ │
│  │       ^                                                                │ │
│  │       │    ┌─── High Threshold (HI_TEMP_INT + HI_TEMP_DEC)             │ │
│  │       │    │    ALERT_H bit set when temp >= threshold                 │ │
│  │  100°C├────┼───────────────────────────────────────────                │ │
│  │       │    │                                                           │ │
│  │       │    │   ~~~~ Actual Temperature ~~~~                            │ │
│  │   75°C├────┤                                                           │ │
│  │       │    │                                                           │ │
│  │       │    └─── Low Threshold (LO_TEMP_INT + LO_TEMP_DEC)              │ │
│  │       │         ALERT_L bit set when temp <= threshold                 │ │
│  │   50°C├─────────────────────────────────────────────────               │ │
│  │       │                                                                │ │
│  │       └──────────────────────────────────────────────> Time            │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  │  STATUS Register (0x01) flags:                                         │ │
│  │    Bit 0: ALERT_L - Temperature at or below low threshold              │ │
│  │    Bit 1: ALERT_H - Temperature at or above high threshold             │ │
│  │    Bit 7: Busy - Temperature conversion in progress                    │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### AMD MCA (Machine Check Architecture) Error Handling

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    AMD MCA Error Collection via APML                        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│  MCA Bank Layout (AMD Zen Architecture):                                    │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  Bank │ Description                    │ Error Types                   │ │
│  │  ─────┼────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────── │ │
│  │  0    │ Load-Store Unit                │ Cache/TLB errors              │ │
│  │  1    │ Instruction Fetch Unit         │ IC/IT errors                  │ │
│  │  2    │ L2 Cache Unit                  │ L2 tag/data errors            │ │
│  │  3    │ Decode Unit                    │ Microcode/instruction errors  │ │
│  │  4    │ Reserved                       │                               │ │
│  │  5    │ Execution Unit                 │ FP/INT execution errors       │ │
│  │  6    │ Floating Point Unit            │ FP register file errors       │ │
│  │  7-15 │ Core-specific banks            │ Varies by generation          │ │
│  │  16+  │ Uncore banks (UMC, DF, etc.)  │ Memory, fabric errors         │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
│  Reading MCA via APML Mailbox:                                              │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  Command: ReadMcaData (0x10)                                           │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  │  Input:                                                                │ │
│  │    InBndMsg[0]: Core/Thread ID                                         │ │
│  │    InBndMsg[1]: MCA Bank number                                        │ │
│  │    InBndMsg[2]: Register offset (0=STATUS, 1=ADDR, 2=MISC, etc.)       │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  │  Output:                                                               │ │
│  │    OutBndMsg[0-7]: 64-bit register value                               │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  │  Example reading MC0_STATUS:                                           │ │
│  │    esmi_oob_tool -s 0 --readmsr --core 0 --bank 0 --offset 0           │ │
│  │                                                                        │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
│  MCA_STATUS Register Format (AMD Zen):                                      │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  Bit   │ Field    │ Description                                        │ │
│  │  ──────┼──────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────── │ │
│  │  63    │ Val      │ Error information valid                            │ │
│  │  62    │ Overflow │ Multiple errors, information may be lost           │ │
│  │  61    │ UC       │ Uncorrected error                                  │ │
│  │  60    │ En       │ Error reporting enabled                            │ │
│  │  59    │ MiscV    │ MCA_MISC register valid                            │ │
│  │  58    │ AddrV    │ MCA_ADDR register valid                            │ │
│  │  57    │ PCC      │ Processor context corrupt                          │ │
│  │  56    │ TCC      │ Task context corrupt                               │ │
│  │  55    │ Poison   │ Poisoned data consumed                             │ │
│  │  54    │ Deferred │ Deferred error (reported later)                    │ │
│  │  47:32 │ ExtErrCode │ Extended error code                              │ │
│  │  31:16 │ ModelErrCode │ Model-specific error code                      │ │
│  │  15:0  │ ErrCode  │ Error code type                                    │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
│  Error Types (ErrCode bits 15:0):                                           │ │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  Pattern     │ Type              │ Description                         │ │
│  │  ────────────┼───────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────── │ │
│  │  0000 0000   │ No error          │                                     │ │
│  │  0000 0001   │ Unclassified      │ Internal parity/protocol error      │ │
│  │  0000 0101   │ Internal parity   │ Core internal error                 │ │
│  │  000x xxxx   │ TLB errors        │ TLB parity/multimatch               │ │
│  │  001x xxxx   │ Memory errors     │ Cache hierarchy errors              │ │
│  │  010x xxxx   │ Bus/Interconnect  │ Data fabric/IF errors               │ │
│  │  1xxx xxxx   │ Memory controller │ DRAM/UMC errors                     │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### Source Code References

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Component | Repository | Key Files |
| --- | --- | --- |
| APML Kernel Modules | [amd/apml_modules](https://github.com/amd/apml_modules) | `sbrmi/apml_sbrmi.c`, `sbtsi/apml_sbtsi.c` |
| E-SMI OOB Library | [amd/esmi_oob_library](https://github.com/amd/esmi_oob_library) | `src/esmi_oob.c`, `src/apml.c` |
| E-SMI In-Band Library | [amd/esmi_ib_library](https://github.com/amd/esmi_ib_library) | `src/e_smi.c` |
| AMDESE OpenBMC | [AMDESE/OpenBMC](https://github.com/AMDESE/OpenBMC) | `meta-amd/` |
| hwmon sbtsi driver | [linux/drivers/hwmon](https://github.com/torvalds/linux) | `drivers/hwmon/sbtsi_temp.c` |

</div>

**Platform**: AMD EPYC 7002 (Rome), 7003 (Milan), 9004 (Genoa), and newer platforms. APML requires Family 17h (Zen) or later processors.

## Overview

    

OpenBMC provides comprehensive logging capabilities through **phosphor-logging** and related services. Logs are accessible via D-Bus, IPMI SEL, and Redfish APIs.

```mermaid
---
title: Logging Architecture
---
flowchart TB
    subgraph interfaces["Access Interfaces"]
        direction LR
        redfish["Redfish  
EventLog"]
        ipmi["IPMI  
SEL"]
        dbus["D-Bus  
busctl"]
        journal["journald  
logs"]
    end

    subgraph logging["phosphor-logging"]
        direction LR
        logmgr["Log Manager  
(D-Bus API)"]
        create["Error Creation  
& Storage"]
        resolve["Resolving  
& Cleanup"]
    end

    storage["/var/lib/phosphor-logging/errors/"]

    subgraph sources["Event Sources"]
        direction LR
        sensors["Sensors  
(thresh)"]
        state["State Mgr  
(power)"]
        firmware["Firmware  
(update)"]
        services["Services  
(errors)"]
    end

    interfaces --> logging
    logging --> storage
    sources --> logging
```

## Setup & Configuration

    

### Build-Time Configuration (Yocto)

    

```bitbake
# In your machine .conf or local.conf

# Include logging packages
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " \
    phosphor-logging \
    phosphor-sel-logger \
    phosphor-log-manager \
"

# Configure logging options
EXTRA_OEMESON:pn-phosphor-logging = " \
    -Dpersistence=enabled \
    -Dremote-host-config=enabled \
"
```

### Meson Build Options

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `persistence` | enabled | Persist logs across reboots |
| `remote-host-config` | disabled | Remote syslog support |
| `openpower-pel` | disabled | IBM PEL format logs |

</div>

### Runtime Configuration

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check logging service</span>
systemctl status phosphor-log-manager

<span class="c"># View service logs</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> phosphor-log-manager <span class="nt">-f</span>

<span class="c"># Log storage location</span>
<span class="nb">ls</span> /var/lib/phosphor-logging/errors/
```

</div></div>
---

## Creating Event Logs

    

### Via D-Bus API

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Create an informational log</span>
busctl call xyz.openbmc_project.Logging <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/logging <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Logging.Create <span class="se">\</span>
    Create ssas <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.Common.Error.InternalFailure"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.Logging.Entry.Level.Informational"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    2 <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"COMPONENT=MyService"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="s2">"REASON=Test log entry"</span>
```

</div></div>

### Log Severity Levels

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Level | Description | Use Case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Emergency | System unusable | Critical failures |
| Alert | Immediate action needed | Security events |
| Critical | Critical conditions | Hardware failures |
| Error | Error conditions | Service errors |
| Warning | Warning conditions | Threshold warnings |
| Notice | Normal but significant | State changes |
| Informational | Informational | Status updates |
| Debug | Debug messages | Development |

</div>

### From Application Code

    

> **Source Reference**: phosphor-logging
>   
>     Logging API: phosphor-logging/log.hpp
>     Error definitions: phosphor-logging/elog.hpp

<div class="language-cpp highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="cp">#include</span> <span class="cpf">
#include 
#include 

using namespace phosphor::logging;

// Log an error
loglevel::ERR>("Sensor read failed",
    entry("SENSOR=%s", "CPU_Temp"),
    entry("ERROR=%d", errno));

// Log an informational message
loglevel::INFO>("Service started",
    entry("VERSION=%s", "1.0.0"));
```

### Using elog for Structured Errors

    

```
#include 

using namespace sdbusplus::xyz::openbmc_project::Common::Error;

// Report a structured error
try {
    // Some operation
    if (error_condition) {
        reportInternalFailure>();
    }
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
    loglevel::ERR>("Exception caught", entry("WHAT=%s", e.what()));
}
```

## Viewing Event Logs

    

### Via D-Bus

    

```
# List all log entries
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.Logging

# Get log entry details
busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.Logging \
    /xyz/openbmc_project/logging/entry/1

# Get log message
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.Logging \
    /xyz/openbmc_project/logging/entry/1 \
    xyz.openbmc_project.Logging.Entry \
    Message
```

### Via Redfish

    

```
# Get event log entries
curl -k -u root:0penBmc \
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/EventLog/Entries

# Get specific entry
curl -k -u root:0penBmc \
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/EventLog/Entries/1
```

### Via IPMI SEL

    

```
# Get SEL entries
ipmitool -I lanplus -H bmc-ip -U root -P 0penBmc sel list

# Get SEL info
ipmitool -I lanplus -H bmc-ip -U root -P 0penBmc sel info
```

## Managing Logs

    

### Delete Single Log

    

```
# Via D-Bus
busctl call xyz.openbmc_project.Logging \
    /xyz/openbmc_project/logging/entry/1 \
    xyz.openbmc_project.Object.Delete \
    Delete

# Via Redfish
curl -k -u root:0penBmc -X DELETE \
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/EventLog/Entries/1
```

### Clear All Logs

    

```
# Via Redfish
curl -k -u root:0penBmc -X POST \
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/EventLog/Actions/LogService.ClearLog

# Via IPMI
ipmitool -I lanplus -H bmc-ip -U root -P 0penBmc sel clear
```

### Log Rotation

    

```
# Log capacity configuration
# Default: 200 entries maximum

# Configure via D-Bus property
busctl set-property xyz.openbmc_project.Logging \
    /xyz/openbmc_project/logging \
    xyz.openbmc_project.Logging.Settings \
    QuiesceOnHwError b false
```

## SEL Logger

    

The SEL Logger creates IPMI-compatible SEL entries from sensor events.

### Configuration

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check SEL logger service</span>
systemctl status phosphor-sel-logger

<span class="c"># SEL logger monitors threshold events</span>
<span class="c"># and creates SEL entries automatically</span>
```

</div></div>

### SEL Record Types

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Type | Description |
| --- | --- |
| System Event | Standard SEL entry |
| OEM Timestamped | Vendor-specific with timestamp |
| OEM Non-timestamped | Vendor-specific without timestamp |

</div>

### IPMI SEL Commands

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get SEL information</span>
ipmitool sel info

<span class="c"># Get SEL entries</span>
ipmitool sel list

<span class="c"># Get extended info</span>
ipmitool sel elist

<span class="c"># Clear SEL</span>
ipmitool sel clear

<span class="c"># Get specific record</span>
ipmitool sel get 1
```

</div></div>
---

## SDR (Sensor Data Record)

    

SDR describes sensors and their properties for IPMI.

### SDR Types

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Type | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Full Sensor | Complete sensor definition |
| Compact Sensor | Abbreviated sensor record |
| Event-Only | Event generation info |
| FRU Device | FRU information |
| MC Device | Management controller |

</div>

### View SDR

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># List all SDR records</span>
ipmitool sdr list

<span class="c"># Get detailed SDR info</span>
ipmitool sdr info

<span class="c"># Get specific sensor type</span>
ipmitool sdr <span class="nb">type </span>Temperature
```

</div></div>

### Dynamic SDR Generation

    

OpenBMC generates SDR dynamically from D-Bus sensor objects:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># SDR is generated from:</span>
<span class="c"># - xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.* interfaces</span>
<span class="c"># - threshold definitions</span>
<span class="c"># - sensor metadata</span>
```

</div></div>
---

## POST Codes

    

POST (Power-On Self-Test) codes capture boot progress.

### Setup

    

```bitbake
# Include POST code manager
IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " phosphor-post-code-manager"
```

### View POST Codes

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Via D-Bus</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.State.Boot.Raw

<span class="c"># Get current POST code</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.State.Boot.Raw <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/state/boot/raw0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.State.Boot.Raw <span class="se">\</span>
    Value

<span class="c"># Via Redfish</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/PostCodes/Entries
```

</div></div>

### POST Code History

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Get POST code history</span>
busctl call xyz.openbmc_project.State.Boot.Raw <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/state/boot/raw0 <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.State.Boot.Raw <span class="se">\</span>
    GetPostCodes q 0  <span class="c"># Boot cycle 0 (current)</span>
```

</div></div>
---

## Debug Collector (dreport)

    

Collect diagnostic information for debugging.

### Create Debug Report

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Generate report</span>
dreport <span class="nt">-d</span> /tmp/debug <span class="nt">-n</span> myreport <span class="nt">-t</span> user

<span class="c"># Report types:</span>
<span class="c"># user     - User-initiated dump</span>
<span class="c"># core     - Core dump</span>
<span class="c"># elog     - Error log dump</span>
<span class="c"># pel      - PEL dump (OpenPOWER)</span>
```

</div></div>

### Via Redfish

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Create dump</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> POST <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{"DiagnosticDataType": "Manager"}'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/LogServices/Dump/Actions/LogService.CollectDiagnosticData

<span class="c"># List dumps</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/LogServices/Dump/Entries

<span class="c"># Download dump</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-o</span> dump.tar.xz <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/LogServices/Dump/Entries/1/attachment
```

</div></div>

### Dump Contents

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Extract and examine</span>
<span class="nb">tar</span> <span class="nt">-xf</span> dump.tar.xz

<span class="c"># Contents typically include:</span>
<span class="c"># - Journal logs</span>
<span class="c"># - D-Bus state</span>
<span class="c"># - System configuration</span>
<span class="c"># - Core files (if applicable)</span>
```

</div></div>
---

## Remote Logging

    

### Syslog Configuration

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Configure remote syslog</span>
<span class="c"># /etc/rsyslog.d/remote.conf</span>
<span class="k">*</span>.<span class="k">*</span> @@remote-server:514
```

</div></div>

### Redfish Event Forwarding

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Create event subscription</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> POST <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-H</span> <span class="s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    <span class="nt">-d</span> <span class="s1">'{
        "Destination": "https://log-server:8080/events",
        "Protocol": "Redfish",
        "EventTypes": ["Alert", "StatusChange"]
    }'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/EventService/Subscriptions
```

</div></div>
---

## Troubleshooting

    

### No Logs Appearing

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check logging service</span>
systemctl status phosphor-log-manager

<span class="c"># Check permissions</span>
<span class="nb">ls</span> <span class="nt">-la</span> /var/lib/phosphor-logging/

<span class="c"># Verify D-Bus service</span>
busctl status xyz.openbmc_project.Logging
```

</div></div>

### SEL Not Updating

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check SEL logger service</span>
systemctl status phosphor-sel-logger

<span class="c"># Verify threshold events are configured</span>
busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.Sensors.<span class="k">*</span> <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/<span class="k">*</span>/<span class="k">*</span>
```

</div></div>

### Logs Fill Up

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check log count</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.Logging | <span class="nb">wc</span> <span class="nt">-l</span>

<span class="c"># Clear old logs</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="nt">-X</span> POST <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/EventLog/Actions/LogService.ClearLog
```

</div></div>

## Custom Event Log Example

    

### Where to Put Error Definitions

    

Custom error definitions live alongside your service code, following the
phosphor-dbus-interfaces YAML format:

<div class="table-wrapper">
| File | Path Convention | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Error YAML | `/xyz/openbmc_project/MyService/MyError.errors.yaml` | Error type definitions |
| Metadata YAML | `/xyz/openbmc_project/MyService/MyError.metadata.yaml` | Additional data fields |
| Generated header | `/xyz/openbmc_project/MyService/error.hpp` | Auto-generated C++ header |

</div>

### Step 1: Define Error Type

    

<div class="language-yaml highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c1"># xyz/openbmc_project/MyService/MyError.errors.yaml</span>
<span class="pi">-</span> <span class="na">name</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">ConfigurationError</span>
  <span class="na">description</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">Configuration file is invalid</span>
  <span class="na">metadata</span><span class="pi">:</span>
    <span class="pi">-</span> <span class="na">name</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">FILE</span>
      <span class="na">type</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">string</span>
    <span class="pi">-</span> <span class="na">name</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">LINE</span>
      <span class="na">type</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">int32</span>
```

</div></div>

### Step 2: Add to Meson Build

    

<div class="language-python highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c1"># In meson.build of your service
</span><span class="n">phosphor_logging_dep</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">dependency</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sh">'</span><span class="s">phosphor-logging</span><span class="sh">'</span><span class="p">)</span>

<span class="c1"># Generate error headers from YAML
</span><span class="n">error_yaml</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">files</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sh">'</span><span class="s">xyz/openbmc_project/MyService/MyError.errors.yaml</span><span class="sh">'</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="n">error_hpp</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">phosphor_logging_gen</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">process</span><span class="p">(</span>
    <span class="n">error_yaml</span><span class="p">,</span>
    <span class="n">preserve_path_from</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">meson</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">current_source_dir</span><span class="p">())</span>
```

</div></div>

### Step 3: Use in Code

    

<div class="language-cpp highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="cp">#include</span> <span class="cpf"><xyz/openbmc_project/MyService/error.hpp></span><span class="cp">
</span>
<span class="k">using</span> <span class="n">MyConfigError</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">sdbusplus</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">xyz</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">openbmc_project</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">MyService</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">Error</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">ConfigurationError</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="c1">// Report the error</span>
<span class="n">report</span><span class="o"><</span><span class="n">MyConfigError</span><span class="o">></span><span class="p">(</span>
    <span class="n">xyz</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">openbmc_project</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">MyService</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">ConfigurationError</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="kt">FILE</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"config.json"</span><span class="p">),</span>
    <span class="n">xyz</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">openbmc_project</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">MyService</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">ConfigurationError</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">LINE</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">42</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="p">);</span>
```

</div></div>

### Remote Syslog Deployment via Yocto

    

To bake a default remote syslog destination into the image:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># meta-myplatform/recipes-phosphor/logging/</span>
<span class="c"># └── files/</span>
<span class="c"># │   └── remote.conf</span>
<span class="c"># └── phosphor-logging_%.bbappend</span>

<span class="nb">cat</span> <span class="o">></span> phosphor-logging_%.bbappend <span class="o"><<</span> <span class="sh">'</span><span class="no">EOF</span><span class="sh">'
FILESEXTRAPATHS:prepend := "</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">THISDIR</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/files:"
SRC_URI += "file://remote.conf"

do_install:append() {
    install -d </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">D</span><span class="k">}${</span><span class="nv">sysconfdir</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/rsyslog.d
    install -m 0644 </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">WORKDIR</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/remote.conf </span><span class="se">\</span><span class="sh">
        </span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">D</span><span class="k">}${</span><span class="nv">sysconfdir</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/rsyslog.d/
}
</span><span class="no">EOF
</span>
```

</div></div>

Example `remote.conf`:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
# Forward all logs to central server
*.* @@log-server.example.com:514
```

</div></div>

### Log Storage Configuration

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Setting | Default | Where to Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Max error entries | 200 | `ERROR_CAP` in phosphor-logging meson options |
| Max info entries | 10 | `ERROR_INFO_CAP` in meson options |
| Persistence path | `/var/lib/phosphor-logging/errors/` | Compiled into binary |
| Remote syslog | Disabled | `/etc/rsyslog.d/*.conf` or Redfish EventService |

</div>

Customize log capacity via Yocto:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># meta-myplatform/recipes-phosphor/logging/phosphor-logging_%.bbappend</span>
EXTRA_OEMESON:append <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s2">" </span><span class="se">\</span><span class="s2">
    -Derror_cap=500 </span><span class="se">\</span><span class="s2">
    -Derror_info_cap=50 </span><span class="se">\</span><span class="s2">
"</span>
```

</div></div>
---

```mermaid
xyz.openbmc_project.Logging"]

├── entry/1  
├── entry/2  
└── entry/N"]
        storage["Storage: /var/lib/phosphor-logging/errors/"]
    end

    redfish["Redfish  
LogService"]
    ipmisel["IPMI SEL  
Logger"]

(syslog)"]
```

### Error Entry Structure

    

**D-Bus Object:** `/xyz/openbmc_project/logging/entry/N`

**Interfaces and Properties:**

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Interface | Property | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `xyz.openbmc_project.Logging.Entry` | `Id` (uint32) | Entry identifier |
|  | `Severity` | Informational/Warning/Critical |
|  | `Message` (string) | Error message (MessageId) |
|  | `Resolved` (bool) | Has error been acknowledged |
|  | `Timestamp` (uint64) | Unix timestamp in milliseconds |
|  | `AdditionalData` | Array of “KEY=VALUE” strings |
| `xyz.openbmc_project.Association.Definitions` | `Associations` | Links to related objects |
| `xyz.openbmc_project.Object.Delete` | `Delete()` | Method to delete entry |

</div>

**AdditionalData Example:**

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
  </span><span class="s2">"SENSOR_PATH=/xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/temp/CPU0"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
  </span><span class="s2">"THRESHOLD_VALUE=95.0"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
  </span><span class="s2">"READING=98.5"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
  </span><span class="s2">"_PID=1234"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
  </span><span class="s2">"CALLOUT_INVENTORY_PATH=/xyz/.../cpu0"</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

> **ASCII-art version (for comparison)**

  <div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Error Log Entry                                      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   D-Bus Object: /xyz/openbmc_project/logging/entry/N                    │
│                                                                         │
│   Interfaces and Properties:                                            │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ xyz.openbmc_project.Logging.Entry                               │   │
│   │ ├── Id (uint32)        - Entry identifier                       │   │
│   │ ├── Severity           - Informational/Warning/Critical         │   │
│   │ ├── Message (string)   - Error message (MessageId)              │   │
│   │ ├── Resolved (bool)    - Has error been acknowledged            │   │
│   │ ├── Timestamp (uint64) - Unix timestamp in milliseconds         │   │
│   │ └── AdditionalData     - Array of "KEY=VALUE" strings           │   │
│   │                                                                 │   │
│   │ xyz.openbmc_project.Association.Definitions                     │   │
```

### Error Reporting API

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Error Reporting Patterns                             │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   1. Simple Error (no metadata):                                        │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ #include 
│   │
│   │ #include                  │   │
│   │                                                                 │   │
│   │ using InternalFailure =                                         │   │
│   │     sdbusplus::xyz::openbmc_project::Common::Error::            │   │
│   │     InternalFailure;                                            │   │
│   │                                                                 │   │
│   │ phosphor::logging::report();                   │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
│   2. Error with Metadata:                                               │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ using namespace phosphor::logging;                              │   │
│   │ using TempError = xyz::openbmc_project::Sensor::Error::         │   │
│   │                   OverTemperature;                              │   │
│   │ using Metadata = xyz::openbmc_project::Sensor::OverTemperature; │   │
│   │                                                                 │   │
│   │ report(                                              │   │
│   │     Metadata::SENSOR_PATH(sensorPath.c_str()),                  │   │
│   │     Metadata::READING(98.5),                                    │   │
│   │     Metadata::THRESHOLD(95.0)                                   │   │
│   │ );                                                              │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
│   3. D-Bus Method Call (from script):                                   │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ busctl call xyz.openbmc_project.Logging \                       │   │
│   │     /xyz/openbmc_project/logging \                              │   │
│   │     xyz.openbmc_project.Logging.Create Create \                 │   │
│   │     ssa{ss} \                                                   │   │
│   │     "xyz.openbmc_project.Common.Error.InternalFailure" \        │   │
│   │     "xyz.openbmc_project.Logging.Entry.Level.Error" \           │   │
│   │     2 "KEY1" "value1" "KEY2" "value2"                           │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### IPMI SEL Integration

    

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    SEL (System Event Log) Integration                   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   phosphor-sel-logger monitors D-Bus for loggable events:               │
│                                                                         │
│   Event Sources:                                                        │
│   ├── Threshold crossing (Sensor.Value PropertiesChanged)               │
│   ├── Discrete sensor state change                                      │
│   ├── phosphor-logging new entry (InterfacesAdded)                      │
│   └── Watchdog timeout                                                  │
│                                                                         │
│   SEL Record Format (IPMI 2.0, Type 02h):                               │
│   ┌────────┬────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ Offset │ Size   │ Description                                   │   │
│   ├────────┼────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────┤   │
│   │ 0-1    │ 2      │ Record ID                                     │   │
│   │ 2      │ 1      │ Record Type (0x02 = System Event)             │   │
│   │ 3-6    │ 4      │ Timestamp                                     │   │
│   │ 7-8    │ 2      │ Generator ID                                  │   │
│   │ 9      │ 1      │ EvM Rev                                       │   │
│   │ 10     │ 1      │ Sensor Type                                   │   │
│   │ 11     │ 1      │ Sensor Number                                 │   │
│   │ 12     │ 1      │ Event Type/Dir                                │   │
│   │ 13-15  │ 3      │ Event Data 1-3                                │   │
│   └────────┴────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
│   Sensor Type to SEL Mapping:                                           │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ D-Bus Sensor Type           │ IPMI Sensor Type                  │   │
│   ├─────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────┤   │
│   │ sensors/temperature/*       │ 0x01 (Temperature)                │   │
│   │ sensors/voltage/*           │ 0x02 (Voltage)                    │   │
│   │ sensors/current/*           │ 0x03 (Current)                    │   │
│   │ sensors/fan_tach/*          │ 0x04 (Fan)                        │   │
│   │ sensors/power/*             │ 0x08 (Power Supply)               │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Log Rotation and Persistence

    

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Log Management                                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│   Storage Location:                                                     │
│   /var/lib/phosphor-logging/errors/                                     │
│   ├── 1        # Serialized error entry                                 │
│   ├── 2                                                                 │
│   └── ...                                                               │
│                                                                         │
│   Configuration:                                                        │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ ERROR_CAP = 200           # Maximum number of error entries     │   │
│   │ ERROR_INFO_CAP = 10       # Max informational entries           │   │
│   │ ERROR_PERSIST_PATH = /var/lib/phosphor-logging/errors/          │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
│   Rotation Behavior:                                                    │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │ When ERROR_CAP reached:                                         │   │
│   │ 1. Find oldest Informational entry → delete                     │   │
│   │ 2. If no Informational, find oldest Warning → delete            │   │
│   │ 3. If no Warning, find oldest Error → delete                    │   │
│   │ 4. Critical entries protected from rotation                     │   │
│   │ 5. Resolved entries deleted before unresolved                   │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                         │
│   Persistence across BMC reboot:                                        │
│   ├── Entries serialized to filesystem using cereal                     │
│   ├── Entry IDs are persistent                                          │
│   └── On startup, entries loaded from /var/lib/phosphor-logging/        │
│                                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Overview

    

**Sensor Data Records (SDR)** describe sensors and their properties for IPMI clients. OpenBMC dynamically generates SDR from D-Bus sensor objects.

```mermaid
---
title: SDR Architecture
---
flowchart TB
    subgraph client["IPMI Client"]
        ipmitool["ipmitool sdr list"]
    end

    subgraph ipmihost["phosphor-ipmi-host"]
        sdrgen["SDR Generation  
(Dynamic from D-Bus sensor objects)"]
    end

    subgraph dbus["D-Bus Sensors"]
        sensorval["xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value"]
        threshold["xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Threshold.*"]
    end

    client --> ipmihost
    ipmihost --> dbus
```

> **ASCII-art version (for comparison)**

  <div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      SDR Architecture                           │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                 │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐│
│  │                    IPMI Client                              ││
│  │               (ipmitool sdr list)                           ││
│  └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘│
│                             │                                   │
│  ┌──────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┐│
│  │                   phosphor-ipmi-host                        ││
│  │                                                             ││
│  │   ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    ││
│  │   │              SDR Generation                        │    ││
│  │   │     (Dynamic from D-Bus sensor objects)            │    ││
│  │   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    ││
│  └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘│
│                             │                                   │
│  ┌──────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┐│
│  │                    D-Bus Sensors                            ││
│  │   xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value                          ││
│  │   xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Threshold.*                    ││
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘│
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div>  </div>

## SDR Record Types

    

### Type 01h - Full Sensor Record

    

Complete sensor definition with thresholds and scaling.

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Sensor Number | Unique sensor ID |
| Sensor Type | Temperature, Voltage, Fan, etc. |
| Unit Type | Celsius, Volts, RPM, etc. |
| M, B, Exp | Linear conversion factors |
| Thresholds | Upper/Lower critical/non-critical |

</div>

### Type 02h - Compact Sensor Record

    

Abbreviated sensor record for simple sensors.

### Type 11h - FRU Device Locator

    

Points to FRU data storage.

### Type 12h - Management Controller Locator

    

Describes management controllers.

---

## Viewing SDR

    

### ipmitool Commands

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># List all SDR records</span>
ipmitool sdr list

<span class="c"># Get full SDR output</span>
ipmitool sdr list full

<span class="c"># Get SDR by type</span>
ipmitool sdr <span class="nb">type </span>Temperature
ipmitool sdr <span class="nb">type </span>Voltage
ipmitool sdr <span class="nb">type </span>Fan

<span class="c"># Get SDR info</span>
ipmitool sdr info

<span class="c"># Get SDR repository info</span>
ipmitool sdr elist
```

</div></div>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">

```
CPU_Temp         | 45 degrees C      | ok
Board_Temp       | 32 degrees C      | ok
Fan0             | 5000 RPM          | ok
P12V             | 12.10 Volts       | ok
PSU1_Status      | 0x00              | ok
```

## SDR Generation

    

### Dynamic Generation

    

OpenBMC generates SDR dynamically from D-Bus:

<div class="language-cpp highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c1">// phosphor-ipmi-host generates SDR from:</span>
<span class="c1">// 1. xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value - sensor readings</span>
<span class="c1">// 2. xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Threshold.* - thresholds</span>
<span class="c1">// 3. xyz.openbmc_project.Association.Definitions - relationships</span>
```

</div></div>

### Sensor to SDR Mapping

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| D-Bus Property | SDR Field |
| --- | --- |
| Value | Current reading |
| Unit | Sensor unit type |
| Scale | M, B, Exp factors |
| MaxValue | Sensor max |
| MinValue | Sensor min |
| CriticalHigh | Upper critical |
| WarningHigh | Upper non-critical |
| CriticalLow | Lower critical |
| WarningLow | Lower non-critical |

</div>
---

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Type | Hex | Description |

## Reading Values

    

### Raw to Display Conversion

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
Display Value = (M × raw + B × 10^Bexp) × 10^Rexp

Where:
  M = Multiplier
  B = Additive offset
  Bexp = B exponent
  Rexp = Result exponent
```

</div></div>

### Example

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
Temperature sensor:
  raw value = 0x2D (45)
  M = 1, B = 0, Bexp = 0, Rexp = 0
  Display = (1 × 45 + 0) × 1 = 45°C
```

</div></div>
---

## Troubleshooting

    

### SDR Not Showing

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check sensor exists in D-Bus</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor

<span class="c"># Check IPMI host daemon</span>
systemctl status phosphor-ipmi-host
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> phosphor-ipmi-host

<span class="c"># Check sensor has required interfaces</span>
busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.HwmonTempSensor <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/temperature/CPU_Temp
```

</div></div>

### Wrong Readings

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Compare D-Bus value with IPMI</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.HwmonTempSensor <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/temperature/CPU_Temp <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value Value

<span class="c"># vs</span>
ipmitool sensor get CPU_Temp

<span class="c"># Check M, B, Exp values match sensor scaling</span>
```

</div></div>

### Missing Thresholds

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Verify thresholds in D-Bus</span>
busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.HwmonTempSensor <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/temperature/CPU_Temp | <span class="nb">grep </span>Threshold

<span class="c"># Check Entity Manager configuration</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /usr/share/entity-manager/configurations/<span class="k">*</span>.json | jq <span class="s1">'.Exposes[] | select(.Name=="CPU_Temp")'</span>
```

</div></div>

```
    xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Threshold.Critical CriticalHigh
```
