### eSPI Channel Types

    

eSPI provides four independent channels, each serving different communication needs:

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Channel | Purpose | Use Cases |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Peripheral** | Memory-mapped I/O and I/O cycles | LPC-compatible peripherals, IPMI KCS, POST codes |
| **Virtual Wire** | GPIO-like signals | Power states (SLP_S3/S4/S5), PLTRST#, interrupts |
| **OOB Message** | SMBus-like messaging | Platform alerts, tunneled SMBus, MCTP |
| **Flash Access** | SPI flash sharing | Host BIOS on BMC-attached flash (eDAF) |

</div>

### Channel Selection Guide

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
What do you need to communicate?
       │
       ├── Register/memory access (I/O ports, MMIO)?
       │        └── Peripheral Channel
       │
       ├── Simple signals (power state, reset, interrupts)?
       │        └── Virtual Wire Channel
       │
       ├── Messages/packets (alerts, SMBus, MCTP)?
       │        └── OOB Message Channel
       │
       └── Flash access (host BIOS, shared flash)?
                └── Flash Access Channel
```

</div></div>
---

## Virtual Wire Channel

    

Virtual wires provide GPIO-like signaling between host and BMC, replacing dedicated LPC signals with software-defined wires.

### Virtual Wire Signal Table

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Index | Signal | Direction | Active | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | SLP_S3# | Host→BMC | Low | S3 sleep state indicator |
| 3 | SLP_S4# | Host→BMC | Low | S4 sleep state indicator |
| 4 | SLP_S5# | Host→BMC | Low | S5 sleep state indicator |
| 5 | SLP_A# | Host→BMC | Low | SLP_A signal |
| 6 | SLP_LAN# | Host→BMC | Low | LAN sleep signal |
| 7 | SLP_WLAN# | Host→BMC | Low | WLAN sleep signal |
| 41 | PLTRST# | Host→BMC | Low | Platform reset |
| 42 | SUS_STAT# | Host→BMC | Low | Suspend status |
| 43 | SUS_PWRDN_ACK | BMC→Host | High | Suspend power down ack |
| 44 | SUS_WARN# | Host→BMC | Low | Suspend warning |
| 45 | OOB_RST_WARN | Host→BMC | High | OOB reset warning |
| 46 | OOB_RST_ACK | BMC→Host | High | OOB reset acknowledge |
| 47 | HOST_RST_WARN | Host→BMC | High | Host reset warning |
| 48 | HOST_RST_ACK | BMC→Host | High | Host reset acknowledge |
| 64-127 | GPIO | Bi-dir | Config | Platform-specific GPIOs |

</div>

### Common Virtual Wires Explained

    

**Power State Signals (SLP_S3#, SLP_S4#, SLP_S5#):**

These signals indicate ACPI sleep states:

* **SLP_S3#**: Low when system enters S3 (suspend to RAM)
* **SLP_S4#**: Low when system enters S4 (hibernate)
* **SLP_S5#**: Low when system enters S5 (soft off)

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
Power State Detection:
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ SLP_S3# │ SLP_S4# │ SLP_S5# │ System State       │
├─────────┼─────────┼─────────┼────────────────────┤
│  High   │  High   │  High   │ S0 (Running)       │
│  Low    │  High   │  High   │ S3 (Suspend RAM)   │
│  High   │  Low    │  High   │ S4 (Hibernate)     │
│  High   │  High   │  Low    │ S5 (Soft Off)      │
│  Low    │  Low    │  Low    │ Mechanical Off     │
└─────────┴─────────┴─────────┴────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

**Platform Reset (PLTRST#):**

PLTRST# indicates platform reset state:

* Low during host reset sequence
* High when host completes reset
* BMC uses this to detect host boot status

### Virtual Wire to GPIO Mapping

    

OpenBMC maps virtual wires to GPIO interfaces for integration with existing services:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Virtual wires appear as GPIO lines</span>
gpioinfo | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> espi
<span class="c"># gpiochip1 - 8 lines:</span>
<span class="c">#     line 0: "espi-vw-slp-s3" input</span>
<span class="c">#     line 1: "espi-vw-slp-s4" input</span>
<span class="c">#     line 2: "espi-vw-slp-s5" input</span>
<span class="c">#     line 3: "espi-vw-pltrst" input</span>

<span class="c"># Read virtual wire state</span>
gpioget gpiochip1 0  <span class="c"># Read SLP_S3#</span>

<span class="c"># Monitor virtual wire changes</span>
gpiomon gpiochip1 0 1 2 3
```

</div></div>

### Device Tree Configuration for Virtual Wires

    

```dts
// ASPEED AST2600 eSPI Virtual Wire configuration

&espi {
    status = "okay";

    espi_vw: espi-vw {
        compatible = "aspeed,ast2600-espi-vw";
        status = "okay";

        /* Map system virtual wires to GPIO lines */
        gpio-controller;
        #gpio-cells = <2>;
        gpio-line-names =
            "espi-vw-slp-s3",    /* VW index 2 */
            "espi-vw-slp-s4",    /* VW index 3 */
            "espi-vw-slp-s5",    /* VW index 4 */
            "espi-vw-pltrst",    /* VW index 41 */
            "espi-vw-sus-stat",  /* VW index 42 */
            "espi-vw-sus-warn",  /* VW index 44 */
            "espi-vw-oob-rst-warn", /* VW index 45 */
            "espi-vw-host-rst-warn"; /* VW index 47 */
    };
};
```

### ASPEED eSPI Virtual Wire Driver

    

**Kernel Configuration:**

```kconfig
CONFIG_ASPEED_ESPI=y
CONFIG_ASPEED_ESPI_VW=y
```

**Driver Module Parameters:**

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># View current parameters</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/module/aspeed_espi_vw/parameters/<span class="k">*</span>

<span class="c"># Virtual wire index mapping configured via device tree</span>
```

</div></div>

**Sysfs Interface:**

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Virtual wire status</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/bus/platform/devices/<span class="k">*</span>.espi-vw/status

<span class="c"># Debug information</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/kernel/debug/aspeed-espi-vw/vw_status
```

</div></div>

### Virtual Wire Troubleshooting

    

**Issue: Virtual wire signals not changing**

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># 1. Verify eSPI controller is enabled</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/bus/platform/devices/<span class="k">*</span>.espi/enabled
<span class="c"># Should show "1"</span>

<span class="c"># 2. Check eSPI negotiation completed</span>
dmesg | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> espi
<span class="c"># Look for "eSPI channel X enabled"</span>

<span class="c"># 3. Verify virtual wire channel enabled</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/bus/platform/devices/<span class="k">*</span>.espi/vw_channel_enabled

<span class="c"># 4. Read raw virtual wire registers</span>
devmem 0x1e6ee080  <span class="c"># ASPEED VW status register (example)</span>

<span class="c"># 5. Check for interrupt activity</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /proc/interrupts | <span class="nb">grep </span>espi
```

</div></div>

**Issue: Wrong polarity or stuck signals**

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check device tree gpio-active-low settings</span>
<span class="c"># Verify host chipset VW configuration</span>
<span class="c"># Check for electrical issues on eSPI bus</span>
```

</div></div>

## eSPI Console/UART

    

eSPI can provide UART functionality through the peripheral channel, replacing dedicated UART pins.

### eSPI UART Operation

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    eSPI UART Flow                           │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                             │
│   Host                                                      │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │  Legacy COM Port (I/O 0x3F8)                        │   │
│   │         │                                           │   │
│   │         ▼                                           │   │
│   │  eSPI Peripheral Channel (I/O Cycles)               │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                           │                                 │
│                    eSPI Bus                                 │
│                           │                                 │
│   BMC                     ▼                                 │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │  eSPI Peripheral Channel Decoder                    │   │
│   │         │                                           │   │
│   │         ▼                                           │   │
│   │  Virtual UART (ttyS* or ttyVUART*)                  │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### Kernel Configuration for eSPI UART

    

```kconfig
# ASPEED eSPI UART support
CONFIG_ASPEED_ESPI=y
CONFIG_ASPEED_ESPI_PERIPHERAL=y
CONFIG_SERIAL_8250=y
CONFIG_SERIAL_8250_ASPEED_VUART=y
```

### Device Tree for eSPI UART

    

```dts
// ASPEED eSPI with UART over peripheral channel

&espi {
    status = "okay";

    espi_peri: espi-peripheral {
        compatible = "aspeed,ast2600-espi-peripheral";
        status = "okay";

        /* UART over eSPI peripheral channel */
        uart-over-espi;
        uart-io-base = <0x3f8>;  /* COM1 I/O address */
    };
};

/* Virtual UART configuration */
&vuart1 {
    status = "okay";
    aspeed,sirq = <4>;  /* IRQ 4 for COM1 */
    aspeed,lpc-io-reg = <0x3f8>;
};
```

### Using eSPI UART

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># List serial devices</span>
<span class="nb">ls</span> <span class="nt">-la</span> /dev/ttyS<span class="k">*</span> /dev/ttyVUART<span class="k">*</span>

<span class="c"># Configure serial parameters</span>
<span class="nb">stty</span> <span class="nt">-F</span> /dev/ttyVUART0 115200 cs8 <span class="nt">-cstopb</span> <span class="nt">-parenb</span>

<span class="c"># Connect to host console</span>
screen /dev/ttyVUART0 115200

<span class="c"># Or use obmc-console</span>
systemctl status obmc-console@ttyVUART0
```

</div></div>

### SOL over eSPI OOB Channel

    

Serial over LAN can also use eSPI OOB channel for IPMI SOL:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Configure IPMI SOL to use eSPI-backed UART</span>
<span class="c"># In phosphor-ipmi-host configuration</span>

<span class="c"># SOL activation uses standard IPMI commands</span>
ipmitool <span class="nt">-I</span> lanplus <span class="nt">-H</span> <bmc-ip> <span class="nt">-U</span> root <span class="nt">-P</span> password sol activate
```

</div></div>
---

## OOB Message Channel

    

The OOB (Out-of-Band) Message Channel provides SMBus-like packet communication between host and BMC.

### OOB Channel Overview

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    OOB Message Format                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                             │
│  ┌─────────┬─────────┬─────────┬─────────────┬───────────┐  │
│  │  Cycle  │   Tag   │  Length │   Address   │  Data     │  │
│  │  Type   │         │         │  (optional) │           │  │
│  │ (1 byte)│(1 byte) │(2 bytes)│  (varies)   │ (varies)  │  │
│  └─────────┴─────────┴─────────┴─────────────┴───────────┘  │
│                                                             │
│  Cycle Types:                                               │
│  - 0x21: OOB SMBus Write                                    │
│  - 0x22: OOB SMBus Read                                     │
│  - 0x23-0x27: Reserved/Vendor-specific                      │
│                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### OOB Use Cases

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Use Case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Platform Alerts** | BMC sends alerts to host (thermal, power, errors) |
| **Tunneled SMBus** | SMBus transactions over eSPI (sensor access) |
| **MCTP over eSPI** | PLDM/MCTP messages over OOB channel |
| **Vendor Commands** | Platform-specific communication |

</div>

### Kernel Configuration for OOB

    

```kconfig
CONFIG_ASPEED_ESPI=y
CONFIG_ASPEED_ESPI_OOB=y
```

### Device Tree for OOB Channel

    

```dts
&espi {
    status = "okay";

    espi_oob: espi-oob {
        compatible = "aspeed,ast2600-espi-oob";
        status = "okay";

        /* OOB channel configuration */
        oob-channel-enable;
    };
};
```

### Sending/Receiving OOB Messages

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># OOB interface (platform-specific)</span>
<span class="c"># Typically accessed via character device or netlink</span>

<span class="c"># Check OOB channel status</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/bus/platform/devices/<span class="k">*</span>.espi-oob/status

<span class="c"># Debug OOB messages</span>
<span class="nb">echo </span>1 <span class="o">></span> /sys/kernel/debug/aspeed-espi-oob/trace_enable
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/kernel/debug/aspeed-espi-oob/trace
```

</div></div>

## Flash Access Channel & eDAF

    

The Flash Access Channel enables the host to access SPI flash attached to the BMC, enabling eDAF (eSPI Direct Attached Flash) boot.

### eDAF Architecture

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        eDAF Architecture                                    │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │                         Host CPU                                    │   │
│   │                                                                     │   │
│   │  1. CPU requests BIOS from flash                                    │   │
│   │         │                                                           │   │
│   │         ▼                                                           │   │
│   │  2. PCH sends flash read via eSPI Flash Channel                     │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                  │                                          │
│                           eSPI Bus                                          │
│                                  │                                          │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │                         BMC                                         │   │
│   │                                                                     │   │
│   │  3. eSPI controller receives flash request                          │   │
│   │         │                                                           │   │
│   │         ▼                                                           │   │
│   │  4. Flash Access Channel controller                                 │   │
│   │         │                                                           │   │
│   │         ▼                                                           │   │
│   │  5. SPI flash controller reads from flash                           │   │
│   │         │                                                           │   │
│   │         ▼                                                           │   │
│   │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │   │
│   │  │              SPI Flash (Shared)                             │    │   │
│   │  │  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────┐  │    │   │
│   │  │  │ BMC Region  │  │ Host BIOS   │  │ Shared/Other        │  │    │   │
│   │  │  │ (U-Boot,    │  │ Region      │  │ Regions             │  │    │   │
│   │  │  │  Kernel,    │  │ (UEFI)      │  │                     │  │    │   │
│   │  │  │  RootFS)    │  │             │  │                     │  │    │   │
│   │  │  └─────────────┘  └─────────────┘  └─────────────────────┘  │    │   │
│   │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │   │
│   │                                                                     │   │
│   │  6. Data returned via eSPI to host                                  │   │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### eDAF Boot Flow

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    eDAF Boot Sequence                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                             │
│  1. System power on                                         │
│         │                                                   │
│         ▼                                                   │
│  2. BMC boots first (from BMC flash region)                 │
│         │                                                   │
│         ▼                                                   │
│  3. BMC initializes eSPI controller                         │
│     - Configures flash access channel                       │
│     - Sets up address mapping                               │
│         │                                                   │
│         ▼                                                   │
│  4. BMC releases host reset (PLTRST#)                       │
│         │                                                   │
│         ▼                                                   │
│  5. Host CPU starts, fetches BIOS via eSPI                  │
│         │                                                   │
│         ▼                                                   │
│  6. eSPI flash reads routed to BMC-attached flash           │
│         │                                                   │
│         ▼                                                   │
│  7. Host BIOS executes, system boots normally               │
│                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### Flash Layout for eDAF

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              Shared SPI Flash Layout (64MB example)         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Offset      │ Size   │ Region         │ Access             │
│ ─────────────┼────────┼────────────────┼──────────────────  │
│  0x00000000  │ 512KB  │ U-Boot         │ BMC only           │
│  0x00080000  │ 64KB   │ U-Boot Env     │ BMC only           │
│  0x00090000  │ ~7MB   │ BMC Kernel     │ BMC only           │
│  0x00800000  │ 24MB   │ BMC RootFS     │ BMC only           │
│  0x02000000  │ 16MB   │ Host BIOS      │ Host via eSPI      │
│  0x03000000  │ 16MB   │ Host BIOS (B)  │ Host via eSPI      │
│                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### MTD Partition Configuration

    

```dts
// Device tree flash partition for eDAF

&fmc {
    status = "okay";
    flash@0 {
        status = "okay";
        m25p,fast-read;
        label = "bmc";
        spi-max-frequency = <50000000>;

        partitions {
            compatible = "fixed-partitions";
            #address-cells = <1>;
            #size-cells = <1>;

            u-boot@0 {
                reg = <0x0 0x80000>;
                label = "u-boot";
            };

            u-boot-env@80000 {
                reg = <0x80000 0x10000>;
                label = "u-boot-env";
            };

            kernel@90000 {
                reg = <0x90000 0x770000>;
                label = "kernel";
            };

            rofs@800000 {
                reg = <0x800000 0x1800000>;
                label = "rofs";
            };

            /* Host BIOS region - accessed via eSPI flash channel */
            host-bios@2000000 {
                reg = <0x2000000 0x1000000>;
                label = "host-bios";
            };

            host-bios-backup@3000000 {
                reg = <0x3000000 0x1000000>;
                label = "host-bios-backup";
            };
        };
    };
};
```

### U-Boot Configuration for eDAF

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># U-Boot environment for eDAF systems</span>

<span class="c"># Ensure BMC doesn't interfere with host BIOS region</span>
<span class="c"># Set flash protection for host region during normal operation</span>

<span class="c"># U-Boot defconfig additions:</span>
<span class="nv">CONFIG_ASPEED_ESPI</span><span class="o">=</span>y
<span class="nv">CONFIG_ASPEED_ESPI_FLASH</span><span class="o">=</span>y

<span class="c"># Environment variables</span>
<span class="nv">flash_protect</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="nb">yes
</span><span class="nv">host_bios_offset</span><span class="o">=</span>0x2000000
<span class="nv">host_bios_size</span><span class="o">=</span>0x1000000
```

</div></div>

### Device Tree for Flash Access Channel

    

```dts
&espi {
    status = "okay";

    espi_flash: espi-flash {
        compatible = "aspeed,ast2600-espi-flash";
        status = "okay";

        /* Flash access channel configuration */
        flash-channel-enable;

        /* Address mapping for host flash access */
        /* Host sees flash starting at 0x0, mapped to BMC flash offset */
        flash-mafs-mode;  /* Master Attached Flash Sharing */

        /* Or SAF mode for more control */
        /* flash-saf-mode; */
    };
};
```

### eDAF Troubleshooting

    

**Issue: Host fails to boot (no BIOS execution)**

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># 1. Verify eSPI flash channel is enabled</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/bus/platform/devices/<span class="k">*</span>.espi-flash/status

<span class="c"># 2. Check flash access channel negotiation</span>
dmesg | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> <span class="s2">"espi.*flash"</span>
<span class="c"># Look for "flash channel enabled"</span>

<span class="c"># 3. Verify host BIOS region is accessible</span>
hexdump <span class="nt">-C</span> /dev/mtd/host-bios | <span class="nb">head</span>
<span class="c"># Should show valid BIOS header (not 0xFF)</span>

<span class="c"># 4. Check eSPI timing</span>
<span class="c"># Host may request flash before BMC is ready</span>
<span class="c"># Verify BMC boot timing vs host release</span>

<span class="c"># 5. Monitor flash access</span>
<span class="nb">echo </span>1 <span class="o">></span> /sys/kernel/debug/aspeed-espi-flash/trace
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/kernel/debug/aspeed-espi-flash/trace
```

</div></div>

**Issue: Flash corruption or read errors**

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check for SPI flash errors</span>
dmesg | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> spi
dmesg | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> mtd

<span class="c"># Verify flash chip detection</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/class/mtd/mtd<span class="k">*</span>/name
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/class/mtd/mtd<span class="k">*</span>/size

<span class="c"># Test flash read</span>
<span class="nb">dd </span><span class="k">if</span><span class="o">=</span>/dev/mtd/host-bios <span class="nv">of</span><span class="o">=</span>/tmp/bios.bin <span class="nv">bs</span><span class="o">=</span>4096 <span class="nv">count</span><span class="o">=</span>1
hexdump <span class="nt">-C</span> /tmp/bios.bin
```

</div></div>

## Kernel Drivers & Device Tree

    

### ASPEED eSPI Kernel Drivers

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Driver | Module | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `aspeed-espi-ctrl` | aspeed_espi | Main eSPI controller |
| `aspeed-espi-vw` | aspeed_espi_vw | Virtual wire channel |
| `aspeed-espi-oob` | aspeed_espi_oob | OOB message channel |
| `aspeed-espi-flash` | aspeed_espi_flash | Flash access channel |
| `aspeed-espi-peri` | aspeed_espi_peri | Peripheral channel |

</div>

### Kernel Configuration Options

    

```kconfig
# Main eSPI support
CONFIG_ASPEED_ESPI=y

# Individual channel support
CONFIG_ASPEED_ESPI_PERIPHERAL=y
CONFIG_ASPEED_ESPI_VW=y
CONFIG_ASPEED_ESPI_OOB=y
CONFIG_ASPEED_ESPI_FLASH=y

# Debug options
CONFIG_ASPEED_ESPI_DEBUG=y
```

### Complete Device Tree Example

    

```dts
// Complete ASPEED AST2600 eSPI configuration

/ {
    compatible = "aspeed,ast2600";

    /* eSPI pin configuration */
    pinctrl {
        espi_default: espi_default {
            function = "ESPI";
            groups = "ESPI";
        };
    };
};

&espi {
    status = "okay";
    pinctrl-names = "default";
    pinctrl-0 = <&espi_default>;

    /* eSPI clock and timing */
    espi,clock-frequency = <66000000>;  /* 66 MHz */

    /* Peripheral channel */
    espi_peri: espi-peripheral {
        compatible = "aspeed,ast2600-espi-peripheral";
        status = "okay";

        /* I/O address decoding */
        io-addr = <0x60 0x64>;  /* KCS interface */
        io-addr = <0x80>;       /* POST code port */

        /* Memory-mapped regions */
        mmio-addr = <0xfed1c000 0x1000>;  /* HECI */
    };

    /* Virtual wire channel */
    espi_vw: espi-vw {
        compatible = "aspeed,ast2600-espi-vw";
        status = "okay";

        gpio-controller;
        #gpio-cells = <2>;
        gpio-line-names =
            "espi-vw-slp-s3",
            "espi-vw-slp-s4",
            "espi-vw-slp-s5",
            "espi-vw-pltrst",
            "espi-vw-sus-stat",
            "espi-vw-sus-warn",
            "espi-vw-oob-rst-warn",
            "espi-vw-host-rst-warn";
    };

    /* OOB message channel */
    espi_oob: espi-oob {
        compatible = "aspeed,ast2600-espi-oob";
        status = "okay";
    };

    /* Flash access channel */
    espi_flash: espi-flash {
        compatible = "aspeed,ast2600-espi-flash";
        status = "okay";
        flash-mafs-mode;
    };
};
```

### Device Tree Properties Reference

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | string | “okay” to enable, “disabled” to disable |
| `compatible` | string | Driver matching string |
| `espi,clock-frequency` | u32 | eSPI bus clock in Hz |
| `io-addr` | u32 array | Peripheral channel I/O addresses |
| `mmio-addr` | u32 array | Peripheral channel MMIO regions |
| `gpio-controller` | flag | Enable GPIO interface for VW |
| `flash-mafs-mode` | flag | Master Attached Flash Sharing |
| `flash-saf-mode` | flag | Slave Attached Flash mode |

</div>

### Pinmux Configuration

    

```dts
// ASPEED AST2600 eSPI pinmux

&pinctrl {
    /* eSPI uses dedicated pins on AST2600 */
    /* No explicit pinmux needed for eSPI function */

    /* For AST2500, explicit pinmux may be required */
    espi_pins: espi_pins {
        function = "ESPI";
        groups = "ESPI";
        /* Pins: ESPI_CLK, ESPI_CS#, ESPI_IO[3:0], ESPI_ALERT#, ESPI_RST# */
    };
};
```

## Platform-Specific Notes

    

### Intel Platform Considerations

    

**Virtual Wire Mapping (Intel PCH):**

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Intel Signal | VW Index | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SLP_S3# | 2 | S3 sleep |
| SLP_S4# | 3 | S4 sleep |
| SLP_S5# | 4 | S5 sleep |
| SLP_A# | 5 | Deep sleep |
| PLTRST# | 41 | Platform reset |
| PME# | 65 | Power management event |
| WAKE# | 66 | Wake signal |

</div>

**Intel ME/CSME Interaction:**

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Intel ME may use OOB channel for HECI over eSPI</span>
<span class="c"># Ensure HECI MMIO region is configured in peripheral channel</span>

<span class="c"># Device tree for HECI</span>
espi_peri: espi-peripheral <span class="o">{</span>
    mmio-addr <span class="o">=</span> <0xfed1c000 0x1000><span class="p">;</span>  /<span class="k">*</span> HECI1 <span class="k">*</span>/
    mmio-addr <span class="o">=</span> <0xfed1d000 0x1000><span class="p">;</span>  /<span class="k">*</span> HECI2 <span class="k">*</span>/
<span class="o">}</span><span class="p">;</span>
```

</div></div>

### AMD Platform Considerations

    

**AMD PSP Interaction:**

AMD platforms may have different eSPI behavior due to PSP (Platform Security Processor):

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># AMD may use different VW indices for some signals</span>
<span class="c"># Check AMD BIOS specification for exact mapping</span>

<span class="c"># AMD-specific timing requirements</span>
<span class="c"># PSP initialization may affect eSPI availability</span>
```

</div></div>

**Virtual Wire Differences:**

<div class="table-wrapper">
| AMD Signal | VW Index | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SLP_S3# | 2 | Same as Intel |
| SLP_S5# | 4 | Same as Intel |
| PLTRST# | 41 | Same as Intel |
| AMD-specific | 64+ | Platform dependent |

</div>

### Intel vs AMD Summary

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Aspect | Intel | AMD |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **VW Indices 2-47** | Standard ACPI signals | Generally compatible |
| **VW Indices 64+** | Vendor-specific | Vendor-specific |
| **Flash Channel** | Supported | Supported |
| **OOB Channel** | HECI tunneling | PSP communication |
| **Timing** | ME initialization | PSP initialization |

</div>
---

## Troubleshooting

    

### Step-by-Step eSPI Debugging

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># 1. Verify eSPI controller detected</span>
dmesg | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> espi
<span class="c"># Expected: "aspeed-espi XXXXX: eSPI controller initialized"</span>

<span class="c"># 2. Check eSPI negotiation</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/bus/platform/devices/<span class="k">*</span>.espi/capabilities
<span class="c"># Shows negotiated channels and frequencies</span>

<span class="c"># 3. Verify channel status</span>
<span class="k">for </span>ch <span class="k">in </span>vw oob flash peripheral<span class="p">;</span> <span class="k">do
    </span><span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"=== </span><span class="nv">$ch</span><span class="s2"> channel ==="</span>
    <span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/bus/platform/devices/<span class="k">*</span>espi-<span class="nv">$ch</span>/status 2>/dev/null
<span class="k">done</span>

<span class="c"># 4. Check for errors</span>
dmesg | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> <span class="s2">"espi.*error</span><span class="se">\|</span><span class="s2">espi.*fail"</span>

<span class="c"># 5. Monitor eSPI activity</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /proc/interrupts | <span class="nb">grep </span>espi
```

</div></div>

### Common Failure Modes

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Symptom | Possible Cause | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No eSPI in dmesg | Driver not loaded | Check kernel config |
| Channel not enabled | Negotiation failed | Check host eSPI config |
| VW signals stuck | Polarity mismatch | Verify device tree |
| Flash timeouts | Timing issues | Check clock frequency |
| Host boot failure | eDAF not ready | Verify BMC boot timing |

</div>

### Relevant Log Messages

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Successful initialization</span>
aspeed-espi: eSPI controller initialized
aspeed-espi: Channel capabilities: VW OOB Flash Peripheral
aspeed-espi-vw: Virtual wire channel enabled

<span class="c"># Common errors</span>
aspeed-espi: Timeout waiting <span class="k">for </span>channel <span class="nb">enable
</span>aspeed-espi: eSPI reset detected
aspeed-espi-flash: Flash <span class="nb">read timeout</span>
```

</div></div>

### Debug Interfaces

    

**Sysfs:**

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># eSPI controller status</span>
/sys/bus/platform/devices/<span class="k">*</span>.espi/
├── capabilities       <span class="c"># Negotiated capabilities</span>
├── enabled           <span class="c"># Controller enable status</span>
├── frequency         <span class="c"># Operating frequency</span>
└── status            <span class="c"># Overall status</span>

<span class="c"># Per-channel status</span>
/sys/bus/platform/devices/<span class="k">*</span>.espi-vw/
├── status            <span class="c"># Channel status</span>
└── vw_gpio/          <span class="c"># GPIO interface for VW</span>
```

</div></div>

**Debugfs:**

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Enable debugfs (if not mounted)</span>
mount <span class="nt">-t</span> debugfs none /sys/kernel/debug

<span class="c"># eSPI debug info</span>
/sys/kernel/debug/aspeed-espi/
├── registers         <span class="c"># Register dump</span>
├── statistics        <span class="c"># Transaction counters</span>
└── trace            <span class="c"># Transaction trace (if enabled)</span>

<span class="c"># Enable tracing</span>
<span class="nb">echo </span>1 <span class="o">></span> /sys/kernel/debug/aspeed-espi/trace_enable
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/kernel/debug/aspeed-espi/trace
```

</div></div>

### Reading eSPI Status Registers

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># ASPEED AST2600 eSPI registers (base 0x1E6EE000)</span>
<span class="c"># Use with caution - direct register access</span>

<span class="c"># eSPI Control Register</span>
devmem 0x1E6EE000

<span class="c"># eSPI Interrupt Status</span>
devmem 0x1E6EE008

<span class="c"># eSPI Interrupt Enable</span>
devmem 0x1E6EE00C

<span class="c"># Virtual Wire Status</span>
devmem 0x1E6EE080

<span class="c"># Flash Channel Status</span>
devmem 0x1E6EE0C0
```

</div></div>

## Overview

    

Unit testing is essential for OpenBMC development. All code submitted upstream must include unit tests. OpenBMC uses:

* **GTest** - Google Test framework for C++ unit tests
* **GMock** - Google Mock for creating mock objects
* **Meson** - Build system with native test support

This guide covers writing tests, mocking D-Bus interfaces, and running tests in OpenBMC.

### Why Unit Test?

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Benefit | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Upstream Requirement** | Code without tests is rejected |
| **Catch Regressions** | Automated testing prevents bugs |
| **Document Behavior** | Tests show expected usage |
| **Enable Refactoring** | Safe code changes with test coverage |

</div>
---

## GTest/GMock Setup with Meson

    

### Meson Configuration

    

Add test configuration to your service’s `meson.build`:

<div class="language-meson highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c1"># Enable testing
</span><span class="n">gtest_dep</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nb">dependency</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">'gtest'</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">main</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="k">true</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">required</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="k">true</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="n">gmock_dep</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nb">dependency</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">'gmock'</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">required</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="k">true</span><span class="p">)</span>

<span class="c1"># Define test executable
</span><span class="n">test_src</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">[</span>
    <span class="s">'test/main_test.cpp'</span><span class="p">,</span>
    <span class="s">'test/service_test.cpp'</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="p">]</span>

<span class="n">test_exe</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nb">executable</span><span class="p">(</span>
    <span class="s">'test-myservice'</span><span class="p">,</span>
    <span class="n">test_src</span><span class="p">,</span>
    <span class="n">dependencies</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">[</span>
        <span class="n">gtest_dep</span><span class="p">,</span>
        <span class="n">gmock_dep</span><span class="p">,</span>
        <span class="n">sdbusplus_dep</span><span class="p">,</span>
        <span class="n">phosphor_logging_dep</span><span class="p">,</span>
    <span class="p">],</span>
    <span class="n">include_directories</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">include_directories</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">'src'</span><span class="p">),</span>
<span class="p">)</span>

<span class="c1"># Register test with Meson
</span><span class="nb">test</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">'myservice-tests'</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">test_exe</span><span class="p">)</span>
```

</div></div>

### Project Structure

    

Organize test files alongside source:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
my-service/
├── meson.build
├── src/
│   ├── main.cpp
│   └── service.cpp
└── test/
    ├── main_test.cpp      # GTest main entry
    ├── service_test.cpp   # Service unit tests
    └── mocks/
        └── mock_dbus.hpp  # D-Bus mocks
```

</div></div>

### Test Main Entry Point

    

Create `test/main_test.cpp`:

<div class="language-cpp highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="cp">#include</span> <span class="cpf"><gtest/gtest.h></span><span class="cp">
</span>
<span class="kt">int</span> <span class="nf">main</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">argc</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="kt">char</span><span class="o">**</span> <span class="n">argv</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="o">::</span><span class="n">testing</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">InitGoogleTest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">&</span><span class="n">argc</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">argv</span><span class="p">);</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">RUN_ALL_TESTS</span><span class="p">();</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
```

</div></div>
---

## Writing GTest Tests

    

### Basic Test Structure

    

<div class="language-cpp highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="cp">#include</span> <span class="cpf"><gtest/gtest.h></span><span class="cp">
#include</span> <span class="cpf">"service.hpp"</span><span class="cp">
</span>
<span class="c1">// Simple test case</span>
<span class="n">TEST</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ServiceTest</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">InitializesCorrectly</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="n">Service</span> <span class="n">svc</span><span class="p">;</span>
    <span class="n">EXPECT_TRUE</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">svc</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">isInitialized</span><span class="p">());</span>
<span class="p">}</span>

<span class="c1">// Test with expected value</span>
<span class="n">TEST</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ServiceTest</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">ReturnsDefaultValue</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="n">Service</span> <span class="n">svc</span><span class="p">;</span>
    <span class="n">EXPECT_EQ</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">svc</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">getValue</span><span class="p">(),</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
```

</div></div>

### Test Fixtures (TEST_F)

    

Use fixtures for common setup/teardown:

<div class="language-cpp highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="cp">#include</span> <span class="cpf"><gtest/gtest.h></span><span class="cp">
#include</span> <span class="cpf">"sensor_manager.hpp"</span><span class="cp">
</span>
<span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">SensorManagerTest</span> <span class="o">:</span> <span class="k">public</span> <span class="o">::</span><span class="n">testing</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">Test</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
  <span class="nl">protected:</span>
    <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="n">SetUp</span><span class="p">()</span> <span class="k">override</span>
    <span class="p">{</span>
        <span class="c1">// Runs before each test</span>
        <span class="n">manager</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">make_unique</span><span class="o"><</span><span class="n">SensorManager</span><span class="o">></span><span class="p">();</span>
    <span class="p">}</span>

    <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">TearDown</span><span class="p">()</span> <span class="k">override</span>
    <span class="p">{</span>
        <span class="c1">// Runs after each test</span>
        <span class="n">manager</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">reset</span><span class="p">();</span>
    <span class="p">}</span>

    <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">unique_ptr</span><span class="o"><</span><span class="n">SensorManager</span><span class="o">></span> <span class="n">manager</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">};</span>

<span class="n">TEST_F</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">SensorManagerTest</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">AddsSensorSuccessfully</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="n">EXPECT_TRUE</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">manager</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">addSensor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"CPU_Temp"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mf">50.0</span><span class="p">));</span>
    <span class="n">EXPECT_EQ</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">manager</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">getSensorCount</span><span class="p">(),</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">);</span>
<span class="p">}</span>

<span class="n">TEST_F</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">SensorManagerTest</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">RejectsDuplicateSensor</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="n">manager</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">addSensor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"CPU_Temp"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mf">50.0</span><span class="p">);</span>
    <span class="n">EXPECT_FALSE</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">manager</span><span class="o">-></span><span class="n">addSensor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"CPU_Temp"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mf">60.0</span><span class="p">));</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
```

</div></div>

### Common Assertions

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Assertion | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `EXPECT_TRUE(cond)` | Condition is true |
| `EXPECT_FALSE(cond)` | Condition is false |
| `EXPECT_EQ(a, b)` | Values are equal |
| `EXPECT_NE(a, b)` | Values are not equal |
| `EXPECT_LT(a, b)` | a < b |
| `EXPECT_GT(a, b)` | a > b |
| `EXPECT_THROW(expr, type)` | Expression throws exception |
| `EXPECT_NO_THROW(expr)` | Expression doesn’t throw |
| `ASSERT_*` | Same as EXPECT but stops test on failure |

</div>
---

## GMock Basics

    

### Creating Mock Classes

    

<div class="language-cpp highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="cp">#include</span> <span class="cpf"><gmock/gmock.h></span><span class="cp">
</span>
<span class="c1">// Interface to mock</span>
<span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">SensorInterface</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
  <span class="nl">public:</span>
    <span class="k">virtual</span> <span class="o">~</span><span class="n">SensorInterface</span><span class="p">()</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">default</span><span class="p">;</span>
    <span class="k">virtual</span> <span class="kt">double</span> <span class="n">getValue</span><span class="p">()</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">;</span>
    <span class="k">virtual</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="n">setValue</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="kt">double</span> <span class="n">value</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">;</span>
    <span class="k">virtual</span> <span class="kt">bool</span> <span class="n">isValid</span><span class="p">()</span> <span class="k">const</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">};</span>

<span class="c1">// Mock implementation</span>
<span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">MockSensor</span> <span class="o">:</span> <span class="k">public</span> <span class="n">SensorInterface</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
  <span class="nl">public:</span>
    <span class="n">MOCK_METHOD</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="kt">double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">getValue</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="p">(),</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="k">override</span><span class="p">));</span>
    <span class="n">MOCK_METHOD</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="kt">void</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">setValue</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="kt">double</span> <span class="n">value</span><span class="p">),</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="k">override</span><span class="p">));</span>
    <span class="n">MOCK_METHOD</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="kt">bool</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">isValid</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="p">(),</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="k">const</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">override</span><span class="p">));</span>
<span class="p">};</span>
```

</div></div>

### Using Mock Objects

    

<div class="language-cpp highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="cp">#include</span> <span class="cpf"><gmock/gmock.h></span><span class="cp">
#include</span> <span class="cpf"><gtest/gtest.h></span><span class="cp">
</span>
<span class="k">using</span> <span class="o">::</span><span class="n">testing</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">Return</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="k">using</span> <span class="o">::</span><span class="n">testing</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">_</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="n">TEST</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ControllerTest</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">ReadsFromSensor</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="n">MockSensor</span> <span class="n">mockSensor</span><span class="p">;</span>

    <span class="c1">// Set up expectations</span>
    <span class="n">EXPECT_CALL</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mockSensor</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">getValue</span><span class="p">())</span>
        <span class="p">.</span><span class="n">WillOnce</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">Return</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mf">45.5</span><span class="p">));</span>

    <span class="n">Controller</span> <span class="n">ctrl</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">&</span><span class="n">mockSensor</span><span class="p">);</span>
    <span class="n">EXPECT_EQ</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ctrl</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">readTemperature</span><span class="p">(),</span> <span class="mf">45.5</span><span class="p">);</span>
<span class="p">}</span>

<span class="n">TEST</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ControllerTest</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">HandlesSensorFailure</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="n">MockSensor</span> <span class="n">mockSensor</span><span class="p">;</span>

    <span class="n">EXPECT_CALL</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mockSensor</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">isValid</span><span class="p">())</span>
        <span class="p">.</span><span class="n">WillOnce</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">Return</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nb">false</span><span class="p">));</span>

    <span class="n">Controller</span> <span class="n">ctrl</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">&</span><span class="n">mockSensor</span><span class="p">);</span>
    <span class="n">EXPECT_THROW</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ctrl</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">readTemperature</span><span class="p">(),</span> <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">runtime_error</span><span class="p">);</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
```

</div></div>

### Common GMock Matchers

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Matcher | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Return(value)` | Return specified value |
| `_` | Match any argument |
| `Eq(value)` | Argument equals value |
| `Gt(value)` | Argument greater than value |
| `WillOnce(action)` | Perform action once |
| `WillRepeatedly(action)` | Perform action every time |
| `Times(n)` | Expect exactly n calls |

</div>
---

## D-Bus Mocking with sdbus++

    

### Why Mock D-Bus?

    

Unit tests should be isolated. Mocking D-Bus:

* Avoids requiring running D-Bus daemon
* Controls responses for testing edge cases
* Enables testing without real hardware

### sdbus++ Mock Utilities

    

OpenBMC’s sdbus++ provides mock helpers. Include the mock headers:

<div class="language-cpp highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="cp">#include</span> <span class="cpf"><sdbusplus/test/sdbus_mock.hpp></span><span class="cp">
</span>
```

</div></div>

### Example: Mocking D-Bus Method Calls

    

<div class="language-cpp highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="cp">#include</span> <span class="cpf"><gtest/gtest.h></span><span class="cp">
#include</span> <span class="cpf"><gmock/gmock.h></span><span class="cp">
#include</span> <span class="cpf"><sdbusplus/test/sdbus_mock.hpp></span><span class="cp">
</span>
<span class="k">using</span> <span class="o">::</span><span class="n">testing</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">_</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="k">using</span> <span class="o">::</span><span class="n">testing</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">Return</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">DBusServiceTest</span> <span class="o">:</span> <span class="k">public</span> <span class="o">::</span><span class="n">testing</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">Test</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
  <span class="nl">protected:</span>
    <span class="n">sdbusplus</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">SdBusMock</span> <span class="n">sdbusMock</span><span class="p">;</span>

    <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="n">SetUp</span><span class="p">()</span> <span class="k">override</span>
    <span class="p">{</span>
        <span class="c1">// Set up mock bus</span>
    <span class="p">}</span>
<span class="p">};</span>

<span class="n">TEST_F</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">DBusServiceTest</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">CallsRemoteMethod</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="c1">// Expect D-Bus method call</span>
    <span class="n">EXPECT_CALL</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">sdbusMock</span><span class="p">,</span>
        <span class="n">sd_bus_call_method</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">_</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">_</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">_</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">_</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">_</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">_</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">_</span><span class="p">))</span>
        <span class="p">.</span><span class="n">WillOnce</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">Return</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">));</span>

    <span class="k">auto</span> <span class="n">bus</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">sdbusplus</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">get_mocked_new</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">&</span><span class="n">sdbusMock</span><span class="p">);</span>
    <span class="n">MyService</span> <span class="n">svc</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">bus</span><span class="p">);</span>

    <span class="n">EXPECT_NO_THROW</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">svc</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">callRemoteMethod</span><span class="p">());</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
```

</div></div>

### Mocking Property Gets/Sets

    

<div class="language-cpp highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="n">TEST_F</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">DBusServiceTest</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">GetsPropertyValue</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="c1">// Mock property read</span>
    <span class="n">EXPECT_CALL</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">sdbusMock</span><span class="p">,</span>
        <span class="n">sd_bus_get_property</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">_</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">_</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">_</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">_</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">_</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">_</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">_</span><span class="p">))</span>
        <span class="p">.</span><span class="n">WillOnce</span><span class="p">([](</span><span class="n">sd_bus</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">const</span> <span class="kt">char</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">const</span> <span class="kt">char</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="p">,</span>
                     <span class="k">const</span> <span class="kt">char</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">sd_bus_error</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">sd_bus_message</span><span class="o">**</span><span class="p">,</span>
                     <span class="k">const</span> <span class="kt">char</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">{</span>
            <span class="c1">// Return mocked property value</span>
            <span class="k">return</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">;</span>
        <span class="p">});</span>

    <span class="k">auto</span> <span class="n">bus</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">sdbusplus</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">get_mocked_new</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">&</span><span class="n">sdbusMock</span><span class="p">);</span>
    <span class="n">MyService</span> <span class="nf">svc</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">bus</span><span class="p">);</span>

    <span class="n">EXPECT_EQ</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">svc</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">getRemoteProperty</span><span class="p">(),</span> <span class="n">expectedValue</span><span class="p">);</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
```

</div></div>

<span class="p">{</span>

## Running Tests

    

### Via Meson (Local Build)

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Configure build with tests enabled</span>
meson setup builddir <span class="nt">-Dtests</span><span class="o">=</span>enabled

<span class="c"># Build and run tests</span>
meson <span class="nb">test</span> <span class="nt">-C</span> builddir

<span class="c"># Run with verbose output</span>
meson <span class="nb">test</span> <span class="nt">-C</span> builddir <span class="nt">-v</span>

<span class="c"># Run specific test</span>
meson <span class="nb">test</span> <span class="nt">-C</span> builddir myservice-tests
```

</div></div>

### Via Bitbake

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Run tests for a specific recipe</span>
bitbake phosphor-logging <span class="nt">-c</span> <span class="nb">test</span>

<span class="c"># Run tests and keep build directory</span>
bitbake phosphor-logging <span class="nt">-c</span> <span class="nb">test</span> <span class="nt">-f</span>

<span class="c"># Check test results</span>
<span class="nb">cat </span>tmp/work/<span class="k">*</span>/phosphor-logging/<span class="k">*</span>/temp/log.do_test
```

</div></div>

### With SDK (Local Development)

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Source SDK environment</span>
<span class="nb">source</span> /opt/openbmc-phosphor/<span class="k">*</span>/environment-setup-<span class="k">*</span>

<span class="c"># Build and test locally</span>
meson setup builddir <span class="nt">--cross-file</span><span class="o">=</span>cross.txt
meson <span class="nb">test</span> <span class="nt">-C</span> builddir
```

</div></div>

## Test Coverage

    

### Enabling Coverage in Meson

    

Add to `meson.build`:

<div class="language-meson highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="k">if</span> <span class="nb">get_option</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">'coverage'</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="nb">add_project_arguments</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">'-fprofile-arcs'</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="s">'-ftest-coverage'</span><span class="p">,</span>
                          <span class="n">language</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="s">'cpp'</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="nb">add_project_link_arguments</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">'-lgcov'</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">language</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="s">'cpp'</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="k">endif</span>
```

</div></div>

Add to `meson_options.txt`:

<div class="language-meson highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="nb">option</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">'coverage'</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">type</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="s">'boolean'</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="k">false</span><span class="p">,</span>
       <span class="n">description</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="s">'Enable code coverage'</span><span class="p">)</span>
```

</div></div>

### Generating Coverage Reports

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Build with coverage enabled</span>
meson setup builddir <span class="nt">-Dcoverage</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="nb">true
</span>meson compile <span class="nt">-C</span> builddir

<span class="c"># Run tests</span>
meson <span class="nb">test</span> <span class="nt">-C</span> builddir

<span class="c"># Generate coverage report with lcov</span>
lcov <span class="nt">--capture</span> <span class="nt">--directory</span> builddir <span class="se">\</span>
     <span class="nt">--output-file</span> coverage.info

<span class="c"># Generate HTML report</span>
genhtml coverage.info <span class="nt">--output-directory</span> coverage-report

<span class="c"># View report</span>
xdg-open coverage-report/index.html
```

</div></div>

### Coverage Report Interpretation

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Metric | Target | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Line Coverage | >80% | Lines executed by tests |
| Function Coverage | >90% | Functions called by tests |
| Branch Coverage | >70% | Decision branches taken |

</div>
---

## Practical Example: phosphor-logging

    

The `phosphor-logging` repository demonstrates OpenBMC testing patterns.

### Test Structure

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
phosphor-logging/
├── test/
│   ├── meson.build
│   ├── log_manager_test.cpp
│   ├── elog_test.cpp
│   └── remote_logging_test.cpp
```

</div></div>

### Example Test from phosphor-logging

    

<div class="language-cpp highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="cp">#include</span> <span class="cpf"><gtest/gtest.h></span><span class="cp">
#include</span> <span class="cpf">"log_manager.hpp"</span><span class="cp">
</span>
<span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">LogManagerTest</span> <span class="o">:</span> <span class="k">public</span> <span class="o">::</span><span class="n">testing</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">Test</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
  <span class="nl">protected:</span>
    <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="n">SetUp</span><span class="p">()</span> <span class="k">override</span>
    <span class="p">{</span>
        <span class="c1">// Create temporary log directory</span>
        <span class="n">tempDir</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">filesystem</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">temp_directory_path</span><span class="p">()</span> <span class="o">/</span> <span class="s">"test-logs"</span><span class="p">;</span>
        <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">filesystem</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">create_directories</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">tempDir</span><span class="p">);</span>
    <span class="p">}</span>

    <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">TearDown</span><span class="p">()</span> <span class="k">override</span>
    <span class="p">{</span>
        <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">filesystem</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">remove_all</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">tempDir</span><span class="p">);</span>
    <span class="p">}</span>

    <span class="n">std</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">filesystem</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">path</span> <span class="n">tempDir</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">};</span>

<span class="n">TEST_F</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">LogManagerTest</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">CreatesLogEntry</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="n">LogManager</span> <span class="n">manager</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">tempDir</span><span class="p">);</span>

    <span class="k">auto</span> <span class="n">id</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">manager</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">createEntry</span><span class="p">(</span>
        <span class="s">"Test message"</span><span class="p">,</span>
        <span class="n">Entry</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">Level</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">Informational</span><span class="p">);</span>

    <span class="n">EXPECT_GT</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">id</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span>
    <span class="n">EXPECT_TRUE</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">manager</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">hasEntry</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">id</span><span class="p">));</span>
<span class="p">}</span>

<span class="n">TEST_F</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">LogManagerTest</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">DeletesLogEntry</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="n">LogManager</span> <span class="n">manager</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">tempDir</span><span class="p">);</span>
    <span class="k">auto</span> <span class="n">id</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">manager</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">createEntry</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"Test"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">Entry</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">Level</span><span class="o">::</span><span class="n">Error</span><span class="p">);</span>

    <span class="n">EXPECT_TRUE</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">manager</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">deleteEntry</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">id</span><span class="p">));</span>
    <span class="n">EXPECT_FALSE</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">manager</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">hasEntry</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">id</span><span class="p">));</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
```

</div></div>

## Best Practices

    

### Test Organization

    

* One test file per source file (`service.cpp` → `service_test.cpp`)
* Group related tests in test fixtures
* Use descriptive test names: `TEST(Component, WhatItDoes)`

### Test Independence

    

* Each test should be independent
* Don’t rely on test execution order
* Clean up resources in TearDown

### Mock Appropriately

    

* Mock external dependencies (D-Bus, filesystem, network)
* Don’t mock the code under test
* Verify mock expectations

### Coverage Goals

    

* Aim for >80% line coverage
* Test error paths, not just happy paths
* Cover boundary conditions

## Overview

    

Robot Framework is the standard integration testing framework for OpenBMC. The `openbmc-test-automation` repository contains comprehensive tests for:

* Redfish API validation
* IPMI command testing
* Power state management
* Sensor and inventory verification
* Firmware update testing

This guide covers setting up Robot Framework and writing tests for OpenBMC.

### Unit Tests vs Integration Tests

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Aspect | Unit Tests (GTest) | Integration Tests (Robot) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Scope** | Single function/class | Full system behavior |
| **Dependencies** | Mocked | Real services |
| **Speed** | Fast (ms) | Slower (seconds) |
| **Environment** | Build machine | Running BMC (QEMU/HW) |
| **Purpose** | Code correctness | System behavior |

</div>
---

## Environment Setup

    

### Install Robot Framework

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Install Python 3 and pip</span>
<span class="nb">sudo </span>apt <span class="nb">install </span>python3 python3-pip

<span class="c"># Install Robot Framework</span>
pip3 <span class="nb">install </span>robotframework

<span class="c"># Install additional libraries</span>
pip3 <span class="nb">install </span>robotframework-sshlibrary
pip3 <span class="nb">install </span>robotframework-requests

## Hello World Test

    

### Minimal Robot Test

    

Create `hello_openbmc.robot`:

<div class="language-robot highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="gh">*** Settings ***</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="bp">Documentation</span><span class="w">     </span><span class="s">Hello World test for OpenBMC</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="bp">Library</span><span class="w">           </span><span class="nf">Collections</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="bp">Library</span><span class="w">           </span><span class="nf">RequestsLibrary</span><span class="w">

</span><span class="gh">*** Variables ***</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="nv">${OPENBMC_HOST}</span><span class="w">       </span><span class="s">localhost</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="nv">${OPENBMC_PORT}</span><span class="w">       </span><span class="s">2443</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="nv">${OPENBMC_USERNAME}</span><span class="w">   </span><span class="s">root</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="nv">${OPENBMC_PASSWORD}</span><span class="w">   </span><span class="s">0penBmc</span><span class="w">

</span><span class="gh">*** Test Cases ***</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="nl">Verify BMC Redfish Service Root</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="bp">Documentation</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">Verify Redfish service is accessible</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="bp">Tags</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">smoke</span><span class="w">

    </span><span class="c"># Create session</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nf">Create Session</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">openbmc</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">https://</span><span class="nv">${OPENBMC_HOST}</span><span class="s">:</span><span class="nv">${OPENBMC_PORT}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nf">...</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">verify=</span><span class="nv">${False}</span><span class="w">

    </span><span class="c"># Get service root</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nv">${resp}</span><span class="nf">=</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">GET On Session</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">openbmc</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">/redfish/v1</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nf">...</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">expected_status=200</span><span class="w">

    </span><span class="c"># Verify response</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nf">Should Be Equal As Strings</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="nv">${resp.status_code}</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">200</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nf">Dictionary Should Contain Key</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="nv">${resp.json()}</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">@odata.id</span><span class="w">

</span><span class="nl">Verify BMC Manager Resource</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="bp">Documentation</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">Verify BMC Manager is accessible</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="bp">Tags</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">smoke</span><span class="w">

    </span><span class="nf">Create Session</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">openbmc</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">https://</span><span class="nv">${OPENBMC_HOST}</span><span class="s">:</span><span class="nv">${OPENBMC_PORT}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nf">...</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">auth=</span><span class="nv">${OPENBMC_AUTH}</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">verify=</span><span class="nv">${False}</span><span class="w">

    </span><span class="nv">${resp}</span><span class="nf">=</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">GET On Session</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">openbmc</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nf">...</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">expected_status=200</span><span class="w">

    </span><span class="nf">Should Be Equal As Strings</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="nv">${resp.json()["Status"]["State"]}</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">Enabled</span><span class="w">

</span><span class="gh">*** Keywords ***</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="nv">${OPENBMC_AUTH}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="bp">Return</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="nv">${OPENBMC_USERNAME}</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="nv">${OPENBMC_PASSWORD}</span><span class="w">
</span>

## Robot Test File Structure

    

### File Organization

    

<div class="language-robot highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="gh">*** Settings ***</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="bp">Documentation</span><span class="w">     </span><span class="s">Description of test suite</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="bp">Library</span><span class="w">           </span><span class="nf">LibraryName</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="bp">Resource</span><span class="w">          </span><span class="nf">resource_file.robot</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="bp">Suite Setup</span><span class="w">       </span><span class="nf">Setup Keyword</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="bp">Suite Teardown</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="nf">Teardown Keyword</span><span class="w">

</span><span class="gh">*** Variables ***</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="nv">${VARIABLE}</span><span class="w">       </span><span class="s">value</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="nv">@{LIST}</span><span class="w">           </span><span class="s">item1</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">item2</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="nv">&{DICT}</span><span class="w">           </span><span class="s">key1=value1</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">key2=value2</span><span class="w">

</span><span class="gh">*** Test Cases ***</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="nl">Test Case Name</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="bp">Documentation</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">Test description</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="bp">Tags</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">             </span><span class="s">tag1</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="s">tag2</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nf">Keyword 1</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nf">Keyword 2</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="nv">${argument}</span><span class="w">

</span><span class="gh">*** Keywords ***</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="nl">Custom Keyword</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="bp">Arguments</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="nv">${arg1}</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="nv">${arg2}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nf">Log</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="nv">${arg1}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="bp">Return</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="nv">${result}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

### Common Settings

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `Library` | Import Python/Robot library |
| `Resource` | Import resource file with keywords |
| `Suite Setup` | Run before all tests |
| `Suite Teardown` | Run after all tests |
| `Test Setup` | Run before each test |
| `Test Teardown` | Run after each test |
