```
│  │   ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────────┐    ││
│  │   │meta-phosphor │ │meta-aspeed   │ │meta-openembedded │    ││
│  │   │(services)    │ │(BMC SoC)     │ │(base packages)   │    ││
│  │   └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └──────────────────┘    ││
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘│
│                             │                                   │
│  ┌──────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┐│
│  │                   BitBake Build System                      ││
│  │              (openbmc-env, bitbake)                         ││
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘│
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div>  </div>

---

## Prerequisites

    

Before porting, ensure you have:

* BMC SoC datasheet and documentation
* Host system specifications
* Hardware schematic
* Working OpenBMC development environment
* QEMU or hardware for testing

---

## Porting Checklist

    

### 1. Layer Setup

    

* Create meta-myplatform layer
* Create conf/layer.conf
* Create conf/machine/myboard.conf
* Add to bblayers.conf

### 2. Machine Configuration

    

* Set MACHINE architecture (armv7/armv8)
* Configure BMC SoC (ASPEED/Nuvoton)
* Set kernel and U-Boot preferences
* Configure flash layout

### 3. Device Tree

    

* Create or modify device tree
* Configure GPIO mappings
* Configure I2C buses
* Configure SPI/UART/etc.

### 4. U-Boot

    

* Configure U-Boot for platform
* Set boot arguments
* Configure flash partitions

### 5. Kernel

    

* Enable required drivers
* Configure hwmon sensors
* Configure GPIO subsystem

### 6. OpenBMC Services

    

* Configure Entity Manager
* Configure sensor mappings
* Configure LED groups
* Configure power control

### 7. Verification

    

* Boot test on hardware/QEMU
* Sensor readings
* Power control
* Network connectivity
* Redfish/IPMI access

---

## Creating the Machine Layer

    

### Layer Structure

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
meta-myplatform/
├── conf/
│   ├── layer.conf
│   └── machine/
│       └── myboard.conf
├── recipes-bsp/
│   └── u-boot/
│       └── u-boot-aspeed_%.bbappend
├── recipes-kernel/
│   └── linux/
│       └── linux-aspeed_%.bbappend
├── recipes-phosphor/
│   ├── configuration/
│   │   └── entity-manager/
│   │       └── myboard-entity-config.bb
│   ├── sensors/
│   ├── leds/
│   └── power/
└── README.md
```

</div></div>

### layer.conf

    

<div class="language-python highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">

```
<span class="c1"># conf/layer.conf
</span>
<span class="n">BBPATH</span> <span class="p">.</span><span class="o">=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s">:${LAYERDIR}</span><span class="sh">"</span>

<span class="n">BBFILES</span> <span class="o">+=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s">${LAYERDIR}/recipes-*/*/*.bb </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="s">            ${LAYERDIR}/recipes-*/*/*.bbappend</span><span class="sh">"</span>

<span class="n">BBFILE_COLLECTIONS</span> <span class="o">+=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s">meta-myplatform</span><span class="sh">"</span>
<span class="n">BBFILE_PATTERN_meta</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="n">myplatform</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s">^${LAYERDIR}/</span><span class="sh">"</span>
<span class="n">LAYERDEPENDS_meta</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="n">myplatform</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s"> </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="s">    core </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="s">    meta-phosphor </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="s">    meta-aspeed </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="sh">"</span>
<span class="n">LAYERSERIES_COMPAT_meta</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="n">myplatform</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s">kirkstone mickledore scarthgap</span><span class="sh">"</span>
```

## Device Tree Configuration

    

### Example Device Tree

    

```dts
// aspeed-bmc-myplatform-myboard.dts

/dts-v1/;

#include "aspeed-g5.dtsi"
#include <dt-bindings/gpio/aspeed-gpio.h>

/ {
    model = "MyPlatform MyBoard BMC";
    compatible = "myplatform,myboard-bmc", "aspeed,ast2500";

    chosen {
        stdout-path = &uart5;
        bootargs = "console=ttyS4,115200 earlyprintk";
    };

    memory@80000000 {
        reg = <0x80000000 0x20000000>;  /* 512MB */
    };

    reserved-memory {
        #address-cells = <1>;
        #size-cells = <1>;
        ranges;

        video_memory: video {
            size = <0x04000000>;  /* 64MB for video */
            alignment = <0x01000000>;
            compatible = "shared-dma-pool";
            reusable;
        };
    };

    leds {
        compatible = "gpio-leds";

        identify {
            label = "identify";
            gpios = <&gpio ASPEED_GPIO(A, 0) GPIO_ACTIVE_HIGH>;
            default-state = "off";
        };

        power {
            label = "power";
            gpios = <&gpio ASPEED_GPIO(A, 1) GPIO_ACTIVE_HIGH>;
            default-state = "on";
        };

        fault {
            label = "fault";
            gpios = <&gpio ASPEED_GPIO(A, 2) GPIO_ACTIVE_HIGH>;
            default-state = "off";
        };
    };

    gpio-keys {
        compatible = "gpio-keys";

        power-button {
            label = "power-button";
            gpios = <&gpio ASPEED_GPIO(B, 0) GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW>;
            linux,code = <116>;  /* KEY_POWER */
        };

        reset-button {
            label = "reset-button";
            gpios = <&gpio ASPEED_GPIO(B, 1) GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW>;
            linux,code = <0x198>;  /* KEY_RESTART */
        };
    };
};

&fmc {
    status = "okay";
    flash@0 {
        status = "okay";
        m25p,fast-read;
        label = "bmc";
        spi-max-frequency = <50000000>;
        #include "openbmc-flash-layout.dtsi"
    };
};

&spi1 {
    status = "okay";
    pinctrl-names = "default";
    pinctrl-0 = <&pinctrl_spi1_default>;
    flash@0 {
        status = "okay";
        m25p,fast-read;
        label = "pnor";
        spi-max-frequency = <100000000>;
    };
};

&uart5 {
    status = "okay";
};

&mac0 {
    status = "okay";
    pinctrl-names = "default";
    pinctrl-0 = <&pinctrl_rmii1_default>;
    use-ncsi;
};

&i2c0 {
    status = "okay";

    tmp75@48 {
        compatible = "ti,tmp75";
        reg = <0x48>;
        label = "cpu_temp";
    };
};

&i2c1 {
    status = "okay";

    eeprom@50 {
        compatible = "atmel,24c256";
        reg = <0x50>;
        label = "fru";
    };
};

&i2c2 {
    status = "okay";

    psu@58 {
        compatible = "pmbus";
        reg = <0x58>;
    };
};

&pwm_tacho {
    status = "okay";
    pinctrl-names = "default";
    pinctrl-0 = <&pinctrl_pwm0_default &pinctrl_pwm1_default>;

    fan@0 {
        reg = <0x00>;
        aspeed,fan-tach-ch = /bits/ 8 <0x00>;
    };

    fan@1 {
        reg = <0x01>;
        aspeed,fan-tach-ch = /bits/ 8 <0x01>;
    };
};

&video {
    status = "okay";
    memory-region = <&video_memory>;
};

&vuart {
    status = "okay";
};
```

## GPIO Configuration

    

### GPIO Pin Mapping

    

Create a GPIO mapping document:

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
# GPIO Pin Mapping for MyBoard

## Power Control
| Signal          | GPIO        | Direction | Active |
|-----------------|-------------|-----------|--------|
| POWER_BTN_IN    | GPIOB0      | Input     | Low    |
| POWER_OUT       | GPIOB2      | Output    | High   |
| RESET_BTN_IN    | GPIOB1      | Input     | Low    |
| RESET_OUT       | GPIOB3      | Output    | High   |

## Status Signals
| Signal          | GPIO        | Direction | Active |
|-----------------|-------------|-----------|--------|
| POST_COMPLETE   | GPIOC0      | Input     | High   |
| S0_SLP_S3       | GPIOC1      | Input     | Low    |
| S0_SLP_S5       | GPIOC2      | Input     | Low    |

## LEDs
| Signal          | GPIO        | Direction | Active |
|-----------------|-------------|-----------|--------|
| LED_IDENTIFY    | GPIOA0      | Output    | High   |
| LED_POWER       | GPIOA1      | Output    | High   |
| LED_FAULT       | GPIOA2      | Output    | High   |
```

</div></div>

### Recipe for Configuration

    

```bitbake
# recipes-phosphor/configuration/entity-manager/myboard-entity-config.bb
SUMMARY = "MyBoard Entity Manager Configuration"
LICENSE = "Apache-2.0"
LIC_FILES_CHKSUM = "file://${COREBASE}/meta/files/common-licenses/Apache-2.0;md5=89aea4e17d99a7cacdbeed46a0096b10"

inherit allarch

SRC_URI = " \
    file://myboard.json \
"

S = "${WORKDIR}"

do_install() {
    install -d ${D}${datadir}/entity-manager/configurations
    install -m 0644 ${S}/myboard.json \
        ${D}${datadir}/entity-manager/configurations/
}

FILES:${PN} = "${datadir}/entity-manager/configurations/*"
```

## Verification Testing

    

### Boot Test

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check boot messages</span>
dmesg | less

<span class="c"># Verify services are running</span>
systemctl status phosphor-<span class="k">*</span>

<span class="c"># Check D-Bus objects</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.ObjectMapper
```

</div></div>

### Sensor Test

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check sensors</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor

<span class="c"># Read temperature sensor</span>
busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.HwmonTempSensor <span class="se">\</span>
    /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors/temperature/CPU_Temp <span class="se">\</span>
    xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value Value

<span class="c"># Via Redfish</span>
curl <span class="nt">-k</span> <span class="nt">-u</span> root:0penBmc <span class="se">\</span>
    https://localhost/redfish/v1/Chassis/chassis/Sensors
```

</div></div>

### Power Control Test

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check state</span>
obmcutil state

<span class="c"># Power on</span>
obmcutil poweron

<span class="c"># Power off</span>
obmcutil poweroff
```

</div></div>

### Network Test

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check interface</span>
ip addr show eth0

<span class="c"># Test connectivity</span>
ping <span class="nt">-c</span> 3 192.168.1.1
```

</div></div>
---

## Common Pitfalls

    

### Device Tree Issues

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Symptom: Device not found</span>
<span class="c"># Check: Device tree binding</span>
<span class="c"># Solution: Verify compatible string matches driver</span>

<span class="c"># Symptom: Wrong GPIO polarity</span>
<span class="c"># Check: GPIO flags in device tree</span>
<span class="c"># Solution: Set GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW/HIGH correctly</span>
```

</div></div>

### I2C Issues

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Symptom: Device not responding</span>
<span class="c"># Check: I2C bus and address</span>
i2cdetect <span class="nt">-y</span> 0

<span class="c"># Solution: Verify address and bus in device tree</span>
```

</div></div>

### Service Failures

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check service status</span>
systemctl status phosphor-pid-control

<span class="c"># Check logs</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> phosphor-pid-control
```

</div></div>
---

## Debugging During Porting

    

When bringing up a new platform, kernel and service debugging is essential.

### Early Boot Debugging

    

For kernel bring-up, enable early console output:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># In device tree chosen node</span>
chosen <span class="o">{</span>
    bootargs <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s2">"console=ttyS4,115200 earlyprintk"</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="o">}</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="c"># Or via U-Boot</span>
fw_setenv bootargs <span class="s2">"console=ttyS4,115200 earlyprintk earlycon=uart8250,mmio32,0x1e784000"</span>
```

</div></div>

### Kernel Debug Configuration

    

Add kernel debug options for porting:

```kconfig
# Recommended for porting
CONFIG_DEBUG_INFO=y
CONFIG_KASAN=y              # Kernel Address Sanitizer
CONFIG_PROVE_LOCKING=y      # Lock debugging
CONFIG_DEBUG_ATOMIC_SLEEP=y
CONFIG_STACKTRACE=y
```

### Memory and Runtime Debugging

    

For debugging services and applications on your new platform:

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Enable ASan for a specific recipe</span>
CFLAGS:append:pn-<recipe> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s2">" -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer"</span>
LDFLAGS:append:pn-<recipe> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s2">" -fsanitize=address"</span>

<span class="c"># Run service under Valgrind</span>
valgrind <span class="nt">--leak-check</span><span class="o">=</span>full /usr/bin/<service>
```

</div></div>

For comprehensive debugging tools including ASan, UBSan, TSan, Valgrind, and kernel debug options (KASAN, KCSAN, lockdep), see the **[Linux Debug Tools Guide](/openbmc-guide-tutorial/docs/05-advanced/08-linux-debug-tools-guide.html)**.

---

## eSPI Configuration

    

For Intel and AMD platforms using eSPI (Enhanced Serial Peripheral Interface) instead of LPC, additional configuration is required:

* **Virtual Wires**: Map host power state signals (SLP_S3, SLP_S5, PLTRST)
* **Flash Channel**: Configure eDAF if host BIOS is on BMC-attached flash
* **Console**: Set up eSPI UART for host console redirection

See the **[eSPI Guide](/openbmc-guide-tutorial/docs/05-advanced/09-espi-guide.html)** for complete eSPI configuration including device tree examples, kernel drivers, and troubleshooting.

---

* [OpenBMC Machine Layer Examples](https://github.com/openbmc/openbmc/tree/master/meta-ibm)
* [ASPEED SDK Documentation](https://github.com/AspeedTech-BMC/openbmc)
* [Yocto Project Documentation](https://docs.yoctoproject.org/)
* [Add New System Guide](https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/development/add-new-system.md)

        <main>
          
            
# Machine Layer Guide

    

Create a Yocto machine layer for your OpenBMC platform.

</li>
  <li><a href="#adding-the-layer-to-build" id="markdown-toc-adding-the-layer-to-build">Adding the Layer to Build</a>    
1. [Update bblayers.conf](#update-bblayersconf)
2. [Set Machine](#set-machine)

  </li>
  <li><a href="#common-customizations" id="markdown-toc-common-customizations">Common Customizations</a>    
1. [Add Entity Manager Configuration](#add-entity-manager-configuration)
2. [Customize LED Configuration](#customize-led-configuration)

  </li>
  <li><a href="#building" id="markdown-toc-building">Building</a></li>
  <li><a href="#example-machine-layer" id="markdown-toc-example-machine-layer">Example Machine Layer</a></li>
  <li><a href="#next-steps" id="markdown-toc-next-steps">Next Steps</a></li>
  <li><a href="#references" id="markdown-toc-references">References</a></li>
</ol>
---

## Overview

    

A machine layer defines your specific hardware platform for OpenBMC. It contains machine configuration, recipes, and customizations.

---

## Layer Structure

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
meta-myplatform/
├── conf/
│   ├── layer.conf                    # Layer metadata
│   └── machine/
│       └── myboard.conf              # Machine configuration
├── recipes-bsp/
│   └── u-boot/
│       └── u-boot-aspeed_%.bbappend  # U-Boot customization
├── recipes-kernel/
│   └── linux/
│       ├── linux-aspeed_%.bbappend   # Kernel config
│       └── linux-aspeed/
│           └── myboard.cfg           # Kernel fragments
├── recipes-phosphor/
│   ├── configuration/
│   │   └── entity-manager/           # Hardware configuration
│   ├── leds/                         # LED configuration
│   ├── sensors/                      # Sensor customization
│   └── gpio/                         # GPIO configuration
└── README.md
```

</div></div>
---

## Creating layer.conf

    

<div class="language-python highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c1"># conf/layer.conf
</span>
<span class="c1"># Add layer to BBPATH
</span><span class="n">BBPATH</span> <span class="p">.</span><span class="o">=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s">:${LAYERDIR}</span><span class="sh">"</span>

<span class="c1"># Recipe locations
</span><span class="n">BBFILES</span> <span class="o">+=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s"> </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="s">    ${LAYERDIR}/recipes-*/*/*.bb </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="s">    ${LAYERDIR}/recipes-*/*/*.bbappend </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="sh">"</span>

<span class="c1"># Layer identification
</span><span class="n">BBFILE_COLLECTIONS</span> <span class="o">+=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s">meta-myplatform</span><span class="sh">"</span>
<span class="n">BBFILE_PATTERN_meta</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="n">myplatform</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s">^${LAYERDIR}/</span><span class="sh">"</span>
<span class="n">BBFILE_PRIORITY_meta</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="n">myplatform</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s">10</span><span class="sh">"</span>

<span class="c1"># Layer dependencies
</span><span class="n">LAYERDEPENDS_meta</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="n">myplatform</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s"> </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="s">    core </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="s">    meta-phosphor </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="s">    meta-aspeed </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="sh">"</span>

<span class="c1"># Compatible Yocto versions
</span><span class="n">LAYERSERIES_COMPAT_meta</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="n">myplatform</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s">kirkstone mickledore scarthgap</span><span class="sh">"</span>
```

</div></div>
---

## Machine Configuration

    

### Basic machine.conf

    

<div class="language-python highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c1"># conf/machine/myboard.conf
</span>
<span class="c1">#@TYPE: Machine
#@NAME: MyBoard BMC
#@DESCRIPTION: Machine configuration for MyBoard
</span>
<span class="c1"># Kernel device tree
</span><span class="n">KERNEL_DEVICETREE</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s">aspeed/aspeed-bmc-myplatform-myboard.dtb</span><span class="sh">"</span>

<span class="c1"># U-Boot configuration
</span><span class="n">PREFERRED_PROVIDER_virtual</span><span class="o">/</span><span class="n">bootloader</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s">u-boot-aspeed</span><span class="sh">"</span>
<span class="n">PREFERRED_PROVIDER_u</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="n">boot</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s">u-boot-aspeed</span><span class="sh">"</span>
<span class="n">PREFERRED_PROVIDER_u</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="n">boot</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="n">fw</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="n">utils</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s">u-boot-aspeed-fw-utils</span><span class="sh">"</span>

<span class="c1"># Flash size (KB)
</span><span class="n">FLASH_SIZE</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s">32768</span><span class="sh">"</span>

<span class="c1"># Console
</span><span class="n">SERIAL_CONSOLES</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s">115200;ttyS4</span><span class="sh">"</span>

<span class="c1"># Machine features - enable OpenBMC capabilities
</span><span class="n">MACHINE_FEATURES</span> <span class="o">+=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s"> </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="s">    obmc-phosphor-fan-mgmt </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="s">    obmc-phosphor-chassis-mgmt </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="s">    obmc-host-state-mgmt </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="sh">"</span>

<span class="c1"># Distro features
</span><span class="n">DISTRO_FEATURES</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="n">append</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s"> obmc-ikvm</span><span class="sh">"</span>
<span class="n">DISTRO_FEATURES</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="n">append</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s"> obmc-virtual-media</span><span class="sh">"</span>

<span class="c1"># Packages to install
</span><span class="n">IMAGE_INSTALL</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="n">append</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="sh">"</span><span class="s"> </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="s">    entity-manager </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="s">    dbus-sensors </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="s">    phosphor-pid-control </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="s">    myboard-entity-config </span><span class="se">\
</span><span class="sh">"</span>

<span class="c1"># Include base configuration
</span><span class="n">require</span> <span class="n">conf</span><span class="o">/</span><span class="n">machine</span><span class="o">/</span><span class="n">include</span><span class="o">/</span><span class="n">aspeed</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">inc</span>
<span class="n">require</span> <span class="n">conf</span><span class="o">/</span><span class="n">machine</span><span class="o">/</span><span class="n">include</span><span class="o">/</span><span class="n">obmc</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="n">bsp</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="n">common</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">inc</span>
```

</div></div>

### Feature Options

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Feature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `obmc-phosphor-fan-mgmt` | Fan control and monitoring |
| `obmc-phosphor-chassis-mgmt` | Chassis power control |
| `obmc-host-state-mgmt` | Host state management |
| `obmc-ikvm` | Remote KVM support |
| `obmc-virtual-media` | Virtual media support |

</div>

## Adding the Layer to Build

    

### Update bblayers.conf

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Add layer path</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s1">'BBLAYERS += "/path/to/meta-myplatform"'</span> <span class="o">>></span> build/conf/bblayers.conf
```

</div></div>

### Set Machine

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># In local.conf</span>
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s1">'MACHINE = "myboard"'</span> <span class="o">>></span> build/conf/local.conf
```

</div></div>
---

## Common Customizations

    

### Add Entity Manager Configuration

    

```bitbake
# recipes-phosphor/configuration/entity-manager/myboard-config.bb

SUMMARY = "MyBoard Entity Manager Configuration"
LICENSE = "Apache-2.0"
LIC_FILES_CHKSUM = "file://${COREBASE}/meta/files/common-licenses/Apache-2.0;md5=89aea4e17d99a7cacdbeed46a0096b10"

inherit allarch

SRC_URI = "file://myboard.json"

S = "${WORKDIR}"

do_install() {
    install -d ${D}${datadir}/entity-manager/configurations
    install -m 0644 ${S}/myboard.json ${D}${datadir}/entity-manager/configurations/
}

FILES:${PN} = "${datadir}/entity-manager/configurations/*"
```

### Customize LED Configuration

    

```bitbake
# recipes-phosphor/leds/myboard-led-config.bb

SUMMARY = "MyBoard LED Configuration"
LICENSE = "Apache-2.0"

inherit allarch

SRC_URI = "file://led.yaml"

do_install() {
    install -d ${D}${datadir}/phosphor-led-manager
    install -m 0644 ${S}/led.yaml ${D}${datadir}/phosphor-led-manager/
}
```

<div id="main-content" class="main-content">
        <main>
          
            
# Device Tree Guide

    

Configure the Linux device tree for your BMC platform.

</li>
  <li><a href="#i2c-bus-configuration" id="markdown-toc-i2c-bus-configuration">I2C Bus Configuration</a></li>
  <li><a href="#spi-flash-configuration" id="markdown-toc-spi-flash-configuration">SPI Flash Configuration</a></li>
  <li><a href="#network-configuration" id="markdown-toc-network-configuration">Network Configuration</a>    
1. [NCSI (Sideband)](#ncsi-sideband)
2. [Dedicated Ethernet](#dedicated-ethernet)

  </li>
  <li><a href="#pwmfan-configuration" id="markdown-toc-pwmfan-configuration">PWM/Fan Configuration</a></li>
  <li><a href="#consoleuart-configuration" id="markdown-toc-consoleuart-configuration">Console/UART Configuration</a></li>
  <li><a href="#video-capture-kvm" id="markdown-toc-video-capture-kvm">Video Capture (KVM)</a></li>
  <li><a href="#adding-device-tree-to-build" id="markdown-toc-adding-device-tree-to-build">Adding Device Tree to Build</a></li>
  <li><a href="#debugging-device-tree" id="markdown-toc-debugging-device-tree">Debugging Device Tree</a></li>
  <li><a href="#references" id="markdown-toc-references">References</a></li>
</ol>
---

## Overview

    

The device tree describes your hardware to the Linux kernel, including GPIO pins, I2C buses, SPI flash, and peripherals.

---

## Device Tree Structure

    

> **Source Reference**: OpenBMC Device Tree examples
>   
>     ASPEED DTS: linux/arch/arm/boot/dts/aspeed/
>     Reference: aspeed-bmc-opp-romulus.dts

```dts
/dts-v1/;

#include "aspeed-g5.dtsi"
#include <dt-bindings/gpio/aspeed-gpio.h>

/ {
    model = "MyPlatform MyBoard BMC";
    compatible = "myplatform,myboard-bmc", "aspeed,ast2500";

    chosen {
        stdout-path = &uart5;
        bootargs = "console=ttyS4,115200 earlyprintk";
    };

    memory@80000000 {
        reg = <0x80000000 0x20000000>;  /* 512MB */
    };
};
```

---

## GPIO Configuration

    

### LED GPIOs

    

```dts
leds {
    compatible = "gpio-leds";

    identify {
        label = "identify";
        gpios = <&gpio ASPEED_GPIO(A, 0) GPIO_ACTIVE_HIGH>;
        default-state = "off";
    };

    power {
        label = "power";
        gpios = <&gpio ASPEED_GPIO(A, 1) GPIO_ACTIVE_HIGH>;
        default-state = "on";
    };

    fault {
        label = "fault";
        gpios = <&gpio ASPEED_GPIO(A, 2) GPIO_ACTIVE_HIGH>;
        default-state = "off";
    };
};
```

### Button GPIOs

    

```dts
gpio-keys {
    compatible = "gpio-keys";

    power-button {
        label = "power-button";
        gpios = <&gpio ASPEED_GPIO(B, 0) GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW>;
        linux,code = <116>;  /* KEY_POWER */
    };

    reset-button {
        label = "reset-button";
        gpios = <&gpio ASPEED_GPIO(B, 1) GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW>;
        linux,code = <0x198>;  /* KEY_RESTART */
    };
};
```

---

## I2C Bus Configuration

    

```dts
&i2c0 {
    status = "okay";

    /* Temperature sensor */
    tmp75@48 {
        compatible = "ti,tmp75";
        reg = <0x48>;
    };
};

&i2c1 {
    status = "okay";

    /* FRU EEPROM */
    eeprom@50 {
        compatible = "atmel,24c256";
        reg = <0x50>;
    };
};

&i2c2 {
    status = "okay";

    /* Power supply */
    psu@58 {
        compatible = "pmbus";
        reg = <0x58>;
    };
};
```

---

## SPI Flash Configuration

    

```dts
&fmc {
    status = "okay";
    flash@0 {
        status = "okay";
        m25p,fast-read;
        label = "bmc";
        spi-max-frequency = <50000000>;
        #include "openbmc-flash-layout.dtsi"
    };
};

&spi1 {
    status = "okay";
    flash@0 {
        status = "okay";
        label = "pnor";
        spi-max-frequency = <100000000>;
    };
};
```

---

## Network Configuration

    

### NCSI (Sideband)

    

```dts
&mac0 {
    status = "okay";
    pinctrl-names = "default";
    pinctrl-0 = <&pinctrl_rmii1_default>;
    use-ncsi;
};
```

### Dedicated Ethernet

    

```dts
&mac1 {
    status = "okay";
    pinctrl-names = "default";
    pinctrl-0 = <&pinctrl_rgmii2_default>;
    phy-mode = "rgmii";
    phy-handle = <&phy1>;
};
```

---

## PWM/Fan Configuration

    

```dts
&pwm_tacho {
    status = "okay";
    pinctrl-names = "default";
    pinctrl-0 = <&pinctrl_pwm0_default &pinctrl_pwm1_default>;

    fan@0 {
        reg = <0x00>;
        aspeed,fan-tach-ch = /bits/ 8 <0x00>;
    };

    fan@1 {
        reg = <0x01>;
        aspeed,fan-tach-ch = /bits/ 8 <0x01>;
    };
};
```

---

## Console/UART Configuration

    

```dts
&uart5 {
    status = "okay";
};

&vuart {
    status = "okay";
};
```

---

## Video Capture (KVM)

    

```dts
reserved-memory {
    video_memory: video {
        size = <0x04000000>;  /* 64MB */
        alignment = <0x01000000>;
        compatible = "shared-dma-pool";
        reusable;
    };
};

&video {
    status = "okay";
    memory-region = <&video_memory>;
};
```

---

## Adding Device Tree to Build

    

```bitbake
# recipes-kernel/linux/linux-aspeed_%.bbappend

FILESEXTRAPATHS:prepend := "${THISDIR}/linux-aspeed:"

SRC_URI += "file://aspeed-bmc-myplatform-myboard.dts"

do_configure:append() {
    cp ${WORKDIR}/aspeed-bmc-myplatform-myboard.dts \
        ${S}/arch/arm/boot/dts/aspeed/
}
```

---

## Debugging Device Tree

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># View compiled device tree</span>
dtc <span class="nt">-I</span> dtb <span class="nt">-O</span> dts /sys/firmware/fdt

<span class="c"># Check GPIO assignments</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /sys/kernel/debug/gpio

<span class="c"># Check I2C buses</span>
i2cdetect <span class="nt">-l</span>
i2cdetect <span class="nt">-y</span> 0
```

</div></div>

## Overview

    

U-Boot is the bootloader for OpenBMC. It initializes hardware, loads the Linux kernel, and supports dual-image boot for failsafe recovery.

---

## U-Boot Configuration

    

### Default Configuration

    

<div class="language-make highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># configs/ast2500_openbmc_defconfig
</span>
<span class="nv">CONFIG_ARM</span><span class="o">=</span>y
<span class="nv">CONFIG_ARCH_ASPEED</span><span class="o">=</span>y
<span class="nv">CONFIG_SYS_TEXT_BASE</span><span class="o">=</span>0x00000000
<span class="nv">CONFIG_ASPEED_AST2500</span><span class="o">=</span>y
<span class="nv">CONFIG_TARGET_MYBOARD</span><span class="o">=</span>y
<span class="nv">CONFIG_DEFAULT_DEVICE_TREE</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"aspeed-bmc-myplatform-myboard"</span>
<span class="nv">CONFIG_FIT</span><span class="o">=</span>y
<span class="nv">CONFIG_FIT_SIGNATURE</span><span class="o">=</span>y
<span class="nv">CONFIG_SPL</span><span class="o">=</span>y
```

</div></div>

### Board Configuration

    

<div class="language-c highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c1">// include/configs/myboard.h</span>

<span class="cp">#ifndef __CONFIG_MYBOARD_H
#define __CONFIG_MYBOARD_H
</span>
<span class="cp">#include</span> <span class="cpf"><configs/aspeed-common.h></span><span class="cp">
</span>
<span class="cp">#define CONFIG_MACH_TYPE    MACH_TYPE_ASPEED
</span>
<span class="cm">/* Memory */</span>
<span class="cp">#define CONFIG_SYS_SDRAM_SIZE   0x20000000  </span><span class="cm">/* 512MB */</span><span class="cp">
</span>
<span class="cm">/* Flash */</span>
<span class="cp">#define CONFIG_SYS_MAX_FLASH_BANKS  1
#define CONFIG_SYS_MAX_FLASH_SECT   512
</span>
<span class="cm">/* Console */</span>
<span class="cp">#define CONFIG_CONS_INDEX   5  </span><span class="cm">/* UART5 */</span><span class="cp">
#define CONFIG_BAUDRATE     115200
</span>
<span class="cm">/* Boot */</span>
<span class="cp">#define CONFIG_BOOTCOMMAND  "run bootcmd_obmc"
#define CONFIG_BOOTARGS     "console=ttyS4,115200 earlyprintk"
</span>
<span class="cp">#endif
</span>
```

</div></div>
---

## Environment Variables

    

### Key Variables

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Variable | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bootcmd` | Boot command | `run bootcmd_obmc` |
| `bootargs` | Kernel arguments | `console=ttyS4,115200` |
| `bootside` | Active boot partition | `a` or `b` |
| `bootcount` | Boot attempt counter | `0` |
| `bootlimit` | Max boot attempts | `3` |

</div>

### Boot Commands

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Default boot command</span>
<span class="nv">bootcmd_obmc</span><span class="o">=</span>run set_bootargs<span class="p">;</span> bootm <span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">kerneladdr</span><span class="k">}</span>

<span class="c"># Set boot arguments</span>
<span class="nv">set_bootargs</span><span class="o">=</span>setenv bootargs <span class="nv">console</span><span class="o">=</span>ttyS4,115200 <span class="nv">root</span><span class="o">=</span>/dev/ram rw

<span class="c"># Load kernel</span>
<span class="nv">loadkernel</span><span class="o">=</span>sf probe 0<span class="p">;</span> sf <span class="nb">read</span> <span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">kerneladdr</span><span class="k">}</span> <span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">kerneloff</span><span class="k">}</span> <span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">kernelsize</span><span class="k">}</span>
```

</div></div>
---

## Dual Boot Support

    

### Partition Layout

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│           U-Boot SPL                 │ 0x000000
├──────────────────────────────────────┤
│           U-Boot                     │ 0x080000
├──────────────────────────────────────┤
│        U-Boot Environment            │ 0x100000
├──────────────────────────────────────┤
│        Image A (Active)              │ 0x200000
│   ┌──────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │         FIT Image            │   │
│   │   (kernel + initramfs + dtb) │   │
│   └──────────────────────────────┘   │
├──────────────────────────────────────┤
│        Image B (Standby)             │ 0x1000000
│   ┌──────────────────────────────┐   │
│   │         FIT Image            │   │
│   └──────────────────────────────┘   │
├──────────────────────────────────────┤
│           RW Partition               │ 0x1E00000
└──────────────────────────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

### Boot Selection Logic

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check boot side</span>
<span class="k">if </span><span class="nb">test</span> <span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">bootside</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s2">"a"</span><span class="p">;</span> <span class="k">then
    </span><span class="nv">kerneladdr</span><span class="o">=</span>0x20200000
<span class="k">else
    </span><span class="nv">kerneladdr</span><span class="o">=</span>0x21000000
<span class="k">fi</span>

<span class="c"># Increment boot counter</span>
setexpr bootcount <span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">bootcount</span><span class="k">}</span> + 1

<span class="c"># Check boot limit</span>
<span class="k">if </span><span class="nb">test</span> <span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">bootcount</span><span class="k">}</span> <span class="nt">-ge</span> <span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">bootlimit</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="p">;</span> <span class="k">then</span>
    <span class="c"># Switch to other side</span>
    <span class="k">if </span><span class="nb">test</span> <span class="s2">"</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">bootside</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="s2">"</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s2">"a"</span><span class="p">;</span> <span class="k">then
        </span>setenv bootside b
    <span class="k">else
        </span>setenv bootside a
    <span class="k">fi
    </span>setenv bootcount 0
<span class="k">fi</span>
```

</div></div>
---

## Adding U-Boot to Build

    

### Recipe Append

    

```bitbake
# recipes-bsp/u-boot/u-boot-aspeed_%.bbappend

FILESEXTRAPATHS:prepend := "${THISDIR}/u-boot-aspeed:"

SRC_URI += " \
    file://myboard_defconfig \
    file://myboard.h \
"

do_configure:prepend() {
    install -m 0644 ${WORKDIR}/myboard_defconfig \
        ${S}/configs/
    install -m 0644 ${WORKDIR}/myboard.h \
        ${S}/include/configs/
}
```

---

## U-Boot Commands

    

### Common Operations

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Print environment</span>
<span class="nb">printenv</span>

<span class="c"># Set variable</span>
setenv bootargs <span class="nv">console</span><span class="o">=</span>ttyS4,115200

<span class="c"># Save environment</span>
saveenv

<span class="c"># Boot kernel</span>
bootm <span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">kerneladdr</span><span class="k">}</span>

<span class="c"># Reset</span>
reset
```

</div></div>

### Flash Operations

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Probe SPI flash</span>
sf probe 0

<span class="c"># Read flash</span>
sf <span class="nb">read </span>0x83000000 0x200000 0x800000

<span class="c"># Erase flash</span>
sf erase 0x200000 0x800000

<span class="c"># Write flash</span>
sf write 0x83000000 0x200000 0x800000
```

</div></div>

### Debug

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Memory dump</span>
md 0x80000000 100

<span class="c"># I2C scan</span>
i2c bus
i2c dev 0
i2c probe

<span class="c"># GPIO</span>
gpio status
```

</div></div>

```
saveenv
reset
```

## Overview

    

Systematic verification ensures your OpenBMC port works correctly. This guide provides test procedures for each major subsystem.

---

## Verification Checklist

    

### Boot & Basic

    

* U-Boot initializes correctly
* Kernel boots without errors
* Root filesystem mounts
* BMC reaches Ready state
* Console access works
* Network connectivity

### Power Control

    

* Power on host
* Power off host
* Graceful shutdown
* Force power off
* Power cycle
* Reset host

### Sensors

    

* Temperature sensors read correctly
* Voltage sensors read correctly
* Fan tach sensors work
* Thresholds trigger events
* Sensors appear in Redfish/IPMI

### Thermal Management

    

* Fan PWM control works
* PID control adjusts fans
* Thermal zones configured
* Over-temperature protection

### Remote Access

    

* SSH login
* WebUI access
* Redfish API
* IPMI over LAN
* KVM (if applicable)
* Virtual media (if applicable)

---

## Boot Verification

    

### U-Boot Check

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># During boot, watch for:</span>
<span class="c"># - Memory initialization</span>
<span class="c"># - Flash detection</span>
<span class="c"># - Kernel loading</span>

<span class="c"># At U-Boot prompt:</span>
<span class="nb">printenv
</span>md 0x80000000 100  <span class="c"># Memory check</span>
```

</div></div>

### Kernel Boot

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Watch console for:</span>
<span class="c"># - Device tree loading</span>
<span class="c"># - Driver initialization</span>
<span class="c"># - Filesystem mount</span>

<span class="c"># Check dmesg after boot</span>
dmesg | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> error
dmesg | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> fail
```

</div></div>

### BMC State

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check BMC state</span>
obmcutil state

<span class="c"># Expected:</span>
<span class="c"># BMC: Ready</span>
<span class="c"># Chassis: Off (initially)</span>
<span class="c"># Host: Off (initially)</span>
```

</div></div>

## Power Control Tests

    

### Basic Power Operations

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Power on</span>
obmcutil poweron
<span class="nb">sleep </span>10
obmcutil state  <span class="c"># Check host is Running</span>

<span class="c"># Power off</span>
obmcutil poweroff
<span class="nb">sleep </span>10
obmcutil state  <span class="c"># Check host is Off</span>

<span class="c"># Power cycle</span>
obmcutil poweron
<span class="nb">sleep </span>30
obmcutil powercycle
<span class="nb">sleep </span>10
obmcutil state
```

</div></div>

## Common Issues

    

### Sensors Not Appearing

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check Entity Manager</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> entity-manager

<span class="c"># Verify configuration</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /usr/share/entity-manager/configurations/<span class="k">*</span>.json

<span class="c"># Check dbus-sensors</span>
journalctl <span class="nt">-u</span> dbus-sensors
```

## Overview

    

This guide covers porting OpenBMC to ARM-based server platforms, using NVIDIA’s OpenBMC fork as a reference implementation. While the [Porting Reference](/openbmc-guide-tutorial/docs/06-porting/01-porting-reference.html) focuses on ASPEED-based BMCs managing x86 hosts, this guide addresses ARM-native server platforms where both the host and BMC may use ARM processors.

**Reference Repository**: [NVIDIA OpenBMC](https://github.com/NVIDIA/openbmc) (develop branch)

---

## ARM vs ASPEED Architecture

    

### Key Differences

    

```mermaid
---
title: ARM vs ASPEED Architecture Comparison
---
flowchart TB
    subgraph aspeed["Traditional ASPEED BMC"]
        direction TB
        aspeed_bmc["ASPEED BMC  
(AST2500/2600)"]
        aspeed_host["x86 Host  
(Intel/AMD CPU)"]
        aspeed_mgmt["BMC manages  
x86 platform"]
        aspeed_bmc <-->|"LPC / eSPI"| aspeed_host
        aspeed_bmc --> aspeed_mgmt
    end

    subgraph arm["ARM Server Platform"]
        direction TB
        arm_bmc["ARM BMC  
(Various ARM SoCs)"]
        arm_host["ARM Host  
(Grace, Ampere, etc.)"]
        arm_mgmt["BMC manages  
ARM platform"]
        arm_bmc <-->|"PCIe / I2C / MCTP"| arm_host
        arm_bmc --> arm_mgmt
    end
```

> **ASCII-art version (for comparison)**

  <div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                    Traditional ASPEED BMC                        |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                  |
|  +------------------+          +----------------------------+    |
|  |   ASPEED BMC     |   LPC    |        x86 Host            |    |
|  |   (AST2500/2600) |<-------->|    (Intel/AMD CPU)         |    |
|  |                  |   eSPI   |                            |    |
|  +------------------+          +----------------------------+    |
|         |                                                        |
|         v                                                        |
|  +--------------+                                                |
|  | BMC manages  |                                                |
|  | x86 platform |                                                |
|  +--------------+                                                |
|                                                                  |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+

+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                    ARM Server Platform                           |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                  |
|  +------------------+          +----------------------------+    |
|  |   ARM BMC        |   PCIe   |        ARM Host            |    |
|  |   (Various ARM   |<-------->|    (Grace, Ampere, etc.)   |    |
|  |    SoCs)         |   I2C    |                            |    |
|  +------------------+   MCTP   +----------------------------+    |
|         |                                                        |
|         v                                                        |
|  +--------------+                                                |
|  | BMC manages  |                                                |
|  | ARM platform |                                                |
|  +--------------+                                                |
|                                                                  |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

</div>  </div>

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Aspect | ASPEED BMC | ARM Platform |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **BMC SoC** | AST2500/AST2600 (ARM core) | Various ARM SoCs |
| **Host CPU** | x86 (Intel/AMD) | ARM (Grace, Ampere, etc.) |
| **Host Interface** | LPC, eSPI | PCIe, I2C, MCTP |
| **Boot Firmware** | ASPEED SDK | TF-A, OP-TEE, U-Boot |
| **Console** | VUART, LPC UART | Physical UART, SSH |
| **POST Codes** | LPC snoop | Platform-specific |

</div>

### Platform Communication

    

ARM platforms typically use different host-BMC communication methods:

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Interface | Description | Use Case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **PCIe** | High-bandwidth link | Firmware updates, data transfer |
| **I2C/SMBus** | Low-speed control bus | Sensor polling, FRU access |
| **MCTP** | Management Component Transport | PLDM, SPDM messaging |
| **GPIO** | Direct signal control | Power control, reset, alerts |
| **Network** | Out-of-band management | Redfish, IPMI-over-LAN |

</div>

## meta-arm Layer Integration

    

ARM platforms use the Yocto Project’s meta-arm layer stack for base support.

### Layer Stack

    

```mermaid
---
title: meta-arm Layer Stack
---
flowchart TB
    platform["Your Platform Layer  
(meta-your-platform)"]
    vendor["Vendor Layer (optional)  
(meta-nvidia, etc.)"]
    armbsp["meta-arm-bsp  
(Reference platform BSPs)"]
    metaarm["meta-arm  
(ARM architecture recipes)"]
    toolchain["meta-arm-toolchain  
(GCC/Clang for ARM)"]
    base["OpenBMC Base Layers  
(meta-phosphor, meta-openembedded, poky)"]

    platform --> vendor
    vendor --> armbsp
    armbsp --> metaarm
    metaarm --> toolchain
    toolchain --> base
```

  <div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                     Your Platform Layer                          |
|                    (meta-your-platform)                          |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                    Vendor Layer (optional)                       |
|                     (meta-nvidia, etc.)                          |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                    meta-arm-bsp                                  |
|              (Reference platform BSPs)                           |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                    meta-arm                                      |
|              (ARM architecture recipes)                          |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |

+------------------------------------------------------------------+

```

### Adding meta-arm to Your Build

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Clone meta-arm layers</span>
<span class="nb">cd</span> /path/to/openbmc
git clone https://git.yoctoproject.org/meta-arm

<span class="c"># Add to bblayers.conf</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> <span class="o">>></span> conf/bblayers.conf <span class="o"><<</span> <span class="sh">'</span><span class="no">EOF</span><span class="sh">'
BBLAYERS += "</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BSPDIR</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/meta-arm/meta-arm"
BBLAYERS += "</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BSPDIR</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/meta-arm/meta-arm-toolchain"
# Optional: Reference BSPs
# BBLAYERS += "</span><span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">BSPDIR</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="sh">/meta-arm/meta-arm-bsp"
</span><span class="no">EOF
</span>
```

</div></div>

| **meta-arm-bsp** | Reference platforms | FVP, Juno, N1SDP |

## Machine Configuration

    

### ARM Machine Template

    

Create your machine configuration based on ARM patterns:

```bitbake
# conf/machine/myarm-bmc.conf

#@TYPE: Machine
#@NAME: My ARM BMC Platform
#@DESCRIPTION: OpenBMC for ARM-based server

# ARM64 architecture
DEFAULTTUNE = "cortexa53"
require conf/machine/include/arm/armv8a/tune-cortexa53.inc

# Kernel configuration
PREFERRED_PROVIDER_virtual/kernel = "linux-aspeed"
KERNEL_IMAGETYPE = "Image"
KERNEL_DEVICETREE = "${KMACHINE}.dtb"

# U-Boot configuration
PREFERRED_PROVIDER_virtual/bootloader = "u-boot"
PREFERRED_PROVIDER_u-boot = "u-boot"
UBOOT_MACHINE = "myarm_bmc_defconfig"

# Flash layout (adjust for your platform)
FLASH_SIZE = "65536"  # 64MB
FLASH_UBOOT_OFFSET = "0"
FLASH_KERNEL_OFFSET = "1024"
FLASH_ROFS_OFFSET = "10240"
FLASH_RWFS_OFFSET = "49152"

# Console configuration
SERIAL_CONSOLES = "115200;ttyAMA0"

# Machine features
MACHINE_FEATURES = "efi"

# OpenBMC features - customize for your platform
OBMC_MACHINE_FEATURES += "\
    obmc-bmc-state-mgmt \
    obmc-phosphor-fan-mgmt \
    obmc-phosphor-flash-mgmt \
"

# Entity Manager for inventory
VIRTUAL-RUNTIME_obmc-inventory-manager = "entity-manager"
```

### Key ARM Machine Variables

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Variable | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DEFAULTTUNE` | CPU tuning | `cortexa53`, `cortexa72` |
| `KERNEL_IMAGETYPE` | Kernel format | `Image` (ARM64), `zImage` (ARM32) |
| `SERIAL_CONSOLES` | Console device | `115200;ttyAMA0` |
| `MACHINE_FEATURES` | Platform features | `efi`, `optee` |

</div>
---

## NVIDIA OpenBMC Reference

    

NVIDIA’s OpenBMC fork provides a production-quality reference for ARM platforms.

### Repository Structure

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
NVIDIA/openbmc (develop branch)
├── meta-nvidia/
│   ├── conf/
│   │   └── layer.conf                    # Layer configuration
│   ├── meta-common/                      # Shared components
│   ├── meta-prime/                       # Server platform support
│   │   └── meta-graceblackwell/          # Grace Blackwell
│   │       └── meta-gb200nvl/            # GB200 NVL machine
│   │           └── meta-bmc/
│   │               └── conf/machine/
│   │                   ├── gb200nvl-bmc.conf
│   │                   └── gb200nvl-bmc-ut3.conf
│   ├── recipes-phosphor/                 # OpenBMC customizations
│   └── recipes-nvidia/                   # NVIDIA-specific recipes
```

</div></div>

**Reference**: [meta-nvidia/conf/layer.conf](https://github.com/NVIDIA/openbmc/blob/develop/meta-nvidia/conf/layer.conf)

### NVIDIA Layer Configuration

    

The NVIDIA layer configuration demonstrates vendor layer patterns:

```bitbake
# Reference: meta-nvidia/conf/layer.conf
# https://github.com/NVIDIA/openbmc/blob/develop/meta-nvidia/conf/layer.conf

# Layer name and compatibility
BBFILE_COLLECTIONS += "nvidia-layer"
LAYERSERIES_COMPAT_nvidia-layer = "whinlatter walnascar"

# Recipe patterns
BBFILES += "${LAYERDIR}/recipes-*/*/*.bb \
            ${LAYERDIR}/recipes-*/*/*.bbappend"
```

**Key patterns (NVIDIA-specific)**:

* Uses nested meta-* layers for platform hierarchy
* Separate layers for BMC, HMC (Hardware Management Controller), PMC (Power Management Controller)
* Repository mirroring for internal GitLab → GitHub

**Generic ARM patterns**:

* Standard layer.conf structure
* Recipe organization by function (recipes-phosphor, recipes-kernel, etc.)

### NVIDIA Machine Configuration Example

    

From `meta-nvidia/meta-prime/meta-graceblackwell/meta-gb200nvl/meta-bmc/conf/machine/gb200nvl-bmc.conf`:

```bitbake
# Reference: gb200nvl-bmc.conf
# NVIDIA GB200 NVL BMC - uses ASPEED AST2600 as BMC SoC

# Device tree
KERNEL_DEVICETREE = "aspeed-bmc-nvidia-gb200nvl-bmc.dtb"

# U-Boot
UBOOT_MACHINE = "ast2600_openbmc_spl_defconfig"
SPL_BINARY = "spl/u-boot-spl.bin"

# Flash layout (64MB)
FLASH_SIZE = "65536"
FLASH_UBOOT_OFFSET:flash-65536 = "0"
FLASH_KERNEL_OFFSET:flash-65536 = "1024"
FLASH_ROFS_OFFSET:flash-65536 = "10240"

# Console
SERIAL_CONSOLES = "115200;ttyS4"

# Use Entity Manager
VIRTUAL-RUNTIME_obmc-inventory-manager = "entity-manager"

# Feature selection
OBMC_IMAGE_EXTRA_INSTALL:remove = "phosphor-snmp"
```

**Note**: The GB200 NVL uses an ASPEED AST2600 as the BMC SoC managing an ARM Grace Hopper host. This is a hybrid architecture.

---

## ARM Boot Flow

    

ARM platforms use a standardized boot flow with Trusted Firmware-A (TF-A).

### Boot Sequence

    

```mermaid
---
title: ARM Boot Flow
---
flowchart LR
    bl1["BL1  
(ROM/Flash)"]
    bl2["BL2  
(Trusted Boot)"]
    bl31["BL31  
(Secure Monitor)"]
    bl32["BL32  
(OP-TEE)  
[Optional]"]
    bl33["BL33  
(U-Boot)"]
    linux["Linux  
Kernel"]

    bl1 --> bl2
    bl2 --> bl31
    bl31 -.-> bl32
    bl32 -.-> bl33
    bl31 --> bl33
    bl33 --> linux
```

**Legend:**

* **BL1** - Boot Loader Stage 1 (ROM or first-stage flash)
* **BL2** - Trusted Boot Firmware
* **BL31** - EL3 Runtime Firmware (Secure Monitor)
* **BL32** - Secure Payload (OP-TEE, optional)
* **BL33** - Non-secure Bootloader (U-Boot)

> **ASCII-art version (for comparison)**

  <div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                      ARM Boot Flow                               |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                  |
|  +------------+     +------------+     +------------+            |
|  |   BL1      |---->|   BL2      |---->|   BL31     |            |
|  | (ROM/Flash)|     | (Trusted   |     | (Secure    |            |
|  |            |     |  Boot)     |     |  Monitor)  |            |
|  +------------+     +------------+     +------+-----+            |
|                                               |                  |
|                           +-------------------+                  |
|                           |                                      |
|                           v                                      |
|  +------------+     +------------+     +------------+            |
|  |   BL32     |     |   BL33     |---->|   Linux    |            |
|  | (OP-TEE)   |     | (U-Boot)   |     |  Kernel    |            |
|  | (Optional) |     |            |     |            |            |
|  +------------+     +------------+     +------------+            |
|                                                                  |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

</div>  </div>

### Boot Components

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Stage | Component | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BL1 | ROM/Flash | First boot code, initializes BL2 |
| BL2 | TF-A | Trusted boot, loads BL31/BL32/BL33 |
| BL31 | TF-A Runtime | Secure Monitor, handles SMC calls |
| BL32 | OP-TEE | Trusted execution environment (optional) |
| BL33 | U-Boot | Standard bootloader, loads Linux |

</div>

### TF-A Configuration

    

```bitbake
# recipes-bsp/trusted-firmware-a/trusted-firmware-a_%.bbappend

# Platform-specific TF-A configuration
TFA_PLATFORM = "myarm"
TFA_BUILD_TARGET = "bl31"

# Optional: Enable secure boot
TFA_MBEDTLS_DIR = "${STAGING_DIR_HOST}${libdir}"
TFA_ARM_ARCH = "8.0"
```

### U-Boot for ARM Platforms

    

```bitbake
# recipes-bsp/u-boot/u-boot_%.bbappend

# ARM-specific U-Boot configuration
UBOOT_MACHINE = "myarm_bmc_defconfig"

# Enable FIT images for secure boot
UBOOT_MKIMAGE_DTCOPTS = "-I dts -O dtb -p 2000"
UBOOT_SIGN_ENABLE = "1"
```

---

## ARM Device Tree

    

ARM platforms use standard Device Tree conventions with some BMC-specific patterns.

### Device Tree Structure

    

```dts
// myarm-bmc.dts
/dts-v1/;

#include "arm-soc-base.dtsi"

/ {
    model = "My ARM BMC Platform";
    compatible = "vendor,myarm-bmc", "arm,cortex-a53";

    chosen {
        stdout-path = "serial0:115200n8";
    };

    aliases {
        serial0 = &uart0;
        i2c0 = &i2c0;
    };
};

// I2C bus for sensor/FRU access
&i2c0 {
    status = "okay";
    clock-frequency = <100000>;

    // Temperature sensor
    tmp75@48 {
        compatible = "ti,tmp75";
        reg = <0x48>;
    };

    // FRU EEPROM
    eeprom@50 {
        compatible = "atmel,24c64";
        reg = <0x50>;
    };
};

// GPIO for platform control
&gpio0 {
    status = "okay";

    power-button {
        gpios = <&gpio0 10 GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW>;
        linux,code = <KEY_POWER>;
    };

    reset-button {
        gpios = <&gpio0 11 GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW>;
        linux,code = <KEY_RESTART>;
    };
};
```

### Common ARM Bindings

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Peripheral | Binding | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UART | `arm,pl011` | Console, host UART |
| I2C | `arm,versatile-i2c` | Sensors, EEPROMs |
| SPI | `arm,pl022` | Flash access |
| GPIO | `arm,pl061` | Power control |
| Watchdog | `arm,sp805` | System watchdog |

</div>
---

## MCTP/PLDM Integration

    

ARM platforms often use MCTP/PLDM for host-BMC communication.

See the [MCTP/PLDM Guide](/openbmc-guide-tutorial/docs/05-advanced/01-mctp-pldm-guide.html) for detailed information.

### Common Configuration

    

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="err">//</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">Entity</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">Manager</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">MCTP</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">endpoint</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="err">configuration</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Exposes"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Host MCTP Endpoint"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"MCTPEndpoint"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Bus"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Address"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"0x08"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"MessageTypes"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">"PLDM"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"SPDM"</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

## Troubleshooting

    

### Common Issues

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Issue | Cause | Solution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No console output | Wrong UART device | Check `SERIAL_CONSOLES` in machine.conf |
| Kernel panic on boot | Missing DT bindings | Verify device tree compatible strings |
| I2C devices not found | Bus numbering mismatch | Check DT aliases and bus assignments |
| TF-A build fails | Missing platform files | Implement platform-specific TF-A port |

</div>

### Debug Tips

    

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="c"># Check boot messages</span>
dmesg | <span class="nb">grep</span> <span class="nt">-i</span> arm

<span class="c"># Verify device tree</span>
<span class="nb">cat</span> /proc/device-tree/model

<span class="c"># List I2C buses</span>
i2cdetect <span class="nt">-l</span>

<span class="c"># Check MCTP endpoints</span>
busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.MCTP
```

</div></div>

## Overview

    

This guide covers advanced Entity Manager topics for complex hardware configurations. For basic Entity Manager concepts, see the [Entity Manager Guide](/openbmc-guide-tutorial/docs/03-core-services/03-entity-manager-guide.html).

Entity Manager dynamically discovers hardware using JSON configuration files with “probes” that match system conditions. When probes match, Entity Manager exposes D-Bus objects that other services (sensors, fan control) use.

### When to Use This Guide

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Scenario | This Guide Helps |
| --- | --- |
| Complex probe conditions (regex, multi-field) | ✅ |
| FRU EEPROM integration | ✅ |
| Migrating from static to dynamic config | ✅ |
| Debugging Entity Manager issues | ✅ |
| Basic Entity Manager setup | Use basic guide |

</div>
---

## Advanced Probe Patterns

    

Probes determine when a configuration applies. Advanced patterns allow precise hardware matching.

### Regex Probes

    

Use regex patterns to match variable hardware identifiers:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Exposes"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="err">...</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Motherboard Sensors"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Probe"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.FruDevice({'PRODUCT_PRODUCT_NAME': '.*Motherboard.*'})"</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

**Regex syntax:**

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Pattern | Matches |
| --- | --- |
| `.*` | Any characters (wildcard) |
| `^ABC` | Starts with “ABC” |
| `XYZ$` | Ends with “XYZ” |
| `V[0-9]+` | “V” followed by digits |
| `(A\\|B)` | Either “A” or “B” |

</div>

**Example: Match multiple product variants:**

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Probe"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.FruDevice({'PRODUCT_PRODUCT_NAME': '^(Server-2U|Server-4U).*'})"</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

### Multi-Condition Probes (AND)

    

Match multiple conditions simultaneously using array syntax:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Probe"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.FruDevice({'PRODUCT_MANUFACTURER': 'ACME'})"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.FruDevice({'PRODUCT_PRODUCT_NAME': 'PowerBoard'})"</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

All conditions must match (logical AND). This ensures the configuration only applies when both manufacturer AND product name match.

### OR Condition Probes

    

For OR logic, use the `OR` keyword:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Probe"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"OR"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"ProbeValue"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.FruDevice({'PRODUCT_PRODUCT_NAME': 'BoardTypeA'})"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.FruDevice({'PRODUCT_PRODUCT_NAME': 'BoardTypeB'})"</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

### GPIO-Based Hardware Detection

    

Detect hardware presence using GPIO pins:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Probe"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Decorator.Asset({'Name': 'Riser Card'})"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Riser Card Sensors"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Exposes"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Riser_Temp"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"TMP75"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Bus"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">6</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Address"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"0x48"</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

For GPIO presence detection, use the GpioPresence daemon which creates inventory objects based on GPIO state:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"GPU Presence"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"GpioPresence"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Pin"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"GPU_PRSNT_N"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"ActiveLow"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kc">true</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

### I2C Address Probes with Wildcards

    

Match devices across multiple I2C buses:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Probe"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.FruDevice({'BUS': '.*', 'ADDRESS': '0x50'})"</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

**Specific bus range:**

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Probe"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.FruDevice({'BUS': '[2-5]', 'ADDRESS': '0x50'})"</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>
---

## FruDevice Integration

    

FruDevice daemon scans I2C buses for FRU EEPROMs and exposes their contents via D-Bus.

### FruDevice Role

    

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────────────┐
│ FRU EEPROM   │───>│  FruDevice   │───>│  D-Bus Objects   │
│ (I2C 0x50)   │    │   Daemon     │    │  FruDevice/*     │
└──────────────┘    └──────────────┘    └──────────────────┘
                                               │
                                               v
                                        ┌──────────────────┐
                                        │  Entity Manager  │
                                        │  (Probe Match)   │
                                        └──────────────────┘
```

</div></div>

FruDevice scans configured I2C buses at boot and exposes discovered FRU data as D-Bus objects that Entity Manager can probe against.

### FRU EEPROM Structure

    

Standard IPMI FRU format (IPMI Platform Management FRU Information Storage Definition):

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Area | Common Fields |
| --- | --- |
| **Board Info** | BOARD_MANUFACTURER, BOARD_PRODUCT_NAME, BOARD_SERIAL_NUMBER, BOARD_PART_NUMBER |
| **Product Info** | PRODUCT_MANUFACTURER, PRODUCT_PRODUCT_NAME, PRODUCT_PART_NUMBER, PRODUCT_VERSION, PRODUCT_SERIAL_NUMBER |
| **Chassis Info** | CHASSIS_TYPE, CHASSIS_PART_NUMBER, CHASSIS_SERIAL_NUMBER |

</div>

### FruDevice Probe Configuration

    

Configure FruDevice to scan specific I2C buses in your machine layer:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Exposes"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Motherboard FRU"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"EEPROM"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Bus"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Address"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"0x50"</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"Baseboard FRU Config"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Probe"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"TRUE"</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

### Referencing FRU Fields in Exposes

    

Use `$` syntax to reference FRU fields dynamically:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Probe"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"xyz.openbmc_project.FruDevice({'PRODUCT_PRODUCT_NAME': 'PowerModule'})"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"$PRODUCT_SERIAL_NUMBER Power Module"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Exposes"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Name"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"$BOARD_PRODUCT_NAME Voltage"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Type"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"ADC"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Index"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"ScaleFactor"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mf">0.001</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w">
</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
</span>
```

</div></div>

The `$FIELD_NAME` syntax substitutes the actual FRU field value at runtime, enabling unique naming for multiple identical modules.

---

## Inventory Manager vs Entity Manager

    

Choose the right approach for your platform:

### Comparison Table

    

<div class="table-wrapper">
| Aspect | Inventory Manager (Static) | Entity Manager (Dynamic) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Configuration** | YAML files at build time | JSON files with runtime probes |
| **Hardware Discovery** | None - predefined | FRU EEPROM, GPIO, I2C scan |
| **Hot-plug Support** | No | Yes |
| **Configuration Complexity** | Simple | More complex |
| **Flexibility** | Low | High |
| **Debugging** | Easy - static | Requires understanding probes |
| **Best For** | Fixed hardware, prototypes | Production with variants |

</div>

### Decision Criteria

    

**Use Inventory Manager (Static) when:**

* Hardware configuration is fixed and known at build time
* Rapid prototyping or proof-of-concept
* Simple platforms without FRU EEPROMs
* Legacy platforms being maintained

**Use Entity Manager (Dynamic) when:**

* Multiple hardware variants share one image
* Hot-pluggable components (risers, drives)
* FRU EEPROMs identify components
* Production platforms with SKU variants

### Migration Path: Static to Dynamic

    

1. **Identify static configurations** in your YAML inventory files
2. **Document hardware variants** and how they differ
3. **Add FRU EEPROMs** to boards (or use existing ones)
4. **Create Entity Manager JSON** with probes matching FRU data
5. **Test each variant** to verify correct probe matching
6. **Remove static YAML** configurations
7. **Update recipes** to install JSON configs instead of YAML

---

## Real-World Configuration Examples

    

### Temperature Sensor Configuration

    

Configure hwmon temperature sensors discovered via Entity Manager:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight">
```
<span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
    </span><span class="nl">"Exposes"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">
        </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">
            </span><span class="nl">"Address"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"0x48"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">

                </span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w">

            </span><span class="nl">"Thresholds"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w">

</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="w">
```
